member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.BaseContext
member.summary: Provides a base context class for logging operations and utility functions across the VisioForge SDK. This class serves as a foundation for other SDK components, offering centralized logging capabilities and shared utilities like random number generation.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.BaseContext.Logger
member.summary: The Serilog logger instance used for structured logging throughout the SDK.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.BaseContext.Rnd
member.summary: Gets a shared random number generator instance for use across the SDK. This provides a convenient way to generate random values for various operations such as unique identifiers, test data, or randomization features.
member.value: A Random instance that can be used for generating random values.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.BaseContext.SetLogger(Serilog.ILogger)
member.summary: Sets the Serilog logger instance to be used for all logging operations in this context. This allows for centralized logging configuration and ensures consistent log formatting across all SDK components that inherit from this base context.
member.param: The Serilog logger instance to use for logging operations. Can be null to disable logging.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.BaseContext.GetLogger
member.summary: Gets the current Serilog logger instance configured for this context.
member.returns: The current ILogger instance, or null if no logger has been set.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.BaseContext.Error(System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Logs an error message with structured context information including class and method names. The message will be written to both the configured Serilog logger and System.Diagnostics.Debug output. Messages containing "unregistered" are treated specially and only written to debug output.
member.param: The name of the class where the error occurred.
The name of the method where the error occurred.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.DeviceEnumerator
member.summary: Provides specialized enumeration for Allied Vision industrial cameras using the Vimba X SDK integration. This partial class handles discovery and management of Allied Vision machine vision cameras including GigE Vision, USB3 Vision, and Camera Link cameras. Integrates with Allied Vision's Vimba X library for native camera enumeration, device information retrieval, and GenTL provider management. Essential for professional machine vision and industrial imaging applications.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.

Provides comprehensive audio device enumeration capabilities across multiple platforms and APIs. This partial class handles discovery and monitoring of audio capture sources and output devices using GStreamer's device monitoring framework. Supports cross-platform audio device detection including DirectSound, WASAPI, PulseAudio, ALSA, and Core Audio with real-time device change notifications and permission handling for mobile platforms.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.

Provides specialized enumeration for Basler industrial cameras using the Pylon SDK integration. This partial class handles discovery and management of Basler machine vision cameras including GigE Vision, USB3 Vision, and Camera Link cameras. Integrates with Basler's Pylon library for native camera enumeration, device information retrieval, and camera capability detection. Essential for professional machine vision and industrial imaging applications.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.

Provides specialized enumeration for Blackmagic Design DeckLink professional video hardware. This partial class handles discovery and management of DeckLink capture and playback devices including video sources, audio sources, video sinks, and audio sinks. Manages professional broadcast hardware interfaces for high-quality video capture, playback, and signal monitoring with real-time device detection and signal loss notifications.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.

Provides GenICam (Generic Interface for Cameras) device enumeration for industrial and scientific cameras. This partial class handles discovery and management of GenICam-compliant cameras including machine vision cameras, scientific imaging devices, and industrial cameras using the GenICam standard. Supports camera enumeration with detailed device information, pixel format detection, and fallback mechanisms for robust camera discovery in professional imaging applications.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.

Cross-platform device enumerator that discovers and manages audio/video input devices, professional hardware, and network sources across all supported platforms. This class provides unified access to webcams, microphones, capture cards, IP cameras (ONVIF), NDI sources, Decklink devices, and industrial cameras (GenICam/GigE Vision). Supports both synchronous and asynchronous device discovery with platform-specific optimizations.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.

Provides Network Device Interface (NDI) source discovery and enumeration capabilities. This partial class handles detection of NDI video and audio sources over IP networks, enabling real-time video streaming and production workflows. Manages NDI device provider lifecycle, source discovery with retry logic, and maintains collections of available NDI sources for professional broadcast and streaming applications.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.

Provides ONVIF (Open Network Video Interface Forum) device discovery for IP-based security cameras and video surveillance systems. This partial class handles network-based discovery of ONVIF-compliant devices including IP cameras, NVRs, and video management systems using WS-Discovery protocol. Supports timeout configuration, cancellation tokens, and asynchronous discovery operations for professional surveillance and security applications.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.

Provides specialized enumeration for FLIR/Teledyne industrial cameras using the Spinnaker SDK integration. This partial class handles discovery and management of FLIR machine vision cameras including GigE Vision, USB3 Vision, and 10GigE cameras. Integrates with FLIR's Spinnaker library for comprehensive camera enumeration, detailed device information retrieval, sensor specifications, and camera capability detection. Essential for professional machine vision, scientific imaging, and industrial automation applications.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.

Provides comprehensive video capture device enumeration and monitoring across multiple platforms. This partial class handles discovery of video capture sources including webcams, capture cards, and virtual devices using GStreamer's device monitoring framework. Supports platform-specific providers like DirectShow (Windows), AVFoundation (macOS/iOS), V4L2 (Linux), and UVC devices with real-time device change notifications and permission handling.
The namespace contains core components and utilities for VisioForge multimedia SDKs. This includes device enumeration, media processing, and various helper classes.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.DLL
member.summary: Cross-platform native library loading and mapping utilities for the VisioForge SDK. Provides automatic resolution of platform-specific native library names and handles dynamic loading of required native dependencies across Windows, Linux, and macOS platforms. This class ensures proper native library loading for ONVIF and other platform-specific components.
member.remarks: The DLL class handles: - Cross-platform native library name mapping (Windows DLL, Linux SO, macOS dylib) - Automatic architecture detection (x86, x64) for proper library selection - Runtime library resolution via NativeLibrary.SetDllImportResolver - Support for ONVIF camera integration libraries across all platforms - Fallback mechanisms for library loading failures This functionality is essential for proper operation of platform-specific features like ONVIF camera support.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.DSP.DSPConst.DefaultSampleSize
member.summary: Used by DSP Filters to Set the default Split Size. This is needed when a large Buffer arrives and the Application would't respond until the DSP is done. If the SampleSize of an Filter is Set to Value > 0 then the Buffer will be splitted at this amount of Samples and processed until all Samples are processed. After every Process, Application.ProcessMessages is called to make the Application respond to Windows. DefaultSampleSize is just a default Value. The SampleSize can be changed on every Filter seperate.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.DSP.DSPConverter
member.summary: Static methods to convert between different sample formats.

remarks.para: Code is mainly based on information available on the original C source code pa_converters.c from Portable Audio I/O Library.
This class try to be as fast as possible without using unsafe code.
Dither isn't currently supported. Currently supported conversions are 'to' and 'from' conversions between the following value types:
Integer 8-bit (byte), Integer 16-bit (Int16), Integer 32-bit (Int32), Single precision 32-bit floating point (float).
Which are the most common PCM formats.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.DSP.Equalizer.AudioEncoding.MPEG_ADTS_AAC
member.summary: Advanced Audio Coding (AAC) audio in Audio Data Transport Stream (ADTS) format. The format block is a WAVEFORMATEX structure with wFormatTag equal to WAVE_FORMAT_MPEG_ADTS_AAC.
member.remarks: The WAVEFORMATEX structure specifies the core AAC-LC sample rate and number of channels, prior to applying spectral band replication (SBR) or parametric stereo (PS) tools, if present. No additional data is required after the WAVEFORMATEX structure.

member.summary: Gets or sets the block alignment, in bytes. The block alignment is the minimum atomic unit of data. member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.FFT
member.summary: Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) implementation for audio frequency analysis and spectrum computation. Provides high-performance FFT calculations for real-time audio processing, frequency analysis, and spectrum visualization within the VisioForge SDK. Based on the Cooley-Tukey FFT algorithm with optimizations for power-of-two sample sizes commonly used in audio processing.
member.remarks: FFT capabilities include: - Forward and inverse FFT computation for complex number arrays - Power spectrum calculation for frequency domain analysis - Peak frequency detection for audio analysis applications - Optimized bit-reversal and butterfly operations for performance - Support for real and imaginary input data processing - Amplitude normalization for proper spectrum scaling This implementation is based on the 1998 version by Don Cross with enhancements for .NET integration. Licensed under a permissive license allowing commercial use and redistribution.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.AlliedVision.VimbaAPI.VmbFeaturesList(System.IntPtr,System.IntPtr,System.UInt32,System.UInt32@,System.UInt32)
member.summary: Lists all the features for this entity.
member.remarks: This function lists all implemented features, whether they are currently available or not. The list of features does not change as long as the entity is connected. This function is usually called twice: once with an empty list to query the length of the list, and then again with a list of the correct length. If VmbErrorMoreData is returned and numFound is non-null, the total number of features has been written to numFound. If there are more elements in featureInfoList than features available, the remaining elements are filled with zero-initialized VmbFeatureInfo_t structs.
member.param: Handle for an entity that exposes features.
An array of VmbFeatureInfo_t to be filled by the API. May be null if numFound is used for size query.
Number of VmbFeatureInfo_t elements found. May be null if featureInfoList is not null.
member.returns: An error code indicating success or the type of error that occurred.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.ArvGentlDevice.ShowIntegrationGuidance
member.summary:
Integration guidance for GenTL devices:
1. Device Creation: - Requires a valid GenTL system handle from ArvGentlSystem - Interface ID and Device ID must be obtained from GenTL discovery
2. Device Operations: - GenTL devices inherit from ArvDevice base functionality - All standard device operations available through ArvDevice.cs - Camera-level operations available through ArvCamera.cs
3. Stream Creation: - Use ArvGentlStream for GenTL stream operations - Streams created through device's create_stream method
4. Error Handling: - Check for IntPtr.Zero return values - Use error parameter for detailed error information - GenTL errors follow standard GError pattern

member.summary:
Integration guidance for GenTL interfaces:
1. Interface Access: - Use GetInstance() to get the singleton GenTL interface - GenTL interface is automatically discovered by Aravis system - Available when GenTL producers are installed on the system
2. Device Discovery: - Use ArvInterface base methods for device enumeration - GenTL devices will be discovered through interface operations - Device IDs can be used with ArvGentlDevice.CreateDevice()
3. Interface Operations: - All standard interface operations available through ArvInterface.cs - GenTL-specific functionality integrated with base interface - Update device list and open device methods work with GenTL
4. System Integration: - GenTL interface works with ArvSystem enumeration - Appears in system interface list when available - Compatible with standard Aravis discovery patterns
5. Error Handling: - Check for IntPtr.Zero return values - GenTL errors follow standard GError pattern - Interface availability depends on GenTL producer installation

T:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.ArvGentlStream
member.summary: C# wrapper for Aravis GenTL Stream functionality. Provides GenTL stream operations for GenTL-compatible camera streaming.
member.remarks:
GenTL (Generic Transport Layer) streams provide standardized streaming operations for GenTL-compatible cameras. This wrapper enables .NET applications to manage GenTL camera data streams with type safety.
GenTL streams extend the base ArvStream functionality with GenTL-specific features: - GenTL producer integration - Transport layer specific optimizations - GenTL buffer management - Producer-specific streaming capabilities

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.ArvGentlStream.ShowIntegrationGuidance
member.summary:
Integration guidance for GenTL streams:
1. Stream Creation: - GenTL streams are created through GenTL device instances - Use ArvDevice.arv_device_create_stream() on GenTL devices - Stream creation handled by GenTL producer automatically
2. Stream Operations: - All standard stream operations available through ArvStream.cs - Buffer management through ArvBuffer.cs - Acquisition control through ArvStream start/stop methods
3. GenTL Features: - GenTL-specific optimizations handled transparently - Producer-specific buffer management automatic - Transport layer optimizations integrated
4. Buffer Handling: - Standard buffer operations through ArvBuffer.cs - GenTL buffer allocation handled by producer - Memory management follows standard patterns
5. Error Handling: - GenTL streams follow standard GError pattern - Stream-specific errors reported through standard mechanisms - Producer errors integrated with Aravis error handling
6. Performance: - GenTL producers may provide optimized streaming - Zero-copy operations where supported by producer - Hardware-specific optimizations automatic

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.ArvGentlStream.ShowUsageExamples
M:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.ArvGentlStream.ShowProducerIntegration
member.summary:
GenTL Producer integration notes:
1. Producer Discovery: - GenTL producers automatically discovered by Aravis - Multiple producers can coexist on the system - Producer selection handled by GenTL system
2. Stream Capabilities: - Producer-specific streaming features automatically available - Hardware acceleration where supported - Transport-specific optimizations integrated
3. Buffer Management: - Producer-optimized buffer allocation - Zero-copy operations where possible - Memory mapping for performance
4. Configuration: - Producer-specific parameters accessible through GenICam - Transport layer configuration through device interface - Streaming parameters through standard Aravis API
5. Compatibility: - Standard Aravis API maintained for compatibility - GenTL features accessible through existing interfaces - Transparent integration with Aravis ecosystem

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.ArvGentlSystem
member.summary: C# wrapper for Aravis GenTL System functionality. Provides GenTL system management for GenTL-compatible transport layers.
member.remarks:
GenTL (Generic Transport Layer) systems provide a standardized framework for managing industrial camera transport protocols. This wrapper enables .NET applications to initialize and manage GenTL systems.
The GenTL system is the entry point for GenTL-based camera operations: 1. Initialize GenTL system 2. Discover interfaces 3. Enumerate devices 4. Create device instances

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.ArvGentlSystem.ShowIntegrationGuidance
member.summary:
Integration guidance for GenTL systems:
1. System Initialization: - GenTL systems are typically initialized through ArvSystem.cs - Use ArvSystem interface enumeration to discover GenTL interfaces - GenTL system instances are managed internally by Aravis
2. Interface Discovery: - Use ArvSystem.arv_system_get_interfaces() to enumerate interfaces - GenTL interfaces will be included in the interface list - Use ArvGentlInterface for GenTL-specific interface operations
3. Device Creation: - Use ArvGentlDevice.arv_gentl_device_new() to create devices - Requires GenTL system handle, interface ID, and device ID - Device IDs obtained through interface enumeration
4. Stream Operations: - Use ArvGentlStream for GenTL-specific streaming - Streams created through GenTL device instances - Standard streaming operations through ArvStream.cs
5. Error Handling: - GenTL systems follow standard GError error handling - Check return values and error parameters - Use GError marshaling for detailed error information
6. Memory Management: - GenTL systems are managed by Aravis internally - No explicit cleanup required for system handles - Device and stream handles require proper cleanup

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.ArvUvStream
member.summary: C# wrapper for Aravis USB Vision Stream functionality. This class provides type definitions for USB Vision stream operations. The USB Vision stream extends the base ArvStream functionality with USB-specific features.
member.remarks:
USB Vision streams are created through the base stream functionality in ArvStream.cs. This wrapper provides type-safe access to USB Vision-specific stream features while maintaining compatibility with the base stream interface.
Usage: - Use ArvStream.cs for general stream operations - Use ArvUvDevice.cs for USB Vision device-specific functionality - This wrapper provides USB Vision stream type identification

member.returns: The type name for USB Vision streams

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.ArvUvStream.ShowIntegrationGuidance
member.summary:
Integration guidance for USB Vision streams:
1. Stream Creation: - Use ArvCamera.arv_camera_create_stream() for USB Vision cameras - Use ArvDevice stream creation methods from ArvUvDevice
2. Stream Operations: - All standard stream operations available through ArvStream.cs - USB-specific configuration through ArvUvDevice.cs
3. Buffer Management: - Standard buffer operations through ArvBuffer.cs - USB Vision payload handling automatic
4. USB Vision Features: - Configure USB mode through ArvUvDevice.arv_uv_device_set_usb_mode() - Set transfer size through ArvUvDevice.arv_uv_device_set_maximum_transfer_size() - USB bandwidth control through ArvCamera USB Vision API

member.summary: Gets or sets the current pixel format name (e.g., "Mono8", "BayerRG8", "RGB8Packed").

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.GenICamCamera.AvailablePixelFormats
member.summary: Gets or sets the array of available pixel format names supported by the camera.
member.remarks:
Common formats include:
"Mono8" - 8-bit monochrome
"Mono16" - 16-bit monochrome
"BayerRG8", "BayerGR8", etc. - Bayer pattern color formats
"RGB8Packed" - 8-bit RGB color
"YUV422Packed" - YUV color format
This array is populated by .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.GenICamCamera.AvailablePixelFormatDisplayNames
member.summary: Gets or sets the array of available pixel format display names for user interfaces.
member.remarks: These are human-readable names corresponding to , suitable for displaying in dropdown lists or configuration interfaces. This array is populated by .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.GenICamCamera.SensorSize
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum sensor size in pixels (full resolution).
member.remarks: This represents the physical sensor dimensions and is the maximum possible resolution. Actual image size may be smaller due to ROI settings. Populated by .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.GenICamCamera.WidthBounds
member.summary: Gets or sets the valid range and increment for image width settings.
member.remarks:
Defines the constraints for ROI width:
Min: Minimum allowed width in pixels
Max: Maximum allowed width in pixels (typically sensor width)
Increment: Width must be a multiple of this value (often 1, 2, 4, or 8)
Use these bounds when calling .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.GenICamCamera.HeightBounds
member.summary: Gets or sets the valid range and increment for image height settings.
member.remarks:
Defines the constraints for ROI height:
Min: Minimum allowed height in pixels
Max: Maximum allowed height in pixels (typically sensor height)
Increment: Height must be a multiple of this value (often 1 or 2)
Use these bounds when calling .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.GenICamCamera.XOffsetBounds
member.summary: Gets or sets the valid range and increment for X offset (horizontal position) of the ROI.
member.remarks:
Defines the constraints for ROI X position:
Min: Minimum X offset (usually 0)
Max: Maximum X offset (sensor width - ROI width)
Increment: X offset must be a multiple of this value
Use these bounds when calling .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.GenICamCamera.YOffsetBounds
member.summary: Gets or sets the valid range and increment for Y offset (vertical position) of the ROI.
member.remarks:
Defines the constraints for ROI Y position:
Min: Minimum Y offset (usually 0)
Max: Maximum Y offset (sensor height - ROI height)
Increment: Y offset must be a multiple of this value
Use these bounds when calling .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.GenICamCamera.BinningAvailable
member.summary: Gets or sets whether pixel binning is supported by the camera.
member.remarks:
Binning combines adjacent pixels to:
Increase sensitivity (brightness) by combining pixel values
Reduce resolution for higher frame rates
Reduce noise in low-light conditions
If true, use to configure binning factors.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.GenICamCamera.XBinningBounds
member.summary: Gets or sets the valid range and increment for horizontal binning factors.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.GenICamCamera.FrameReceived
member.summary: Event fired when a new frame is received during streaming operations.

remarks.para: This event is raised from a background timer thread, so UI updates should be marshaled to the appropriate thread.
Frame processing should be kept minimal to avoid blocking the acquisition pipeline.
The frame data is copied, so it's safe to access after the event handler returns.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.GenICamCamera.FrameError
member.summary: Event fired when a frame acquisition error occurs during streaming.

remarks.para: Common causes include:

item.description: Buffer underrun (camera producing frames faster than they can be processed)
Network packet loss (GigE cameras)
USB bandwidth limitations (USB3 cameras)
Insufficient system resources

remarks.para: The streaming will typically continue after an error, but consider reducing frame rate or increasing buffer count.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.GenICamCamera.StreamingStarted
member.summary: Event fired when streaming starts successfully.
member.remarks: This event indicates that the camera acquisition has started and buffers are available for frame capture.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.GenICamCamera.StreamingStopped
member.summary: Event fired when streaming stops.

remarks.para: This method provides detailed information about the streaming subsystem:

item.description: Buffer Information: Input, output, and filling buffer counts
Statistics: Completed frames, failed frames, and underrun counts
State Information: Whether streaming is active and stream handle validity
Error Information: Any error messages from the streaming subsystem
High Failed Buffers: Indicates camera producing frames faster than processing - reduce frame rate or increase buffer count
High Underruns: Suggests insufficient buffers or slow processing - increase buffer count or optimize frame handling
Zero Completed Buffers: Camera may not be producing frames - check exposure settings and triggers
No Input Buffers: Stream buffer creation failed - check memory availability

remarks.para: Performance Note: This method queries the stream in real-time, so it reflects current state.

item.description: Ensures camera is connected (connects if necessary)
Creates stream and buffers if they don't exist
Sets acquisition mode to continuous
Starts camera acquisition
Begins frame polling timer
Fires event on success

remarks.para: Event Handling: Subscribe to before calling this method to receive frame data. Frames are delivered asynchronously via events.
Buffer Management: Buffers are created and managed automatically. The default buffer count is 10, which should be sufficient for most applications.
Thread Safety: This method is not thread-safe with respect to other camera operations.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.GenICamCamera.CaptureFrame(System.Int32)
member.summary: Captures a single frame in one-shot mode with specified timeout.
member.param: Timeout in milliseconds to wait for frame capture (default: 5000). Use larger values for slow cameras or longer exposures.
member.returns: Frame data containing image information and pixel data, or null if capture failed or timed out.
member.exception: Thrown if the camera instance has been disposed.

remarks.para: This method performs a synchronous single frame capture:

item.description: Ensures camera is connected (connects if necessary)
Creates stream and buffers if they don't exist
Sets acquisition mode to single frame
Starts acquisition and waits for frame
Extracts frame data and stops acquisition

remarks.para: Timeout Considerations: The timeout should be longer than the exposure time plus any camera processing delays. For very long exposures (>1 second), increase the timeout accordingly.
Performance: This method is suitable for infrequent captures. For continuous imaging, use instead for better performance.
Thread Safety: This method blocks the calling thread until the frame is captured or timeout occurs.

Checks if the camera is already connected (returns true if so)
Establishes a hardware connection to the camera
Reads camera information to populate detailed properties

remarks.para: Thread Safety: This method is thread-safe and uses internal locking.
Resource Management: Always call when done with the camera to properly release resources.
Error Handling: Detailed error information is logged. Check logs for specific failure reasons.

Disconnects the camera from the hardware
Keeps the camera instance in cache for potential reuse

remarks.para: Thread Safety: This method is thread-safe and uses internal locking.
Resource Management: This method properly releases hardware resources while maintaining the camera instance for future use.
Idempotent: It's safe to call this method multiple times on the same camera.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.GenICamCameraManager.ForceCleanup
member.summary: Forces removal and disposal of all cameras from the cache, regardless of their current state.

remarks.para: ⚠️ WARNING: This method should be used with extreme caution as it will dispose all camera instances even if they are currently in use. This can cause exceptions in other parts of the application that are actively using cameras.
This method is intended for use in the following scenarios:

item.description: Application shutdown
Recovery from unrecoverable camera states
Memory cleanup in testing scenarios

remarks.para: Thread Safety: This method is thread-safe but will affect all threads using cameras.
Recovery: After calling this method, you must call to repopulate the camera cache before using cameras again.

Camera discovery and enumeration interfaces

Camera selection based on specifications

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.GStreamer.DSP.DSPConverter
member.summary: Static methods to convert between different sample formats.

remarks.para: Code is mainly based on information available on the original C source code pa_converters.c from Portable Audio I/O Library.
This class try to be as fast as possible without using unsafe code.
Dither isn't currently supported. Currently supported conversions are 'to' and 'from' conversions between the following value types:
Integer 8-bit (byte), Integer 16-bit (Int16), Integer 32-bit (Int32), Single precision 32-bit floating point (float).
Which are the most common PCM formats.

member.summary: Platform invoke declaration for the native memcmp function from the Microsoft Visual C Runtime library.
member.param: The first byte array to compare.
The second byte array to compare.
The number of bytes to compare.
member.returns: Zero if the arrays are equal, a negative value if b1 is less than b2, or a positive value if b1 is greater than b2.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.ArrayHelper.Compare(System.Byte[],System.Byte[],System.Int32)
member.summary: Compares two byte arrays for equality using the native memcmp function for optimal performance.
member.param: The first byte array to compare.
The second byte array to compare.
The number of bytes to compare from the beginning of each array.
member.returns: true if the specified number of bytes are equal in both arrays; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: This method is only available on Windows platforms and uses the native memcmp function for high-performance comparison. For other platforms, use the CompareSlow method.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.ArrayHelper.CompareSlow(System.Byte[],System.Byte[],System.Int32)
member.summary: Compares two byte arrays for equality using a managed byte-by-byte comparison.
member.param: The first byte array to compare.
The second byte array to compare.
The number of bytes to compare from the beginning of each array.
member.returns: true if the specified number of bytes are equal in both arrays; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: This method provides a cross-platform compatible array comparison but is slower than the native Compare method. Use this method on non-Windows platforms or when native interop is not available. The comparison stops at the first non-matching byte for efficiency.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.ByteArrayComparer
member.summary: Provides functionality to compare byte arrays for equality and generate hash codes for byte arrays. This class implements for byte arrays, allowing byte arrays to be used as keys in hash-based collections such as Dictionary and HashSet.
member.remarks: This comparer performs element-by-element comparison of byte arrays and generates hash codes based on the sum of all bytes in the array. Note that the hash code algorithm is simple and may not provide optimal distribution for all use cases.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.ByteArrayComparer.Equals(System.Byte[],System.Byte[])
member.summary: Determines whether two byte arrays are equal by comparing their elements.
member.param: The first byte array to compare. Can be null.
The second byte array to compare. Can be null.
member.returns: true if both arrays are null, or if both arrays have the same length and contain the same sequence of bytes; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: This method handles null arrays gracefully. Two null arrays are considered equal. If only one array is null, they are considered not equal.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.ByteArrayComparer.GetHashCode(System.Byte[])
member.summary: Generates a hash code for the specified byte array.
member.param: The byte array for which to generate a hash code. Must not be null.
member.returns: A hash code calculated as the sum of all bytes in the array. This provides a simple hash that is sufficient for many use cases.
member.remarks: The hash code is calculated by summing all byte values in the array. While simple, this approach may result in hash collisions for arrays with the same sum but different byte arrangements. For performance-critical applications with large datasets, consider using a more sophisticated hash algorithm.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CairoHelper
member.summary: Provides extension methods and utilities for converting SkiaSharp types to Cairo graphics library types.
member.remarks: This helper class is used internally to bridge the gap between SkiaSharp (used for cross-platform graphics) and Cairo (used by GStreamer for text and graphics rendering). All methods are extension methods that provide seamless conversion capabilities.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CairoHelper.ToCairoColor(SkiaSharp.SKColor)
member.summary: Converts a SkiaSharp color to a Cairo color.
member.param: The SkiaSharp color to convert. This color contains RGBA values in the range 0-255.
member.returns: A Cairo.Color instance with normalized RGBA values in the range 0.0-1.0.
member.remarks: This method normalizes the 8-bit color channel values (0-255) from SkiaSharp to the floating-point values (0.0-1.0) expected by Cairo.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CairoHelper.ToCairo(VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEffects.FontWeight)
member.summary: Converts a VisioForge font weight enumeration to a Cairo font weight.
member.param: The VisioForge font weight to convert.
member.returns: Cairo.FontWeight.Bold if the weight value is 600 or greater (semi-bold and above); otherwise, Cairo.FontWeight.Normal.
member.remarks: Cairo has limited font weight options compared to modern font specifications. This method maps all weights of 600 and above to Bold, and everything else to Normal. The threshold of 600 corresponds to the standard semi-bold weight in typography.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CairoHelper.ToCairo(VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEffects.FontStyle)
member.summary: Converts a VisioForge font style enumeration to a Cairo font slant.
member.param: The VisioForge font style to convert.
member.returns: The corresponding Cairo.FontSlant value: - Normal returns Cairo.FontSlant.Normal - Oblique returns Cairo.FontSlant.Oblique - Italic returns Cairo.FontSlant.Italic - Any other value defaults to Cairo.FontSlant.Normal
member.remarks: This method provides a direct mapping between VisioForge font styles and Cairo font slants, which are used to control the slanting or italicization of text in Cairo graphics contexts.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1
member.summary: A generic circular buffer implementation that allows efficient insertion and removal of elements at both ends of the buffer. When the buffer reaches full capacity, adding new elements will automatically remove elements from the opposite end.

remarks.para: When writing to a full buffer:

item.description: PushBack() removes the element at Front() (this[0])
PushFront() removes the element at Back() (this[Size-1])

remarks.para: This implementation is inspired by the Boost circular_buffer library: http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_53_0/libs/circular_buffer/doc/circular_buffer.html

member.typeparam: The type of elements stored in the circular buffer.

member.summary: The internal array that stores the buffer elements.

member.summary: The index of the first element in the circular buffer.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1._end
member.summary: The index position after the last element in the circular buffer.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1._size
member.summary: The current number of elements stored in the buffer.

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with the specified capacity.

member.exception: Thrown when capacity is less than 1.

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with the specified capacity and pre-fills it with the provided items.

Initial items to fill the buffer with. The length must not exceed the capacity. Tip: Use Skip(x).Take(y).ToArray() to build this parameter from any enumerable.
member.exception: Thrown when capacity is less than 1 or when items length exceeds capacity.

member.summary: Gets the maximum capacity of the circular buffer.
member.remarks: When the buffer reaches maximum capacity (IsFull = true), pushing new elements will automatically remove elements from the opposite end to maintain the capacity limit.
member.value: The maximum number of elements that can be stored in the buffer.

member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the circular buffer is at full capacity.

member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the circular buffer is empty.

member.summary: Gets the current number of elements contained in the circular buffer.
member.value: The number of elements currently stored in the buffer.

member.summary: Returns the element at the front of the buffer without removing it.
member.returns: The element at the front of the buffer (equivalent to this[0]).
member.exception: Thrown when the buffer is empty.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.Back
member.summary: Returns the element at the back of the buffer without removing it.
member.returns: The element at the back of the buffer (equivalent to this[Size - 1]).
member.exception: Thrown when the buffer is empty.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.Item(System.Int32)
member.summary: Gets or sets the element at the specified index in the buffer.
member.param: The zero-based index of the element to get or set.
member.returns: The element at the specified index.
member.remarks: The index does not wrap around; valid indices are in the range [0, Size).
member.exception: Thrown when index is negative, greater than or equal to Size, or when the buffer is empty.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.PushBack(`0)
member.summary: Adds an element to the back of the circular buffer.
member.param: The element to add to the back of the buffer.
member.remarks: After this operation, Back() and this[Size-1] will return the newly added element. If the buffer is full, the element at the front (Front()/this[0]) will be removed to make room for the new element.

member.summary: Adds an element to the front of the circular buffer.
member.param: The element to add to the front of the buffer.
member.remarks: After this operation, Front() and this[0] will return the newly added element. If the buffer is full, the element at the back (Back()/this[Size-1]) will be removed to make room for the new element.

member.summary: Removes and discards the element at the back of the circular buffer.

member.summary: Removes and discards the element at the front of the circular buffer.

member.summary: Removes all elements from the circular buffer.

member.summary: Copies all elements from the circular buffer to a new array.
member.returns: A new array containing copies of the elements in the buffer, ordered from front to back.
member.remarks: The returned array preserves the logical order of elements (from front to back), regardless of their physical arrangement in the internal buffer.

member.summary: Gets the contents of the buffer as two ArraySegment instances without copying the elements.
member.returns: An IList containing two ArraySegment instances that represent the buffer contents.

remarks.para: This method provides a zero-copy view of the buffer contents, which is useful for performance-critical scenarios such as network operations (e.g., Send(IList<ArraySegment<byte>>)).
The segments preserve the logical order of elements from front to back. Either or both segments may be empty depending on the buffer state.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.FrameRateHelper.AverageTimePerFrameToFrameRate(System.UInt64,System.Int32@,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Converts average time per frame duration to a fractional frame rate representation.
member.param: The average time per frame in 100-nanosecond units (as used in Windows media frameworks).
When this method returns, contains the numerator of the frame rate fraction.
When this method returns, contains the denominator of the frame rate fraction.
member.remarks: This method first checks against a list of known standard frame rates for exact matches. If no match is found, it calculates the frame rate by converting the duration to a fraction and simplifying it using GCD. The frame rate is represented as numerator/denominator (e.g., 30000/1001 for 29.97 fps, 24/1 for 24 fps). Common frame rates include: - 23.976 fps (24000/1001) - 24 fps (24/1) - 25 fps (25/1) - 29.97 fps (30000/1001) - 30 fps (30/1) - 50 fps (50/1) - 59.94 fps (60000/1001) - 60 fps (60/1)

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.PathHelper.GetAssemblyPath
member.summary: Determines and returns the directory path of the currently executing assembly.
member.returns: The directory path where the executing assembly is located, or null if unable to determine.
member.remarks:
This method attempts to retrieve the assembly path using multiple fallback strategies:
First attempts to get the location of the executing assembly
Falls back to AppContext.BaseDirectory if the first attempt returns null or empty
Finally attempts to get the entry assembly location if previous attempts fail
This approach ensures compatibility across different hosting scenarios including single-file deployments, self-contained applications, and traditional deployments.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.TextUtils.ToStringWithMask(System.DateTime,System.String)
member.summary: Formats a DateTime object using a custom mask pattern with percent-prefixed format specifiers.
member.param: The mask string containing format specifiers prefixed with '%'. For example: "%yyyy-%MM-%dd %HH:%mm:%ss" would format as "2023-12-25 14:30:45".
member.returns: A string with all percent-prefixed format specifiers replaced with their corresponding DateTime values. Returns an empty string if the mask is null or empty.

remarks.para: This extension method supports all standard .NET DateTime format specifiers when prefixed with '%':

item.description: Day: %d, %dd, %ddd, %dddd
Month: %M, %MM, %MMM, %MMMM
Year: %y, %yy, %yyy, %yyyy, %yyyyy
Hour: %h, %hh (12-hour), %H, %HH (24-hour)
Minute: %m, %mm
Second: %s, %ss
Fraction: %f through %ffffff, %F through %FFFFFFF
AM/PM: %t, %tt
Timezone: %z, %zz, %zzz, %K
Era: %g, %gg

remarks.para: The method processes format specifiers from longest to shortest to avoid partial replacements.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.UIUtils.IsInDesignMode
member.summary: Determines whether the current code is executing within a design-time environment.
member.returns: true if the code is executing in a design-time environment (such as Visual Studio designer for WPF or Windows Forms); otherwise, false if executing at runtime.
member.remarks:
This method checks for both WPF and Windows Forms design-time environments:
For WPF: Uses to detect design-time mode.
For Windows Forms: Checks if the current process is "devenv" (Visual Studio).
This detection is useful for controls and components that need to avoid certain operations (like media playback, network access, or hardware initialization) during design time.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHook
member.summary: Provides system-wide keyboard hook functionality using Windows Low-Level Keyboard Hook API. Enables monitoring of global keyboard events across all applications with optional key filtering. This class implements a low-level keyboard hook that captures keyboard events before they reach the target application.
member.remarks: This class uses Windows API SetWindowsHookEx with WH_KEYBOARD_LL to install a low-level keyboard hook. The hook procedure receives keyboard events system-wide and can optionally filter specific keys. Proper disposal is critical to ensure the hook is removed when no longer needed.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHook.KeyboardPressed
member.summary: Occurs when a registered keyboard key is pressed or released. This event is triggered for key events that match the registered keys filter, or for all keys if no filter is specified in the constructor.
member.remarks: The event provides detailed information about the key event including: - Key code and state (pressed/released) - Hardware scan code and timing information - Modifier key states (Ctrl, Shift) - Ability to suppress the key event by setting Handled = true

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHook.#ctor(System.Windows.Forms.Keys[])
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class. Sets up the low-level keyboard hook and loads the required User32 library.
member.param: Array of keys that should trigger the KeyboardPressed event. Pass null to capture all keyboard events system-wide.
member.exception: Thrown when User32.dll cannot be loaded or the keyboard hook cannot be installed.
member.remarks: This constructor performs the following operations: 1. Loads User32.dll library for Windows API access 2. Installs a low-level keyboard hook using SetWindowsHookEx 3. Stores the hook procedure delegate to prevent garbage collection The hook remains active until the object is disposed.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHook.Dispose(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Releases unmanaged and - optionally - managed resources.
member.param: true to release both managed and unmanaged resources; false to release only unmanaged resources.

member.summary: Finalizes an instance of the class.

member.summary: Disposes this instance.

member.summary: Handle to the installed Windows keyboard hook returned by SetWindowsHookEx. Used to identify and remove the hook when disposing the object.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHook._user32LibraryHandle
member.summary: Handle to the loaded User32.dll library obtained from LoadLibrary. Must be freed using FreeLibrary when the object is disposed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHook._hookProc
member.summary: Delegate instance for the hook procedure callback. Stored as a field to prevent garbage collection while the hook is active. Points to the LowLevelKeyboardProc method that processes keyboard events.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHook.HookProc
member.summary: Delegate for the Windows keyboard hook procedure callback. Defines the signature for the low-level keyboard hook procedure that processes keyboard events.
member.param: Hook code that determines how to process the message. Should be passed to CallNextHookEx if less than zero.
Identifier of the keyboard message (WM_KEYDOWN, WM_KEYUP, etc.).
Pointer to a KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT structure containing keyboard input information.
member.returns: If the hook procedure processes the message, it should return a nonzero value to prevent the system from passing the message to the rest of the hook chain or the target window procedure. Otherwise, return the result of CallNextHookEx.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHook.LoadLibrary(System.String)
member.summary: Loads the library.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHook.FreeLibrary(System.IntPtr)
member.summary: Frees the library.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHook.SetWindowsHookEx(System.Int32,VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHook.HookProc,System.IntPtr,System.Int32)
member.summary: The SetWindowsHookEx function installs an application-defined hook procedure into a hook chain. You would install a hook procedure to monitor the system for certain types of events. These events are associated either with a specific thread or with all threads in the same desktop as the calling thread.
member.returns: If the function succeeds, the return value is the handle to the hook procedure.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHook.UnhookWindowsHookEx(System.IntPtr)
member.summary: The UnhookWindowsHookEx function removes a hook procedure installed in a hook chain by the SetWindowsHookEx function.
member.returns: If the function succeeds, the return value is true.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHook.CallNextHookEx(System.IntPtr,System.Int32,System.IntPtr,System.IntPtr)
member.summary: The CallNextHookEx function passes the hook information to the next hook procedure in the current hook chain. A hook procedure can call this function either before or after processing the hook information.
member.param: hook code passed to hook procedure.
W value passed to hook procedure.
L value passed to hook procedure.
member.returns: If the function succeeds, the return value is true.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHook.LowLevelKeyboardInputEvent
member.summary: Represents low-level keyboard input event data from the Windows KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT structure. Contains detailed information about a keyboard event captured by the low-level keyboard hook.
member.remarks: This structure corresponds to the Windows KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT and provides access to: - Virtual key code and hardware scan code - Event flags and timing information - Additional context data from the system The layout is sequential to match the native Windows structure.

member.summary: The extended-key flag, event-injected Flags, context code, and transition-state flag. This member is specified as follows. An application can use the following values to test the keystroke Flags. Testing LLKHF_INJECTED (bit 4) will tell you whether the event was injected. If it was, then testing LLKHF_LOWER_IL_INJECTED (bit 1) will tell you whether or not the event was injected from a process running at lower integrity level.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHook.LowLevelKeyboardProc(System.Int32,System.IntPtr,System.IntPtr)
member.summary: Low-level keyboard hook procedure that processes keyboard events from the Windows hook system. This method is called by Windows for each keyboard event when the hook is active.
member.param: Hook code that determines how to process the message. If less than zero, the hook procedure must pass the message to CallNextHookEx without further processing.
Identifier of the keyboard message (WM_KEYDOWN, WM_KEYUP, WM_SYSKEYDOWN, WM_SYSKEYUP).
Pointer to a KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT structure containing keyboard input information.
member.returns: If the event should be suppressed, returns 1. Otherwise, returns the result of CallNextHookEx to allow the event to continue through the hook chain.
member.remarks: This method: 1. Extracts keyboard event data from the lParam structure 2. Checks if the key matches the registered keys filter 3. Determines modifier key states (Ctrl, Shift) 4. Raises the KeyboardPressed event if criteria are met 5. Suppresses the event if the event handler sets Handled = true

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHookEventArgs
member.summary: Provides event data for global keyboard hook events. Contains detailed information about a keyboard event captured by the GlobalKeyboardHook, including the key data, state, and modifier key information.
member.remarks: This class extends HandledEventArgs to provide the ability to suppress keyboard events by setting the Handled property to true. When handled, the original keyboard event will not be passed to the target application.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.GlobalKeyboardHookEventArgs.KeyboardState

member.value: The keyboard event state as defined by the KeyboardState enumeration.
member.remarks: System key events (SysKeyDown, SysKeyUp) typically involve Alt key combinations and are used for system-level keyboard shortcuts.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.OutputFormats.CustomFormatSettingsDialog
member.summary: Windows Forms dialog for configuring custom output format settings. Provides a comprehensive interface for configuring video and audio encoders, multiplexer filters, and file writer options for custom media output formats.
member.remarks: This dialog allows users to configure custom output formats by selecting: - Video encoders from either Video Codecs or DirectShow Filters categories - Audio encoders from either Audio Codecs or DirectShow Filters categories - Multiplexer filters for combining video and audio streams - Special file writer filters when needed The dialog supports configuration for DirectCaptureMP4Output, DirectCaptureCustomOutput, and CustomOutput formats.
member.summary: Designer class for CustomFormatSettingsDialog containing auto-generated UI component initialization code. This partial class contains the Windows Forms designer generated code for the custom format settings dialog UI.
member.remarks: This class is automatically generated by the Visual Studio Windows Forms designer. Manual modifications to this file may be lost when the designer regenerates the code. The UI provides comprehensive configuration options for custom output formats including: - Video encoder selection from codec or DirectShow filter categories - Audio encoder selection from codec or DirectShow filter categories - Multiplexer filter configuration - Special file writer filter options

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.OutputFormats.FFMPEGEXESettingsDialog.FFEXEDisableVideoMode
member.summary: Disables all video encoding mode options and related controls. Resets the UI state for video encoding mode selection.
member.remarks: This method is called before enabling specific video encoding modes to ensure a clean state. It disables all mode radio buttons and their associated controls such as quality slider and bitrate text boxes.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.OutputFormats.FFMPEGEXESettingsDialog.FFEXEEnableVideoCBR
member.summary: Enables Constant Bitrate (CBR) video encoding mode. Activates CBR mode and enables the target bitrate control.
member.remarks: CBR mode maintains a constant bitrate throughout the video stream, useful for streaming scenarios where consistent bandwidth is required.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.OutputFormats.FFMPEGEXESettingsDialog.FFEXEEnableVideoABR
member.summary: Enables Average Bitrate (ABR) video encoding mode. Activates ABR mode and enables bitrate range controls.
member.remarks: ABR mode allows bitrate variation within specified limits while maintaining an average target bitrate. This provides better quality than CBR while keeping file size predictable.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.OutputFormats.FFMPEGEXESettingsDialog.FFEXEEnableVideoQuality
member.summary: Enables quality-based video encoding mode. Activates quality mode and enables the quality slider control.
member.remarks: Quality mode (CRF/quantizer) encodes video to maintain consistent quality rather than bitrate. This typically provides the best quality-to-size ratio but results in variable file sizes.

member.param: The source of the event (profile combobox).
member.remarks: This method configures output format, video codec, and audio codec settings based on predefined profiles such as MPEG-1, MP4 H.264/AAC, WebM, etc. It provides quick configuration for common encoding scenarios.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.OutputFormats.FFMPEGEXESettingsDialog.FFEXEDisableAudioMode
member.summary: Disables all audio encoding mode options and related controls. Resets the UI state for audio encoding mode selection.
member.remarks: This method is called before enabling specific audio encoding modes to ensure a clean state. It disables all mode radio buttons and their associated controls such as quality slider and bitrate dropdown.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.OutputFormats.FFMPEGEXESettingsDialog.FFEXEEnableAudioCBR
member.summary: Enables Constant Bitrate (CBR) audio encoding mode. Activates CBR mode and enables the bitrate selection control.
member.remarks: CBR mode maintains a constant bitrate for audio streams, providing predictable file sizes and compatibility with streaming.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.OutputFormats.FFMPEGEXESettingsDialog.FFEXEEnableAudioQuality
member.summary: Enables quality-based audio encoding mode. Activates quality mode and enables the quality slider control.
member.remarks: Quality mode encodes audio based on perceptual quality rather than fixed bitrate, providing better quality-to-size ratio for formats that support it (e.g., MP3, Vorbis, Opus).

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.Dialogs.OutputFormats.FFMPEGEXESettingsDialog.FFEXEEnableAudioLossless
member.summary: Enables lossless audio encoding mode. Activates lossless mode for codecs that support it.
member.remarks: Lossless mode preserves the original audio quality perfectly at the cost of larger file sizes. Available for codecs like FLAC, ALAC, and WavPack.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.PeakMeterData
member.summary: Represents data for a single band in the peak meter control.
member.remarks: This structure holds the current state of a peak meter band including its current value, falloff position, and animation speed. Each band in the peak meter control maintains its own instance of this data.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.PeakMeterData.Value
member.summary: Gets or sets the current value of the peak meter band.
member.remarks: This value represents the current signal level for this band, typically ranging from 0 to the maximum range value defined in the peak meter control.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.PeakMeterData.Falloff
member.summary: Gets or sets the falloff indicator position for the band.
member.remarks: The falloff value tracks the peak level and gradually decreases over time to create a visual "peak hold" effect. This provides a visual indication of recent peak levels even after the actual signal level has decreased.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.PeakMeterData.Speed
member.summary: Gets or sets the falloff animation speed counter.
member.remarks: This counter controls how quickly the falloff indicator decreases. When greater than 0, the falloff indicator remains at its current position. When it reaches 0, the falloff indicator begins to drop. The initial value is set by the FalloffSpeed property of the control.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.PeakMeterStyle
member.summary: Specifies the orientation style for the peak meter control display.
member.remarks: This enumeration determines how the peak meter bands are arranged and animated within the control. The orientation affects both the visual appearance and the direction of the level indicators and falloff effects.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.PeakMeterStyle.Horizontal
member.summary: Displays the peak meter with horizontal bands.
member.remarks: In horizontal mode, the meter bands are arranged side by side, with levels increasing from left to right. This style is commonly used for multi-channel audio displays where each band represents a different frequency range or audio channel.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.UI.WinForms.PeakMeterStyle.Vertical
member.summary: Displays the peak meter with vertical bands.
member.remarks: In vertical mode, the meter bands are stacked on top of each other, with levels increasing from bottom to top. This style mimics traditional VU meters and is often preferred for single-channel displays or when vertical space is more readily available than horizontal space.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.ScreenExtensions
member.summary: Provides extension methods for working with screen displays and DPI awareness.
member.remarks: This class contains helper methods for retrieving display-specific information, particularly DPI (dots per inch) settings for multi-monitor configurations. These extensions are essential for proper scaling in high-DPI environments.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.ScreenExtensions.GetDpi(System.Windows.Forms.Screen,VisioForge.Core.Types.DpiType,System.UInt32@,System.UInt32@)
member.summary: Gets the DPI (dots per inch) settings for the specified screen.
member.param: The screen to query for DPI information.
The type of DPI to retrieve (effective, angular, or raw).
When this method returns, contains the horizontal DPI value.
When this method returns, contains the vertical DPI value.
member.remarks: This method retrieves per-monitor DPI settings on Windows 8.1 and later. On earlier versions of Windows, it returns the standard 96 DPI value. Per-monitor DPI awareness is crucial for applications that span multiple displays with different DPI settings.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.ScreenExtensions.MonitorFromPoint(System.Drawing.Point,System.UInt32)
member.summary: Retrieves a handle to the display monitor that contains a specified point.
member.param: A point structure that specifies the point of interest in virtual-screen coordinates.
Determines the function's return value if the point is not contained within any display monitor.
member.returns: Handle to the display monitor that contains the point.
member.remarks: This is a wrapper for the Windows API MonitorFromPoint function. The dwFlags parameter value of 2 corresponds to MONITOR_DEFAULTTONEAREST, which returns the nearest monitor when the point is not contained in any monitor.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.UI.ScreenExtensions.GetDpiForMonitor(System.IntPtr,VisioForge.Core.Types.DpiType,System.UInt32@,System.UInt32@)
member.summary: Queries the DPI of a display monitor.
member.param: Handle of the monitor being queried.
The type of DPI to retrieve.
The horizontal DPI value of the monitor.
The vertical DPI value of the monitor.
member.returns: An HRESULT value indicating success or failure.
member.remarks: This function is available on Windows 8.1 and later versions. It enables applications to retrieve the DPI settings for individual monitors, which is essential for proper scaling in multi-monitor environments where different monitors may have different DPI settings.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WPF.Dialogs.OutputFormats.Pages.NVENCHEVCEncoderPage
member.summary: Configuration page for the NVIDIA NVENC HEVC (H.265) hardware video encoder.

remarks.para: The NVENC HEVC encoder provides hardware-accelerated H.265/HEVC video encoding on compatible NVIDIA graphics cards. HEVC offers improved compression efficiency compared to H.264, typically achieving 25-50% better compression at the same quality level. This encoder is ideal for 4K and high-resolution video encoding where bandwidth efficiency is critical.

Key features of the NVENC HEVC encoder: - Multiple rate control modes including constant QP, CBR, VBR, and quality-based VBR - Support for Main and Main10 profiles for standard and 10-bit encoding - Hardware acceleration with minimal CPU usage - Optimized presets for different use cases (quality, performance, low latency) - Zero-latency mode for real-time streaming applications - Configurable GOP size and quantization parameters
Hardware requirements: - NVIDIA GPU with NVENC support (GTX 10 series or newer for HEVC) - Updated NVIDIA graphics drivers - Sufficient GPU memory for encoding resolution

This page allows configuration of all major NVENC HEVC encoding parameters including bitrate control, quality settings, encoding presets, and advanced options for professional video production workflows.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WPF.Dialogs.OutputFormats.Pages.OpenH264EncoderPage
member.summary: Configuration page for the OpenH264 video encoder.

remarks.para: OpenH264 is an open-source H.264/AVC video encoder developed by Cisco and released under the BSD license. It provides a royalty-free implementation of the H.264 standard, making it suitable for applications where licensing costs are a concern. The encoder is optimized for real-time communication scenarios.

Key features of the OpenH264 encoder: - Baseline, Main, and High profile support - Optimized for real-time video conferencing - Background detection for bandwidth optimization - Denoising filter for improved quality in noisy environments - Frame skipping for maintaining real-time performance - Flexible rate control with bitrate and quality modes

Common use cases: - WebRTC video communication - Video conferencing applications - Real-time streaming with low latency requirements - Applications requiring royalty-free H.264 encoding - Cross-platform video encoding solutions

This page allows configuration of encoding parameters including bitrate control, quality settings, GOP structure, and special features like denoising and background detection that enhance video quality in communication scenarios.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WPF.Dialogs.OutputFormats.Pages.OPUSEncoderPage
member.summary: Configuration page for the Opus audio encoder.

remarks.para: Opus is a modern, open-source audio codec designed to efficiently code speech and general audio in a single format. It provides excellent quality at low bitrates and scales from narrow-band speech at 6 kbps to high-quality stereo music at 510 kbps. Opus is standardized by the IETF as RFC 6716 and is widely supported in WebRTC, streaming, and VoIP applications.

Key features of the Opus encoder: - Hybrid codec combining SILK (speech) and CELT (music) technologies - Wide bitrate range from 6 to 510 kbps - Support for mono and stereo audio - Multiple rate control modes (VBR, CBR, constrained VBR) - Low latency suitable for real-time communication - Excellent quality at low bitrates for voice applications

Common use cases: - VoIP and video conferencing (WebRTC) - Streaming audio over limited bandwidth - Podcast and audiobook encoding - Game audio and interactive applications - Internet radio broadcasting
This page provides configuration options for bitrate and rate control mode selection, allowing optimization for different audio content types and network conditions.

member.summary: Configuration page for the Intel Quick Sync Video (QSV) AV1 hardware encoder.

remarks.para: The QSV AV1 encoder provides hardware-accelerated AV1 video encoding using Intel's integrated graphics. AV1 is a next-generation, royalty-free video codec that offers superior compression efficiency compared to H.264 and HEVC, typically achieving 30-50% better compression at the same quality level.

Key features of the QSV AV1 encoder: - Hardware acceleration on Intel Arc GPUs and newer integrated graphics - Significantly improved compression efficiency over older codecs - Royalty-free and open-source codec standard - Optimized for streaming and web video delivery - Support for modern video features including HDR

Hardware requirements: - Intel Arc discrete GPU or 12th Gen Intel Core processors (Alder Lake) and newer - Updated Intel graphics drivers with AV1 encoding support - Operating system support for Intel Media SDK or oneVPL
Note: This encoder page is currently a placeholder as QSV AV1 encoding support is still evolving. Configuration options will be added as the encoder implementation matures.

member.summary: Configuration page for the Intel Quick Sync Video (QSV) H.264 hardware encoder.

remarks.para: The QSV H.264 encoder leverages Intel's integrated graphics hardware to provide high-performance H.264/AVC video encoding with minimal CPU usage. Quick Sync Video is Intel's dedicated media processing technology built into Intel processors with integrated graphics.

Key features of the QSV H.264 encoder: - Hardware-accelerated encoding using Intel GPU - Multiple rate control modes including CQP, CBR, VBR, AVBR, and LA (lookahead) variants - Support for all H.264 profiles (Baseline, Main, High) - Low latency mode for real-time streaming - Per-frame type QP control (I, P, B frames) - CABAC entropy coding support - Efficient power consumption compared to CPU encoding

Rate control modes: - CQP: Constant Quantization Parameter for consistent quality - CBR: Constant Bitrate for streaming with fixed bandwidth - VBR: Variable Bitrate for optimal quality/size balance - AVBR: Average Variable Bitrate with better rate control - ICQ/LA_ICQ: Intelligent Constant Quality modes - LA: Lookahead modes for improved quality and rate control
Hardware requirements: - Intel processor with HD Graphics 2000 or newer - Intel Media SDK or oneVPL runtime installed - Sufficient system memory for encoding resolution

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WPF.Dialogs.OutputFormats.Pages.QSVHEVCEncoderPage
member.summary: Configuration page for the Intel Quick Sync Video (QSV) HEVC/H.265 hardware encoder.

remarks.para: The QSV HEVC encoder provides hardware-accelerated H.265/HEVC video encoding using Intel's integrated graphics processors. HEVC offers approximately 50% better compression efficiency compared to H.264, making it ideal for 4K video and bandwidth-constrained streaming scenarios.

Key features of the QSV HEVC encoder: - Hardware acceleration on Intel 6th generation (Skylake) processors and newer - Support for Main and Main10 profiles (8-bit and 10-bit encoding) - Multiple rate control modes including CQP, CBR, VBR, and ICQ - Per-frame type quantization control - Low latency mode for real-time applications - Efficient encoding for 4K and high-resolution content - Power-efficient encoding using dedicated hardware

Rate control modes: - CQP: Constant QP for predictable quality - CBR: Constant bitrate for streaming - VBR: Variable bitrate for storage - AVBR: Average VBR with better stability - ICQ: Intelligent constant quality - QVBR: Quality-defined VBR mode
Hardware requirements: - Intel 6th Gen Core processors (Skylake) or newer for HEVC encoding - Intel Graphics driver with HEVC support - Intel Media SDK or oneVPL runtime

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WPF.Dialogs.OutputFormats.Pages.QSVMJPEGEncoderPage
member.summary: Configuration page for the Intel Quick Sync Video (QSV) Motion JPEG hardware encoder.

remarks.para: The QSV MJPEG encoder provides hardware-accelerated Motion JPEG encoding using Intel's integrated graphics. Motion JPEG encodes each frame as a separate JPEG image, resulting in a video stream composed of individual JPEG frames. This format is commonly used in digital cameras and video editing applications.

Key features of the QSV MJPEG encoder: - Hardware-accelerated JPEG compression for video streams - Simple quality-based encoding control - Frame-independent compression (each frame is a complete image) - Easy frame extraction and editing - Wide compatibility with video editing software - Suitable for intermediate format in video production

Common use cases: - Digital camera video recording - Video editing intermediate format - Archival storage where frame access is important - Applications requiring simple frame extraction - Legacy system compatibility
Hardware requirements: - Intel processor with HD Graphics supporting MJPEG encoding - Intel Media SDK or oneVPL runtime - Sufficient memory bandwidth for uncompressed frame data
Note: While MJPEG provides good quality and editing flexibility, it produces larger files compared to modern inter-frame codecs like H.264 or HEVC.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WPF.Dialogs.OutputFormats.Pages.QSVVP9EncoderPage
member.summary: Configuration page for the Intel Quick Sync Video (QSV) VP9 hardware encoder.

remarks.para: The QSV VP9 encoder provides hardware-accelerated VP9 video encoding using Intel's integrated graphics. VP9 is an open-source, royalty-free video codec developed by Google that offers comparable compression efficiency to HEVC while avoiding licensing fees. It's widely used for web video and streaming platforms.

Key features of the QSV VP9 encoder: - Hardware acceleration on select Intel processors - Royalty-free codec suitable for web deployment - Excellent compression efficiency similar to HEVC - Multiple rate control modes (CQP, CBR, VBR, ICQ) - Low latency mode for real-time applications - Widely supported by web browsers and streaming platforms
Common use cases: - YouTube and web video streaming - WebRTC video communication - Progressive download video delivery - Applications requiring royalty-free codecs - Cross-platform video distribution

Hardware requirements: - Intel 11th Gen (Tiger Lake) or newer processors with VP9 encoding support - Intel Iris Xe graphics or newer - Intel Media SDK or oneVPL runtime with VP9 support - Updated graphics drivers
Note: This encoder page is partially implemented as QSV VP9 support is relatively new and may have limited availability depending on hardware and driver versions.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WPF.Dialogs.OutputFormats.Pages.SpeexEncoderPage
member.summary: Configuration page for the Speex audio encoder.

remarks.para: Speex is an open-source audio codec specifically designed for speech compression. It was developed as part of the Xiph.org project and is optimized for Voice over IP (VoIP) and other speech applications. Speex provides excellent compression for speech while maintaining intelligibility at very low bitrates.

Key features of the Speex encoder: - Optimized for speech compression (8-32 kHz sampling rates) - Multiple encoding modes (narrowband, wideband, ultra-wideband) - Variable bitrate (VBR) encoding for optimal quality/size ratio - Voice Activity Detection (VAD) to reduce bandwidth during silence - Adjustable quality settings (0-10 scale) - Low computational complexity - Patent-free and royalty-free codec

Encoding modes: - Narrowband (8 kHz): Telephone quality speech - Wideband (16 kHz): Higher quality speech, comparable to AM radio - Ultra-wideband (32 kHz): Very high quality speech - Auto: Automatically selects mode based on input
Common use cases: - VoIP applications and softphones - Podcast recording and distribution - Voice messaging systems - Speech recording and archival - Low-bandwidth communication systems
Note: While Speex excels at speech compression, it's not suitable for music or general audio. For music encoding, consider using Vorbis or Opus instead.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WPF.Dialogs.OutputFormats.Pages.TheoraEncoderPage
member.summary: Configuration page for the Theora video encoder.

remarks.para: Theora is an open-source, royalty-free video codec developed by the Xiph.Org Foundation as part of the Ogg project. It was designed to compete with proprietary video codecs while remaining completely free from patent restrictions. Theora is based on the VP3 codec donated by On2 Technologies.

Key features of the Theora encoder: - Completely royalty-free and patent-unencumbered - Part of the Ogg multimedia framework - Comparable quality to early MPEG-4 implementations - Variable bitrate (VBR) and constant bitrate (CBR) encoding - Support for arbitrary video dimensions - Designed for web video streaming

Common use cases: - Web video streaming on open-source platforms - Video archival in patent-free formats - Educational and non-commercial video projects - Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons video content - Free software distributions requiring unencumbered codecs
Limitations: - Lower compression efficiency compared to modern codecs (H.264, VP9, AV1) - Limited hardware acceleration support - Primarily historical significance in modern applications
Note: This encoder page is currently a placeholder. While Theora remains supported for compatibility, newer royalty-free codecs like VP9 and AV1 offer superior performance.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.UI.WPF.Dialogs.OutputFormats.Pages.VOAACEncoderPage
member.summary: Configuration page for the VisualOn AAC (Advanced Audio Coding) encoder.

remarks.para: The VisualOn AAC encoder (vo-aacenc) is an open-source implementation of the AAC audio codec, originally developed by VisualOn for Android. It provides a patent-licensed AAC-LC encoder that offers good quality at moderate to high bitrates and is widely compatible with AAC playback devices.

Key features of the VO-AAC encoder: - AAC-LC (Low Complexity) profile support - Constant bitrate (CBR) encoding - Wide bitrate range from 16 to 320 kbps - Support for mono and stereo audio - Optimized for mobile and embedded devices - Good quality/performance balance
Common use cases: - Mobile application audio encoding - Streaming audio for compatibility - Digital radio and podcasting - Audio tracks in MP4/M4A containers - Cross-platform audio encoding
Comparison with other AAC encoders: - FDK-AAC: Higher quality but more restrictive licensing - FAAC: Lower quality, deprecated - Native platform encoders: May offer better performance
Note: While VO-AAC provides decent quality, for the best AAC encoding quality, consider using FDK-AAC or platform-specific encoders when licensing permits.
