member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSFlangerPhase
member.summary: Defines the phase relationship between the original (dry) signal and the delayed (wet) signal in a flanger effect.

remarks.para: The flanger effect is created by mixing an audio signal with a slightly delayed copy of itself, where the delay time is varied continuously using a low-frequency oscillator (LFO). The phase parameter determines the initial phase offset of this LFO, which affects how the comb filtering sweeps through the frequency spectrum.

Phase values represent the angular offset in degrees:
Negative phases (-180°, -90°) start the LFO cycle below the center position, initially creating notches at lower frequencies
Zero phase (0°) starts the LFO at its center position
Positive phases (90°, 180°) start the LFO cycle above the center position, initially creating notches at higher frequencies

The choice of phase affects the initial character of the flanging effect and how it evolves over time. Different phase settings can create subtle variations in the "whooshing" or "jet plane" sound characteristic of flangers.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSFlangerPhase.PhaseNeg180
member.summary: Phase offset of -180 degrees. The LFO starts at its most negative position, creating the maximum initial delay. This produces deep initial notches in the frequency spectrum and a pronounced downward sweep at the start.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSFlangerPhase.PhaseNeg90
member.summary: Phase offset of -90 degrees. The LFO starts at a negative quarter-cycle position. This creates a moderate initial delay with notches starting in the lower-mid frequency range.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSFlangerPhase.PhaseZero
member.summary: Phase offset of 0 degrees. The LFO starts at its center (neutral) position. This is the most common setting, providing a balanced flanging effect that sweeps equally in both directions.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSFlangerPhase.Phase90
member.summary: Phase offset of 90 degrees. The LFO starts at a positive quarter-cycle position. This creates a moderate initial advance with notches starting in the upper-mid frequency range.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSFlangerPhase.Phase180
member.summary: Phase offset of 180 degrees. The LFO starts at its most positive position, creating the minimum initial delay. This produces shallow initial notches and a pronounced upward sweep at the start.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSFlangerWaveForm
member.summary: Defines the waveform shape used by the Low-Frequency Oscillator (LFO) to modulate the delay time in a flanger effect.

remarks.para: The flanger effect creates its characteristic "swooshing" sound by continuously varying the delay time of a delayed signal that is mixed with the original. This variation is controlled by an LFO, and the waveform shape determines how smoothly or abruptly the delay time changes over each cycle.

The waveform choice significantly impacts the sonic character of the flanging effect:
Different waveforms create different sweep patterns through the frequency spectrum
The shape affects how the comb filter notches move, creating either smooth or more pronounced transitions
Each waveform imparts a unique rhythmic quality to the effect
Typical LFO rates for flanging range from 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz, with slower rates creating gentle sweeps and faster rates producing more intense, vibrato-like effects.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSFlangerWaveForm.Triangle
member.summary: Triangle waveform - Creates linear transitions between minimum and maximum delay values.

remarks.para:
The triangle wave produces a constant rate of change in the delay time, resulting in:
Smooth, predictable sweeps through the frequency spectrum
Even distribution of time spent at all delay values
A mechanical, rhythmic quality that works well for steady, hypnotic effects
Sharp direction changes at the peaks and troughs, creating subtle "clicks" at extreme settings

Triangle waves are often preferred for more pronounced, dramatic flanging effects where the sweep pattern should be clearly audible and predictable. They're particularly effective on percussion and rhythmic material.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSFlangerWaveForm.Sin
member.summary: Sine (sinusoidal) waveform - Creates smooth, curved transitions with gradual acceleration and deceleration.

remarks.para:
The sine wave produces a natural, organic modulation pattern with:
Smooth acceleration and deceleration at the extremes of the sweep
More time spent near the minimum and maximum delay values
Gentle, musical transitions without abrupt changes
A more subtle, vintage character reminiscent of classic analog flangers

Sine waves are ideal for creating natural, breathing effects that blend well with the source material. They're particularly effective on vocals, strings, and pad sounds where a smooth, non-intrusive modulation is desired. The sinusoidal shape mimics many natural phenomena, making it sound more organic.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSGargleWaveForm
member.summary: Defines the waveform shape used to modulate the amplitude in a gargle audio effect.

remarks.para: The gargle effect creates a distinctive "underwater" or "robotic" sound by rapidly modulating the amplitude (volume) of an audio signal at a specific rate. Unlike other modulation effects that affect pitch or timing, gargle specifically creates a rhythmic gating effect by periodically reducing the signal amplitude.

The effect works by multiplying the input signal with a low-frequency oscillator (LFO) waveform, typically operating between 1 Hz and 1000 Hz. The waveform shape determines the character of the amplitude modulation:
Different waveforms create different rhythmic patterns
The shape affects how abruptly the volume changes
Each waveform imparts a unique texture to the gargled sound
Common applications include creating robotic voice effects, simulating underwater speech, adding rhythmic gating to instruments, and producing various special effects for games and multimedia.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSGargleWaveForm.Triangle
member.summary: Triangle waveform - Creates smooth, linear amplitude transitions for a softer gargle effect.

remarks.para:
The triangle wave modulates amplitude with linear ramping, producing:
Gradual volume increases and decreases with no sudden jumps
A smoother, less aggressive sound compared to square wave modulation
Better preservation of the original signal's character and intelligibility
A tremolo-like effect at lower rates (1-10 Hz)
A buzzing quality at higher rates (20-1000 Hz) due to the harmonic content

Triangle wave gargle is ideal for:
Creating vintage sci-fi communication effects
Subtle underwater or telephone-like voice processing
Musical tremolo effects on instruments
Maintaining better speech intelligibility while adding character

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSGargleWaveForm.Square
member.summary: Square waveform - Creates abrupt on/off amplitude switching for a harsh, rhythmic gargle effect.

remarks.para:
The square wave modulates amplitude with instant transitions between full volume and silence, producing:
Hard gating effect with complete on/off switching
Sharp, percussive amplitude modulation
More dramatic and noticeable effect than triangle modulation
Rhythmic stuttering at lower rates (1-20 Hz)
Harsh, ring-modulator-like tones at higher rates (50-1000 Hz)

Square wave gargle is ideal for:
Classic robot or Dalek-style voice effects
Extreme special effects and alien communications
Rhythmic gating effects in electronic music
Creating stutter effects synchronized to tempo
Simulating digital transmission errors or glitches
Note: Square wave modulation can significantly reduce intelligibility at higher rates, making it more suitable for special effects than for maintaining comprehensible speech.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset
member.summary: Defines preset configurations for a 10-band graphic equalizer, optimized for different music genres and listening environments.

remarks.para: A graphic equalizer divides the audio spectrum into frequency bands, allowing independent gain control for each band. This enables compensation for acoustic deficiencies, enhancement of specific instruments, or creation of desired tonal characteristics.

All presets (except 'Custom') use a standard 10-band configuration with center frequencies at: 60 Hz, 170 Hz, 310 Hz, 600 Hz, 1 kHz, 3 kHz, 6 kHz, 12 kHz, 14 kHz, and 16 kHz. These frequencies follow a quasi-logarithmic spacing that corresponds to how humans perceive pitch.

Frequency band characteristics:
60 Hz: Sub-bass - Felt more than heard, adds power and rumble
170 Hz: Bass - Fundamental frequencies of bass instruments and kick drums
310 Hz: Upper bass/Lower midrange - Warmth and body of instruments
600 Hz: Midrange - Fundamental tones of many instruments and lower harmonics
1 kHz: Upper midrange - Crucial for vocal clarity and instrument definition
3 kHz: Presence - Human ear's most sensitive region, affects perceived loudness
6 kHz: Brilliance - Clarity, definition, and "bite" of instruments
12 kHz: High treble - Sparkle, air, and cymbal shimmer
14 kHz: Very high treble - Overtones and harmonics
16 kHz: Ultra-high frequencies - Airiness and spaciousness

Each preset applies specific gain values (typically ranging from -12 dB to +12 dB) to these bands, creating frequency response curves tailored to enhance particular genres or compensate for common playback system deficiencies.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.Default
member.summary: Default flat response with all frequency bands set to 0 dB gain.
member.remarks:
The default preset provides a neutral, uncolored sound with no frequency enhancement or attenuation. This is the reference setting that:
Preserves the original mix as intended by the recording engineer
Provides a baseline for comparing other presets
Works well with high-quality recordings on accurate playback systems
Allows the natural frequency balance of the source material to shine through

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.Custom
member.summary: Custom equalizer configuration allowing user-defined band count, frequencies, and gain values.
member.remarks:
The custom preset enables complete control over the equalizer configuration:
Variable number of bands (not limited to 10)
User-definable center frequencies for each band
Adjustable Q factor (bandwidth) for each band if supported
Independent gain control for each frequency band
This mode is ideal for professional audio work, room correction, hearing compensation, or creating unique frequency response curves for special effects.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.Classical
member.summary: Classical music preset emphasizing clarity and natural instrument timbre.
member.remarks:
Optimized for orchestral, chamber, and acoustic music with typical adjustments:
Slight boost in sub-bass (60 Hz) for orchestra foundation and timpani
Gentle rise in upper midrange (1-3 kHz) for string section clarity
Moderate high-frequency boost (12-16 kHz) for violin harmonics and hall ambience
Controlled midrange to prevent muddiness in complex passages
This preset enhances the spaciousness of concert hall recordings while maintaining the natural balance between instrument sections.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.Club
member.summary: Club preset simulating the frequency response of a dance club sound system.
member.remarks:
Designed to recreate the visceral impact of club PA systems with:
Heavy bass boost (60-170 Hz) for chest-thumping kick drums
Recessed midrange (600 Hz - 1 kHz) to create space for the bass
Boosted upper frequencies (6-16 kHz) for crisp hi-hats and effects
Enhanced presence region (3 kHz) for vocal cut-through
This V-shaped response curve emphasizes rhythm and energy while maintaining clarity for electronic dance music, hip-hop, and other bass-heavy genres.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.Dance
member.summary: Dance music preset optimized for electronic and high-energy music genres.
member.remarks:
Tailored for EDM, techno, house, and similar genres with:
Strong bass emphasis (60-310 Hz) for driving basslines and kick drums
Slight midrange dip to prevent fatigue during extended listening
Bright treble boost (6-16 kHz) for synthesizer sparkle and cymbal sizzle
Enhanced sub-bass for systems capable of deep frequency reproduction
Creates an exciting, energetic sound that emphasizes rhythm and synthetic textures while maintaining clarity in the mix.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.FullBass
member.summary: Full bass preset providing maximum low-frequency enhancement.
member.remarks:
Dramatically boosts all bass frequencies for systems or preferences requiring extra low-end:
Maximum boost at 60-170 Hz for deep, powerful bass response
Extended boost through 310 Hz for fuller instrument body
Flat or slightly reduced midrange and treble to balance the bass emphasis
Ideal for small speakers lacking natural bass extension
Use with caution as excessive bass boost can cause distortion, muddy the mix, or damage speakers not designed for extended low-frequency reproduction.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.FullBassTreble
member.summary: Full bass and treble preset creating a pronounced "smile" curve EQ response.
member.remarks:
Boosts both frequency extremes while reducing midrange for a "scooped" sound:
Strong bass boost (60-310 Hz) for powerful low-end impact
Significant midrange cut (600 Hz - 3 kHz) creating the characteristic "scoop"
Elevated treble (6-16 kHz) for enhanced brightness and detail
Creates an immediately impressive but potentially fatiguing sound
Popular for rock, metal, and electronic music on systems with limited dynamic range. The dramatic V-shape can mask important midrange details in vocals and instruments.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.FullTreble
member.summary: Full treble preset maximizing high-frequency content for enhanced clarity and detail.
member.remarks:
Aggressively boosts upper frequencies for maximum brightness:
Progressive boost from 3 kHz upward for enhanced presence
Maximum elevation at 12-16 kHz for extreme sparkle and air
Flat or reduced bass/midrange to balance the treble emphasis
Reveals subtle details, breath sounds, and room ambience
Useful for dull recordings, hearing loss compensation in high frequencies, or systems with rolled-off treble response. Can cause listener fatigue and sibilance.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.Labtop
member.summary: Laptop speaker compensation preset (note: "Labtop" appears to be a typo for "Laptop").
member.remarks:
Optimized to compensate for typical laptop speaker limitations:
Reduced sub-bass (60 Hz) to prevent distortion from tiny drivers
Boosted upper bass/lower midrange (170-600 Hz) for warmth
Enhanced presence region (3-6 kHz) for dialog clarity
Controlled high treble to reduce harshness from small tweeters
Improves intelligibility and reduces fatigue when using built-in laptop speakers for extended periods, particularly for voice, podcasts, and video content.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.LargeHall
member.summary: Large hall preset simulating the acoustics of a concert hall or auditorium.
member.remarks:
Recreates the frequency characteristics of large acoustic spaces:
Gentle bass boost (60-170 Hz) simulating boundary reinforcement
Slight midrange dip (600 Hz - 1 kHz) mimicking distance absorption
Presence boost (3-6 kHz) for clarity despite simulated distance
Extended high-frequency lift (12-16 kHz) for spaciousness and air
Creates a sense of space and grandeur, particularly effective with live recordings, classical music, and any content benefiting from an expansive soundstage.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.Live
member.summary: Live performance preset enhancing the energy and presence of live recordings.
member.remarks:
Designed to emphasize the excitement and immediacy of live performances:
Moderate bass boost (60-310 Hz) for crowd energy and stage rumble
Enhanced upper midrange (1-3 kHz) for vocal presence and guitar bite
Bright treble (6-16 kHz) for audience ambience and cymbal splash
Overall "forward" presentation bringing the performance closer
Particularly effective with concert recordings, bootlegs, and any content where recreating the "being there" feeling is desired.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.Loudness
member.summary: Loudness compensation preset based on equal-loudness contours (Fletcher-Munson curves).
member.remarks:
Compensates for the human ear's reduced sensitivity to bass and treble at low volumes:
Significant bass boost (60-310 Hz) to maintain fullness at low levels
Moderate treble boost (6-16 kHz) for maintained clarity and detail
Relatively flat midrange where hearing sensitivity is naturally highest
Follows psychoacoustic principles for perceptually balanced sound
Essential for late-night or background listening where volume must be kept low but full frequency perception is desired. Less effective at high volumes.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.Party
member.summary: Party preset optimized for background music at social gatherings.
member.remarks:
Balanced for clarity in noisy environments while maintaining energy:
Controlled bass boost (60-170 Hz) for rhythm without overwhelming conversation
Slightly recessed lower midrange (310-600 Hz) to reduce muddiness
Enhanced presence (3-6 kHz) ensuring vocals cut through ambient noise
Bright treble (12-16 kHz) for excitement without harshness
Creates an energetic but non-fatiguing sound suitable for extended playback in social settings where music provides atmosphere rather than focus.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.Reggae
member.summary: Reggae preset emphasizing the genre's characteristic bass-heavy groove.
member.remarks:
Tailored for reggae, dub, and dancehall's unique frequency requirements:
Deep bass boost (60-170 Hz) for the essential reggae bass lines
Warm lower midrange (310-600 Hz) for drum and bass interaction
Controlled upper midrange for laid-back vocal presentation
Crisp treble (6-16 kHz) for hi-hat patterns and percussion detail
Emphasizes the rhythmic elements crucial to reggae while maintaining the genre's characteristic warmth and groove-oriented mix balance.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.Rock
member.summary: Rock music preset emphasizing power, energy, and instrument separation.
member.remarks:
Optimized for rock, hard rock, and alternative genres:
Strong bass (60-170 Hz) for powerful drums and bass guitar
Slight midrange scoop (600 Hz - 1 kHz) for the "wall of sound" effect
Boosted upper midrange (3 kHz) for guitar presence and vocal cut
Enhanced treble (6-16 kHz) for cymbal crash and guitar harmonics
Creates the aggressive, energetic sound associated with rock music while maintaining clarity between instruments in dense, distorted mixes.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.Ska
member.summary: Ska preset optimized for the genre's distinctive brass and rhythm sections.
member.remarks:
Balanced for ska, two-tone, and ska-punk's unique instrumentation:
Punchy bass (60-170 Hz) for the walking bass lines
Prominent midrange (600 Hz - 3 kHz) for brass section clarity
Enhanced upper midrange for guitar upstrokes and vocal energy
Bright treble (6-16 kHz) for hi-hat emphasis and horn harmonics
Highlights the interplay between rhythm section and horns while maintaining the genre's characteristic energy and danceability.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.Soft
member.summary: Soft preset providing a gentle, relaxed tonal balance.
member.remarks:
Creates a smooth, non-fatiguing sound for easy listening:
Gentle bass reduction to prevent boominess
Slight midrange boost (600 Hz - 1 kHz) for warmth and body
Controlled presence region (3 kHz) to reduce harshness
Rolled-off extreme treble (14-16 kHz) for smoothness
Ideal for background music, quiet listening, or reducing fatigue during extended sessions. Particularly effective with acoustic and jazz recordings.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.SoftRock
member.summary: Soft rock preset balancing rock energy with smooth, polished production.
member.remarks:
Optimized for adult contemporary, soft rock, and melodic rock:
Moderate bass boost (60-170 Hz) for fullness without aggression
Warm midrange (310 Hz - 1 kHz) for vocal and instrument richness
Gentle presence boost (3-6 kHz) for clarity without harshness
Smooth treble (12-16 kHz) for polish without excessive brightness
Provides the melodic emphasis and production sheen characteristic of the genre while maintaining a relaxed, radio-friendly tonal balance.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.EqualizerPreset.Techno
member.summary: Techno preset emphasizing electronic music's synthetic textures and driving rhythms.
member.remarks:
Optimized for techno, trance, and electronic dance music production:
Deep sub-bass boost (60 Hz) for club-system impact
Strong bass (170-310 Hz) for synthesizer bass lines
Recessed midrange (600 Hz - 1 kHz) creating space for bass and treble
Aggressive treble boost (6-16 kHz) for synthesizer brilliance and effects
Creates the characteristic "smiley face" EQ curve that emphasizes the frequency extremes crucial to electronic music's impact and energy.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat
member.summary: Defines the audio format for raw audio data, specifying whether it is Pulse-Code Modulation (PCM), IEEE floating-point, or encoded. This enumeration is crucial for configuring audio streams and ensuring correct data interpretation throughout the framework.
member.remarks: Use this enumeration to specify the sample format for audio capture, processing, and playback. For example, when setting up an audio source, you would select a member of this enum to define the expected audio data format.

example.code: // To configure an audio source to use 16-bit PCM audio: var audioFormat = AudioFormat.PCM16;

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.PCM8
member.summary: 8-bit unsigned integer Pulse-Code Modulation (PCM) format. This format provides a basic level of audio quality.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.PCM16
member.summary: 16-bit signed integer PCM format. This is a standard format for CD-quality audio.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.PCM24
member.summary: 24-bit signed integer PCM format. Used in professional audio for higher dynamic range.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.PCM32
member.summary: 32-bit signed integer PCM format. Offers even greater precision than 24-bit PCM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.IEEE32
member.summary: 32-bit floating-point (IEEE 754) format. Commonly used in audio processing to prevent clipping and preserve quality during intermediate calculations.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.Unknown
member.summary: Represents an unknown or unspecified audio format. This value is typically used as a default or to indicate an error state.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.IEEE64
member.summary: 64-bit double-precision floating-point (IEEE 754) format. Provides the highest level of precision for audio processing, though it is less common and more resource-intensive.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFormat.Encoded
member.summary: Indicates that the audio data is in a compressed or encoded format (e.g., MP3, AAC), rather than raw PCM samples.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFrame

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFrame.Data

member.remarks: This pointer provides direct memory access to the audio samples. Handle with care to avoid memory corruption.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFrame.DataSize

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFrame.Info

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFrame.Timestamp

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFrame.Duration

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFrame.Caps

member.remarks: A caps string might look like: "audio/x-raw, format=S16LE, layout=interleaved, rate=44100, channels=2".

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFrame.#ctor

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFrame.ClearData

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFrame.GetDataArray

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioFrame.ToString

member.remarks: This class is particularly useful for handling custom data streams or metadata. The consumer of this class is responsible for allocating and freeing the memory for the data buffer using the and methods.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.DataFrame.Timestamp

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.AudioLevelEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for audio level events, containing audio level information for individual channels and overall average values.
member.remarks: This event args class is used to report audio levels during audio processing, playback, or recording operations. Audio levels are provided in both percentage (0-100) and decibel (dB) formats for flexibility in different use cases. The class supports multi-channel audio with individual level information for each channel.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.AudioLevelEventArgs.ChannelLevels
member.summary: Gets or sets the audio levels for each channel as percentage values.
member.value: An array of byte values representing the audio level for each channel. Values range from 0 (silence) to 100 (maximum level). The array length corresponds to the number of audio channels.
member.remarks: For stereo audio, index 0 typically represents the left channel and index 1 represents the right channel. For multi-channel audio (e.g., 5.1 surround), the channel mapping follows standard audio conventions.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.AudioLevelEventArgs.ChannelLevelsDb
member.summary: Gets or sets the audio levels for each channel in decibels (dB).
member.value: An array of float values representing the audio level for each channel in decibels. Typical values range from -∞ (silence) to 0 dB (maximum level), with negative values indicating levels below maximum. The array length corresponds to the number of audio channels.
member.remarks: Decibel values provide a logarithmic representation of audio levels, which better matches human perception of loudness. A value of -6 dB represents approximately half the perceived loudness of 0 dB. Values below -60 dB are typically considered effectively silent.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.AudioLevelEventArgs.Average
member.summary: Gets or sets the average audio level across all channels as a percentage value.
member.value: A byte value representing the average audio level across all channels. Values range from 0 (silence) to 100 (maximum level).
member.remarks: This value provides a quick reference for overall audio activity without needing to process individual channels. It is useful for simple level meters or threshold-based audio detection.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.AudioLevelEventArgs.AverageDb
member.summary: Gets or sets the average audio level across all channels in decibels (dB).
member.value: A float value representing the average audio level across all channels in decibels. Typical values range from -∞ (silence) to 0 dB (maximum level).
member.remarks: This provides the average level in a logarithmic scale, which is more suitable for professional audio applications and level matching between different audio sources.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.AudioLevelEventArgs.Timestamp
member.summary: Gets or sets the timestamp indicating when this audio level measurement was taken.
member.value: A value representing the position in the media stream where the level was measured. May be if timestamp information is not available.
member.remarks: This property is optional and may not be populated in all scenarios. When available, it allows for synchronization of audio level data with the media timeline, useful for creating waveform visualizations or time-based audio analysis.

This event is typically raised when: - A channel is selected or changed - Channel information is updated - A channel scan discovers a new channel - Channel properties are modified
This class is only available on Windows platforms where BDA is supported.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.ClosedCaptionsBufferEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for closed captions buffer events, containing raw closed caption data and timing information.

remarks.para: This event args class is used when raw closed caption data is extracted from video streams. Closed captions are textual representations of audio content, including dialogue, sound effects, and other audio information, designed for viewers who are deaf or hard of hearing.

The buffer contains raw closed caption data in various formats such as: - CEA-608 (Line 21) captions for analog and digital TV - CEA-708 captions for digital TV - WebVTT for web-based video - Other proprietary closed caption formats
This event provides low-level access to caption data before it is decoded into text. For decoded text captions, use instead.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.ClosedCaptionsBufferEventArgs.Buffer
member.summary: Gets the pointer to the buffer containing raw closed caption data.
member.value: An pointing to the unmanaged memory buffer containing the closed caption data. The buffer remains valid only during the event handler execution.

remarks.para: This buffer contains raw, undecoded closed caption data. The format of the data depends on the source video stream and may require specific decoders to interpret.
Important: The buffer is only valid during the event handler execution. If you need to process the data asynchronously, copy it to a managed array first using .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.ClosedCaptionsBufferEventArgs.BufferSize
member.summary: Gets the size of the closed caption data buffer in bytes.
member.value: The number of bytes in the buffer pointed to by .
member.remarks: Use this value when copying data from the unmanaged buffer to ensure you don't read beyond the allocated memory. The actual caption data may be smaller than the buffer size if padding is present.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.ClosedCaptionsBufferEventArgs.StartTime
member.summary: Gets the start time for when this caption data should be displayed.
member.value: A indicating the position in the media timeline when the caption should begin displaying.

remarks.para: This timestamp is relative to the beginning of the media stream. It indicates when the closed caption text should first appear on screen.
For continuous captions (like live broadcasts), the start time may be very close to the stop time. For pre-recorded content, there may be a longer duration between start and stop times.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.ClosedCaptionsBufferEventArgs.StopTime
member.summary: Gets the stop time for when this caption data should no longer be displayed.
member.value: A indicating the position in the media timeline when the caption should stop displaying.

remarks.para: This timestamp indicates when the closed caption text should be removed from the display. The duration between and represents how long the caption should remain visible.
For scrolling or paint-on captions, multiple buffer events may be received with overlapping time ranges.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.ClosedCaptionsTextEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for closed captions text events, containing decoded caption text and timing information.

remarks.para: This event args class is used when closed caption data has been decoded into readable text. Unlike which provides raw caption data, this class provides the actual text content ready for display.

Closed captions include not only dialogue but also: - Sound effects (e.g., "[door slams]", "[music playing]") - Speaker identification (e.g., "NARRATOR:", "JOHN:") - Musical notes (♪) for songs - Other audio cues important for understanding the content
The timing information ensures captions are synchronized with the audio/video content, appearing and disappearing at the appropriate times.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.ClosedCaptionsTextEventArgs.Text
member.summary: Gets the decoded closed caption text content.
member.value: A string containing the closed caption text to be displayed. May include formatting information, speaker names, or sound effect descriptions.

remarks.para: The text may contain special formatting or markup depending on the caption source: - Line breaks for multi-line captions - Speaker identifications in uppercase - Sound effects in square brackets [sound effect] - Musical notes (♪) for songs or background music
The text encoding is typically UTF-8 or UTF-16, supporting international characters and special symbols used in closed captions.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.ClosedCaptionsTextEventArgs.StartTime
member.summary: Gets the start time when this caption text should begin displaying.
member.value: A indicating the position in the media timeline when the caption should appear.

remarks.para: This timestamp is synchronized with the media playback position. When the media reaches this time position, the caption should be displayed to the viewer.
For real-time captioning (like live TV), this may be very close to the current playback time. For pre-recorded content, captions are typically prepared with precise timing.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.ClosedCaptionsTextEventArgs.StopTime
member.summary: Gets the stop time when this caption text should be removed from display.
member.value: A indicating the position in the media timeline when the caption should disappear.

remarks.para: The duration between and determines how long the caption remains visible. This duration varies based on: - The length of the text - The pace of dialogue - Reading speed considerations - Caption style (pop-on, paint-on, or roll-up)
Typical display durations range from 1-7 seconds, with most captions displayed for 2-4 seconds.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.ClosedCaptionsTextEventArgs.#ctor(System.String,System.TimeSpan,System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with decoded caption text and timing.
member.param: The decoded closed caption text to be displayed. Can be null or empty for clearing captions.
The media timeline position when this caption should start displaying.
The media timeline position when this caption should stop displaying. Must be greater than or equal to .

remarks.para: This constructor is typically called by closed caption decoders after processing raw caption data into displayable text. The timing information ensures proper synchronization with the media content.
Empty or null text is valid and may be used to clear the caption display area.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.DeviceRemovedAddedEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for device removal and addition events, notifying when media devices are connected or disconnected from the system.

remarks.para: This event args class is used to notify applications about hardware changes in real-time, allowing them to respond appropriately when devices are plugged in or removed. This is particularly important for media applications that need to maintain awareness of available capture devices, audio devices, and other media hardware.

Common scenarios that trigger these events include: - USB webcams being connected or disconnected - Audio devices (microphones, speakers) being plugged in or removed - Capture cards being installed or removed - Virtual devices being created or destroyed - Bluetooth audio devices connecting or disconnecting
This functionality is only available on Windows platforms where device change notifications are supported through Windows APIs. On other platforms, periodic device enumeration may be needed.

member.summary: Gets the name of the device that was added or removed.
member.value: A string containing the device name as reported by the operating system. This is typically the friendly name of the device that users would recognize.

remarks.para: The device name format varies by device type and manufacturer: - Webcams: Often include manufacturer and model (e.g., "Logitech HD Pro Webcam C920") - Audio devices: May include type and model (e.g., "Blue Yeti USB Microphone") - Virtual devices: Usually have descriptive names (e.g., "OBS Virtual Camera")
This name can be used to match against device enumerations to identify specific devices or to display user-friendly notifications about device changes.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.DeviceRemovedAddedEventArgs.Type
member.summary: Gets the type of device change that occurred, indicating both the device category and whether it was added or removed.
member.value: A enumeration value that specifies: - The category of device (video capture, audio capture, audio renderer) - Whether the device was added or removed

remarks.para: The type information allows applications to filter events and respond only to relevant device changes. For example: - A video recording application might only care about video capture devices - An audio mixing application might monitor both audio capture and renderer devices - A streaming application might need to track all device types
Use this property to implement appropriate responses based on device category and the nature of the change (addition vs. removal).

DVD parental levels typically range from 1 (General Audiences) to 8 (Adults Only).

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.NewFilePlaybackEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for the new file playback event. This event is raised when a media player starts playing a new file, typically in playlist scenarios.
member.remarks: This event is particularly useful in playlist playback scenarios where you need to be notified when the player transitions from one media file to another. It can be used to update UI elements, load subtitles, or perform any other actions needed when a new file starts playing.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.NewFilePlaybackEventArgs.Filename
member.summary: Gets the full path of the file that has started playing.
member.value: The complete file path of the media file. This can be a local file path or a URL for network streams.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.OnDeviceCanStartEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for the device startup validation event. This event allows applications to control whether a device should be allowed to start.
member.remarks: This event is raised before a device (camera, microphone, etc.) is started, giving the application a chance to prevent the device from starting based on custom logic. This is useful for implementing device access control, exclusive device usage, or conditional device activation based on application state. The event handler can set the property to control the device startup.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.OnDeviceCanStartEventArgs.CanStart
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the device is allowed to start.
member.value: true if the device can start; otherwise, false. Default value is typically true, but event handlers can set this to false to prevent the device from starting.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.OnDeviceCanStartEventArgs.DeviceName
member.summary: Gets the friendly name of the device attempting to start.
member.value: The human-readable name of the device, such as "HD Webcam" or "USB Audio Device".

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.OnDeviceCanStartEventArgs.DevicePath
member.summary: Gets the system path or identifier of the device.
member.value: The unique device path or identifier used by the system to access the device. This could be a device instance path on Windows or a device node path on Linux.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.OnDeviceCanStartEventArgs.#ctor(System.String,System.String)

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.SeparateCaptureFileEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for the separate capture file event that occurs when a new segment is created during multi-segment recording or when a secondary capture file is created.
member.remarks:
This event is raised in several scenarios:
When recording with file size or duration limits and a new segment is created
When using separate audio/video capture and a new file is started
During time-based segmentation (e.g., hourly recordings)
When dynamic file splitting is triggered by user action

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.SeparateCaptureFileEventArgs.Filename
member.summary: Gets or sets the full path to the newly created capture file.
member.remarks:
The filename typically includes:
Original filename base with segment number appended
Timestamp information if configured
Proper file extension based on the recording format

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.SeparateCaptureFileEventArgs.#ctor(System.String)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.SourceConnectedEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for the source connected event that occurs when a media source (camera, file, stream, etc.) successfully connects and provides its media properties.
member.remarks:
This event is crucial for:
Detecting when a media source is ready for processing
Obtaining source video dimensions for UI layout
Validating source compatibility with processing requirements
Triggering automatic adjustments based on source properties
The event fires after the source negotiates its format and before the first frame is rendered.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.SourceConnectedEventArgs.Width
member.summary: Gets the width of the connected video source in pixels.
member.remarks: This represents the native width of the source before any scaling or transformation. Common values include 640, 1280, 1920, 3840 for standard resolutions.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.SourceConnectedEventArgs.Height
member.summary: Gets the height of the connected video source in pixels.
member.remarks: This represents the native height of the source before any scaling or transformation. Common values include 480, 720, 1080, 2160 for standard resolutions.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.SourceConnectedEventArgs.TimeStamp
member.summary: Gets the start timestamp of the media source.
member.remarks: For live sources (cameras, streams), this is typically TimeSpan.Zero. For file sources, this may indicate the position from which playback will begin, especially useful when resuming playback or starting from a specific position.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.SourceConnectedEventArgs.#ctor(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.SubtitlesSettingsEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for the subtitles settings event that occurs when DirectVobSub subtitle filter is initialized and ready for configuration.
member.remarks:
This event provides access to the IDirectVobSub3 interface for advanced subtitle configuration. DirectVobSub is a DirectShow filter that supports various subtitle formats including:
SUB/IDX (VobSub) format
SRT (SubRip) text subtitles
SSA/ASS (Advanced SubStation Alpha)
Embedded DVD subtitles
The event fires after the subtitle filter is added to the graph but before playback starts.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.SubtitlesSettingsEventArgs.Interface
member.summary: Gets the DirectVobSub interface for subtitle configuration.
member.remarks:
Cast this object to IDirectVobSub3 to access subtitle configuration methods. This interface provides comprehensive control over subtitle display including:
Language/track selection
Text appearance (font, size, colors)
Positioning and margins
Timing adjustments
External subtitle file loading
Note: This interface is only available on Windows platforms with DirectShow.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.SubtitlesSettingsEventArgs.#ctor(System.Object)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.TimeshiftFileEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for the timeshift file event that occurs when a new timeshift buffer file is created during live TV/stream viewing with pause capabilities.
member.remarks:
Timeshift functionality allows users to pause, rewind, and fast-forward live content by buffering it to disk. This event fires when:
A new timeshift buffer file is created at the start of viewing
The buffer rotates to a new file due to size/duration limits
Manual buffer management operations create new files
Timeshift files are typically temporary and managed automatically, but this event allows for custom management, archiving, or monitoring of buffer usage.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.TimeshiftFileEventArgs.Filename
member.summary: Gets the full path to the timeshift buffer file.
member.remarks:
The filename typically includes:
A timestamp or sequence number for ordering
The channel or stream identifier
Appropriate extension (.ts, .m2ts, etc.) based on format
These files are usually stored in a temporary directory and should be treated as transient unless explicitly preserved.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.TimeshiftFileEventArgs.#ctor(System.String)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.TVTunerTuneChannelsEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for the TV tuner channel scanning event that occurs during automatic channel discovery or manual frequency tuning operations.
member.remarks:
This event is raised repeatedly during channel scanning to provide real-time feedback about:
Signal detection at each frequency
Channel identification when signals are found
Overall scanning progress
The event enables applications to build channel lists, show scanning progress, and make decisions about signal quality during the tuning process.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.TVTunerTuneChannelsEventArgs.SignalPresent
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether a valid signal is present at the current frequency.
member.remarks: True indicates that a broadcast signal has been detected and locked. This doesn't guarantee the signal quality is good enough for viewing, but indicates that a carrier is present and demodulation is possible.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.TVTunerTuneChannelsEventArgs.Channel
member.summary: Gets the physical or virtual channel number.
member.remarks: For analog TV, this is typically the channel number (2-69). For digital TV, this might be the physical channel containing multiple virtual channels. The exact meaning depends on the broadcast standard (ATSC, DVB, ISDB, etc.).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.TVTunerTuneChannelsEventArgs.Frequency
member.summary: Gets the frequency in Hertz (Hz) being tuned.
member.remarks:
The frequency is provided in Hz for precision. Common conversions:
MHz = Frequency / 1,000,000
kHz = Frequency / 1,000
Typical ranges:
VHF-Low (channels 2-6): 54-88 MHz
VHF-High (channels 7-13): 174-216 MHz
UHF (channels 14-69): 470-806 MHz

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.TVTunerTuneChannelsEventArgs.Progress
member.summary: Gets the overall scanning progress as a percentage (0-100).
member.remarks: This value indicates how much of the total frequency range or channel list has been scanned. It's useful for progress bars and determining when the scan is complete (Progress = 100).

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.TVTunerTuneChannelsEventArgs.#ctor(System.Boolean,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.GIFResizeStretchMode
member.summary: Defines how a GIF frame should be resized or stretched to fit a target dimension.
member.remarks: This enumeration is used to control the aspect ratio and scaling behavior when creating GIFs from source video frames that may have a different size.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.GIFResizeStretchMode.Stretch
member.summary: Stretches the frame to fill the target dimensions completely, which may distort the original aspect ratio.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.GIFResizeStretchMode.Letterbox
member.summary: Resizes the frame to fit within the target dimensions while maintaining the original aspect ratio. Black bars (letterboxing) will be added to fill any empty space if the aspect ratios do not match.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.GIFResizeStretchMode.Crop
member.summary: Resizes the frame to fill the target dimensions while maintaining the original aspect ratio. The frame will be cropped if its aspect ratio does not match the target, ensuring no black bars are present.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.GIFResizeStretchMode.None
member.summary: The frame is not resized. It will be centered in the output, and if it is larger than the target dimensions, it will be cropped. If it is smaller, the surrounding area will be filled with a background color.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.IBitmap
member.summary: Represents a platform-agnostic bitmap image. This interface is used as a common wrapper for different bitmap implementations across various platforms (e.g., Windows, Android, iOS).
member.remarks: The primary purpose of this interface is to allow for the manipulation and passing of bitmap images in a generic way, without coupling the core logic to a specific UI framework or image library. Implementations of this interface are expected to handle the platform-specific details of bitmap creation, manipulation, and disposal. As it implements , instances should be properly disposed of to release underlying resources.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.IMediaPlayerControls
member.summary: Defines a standard set of controls for a media player component. This interface provides a common API for controlling playback of media files, including play, pause, stop, seek, and volume adjustments. It also includes asynchronous versions of most methods for use in responsive UI applications.
member.remarks: This interface inherits from , providing access to video effect adjustments in addition to playback controls. Implementations of this interface are expected to manage the underlying media playback engine.

member.param: If set to true, the media is loaded and ready to play but does not start automatically.
member.returns: true if the operation is successful, false otherwise.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.IStatusOverlay
member.summary: Defines an interface for a status overlay, which is used to display real-time information on top of a video stream. This can include details like frame rate, resolution, or custom text provided by the application.
member.remarks: This interface is intended to be implemented by components that provide video rendering or processing. It standardizes the way status information is enabled, configured, and displayed, without exposing the underlying implementation details.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.IVideoCaptureControls

member.remarks: This interface inherits from , allowing for the application of real-time video effects during capture. Implementations of this interface are expected to manage the underlying capture engine (e.g., GStreamer, Media Foundation).

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.IVideoEffectsControls
member.summary: Defines a standard set of controls for applying basic real-time video effects. This interface provides methods to adjust common image properties such as brightness, contrast, and saturation, as well as apply simple transformations like grayscale, flip, and invert.
member.remarks: This interface is intended to be implemented by components that handle video rendering or processing, such as media players or video capture controls. It provides a unified way to manipulate the visual appearance of the video stream.

member.summary: Sets the color saturation level of the video.
member.param: The saturation value. Typically, 1.0 is the default; 0.0 results in a grayscale image, and values greater than 1.0 intensify colors.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.IVideoView
member.summary: Defines a platform-agnostic interface for a video rendering view. This interface abstracts the underlying UI control used for displaying video, allowing the core engine to remain independent of any specific UI framework (e.g., WinForms, WPF, Android, iOS).
member.remarks: Implementations of this interface are responsible for managing a native UI element that can render video frames. It provides methods for lifecycle management, UI interaction, and event handling, including mouse input. The interface includes platform-specific sections to handle the unique requirements of different operating systems.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.IVideoViewNativeRendering
member.summary: Defines an interface for video view components that support switching to a native rendering backend. This is typically used to improve performance in demanding scenarios, such as playing high-resolution (4K/8K) video or using hardware-accelerated GPU decoding.
member.remarks: When native rendering is enabled, the video is rendered directly by the underlying system's graphics API (e.g., DirectX, OpenGL) instead of through a higher-level UI framework like WPF. This can significantly reduce CPU usage and improve rendering smoothness, but may have implications for UI integration and layering.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.IVideoViewNativeRendering.SetNativeRendering(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Enables or disables native rendering for the video view.
member.param: Set to true to enable native rendering; false to use the default framework rendering (e.g., WPF).
member.remarks: It is recommended to enable this for performance-critical applications, such as those involving GPU-accelerated decoding or ultra-high-definition video.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.IVideoViewPushFrame
member.summary: Defines an interface for video views that support direct pushing of video frames for rendering. This interface is crucial for scenarios where raw video data needs to be displayed without relying on a traditional media pipeline (e.g., for custom video processing or real-time frame injection).
member.remarks: Implementations of this interface are responsible for taking raw video frame data and rendering it efficiently to the display. This allows for fine-grained control over the video rendering process.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.IVideoViewPushFrame.PushFrame(VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoFrame)
member.summary: Pushes a to the view for rendering. This method is typically used for raw video frames that conform to the legacy structure.
member.param: The containing the video data to be rendered.

member.summary: Pushes a to the view for rendering. This method is used for video frames generated by the MediaBlocks engine, offering more advanced frame metadata.
member.param: The containing the video data and extended metadata to be rendered.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.IVRVideoControl
member.summary: Defines an interface for controlling Virtual Reality (VR) video playback parameters. This interface allows manipulation of camera orientation (yaw, pitch, roll), field of view, and the VR projection mode.
member.remarks: Implementations of this interface are typically found in video renderers or effects that support 360-degree or VR video content. It enables interactive viewing of immersive video by adjusting the viewer's perspective.

member.summary: Gets or sets the roll (tilt) of the VR camera in degrees.

member.summary: Gets or sets the field of view (FOV) of the VR camera in degrees. This controls the zoom level or how much of the scene is visible.

member.summary: Gets or sets the current VR projection mode.

member.summary: Checks if a specific VR mode is supported by the implementing component (e.g., video block, effect, or renderer).
member.returns: true if the mode is supported; otherwise, false.

member.summary: Occurs when any of the VR control settings (Yaw, Pitch, Roll, FieldOfView, Mode) have changed.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VRMode
member.summary: Specifies the different Virtual Reality (VR) projection modes supported for video playback. Not all modes may be supported by every component (e.g., specific video blocks, effects, or renderers).

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VRMode.Normal
member.summary: Standard video mode, where no VR projection is applied. The video is displayed as a flat 2D image.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VRMode.Equirectangular
member.summary: Equirectangular projection mode, commonly used for 360-degree videos. The video is mapped onto a sphere, allowing the viewer to look around.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VRMode.Cubemap
member.summary: Cubemap projection mode, where the 360-degree video is represented as six faces of a cube. This can offer better visual quality at the poles compared to equirectangular projection.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAppMode
member.summary: Defines the application mode for DVD audio streams, indicating the primary purpose or special features of the audio track.
member.remarks: DVD audio tracks can serve different purposes beyond standard playback. This enumeration helps identify special audio track types that may require specific handling or user interface options. The application mode is part of the DVD-Video specification and helps players determine how to present audio options to users.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAppMode.None
member.summary: No special application mode is specified for this audio track.
member.remarks: This is the default value for standard audio tracks that don't have any special features or requirements. Most movie and TV show audio tracks will use this mode.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAppMode.Karaoke
member.summary: The audio track is designed for karaoke playback with vocal suppression capabilities.
member.remarks: Karaoke mode indicates that the audio track supports features like vocal channel isolation, allowing the player to reduce or remove vocals for sing-along functionality. This mode typically includes separate channels for music and vocals that can be mixed independently.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAppMode.Surround
member.summary: The audio track contains surround sound information for enhanced spatial audio.
member.remarks: Surround mode indicates that the audio track is specifically encoded with multichannel surround sound (e.g., 5.1, 7.1). This helps players optimize decoding and speaker configuration for the best surround sound experience.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAppMode.Other
member.summary: The audio track has a special application mode not covered by the standard categories.
member.remarks: This value is used for proprietary or future audio modes that don't fit into the predefined categories. The specific functionality would depend on the DVD authoring and may require special player support.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAttributes
member.summary: Represents the complete set of attributes for a DVD audio stream, including format, language, and technical specifications.
member.remarks: This structure encapsulates all the metadata associated with a DVD audio track as defined in the DVD-Video specification. It provides comprehensive information about the audio stream's encoding, language settings, and technical parameters. This information is typically extracted from the DVD's IFO (Information) files and is used by media players to properly decode and present audio options to users.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAttributes.AppMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the application mode that indicates the special purpose or features of this audio track.
member.value: The application mode such as karaoke, surround, or standard playback.
member.remarks: The application mode helps players determine special handling requirements for the audio track, such as enabling karaoke features or optimizing surround sound processing.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAttributes.AppModeData
member.summary: Gets or sets additional data specific to the application mode.
member.value: Application-specific data byte that provides extra configuration for the AppMode.
member.remarks: This byte contains mode-specific information. For karaoke mode, it might indicate the channel configuration for vocals. The interpretation depends on the AppMode value.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAttributes.AudioFormat
member.summary: Gets or sets the audio encoding format used for this track.
member.value: The audio format such as AC3, DTS, LPCM, or MPEG audio.
member.remarks: The audio format determines which decoder is needed to process the audio stream. Different formats offer various trade-offs between quality, compression, and features.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAttributes.Language
member.summary: Gets or sets the language of the audio track as a human-readable string.
member.value: The language name, typically in English (e.g., "English", "Spanish", "Japanese").
member.remarks: This is usually derived from the LanguageID and provides a user-friendly representation of the audio track's language for display in player interfaces.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAttributes.LanguageID
member.summary: Gets or sets the Windows Language Code Identifier (LCID) for the audio track.
member.value: The LCID value representing the language and regional variant.
member.remarks: The LCID is a 32-bit value that uniquely identifies a language and its regional variant. For example, 1033 represents English (United States), while 2057 represents English (United Kingdom). This allows for precise language identification including regional dialects.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAttributes.LanguageExtension
member.summary: Gets or sets the language extension that indicates special audio track types.
member.value: The language extension type such as captions, visually impaired, or director's commentary.
member.remarks: Language extensions identify special-purpose audio tracks that accompany the main content. These tracks provide alternative audio experiences like descriptive audio for visually impaired viewers or commentary tracks with behind-the-scenes information.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAttributes.HasMultichannelInfo
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this audio stream contains explicit multichannel information.
member.value: true if the stream has dedicated multichannel encoding; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: This flag indicates whether the audio stream contains discrete multichannel information (e.g., 5.1 or 7.1 surround) as opposed to stereo or mono. It helps players configure the appropriate audio output settings.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAttributes.Frequency
member.summary: Gets or sets the sampling frequency of the audio stream in Hz.
member.value: The sampling frequency, typically 48000 Hz or 96000 Hz for DVD audio.
member.remarks: DVD-Video supports sampling rates of 48 kHz and 96 kHz. Higher sampling rates provide better audio quality but require more storage space. LPCM tracks may use 96 kHz, while compressed formats typically use 48 kHz.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAttributes.Quantization
member.summary: Gets or sets the bit depth (quantization) of the audio samples.
member.value: The number of bits per sample, typically 16, 20, or 24 bits.
member.remarks: Quantization determines the dynamic range and precision of the audio. DVD supports 16-bit (standard), 20-bit, and 24-bit (high-end) quantization. Higher bit depths provide better dynamic range but increase data size. This property primarily applies to LPCM audio; compressed formats have their own internal precision.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioAttributes.NumberOfChannels
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of audio channels in the stream.
member.value: The channel count, ranging from 1 (mono) to 8 (7.1 surround).
member.remarks: Common configurations include: - 1: Mono - 2: Stereo - 6: 5.1 surround (front left/right, center, rear left/right, subwoofer) - 8: 7.1 surround (adds side left/right to 5.1) The actual speaker mapping depends on the audio format and DVD authoring.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioCaps
member.summary: Defines the audio format capabilities supported by a DVD player or decoder, represented as bit flags.
member.remarks: This enumeration uses bit flags to indicate which audio formats a DVD player or decoder can handle. Multiple formats can be supported simultaneously by combining flags using bitwise OR operations. The values correspond to the audio formats defined in the DVD-Video specification, and a player must support at least one of these formats to be DVD-compliant. These capabilities are typically queried during DVD playback initialization to determine the optimal audio stream to select.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioCaps.None
member.summary: No audio format capabilities are supported or specified.
member.remarks: This value indicates that either no audio capabilities have been queried yet, or the device doesn't support any DVD audio formats.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioCaps.AC3
member.summary: Supports AC3 (Dolby Digital) audio decoding.
member.remarks: AC3, also known as Dolby Digital, is the most common audio format on DVDs. It provides compressed 5.1 surround sound at bitrates from 192 to 448 kbps. This format is mandatory for NTSC DVDs and very common on PAL DVDs. AC3 offers good quality with efficient compression, making it the standard choice for most DVD releases.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioCaps.MPEG2
member.summary: Supports MPEG-2 audio decoding (including MPEG-1 Layer II).
member.remarks: MPEG-2 audio includes both MPEG-1 Layer II (commonly used in Europe) and MPEG-2 multichannel extensions. This format is mandatory for PAL DVDs and optional for NTSC. It supports stereo and multichannel configurations with bitrates typically ranging from 64 to 384 kbps.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioCaps.LPCM
member.summary: Supports LPCM (Linear Pulse Code Modulation) uncompressed audio.
member.remarks: LPCM provides uncompressed digital audio with the highest quality possible on DVD. It supports various sampling rates (48/96 kHz) and bit depths (16/20/24-bit). While offering superior audio quality, LPCM requires significantly more disc space than compressed formats. It's commonly used for music DVDs, concert recordings, and high-end releases where audio quality is paramount.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioCaps.DTS
member.summary: Supports DTS (Digital Theater Systems) audio decoding.
member.remarks: DTS is an optional high-quality audio format that competes with Dolby Digital. It typically uses higher bitrates (768-1536 kbps) than AC3, potentially offering better audio quality. DTS support is optional for DVD players, so content with only DTS audio may not play on all devices. Many DVDs include both AC3 and DTS tracks to ensure compatibility while offering enhanced quality for capable systems.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioCaps.SDDS
member.summary: Supports SDDS (Sony Dynamic Digital Sound) audio decoding.
member.remarks: SDDS is a rare format developed by Sony that supports up to 7.1 channels. It uses ATRAC compression and was primarily designed for theatrical releases. Very few DVDs include SDDS tracks, and support in consumer players is extremely limited. This capability flag is mostly relevant for professional or specialized playback systems.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioFormat
member.summary: Specifies the audio encoding format used in a DVD audio stream.
member.remarks: This enumeration identifies the specific audio codec used to encode an audio stream on a DVD. Unlike DVDAudioCaps which represents capabilities, this enum identifies the actual format of a specific audio track. DVD-Video supports multiple audio formats to balance quality, compression efficiency, and compatibility. The format directly affects playback requirements, audio quality, and the amount of disc space consumed by the audio track.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioFormat.AC3
member.summary: AC3 (Dolby Digital) compressed audio format.
member.remarks: AC3 is the most widely used audio format on DVDs, providing multichannel surround sound (up to 5.1 channels) with efficient compression. It's mandatory for NTSC DVDs and offers bitrates from 192 to 448 kbps. AC3 provides a good balance between audio quality and file size, making it the standard choice for most commercial DVD releases.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioFormat.MPEG1
member.summary: MPEG-1 Layer II audio format (stereo only).
member.remarks: MPEG-1 audio is limited to stereo (2-channel) playback and uses Layer II compression, commonly known as MP2. This format is often found on older DVDs or those targeting regions where MPEG audio is standard. It typically uses bitrates from 64 to 384 kbps and provides good quality for stereo content.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioFormat.MPEG1_DRC
member.summary: MPEG-1 audio with Dynamic Range Compression metadata.
member.remarks: This variant of MPEG-1 audio includes Dynamic Range Compression (DRC) information, allowing players to automatically adjust the audio's dynamic range. DRC is useful for late-night viewing or in noisy environments, as it reduces the difference between quiet and loud passages. The compression can typically be enabled or disabled by the user.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioFormat.MPEG2
member.summary: MPEG-2 multichannel audio format.
member.remarks: MPEG-2 audio extends MPEG-1 with support for multichannel surround sound (up to 5.1 or 7.1). It's mandatory for PAL DVDs and optional for NTSC. This format maintains backward compatibility with MPEG-1 decoders for the stereo channels while adding surround information. It's commonly used in European DVD releases.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioFormat.MPEG2_DRC
member.summary: MPEG-2 audio with Dynamic Range Compression metadata.
member.remarks: Similar to MPEG1_DRC, this format includes DRC metadata for MPEG-2 multichannel audio. The DRC information allows automatic adjustment of the audio dynamics, particularly useful for maintaining dialogue clarity while reducing loud effects and music. This helps prevent disturbing others when watching at low volumes.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioFormat.LPCM
member.summary: Linear PCM (uncompressed) audio format.
member.remarks: LPCM provides the highest audio quality on DVD as it stores uncompressed digital audio. It supports various configurations: 48/96 kHz sampling rates, 16/20/24-bit depth, and up to 8 channels. While offering pristine audio quality, LPCM consumes significant disc space (approximately 4.6 Mbps for stereo 48kHz/16-bit). It's commonly used for music DVDs, audiophile releases, and bonus audio tracks.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioFormat.DTS
member.summary: DTS (Digital Theater Systems) compressed audio format.
member.remarks: DTS is a high-quality compressed audio format that typically uses higher bitrates than AC3 (768-1536 kbps), potentially offering better sound quality. It supports up to 6.1 channels on DVD. DTS is optional for DVD players, so discs usually include an AC3 track as well. It's favored by home theater enthusiasts and is common on special editions and concert DVDs.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioFormat.SDDS
member.summary: SDDS (Sony Dynamic Digital Sound) compressed audio format.
member.remarks: SDDS is a rare format on consumer DVDs that supports up to 7.1 channels using Sony's ATRAC compression. Originally developed for theatrical presentations, it offers high-quality multichannel audio but has very limited support in consumer DVD players. When present, it's typically alongside more common formats like AC3 or DTS.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioFormat.Other
member.summary: Other or proprietary audio format not covered by standard types.
member.remarks: This value is reserved for future audio formats or proprietary extensions that don't fit into the standard DVD-Video audio format categories. Players encountering this format may not be able to decode the audio unless they have specific support for the proprietary format.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioLangExt
member.summary: Defines language extension codes that identify special-purpose audio tracks on a DVD.
member.remarks: Language extensions provide additional context about the purpose of an audio track beyond just its language. This allows DVD authors to include multiple audio tracks in the same language but serving different purposes. For example, a DVD might have an English main audio track, an English descriptive audio track for visually impaired viewers, and two English commentary tracks. The language extension helps players present these options clearly to users and enables accessibility features.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioLangExt.NotSpecified
member.summary: No special language extension is specified; this is a standard audio track.
member.remarks: This is the default value for regular audio tracks that contain the main program audio. Most audio tracks on a DVD will have this extension, indicating they're intended for normal playback without any special purpose or additional content.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioLangExt.Captions
member.summary: Audio track contains normal dialog plus additional narration for captions.
member.remarks: Caption audio tracks include the regular program audio plus a narrator reading on-screen text, captions, and titles. This helps viewers who cannot read the on-screen text or subtitles. It's different from descriptive audio as it focuses on reading text rather than describing visual elements. This feature is particularly useful for audiences with reading difficulties or visual impairments.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioLangExt.VisuallyImpaired
member.summary: Audio track contains descriptive narration for visually impaired viewers.
member.remarks: Descriptive audio (also called audio description or video description) includes the main program audio plus additional narration that describes important visual elements during pauses in dialog. The narrator describes actions, scenes, facial expressions, costumes, and other visual information that would otherwise be missed by visually impaired viewers. This is an important accessibility feature required by law in many jurisdictions.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioLangExt.DirectorComments1
member.summary: First director's commentary track providing behind-the-scenes information.
member.remarks: Director commentary tracks typically feature the film's director (and sometimes other crew members) discussing the making of the film, creative decisions, technical challenges, and anecdotes from production. This is the primary commentary track when multiple commentaries are available. Commentary tracks are popular bonus features that provide insight into the filmmaking process.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioLangExt.DirectorComments2
member.summary: Second director's commentary track or alternative commentary.
member.remarks: This indicates a secondary commentary track, which might feature different participants than the first commentary. For example, it could include actors, producers, writers, or technical crew. Some DVDs feature multiple commentary tracks to provide different perspectives on the same content. The specific participants and focus would be indicated in the DVD's menu system.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioStream
member.summary: Represents information about a single audio stream within a DVD title.

remarks.para: DVDs support multiple audio streams per title, allowing viewers to choose between different languages, audio formats (Dolby Digital, DTS, PCM), or specialized tracks like director's commentary. Each audio stream can have different characteristics such as sample rate, bit depth, and channel configuration.

This class encapsulates all the metadata associated with a DVD audio stream, including: - Audio format and encoding attributes - Language information - Karaoke capabilities (for music/singing DVDs) - Stream enable/disable state
DVD audio streams are indexed starting from 0, and viewers can switch between available streams during playback using the DVD menu or player controls.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioStream.Attributes
member.summary: Gets or sets the audio format and encoding attributes for this stream.
member.value: The containing details about the audio format, sample rate, bit depth, channel configuration, and compression type.
member.remarks: Common DVD audio formats include: - AC3 (Dolby Digital): Up to 5.1 channels, compressed - DTS: High-quality compressed audio, often 5.1 or 7.1 - PCM: Uncompressed audio, typically stereo at 48kHz or 96kHz - MPEG Audio: Compressed stereo audio

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioStream.IsAudioStreamEnabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this audio stream is currently enabled and available for playback.
member.value: true if this audio stream can be selected and played; false if the stream is present but disabled (possibly due to region restrictions or disc authoring choices).
member.remarks: A DVD may contain audio streams that are present in the data structure but disabled for various reasons, such as regional restrictions or content protection.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioStream.KaraokeAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets the karaoke-specific attributes for this audio stream, if applicable.
member.value: The containing karaoke channel assignments and mixing options, or null if this is not a karaoke-enabled audio stream.
