member.remarks: Karaoke DVDs use special multi-channel audio configurations where different channels contain different elements (music, lead vocals, backing vocals). The karaoke attributes define how these channels can be mixed for different karaoke modes.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDAudioStream.Language
member.summary: Gets or sets the language code for this audio stream.
member.value: An integer representing the ISO 639 language code, where common values include: - 0x656E (25966): English - 0x6672 (26226): French - 0x6573 (25971): Spanish - 0x6465 (25701): German - 0x6A61 (27489): Japanese
member.remarks: The language code helps players display the appropriate language name in the audio selection menu. Use language conversion utilities to convert between the integer code and readable language names.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDDecoderCaps
member.summary: Represents the capabilities of a DVD decoder, including supported playback rates and audio format capabilities.

remarks.para: DVD decoders have varying capabilities depending on their implementation (hardware vs. software) and design. This class provides information about what a particular DVD decoder can handle, including maximum data rates for different stream types and special playback features.

The capability information is crucial for: - Determining if smooth fast-forward and reverse playback are supported - Understanding the decoder's performance limits - Checking audio format support (AC3, DTS, PCM, etc.) - Validating if a DVD can be played properly on the current system

Data rates are typically expressed as multipliers of normal playback speed (1x). For example, a FwdMaxRateVideo of 16.0 means the decoder can handle video playback at up to 16 times normal speed while maintaining smooth motion.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDDecoderCaps.Size
member.summary: Gets or sets the size of the decoder capabilities structure in bytes.
member.value: The size of the structure, used for version compatibility and validation.
member.remarks: This field helps ensure compatibility between different versions of the decoder interface by indicating the expected structure size.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDDecoderCaps.AudioCaps
member.summary: Gets or sets the audio decoding capabilities of the DVD decoder.
member.value: A object containing detailed information about supported audio formats, channels, and features.
member.remarks: Audio capabilities include support for various formats like AC3 (Dolby Digital), DTS, PCM, and MPEG audio, as well as multi-channel configurations.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDDecoderCaps.FwdMaxRateVideo
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum video data rate supported in the forward direction.
member.value: The maximum playback rate multiplier for video streams (e.g., 2.0 for 2x speed, 16.0 for 16x speed). A value of 1.0 indicates normal playback speed only.
member.remarks: This value indicates how fast the decoder can process video data during fast-forward operations while maintaining smooth playback. Higher values allow for faster scanning through content. Typical values range from 2.0 to 32.0 for modern decoders.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDDecoderCaps.FwdMaxRateAudio
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum audio data rate supported in the forward direction.
member.value: The maximum playback rate multiplier for audio streams during fast-forward. Often lower than video rates due to audio processing limitations.
member.remarks: Audio typically cannot be played at the same high speeds as video. Many decoders mute audio above certain speeds (typically 2x or 4x) to avoid distortion.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDDecoderCaps.FwdMaxRateSP
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum subpicture (subtitle) data rate supported in the forward direction.
member.value: The maximum playback rate multiplier for subpicture streams during fast-forward.
member.remarks: Subpictures include subtitles, menu highlights, and other overlay graphics. These typically follow the video rate but may have independent limitations.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDDecoderCaps.BwdMaxRateVideo
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum video data rate supported in the reverse direction.
member.value: The maximum reverse playback rate multiplier for video streams. Returns 0 if the decoder does not support smooth reverse playback.
member.remarks: Smooth reverse playback is technically challenging because MPEG video uses inter-frame compression. Decoders that return 0 will use I-frame stepping for reverse playback instead, which appears jerky but requires less processing. Values typically range from -1.0 to -16.0 when supported.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDDecoderCaps.BwdMaxRateAudio
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum audio data rate supported in the reverse direction.
member.value: The maximum reverse playback rate multiplier for audio streams. Returns 0 if smooth reverse audio playback is not supported.
member.remarks: Reverse audio playback is rarely supported due to the complexity of playing compressed audio formats in reverse. Most decoders mute audio during reverse playback.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDDecoderCaps.BwdMaxRateSP
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum subpicture data rate supported in the reverse direction.
member.value: The maximum reverse playback rate multiplier for subpicture streams. Returns 0 if smooth reverse subpicture display is not supported.
member.remarks: Like audio, subpictures are often disabled during reverse playback, especially at higher speeds, to reduce processing overhead.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDDiscSide
member.summary: Specifies which side of a double-sided DVD disc is currently being accessed or referenced.

remarks.para: DVD discs can be manufactured as either single-sided or double-sided media. Double-sided DVDs essentially contain two separate discs bonded back-to-back, each with its own data layer. This allows for increased storage capacity without using dual-layer technology.

Key characteristics of double-sided DVDs: - Each side can hold approximately 4.7 GB (single layer) or 8.5 GB (dual layer) - The disc must be physically flipped to access the other side - Each side can contain completely different content (e.g., widescreen on one side, fullscreen on the other) - Each side has its own label area and can be identified visually - Less common than dual-layer single-sided discs due to user inconvenience

Double-sided DVDs were more common in the early days of the DVD format when dual-layer technology was expensive. They're still occasionally used for special editions where different versions of content are provided on each side.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDDiscSide.SideA
member.summary: Indicates Side A of a double-sided DVD disc.
member.remarks: Side A is typically the primary side containing the main feature or content. On retail DVDs, this is usually labeled more prominently and contains the theatrical version or primary content that users expect to see.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDDiscSide.SideB
member.summary: Indicates Side B of a double-sided DVD disc.
member.remarks: Side B often contains supplementary content such as: - Special features and bonus content - Alternate versions (fullscreen vs widescreen) - Additional episodes for TV series - Director's commentary or making-of documentaries

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDGPRMArray.Registers
member.summary: Gets or sets the array containing all 16 General Purpose Register Memory (GPRM) values.
member.value: An array of 16 signed 16-bit integers representing the current values stored in GPRMs 0-15. Each value can range from -32768 to 32767 when interpreted as signed, or 0 to 65535 when interpreted as unsigned.
member.remarks: These registers are volatile and exist only during the current playback session. They are used by DVD navigation commands to implement interactive features, track user choices, and control conditional branching in DVD menus and playback. The interpretation of each register's value depends on how the DVD author programmed the disc's navigation logic.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo
member.summary: Provides comprehensive information about a DVD disc, including its structure, content, capabilities, and current playback state.

remarks.para: The DVDInfo class serves as a central repository for all DVD-related metadata and state information. It encompasses disc-level properties, title information, audio/video streams, navigation state, and decoder capabilities. This information is essential for DVD player applications to properly handle disc navigation, stream selection, and user interface presentation.

DVD Structure Overview: - A DVD contains one or more titles (movies, episodes, etc.) - Each title can have multiple chapters (scenes) - Each title can contain multiple audio streams (languages, commentary) - Each title can contain multiple subpicture streams (subtitles) - Menus provide navigation between titles and configuration options - Navigation is controlled by a Virtual Machine using registers (GPRMs/SPRMs)

Key concepts represented in this class: - Title structure and navigation - Multi-language support for audio, subtitles, and menus - Parental control ratings - Region coding and copy protection - Hardware decoder capabilities - Current playback state and user selections

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Audio_CurrentStream
member.summary: Gets or sets the currently selected audio stream index.
member.value: Zero-based index of the active audio stream. Range is 0 to (Audio_StreamsCount - 1). A value of -1 typically indicates no audio stream is selected.
member.remarks: Users can switch between available audio streams during playback to select different languages, commentary tracks, or audio formats (e.g., stereo vs. 5.1 surround).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Audio_DefaultAudioLanguage
member.summary: Gets or sets the default audio language code as specified by the DVD author.
member.value: An integer representing the ISO 639 language code for the preferred audio language. Common values include 0x656E (English), 0x6672 (French), 0x6573 (Spanish).
member.remarks: This is the audio stream that will be selected by default when the DVD starts playing, unless overridden by player settings or user preferences.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Audio_DefaultAudioLanguageS
member.summary: Gets or sets the default audio language as a human-readable string.
member.value: The language name (e.g., "English", "French", "Spanish") corresponding to the Audio_DefaultAudioLanguage code.
member.remarks: This provides a user-friendly representation of the default audio language for display in user interfaces.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Audio_DefaultAudioLanguageExt
member.summary: Gets or sets the extension type for the default audio language.
member.value: A value indicating special audio track types such as director's commentary, visually impaired audio description, or standard audio.
member.remarks: Language extensions help differentiate between multiple audio tracks in the same language that serve different purposes (e.g., normal dialogue vs. commentary).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Audio_StreamsCount
member.summary: Gets or sets the total number of audio streams available on the current DVD title.
member.value: The count of available audio streams. DVDs can have up to 8 audio streams per title.
member.remarks: Multiple audio streams allow for different languages, audio formats, or special tracks like commentary. Not all streams may be accessible due to regional restrictions.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.DecoderCaps
member.summary: Gets or sets the capabilities of the DVD decoder being used for playback.
member.value: A object containing information about supported playback rates, audio formats, and special features.
member.remarks: Decoder capabilities determine what features are available during playback, such as fast-forward/reverse speeds, audio format support, and smooth motion capabilities. This information helps applications adjust their UI and features based on hardware limitations.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Disc_CountryCode
member.summary: Gets or sets the country code associated with this DVD disc.
member.value: A 2-byte array representing the ISO 3166 country code. This is used for region-specific content and parental rating systems.
member.remarks: The country code helps determine which parental rating system to use and may affect available content based on regional restrictions.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Disc_CurrentUOPS
member.summary: Gets or sets the current User Operation Prohibitions (UOPs) flags.
member.value: A indicating which user operations are currently prohibited by the DVD author at this point in playback.
member.remarks: UOPs control what actions users can perform at any given time. For example, some DVDs prohibit skipping FBI warnings or studio logos, while others may disable fast-forward during certain scenes.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Disc_DVD_Side
member.summary: Gets or sets which side of a double-sided DVD is currently active.
member.value: A value indicating Side A or Side B. For single-sided discs, this will typically be SideA.
member.remarks: Double-sided DVDs require manual flipping to access content on the other side. Each side functions as an independent disc with its own content structure.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Disc_GPRMs
member.summary: Gets or sets the current General Purpose Register Memory (GPRM) values.
member.value: A containing 16 general-purpose registers used by the DVD Virtual Machine for navigation logic and state tracking.
member.remarks: GPRMs are used by DVD authors to implement interactive features, track user choices, and control conditional navigation. They function as variables in the DVD's programming logic.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Disc_ID
member.summary: Gets or sets the unique identifier for this DVD disc.
member.value: A 64-bit integer that uniquely identifies this DVD. This ID is typically derived from disc metadata and can be used for disc recognition.
member.remarks: The disc ID can be used to remember user preferences, playback positions, or to look up disc information in online databases.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Disc_NumOfTitles
member.summary: Gets or sets the total number of titles available on this DVD.
member.value: The count of titles (main features, episodes, extras) on the disc. Most movie DVDs have 1-5 titles, while TV series DVDs may have many more.
member.remarks: Titles are the primary content divisions on a DVD. Title 1 is usually the main feature, while subsequent titles often contain special features, trailers, or additional episodes.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Disc_NumOfVolumes
member.summary: Gets or sets the total number of volumes in this DVD set.
member.value: The total volume count for multi-disc sets. Single discs will have a value of 1.
member.remarks: Multi-volume sets are common for TV series, extended editions, or collections. This helps users understand the complete scope of the content set.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Disc_SPRMs
member.summary: Gets or sets the current System Parameter Register Memory (SPRM) values.
member.value: A containing system registers that track player state, user preferences, and hardware capabilities.
member.remarks: SPRMs are read-only registers that provide information about the current playback state, selected streams, parental level, region code, and player capabilities. Unlike GPRMs, these cannot be modified by DVD commands.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Disc_Volume
member.summary: Gets or sets the current volume number within a multi-volume DVD set.
member.value: The volume number of the currently loaded disc, starting from 1. For single-disc releases, this will be 1.
member.remarks: Used in conjunction with Disc_NumOfVolumes to track position within multi-disc sets and potentially prompt users to insert the next disc.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Menu_DefaultLanguage
member.summary: Gets or sets the default menu language code.
member.value: An integer representing the ISO 639 language code for the default menu language. This determines which language version of the DVD menus will be displayed initially.
member.remarks: DVDs can contain menus in multiple languages. The default is typically set based on the disc's target market or region.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Menu_DefaultLanguageS
member.summary: Gets or sets the default menu language as a human-readable string.
member.value: The language name (e.g., "English", "French", "Japanese") for the default menu language.
member.remarks: This provides a user-friendly representation of the menu language for display purposes, converted from the Menu_DefaultLanguage code.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Menu_Languages
member.summary: Gets or sets the list of all available menu languages on this DVD.
member.value: A list of language names representing all menu languages available on the disc. Users can switch between these languages for menu navigation.
member.remarks: Multi-language menu support allows DVDs to be marketed internationally. Common languages include English, French, Spanish, German, and Japanese, but availability varies by disc region and publisher.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Menu_VMG_Attributes
member.summary: Gets or sets the Video Manager (VMG) menu attributes.
member.value: A object containing properties of the main disc menu, including video format, aspect ratio, and display capabilities.
member.remarks: The VMG menu is the top-level menu system that provides access to all titles and disc features. It typically includes the main menu, setup menu, and special features menu.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.ParentalLevel
member.summary: Gets or sets the current parental control level setting.
member.value: An integer from 1 to 8 representing the parental control level: - 1: G (General Audiences) - Suitable for all ages - 2-3: PG (Parental Guidance) - Some material may not be suitable for children - 4: PG-13 - Parents strongly cautioned, some material inappropriate for children under 13 - 5-6: R (Restricted) - Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian - 7-8: NC-17 - No one 17 and under admitted
member.remarks: DVDs can contain multiple versions of scenes with different ratings. The parental level setting determines which version is played. If the disc's rating exceeds the player's setting, playback may be blocked or require a password. The exact meaning of levels can vary by country (MPAA for US, different systems elsewhere).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Subpicture_CurrentStream
member.summary: Gets or sets the currently selected subpicture (subtitle) stream index.
member.value: Zero-based index of the active subpicture stream. Range is 0 to (Subpicture_StreamsCount - 1). A value of -1 typically indicates no subpicture stream is selected.
member.remarks: Subpicture streams contain subtitles, captions, and menu highlight overlays. Users can switch between available streams to select different subtitle languages or turn subtitles off entirely.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Subpicture_DefaultLanguage
member.summary: Gets or sets the default subpicture language code.
member.value: An integer representing the ISO 639 language code for the preferred subtitle language. Common values include 0x656E (English), 0x6672 (French), 0x6573 (Spanish).
member.remarks: This is the subtitle stream that may be selected by default based on player settings or disc authoring. Many DVDs don't enable subtitles by default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Subpicture_DefaultLanguageS
member.summary: Gets or sets the default subpicture language as a human-readable string.
member.value: The language name (e.g., "English", "French", "Spanish") corresponding to the Subpicture_DefaultLanguage code.
member.remarks: This provides a user-friendly representation of the default subtitle language for display in user interfaces.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Subpicture_DefaultLanguageExt
member.summary: Gets or sets the extension type for the default subpicture language.
member.value: A value indicating special subtitle types such as normal subtitles, large captions for hearing impaired, or director's commentary.
member.remarks: Subpicture extensions help differentiate between multiple subtitle tracks in the same language that serve different purposes (e.g., normal subtitles vs. SDH/CC).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Subpicture_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether subpicture display is currently enabled.
member.value: true if subtitles/subpictures are being displayed; false if they are hidden.
member.remarks: This controls the global visibility of subpictures. When false, no subtitles will be displayed regardless of stream selection. When true, the selected subpicture stream (if any) will be displayed.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Subpicture_StreamsCount
member.summary: Gets or sets the total number of subpicture streams available on the current DVD title.
member.value: The count of available subpicture streams. DVDs can have up to 32 subpicture streams per title.
member.remarks: Multiple subpicture streams allow for subtitles in different languages, as well as special tracks like closed captions for the hearing impaired or director's commentary subtitles. Not all streams may be accessible due to regional restrictions.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.Titles
member.summary: Gets or sets the collection of all titles available on this DVD.
member.value: A list of objects, each containing detailed information about a title including duration, chapters, angles, and available streams.
member.remarks: Titles are the main content divisions on a DVD: - Title 1 is typically the main feature film or first episode - Subsequent titles often contain special features, deleted scenes, or additional episodes - Each title can have different audio/subtitle options and chapter divisions - Some titles may be hidden and only accessible through specific menu paths

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDInfo.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with default values.
member.remarks: Initializes all collections and sets appropriate default values for string properties. The country code array is initialized to the standard 2-byte size required for ISO 3166 codes.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeAssignment
member.summary: Defines the channel assignment modes for DVD karaoke audio tracks.

remarks.para: DVD karaoke discs use multichannel audio to provide different audio elements that can be mixed in real-time. This enumeration specifies how audio channels are assigned to carry different karaoke elements such as the main vocals, guide vocals, and instrumental tracks.

The channel assignment determines which audio channels contain specific karaoke content: - L (Left channel): Typically contains instrumental music or guide melodies - R (Right channel): Typically contains instrumental music or guide melodies - M (Mono/Center): Often used for vocal tracks that need to be centered - 1, 2: Additional channels for guide vocals or alternative mixes

This allows karaoke systems to mix channels differently based on user preferences, such as fading out guide vocals as the singer becomes more confident, or adjusting the balance between instrumental and vocal tracks.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeAssignment.reserved0
member.summary: Reserved for future use. Not currently defined in the DVD specification.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeAssignment.reserved1
member.summary: Reserved for future use. Not currently defined in the DVD specification.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeAssignment.LR
member.summary: Left and Right channel assignment. Typically used for stereo instrumental tracks without center channel content.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeAssignment.LRM
member.summary: Left, Right, and Mono (center) channel assignment. Common configuration where L/R contain instrumental music and M contains guide vocals.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeAssignment.LR1
member.summary: Left, Right, and channel 1 assignment. Channel 1 typically contains the first guide vocal track for duet songs.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeAssignment.LRM1
member.summary: Left, Right, Mono (center), and channel 1 assignment. Provides both centered vocals and an additional guide vocal channel.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeAssignment.LR12
member.summary: Left, Right, channel 1, and channel 2 assignment. Used for duet karaoke where channels 1 and 2 contain separate guide vocals for each singer.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeAssignment.LRM12
member.summary: Left, Right, Mono (center), channel 1, and channel 2 assignment. Full multichannel configuration supporting instrumental, centered vocals, and two guide vocal tracks.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeAttributes
member.summary: Represents the attributes and configuration of DVD karaoke audio tracks.

remarks.para: DVD karaoke is a specialized format that extends standard DVD audio capabilities to support interactive singing experiences. This class encapsulates the metadata that describes how karaoke content is structured on the disc, including channel assignments, duet support, and guide vocal configurations.

Key concepts in DVD karaoke: - Multiple audio channels carry different elements (instrumental, guide vocals, effects) - Channels can be dynamically mixed based on user preferences - Support for solo and duet performances - Master of Ceremonies (MC) tracks for instruction or entertainment

The karaoke player uses these attributes to: - Configure the audio mixer for proper channel routing - Enable/disable guide vocals based on user skill level - Support duet mode with separate guide tracks for each singer - Display appropriate on-screen information about available features

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeAttributes.Version
member.summary: Gets or sets the karaoke format version number.
member.value: The version number of the DVD karaoke specification used.
member.remarks: Different versions may support different features or channel configurations. Version 1 is the most common and widely supported.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeAttributes.MasterOfCeremoniesInGuideVocal1
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether a Master of Ceremonies (MC) track is present in guide vocal channel 1.
member.value: true if guide vocal channel 1 contains MC announcements or instructions; false if it contains only singing guide vocals.

remarks.para: The Master of Ceremonies track typically contains: - Song introductions and announcements - Singing instructions or encouragement - Entertainment between verses
When enabled, the karaoke system can optionally play these announcements to enhance the karaoke experience, especially for beginners.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeAttributes.Duet
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this karaoke track supports duet mode.
member.value: true if the track contains separate guide vocals for two singers; false for solo performance tracks.

remarks.para: In duet mode: - Channel 1 typically contains guide vocals for the first singer - Channel 2 contains guide vocals for the second singer - Each singer can independently control their guide vocal volume - On-screen lyrics may be color-coded for each singer

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeAttributes.ChannelAssignment
member.summary: Gets or sets the channel assignment mode for this karaoke track.
member.value: The value indicating how audio channels are configured.
member.remarks: The channel assignment determines which audio channels contain instrumental music, guide vocals, and other karaoke elements. This affects how the audio mixer routes and combines channels during playback.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeAttributes.ChannelContents
member.summary: Gets or sets an array describing the content type of each audio channel.
member.value: An array of flags for each channel, indicating what type of audio content each channel contains.

remarks.para: Each element in the array corresponds to an audio channel and uses flags to indicate the types of content present in that channel. A channel may contain multiple content types (e.g., both guide vocal and sound effects).
The array size depends on the : - LR: 2 channels - LRM: 3 channels - LR1: 3 channels - LRM1: 4 channels - LR12: 4 channels - LRM12: 5 channels

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeContents
member.summary: Defines the types of audio content that can be present in DVD karaoke channels.

remarks.para: This flags enumeration identifies the different types of audio content that can be mixed within DVD karaoke channels. Each channel can contain multiple content types simultaneously, allowing for complex audio arrangements that support various karaoke performance scenarios.

DVD karaoke systems use these content identifiers to: - Allow users to selectively enable/disable specific audio elements - Provide appropriate mixing controls for each content type - Support progressive learning by fading guide elements as users improve - Enable special effects and enhancements during performances

The distinction between guide vocals and guide melodies is important: - Guide vocals: Full vocal performances with lyrics to help singers follow along - Guide melodies: Instrumental melody lines (often synthesized) that indicate pitch without words

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeContents.None
member.summary: No karaoke content present in this channel.
member.remarks: Indicates that the channel contains only instrumental music without any guide vocals, melodies, or special effects.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeContents.GuideVocal1
member.summary: Guide vocal track 1 - Primary guide vocals for the main melody.

remarks.para: Contains a full vocal performance of the song to help singers learn timing, phrasing, and expression. This is typically the main guide vocal track for solo performances or the first singer's part in duets.

Users can adjust the volume of this track independently, allowing them to: - Sing along with full support when learning - Reduce the guide volume as they become more confident - Completely mute it for unassisted performance

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeContents.GuideVocal2
member.summary: Guide vocal track 2 - Secondary guide vocals for harmony or duet parts.

remarks.para: Contains guide vocals for: - The second singer in duet performances - Harmony parts in solo songs - Alternative vocal interpretations
In duet mode, this allows each singer to have independent control over their respective guide vocal assistance.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeContents.GuideMelody1
member.summary: Guide melody 1 - Primary instrumental melody line.

remarks.para: An instrumental version of the main vocal melody, often played by a synthesized instrument (e.g., piano, flute, or bell sounds). This helps singers follow the pitch without hearing actual vocals.
Useful for: - Singers who know the words but need pitch guidance - Creating a less intrusive guide than full vocals - Practicing pitch accuracy without lyrical distraction

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeContents.GuideMelody2
member.summary: Guide melody 2 - Secondary instrumental melody line.
member.remarks: Similar to GuideMelody1 but for: - The second singer's part in duets - Harmony melody lines - Alternative melodic interpretations

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeContents.GuideMelodyA
member.summary: Guide melody A - Alternative or supplementary melody line.

remarks.para: Additional melodic guidance that may represent: - Simplified versions of complex melodies - Regional variations of the song - Optional ornamentations or improvisations
The A/B designation allows for multiple alternative interpretations to be included on the same disc.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeContents.GuideMelodyB
member.summary: Guide melody B - Second alternative or supplementary melody line.
member.remarks: Another alternative melodic interpretation, providing even more flexibility for different performance styles or skill levels.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeContents.SoundEffectA
member.summary: Sound effect A - First set of audio effects or enhancements.

remarks.para: Special audio effects that enhance the karaoke experience: - Audience reactions (applause, cheering) - Vocal effects (echo, reverb presets) - Transition sounds between song sections - Comedic or dramatic sound effects for entertainment
These effects can be triggered automatically at specific points in the song or controlled by the karaoke system operator.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDKaraokeContents.SoundEffectB
member.summary: Sound effect B - Second set of audio effects or enhancements.
member.remarks: Additional sound effects providing more variety or alternative effect options. May include different audience reactions or special effects suited to different performance contexts.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMenuAttributes
member.summary: Represents the attributes of a DVD menu, providing comprehensive information about the menu's multimedia components.

remarks.para: DVD menus are interactive screens that allow users to navigate and select various options on a DVD disc. They typically include a background video or still image, optional audio (such as background music), and subpicture overlays for buttons and navigation elements.

The menu system in DVD-Video consists of several types: - Title Menu: The main menu accessed when a disc is first played - Root Menu: Top-level menu for disc navigation - Subpicture Menu: For selecting subtitle tracks - Audio Menu: For choosing audio streams - Angle Menu: For multi-angle content selection - Chapter Menu: For direct chapter access
Menu attributes define the technical characteristics of these interactive elements, including video format, audio properties, and subpicture specifications for button highlights and text overlays.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMenuAttributes.CompatibleRegion
member.summary: Gets or sets an array indicating which DVD regions are compatible with this menu.

remarks.para: DVD region coding is a digital rights management technique that restricts playback to specific geographical regions. The array contains 8 boolean values corresponding to regions 1-8:

list.item: Region 1: USA, Canada, US Territories
Region 2: Europe, Japan, Middle East, South Africa
Region 3: Southeast Asia, South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong
Region 4: Australia, New Zealand, Latin America
Region 5: Eastern Europe, Russia, India, Africa
Region 6: China
Region 7: Reserved for future use
Region 8: International venues (aircraft, cruise ships)

remarks.para: A value of true at index [n-1] indicates the menu is playable in region n. Region-free menus will have all values set to true.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMenuAttributes.VideoAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets the video attributes of the menu, including resolution, aspect ratio, and encoding format.

remarks.para: Menu video can be either motion video (typically MPEG-2) or still images. Common menu video specifications include: - NTSC: 720x480 at 29.97 fps - PAL: 720x576 at 25 fps - Aspect ratios: 4:3 or 16:9 (anamorphic)
Still menus use single frames but maintain the same resolution and aspect ratio specifications as motion menus.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMenuAttributes.AudioPresent
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether audio is present in the menu.

remarks.para: Menu audio is optional and typically used for: - Background music to enhance the viewing experience - Sound effects for button navigation - Ambient sounds matching the menu theme
Not all DVD menus include audio; simple text-based menus often omit it to reduce disc space usage.

member.value: true if the menu includes an audio stream; otherwise, false.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMenuAttributes.AudioAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets the audio attributes when audio is present in the menu.

remarks.para: Menu audio typically uses simpler encoding than main feature audio: - Common formats: AC-3 (Dolby Digital) 2.0, PCM - Lower bitrates than feature audio (e.g., 192 kbps) - Usually stereo rather than surround sound
This property is only valid when is true.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMenuAttributes.SubpicturePresent
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether subpicture streams are present in the menu.

remarks.para: Subpictures in DVD menus are used for: - Button highlight graphics (selection rectangles, color changes) - Text overlays for button labels - Animated transitions between button states - Visual feedback for user navigation
Subpictures use a 2-bit color depth (4 colors) with transparency, allowing for simple but effective overlay graphics without consuming significant bandwidth.

member.value: true if the menu includes subpicture overlays; otherwise, false.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMenuAttributes.SubpictureAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets the subpicture attributes when subpictures are present in the menu.

remarks.para: Menu subpictures define the interactive elements: - Button highlight colors and transparency - Selection state graphics (normal, selected, activated) - Positioning and dimensions of interactive areas - Color lookup table (CLUT) for the 4-color palette
The DVD specification allows menus to have up to 36 buttons per page, with sophisticated highlight and selection effects defined through subpicture streams.
This property is only valid when is true.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMUACoeff
member.summary: Represents the mixing coefficients for DVD Multi-channel User Audio (MUA) downmixing.

remarks.para: DVD MUA (Multi-channel User Audio) allows for dynamic downmixing of multichannel audio to stereo output. This class defines the logarithmic mixing coefficients that control how each source channel contributes to the final left (channel 0) and right (channel 1) stereo output channels.

The coefficients are stored as logarithmic values (base 2) for several reasons: - Efficient computation in digital signal processors - Better precision across a wide dynamic range - Natural representation of audio levels in decibels

In the context of DVD karaoke: - These coefficients allow proper stereo imaging of multichannel karaoke content - Guide vocals can be centered or panned as needed - Instrumental tracks maintain proper stereo separation - Effects can be positioned in the stereo field for optimal impact

The actual mixing gain is calculated as: gain = 2^(Log2Coefficient) For example: - Log2Alpha = 0.0 results in unity gain (1.0) - Log2Alpha = -1.0 results in -6dB attenuation (0.5) - Log2Alpha = 1.0 results in +6dB amplification (2.0)

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMUACoeff.Log2Alpha
member.summary: Gets or sets the logarithmic mixing coefficient for contributing this channel to the left stereo output (channel 0).
member.value: The base-2 logarithm of the mixing gain. A value of 0.0 represents unity gain, negative values represent attenuation, and positive values represent amplification.

remarks.para: This coefficient determines how much of the source channel is mixed into the left speaker. Common values: - 0.0: Full contribution (unity gain) - -1.0: Half contribution (-6dB) - -2.0: Quarter contribution (-12dB) - -Infinity: No contribution (muted)
For karaoke applications, this helps position audio elements in the stereo field. For example, centering a guide vocal requires equal coefficients for both channels.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMUACoeff.Log2Beta
member.summary: Gets or sets the logarithmic mixing coefficient for contributing this channel to the right stereo output (channel 1).
member.value: The base-2 logarithm of the mixing gain. A value of 0.0 represents unity gain, negative values represent attenuation, and positive values represent amplification.

remarks.para: This coefficient determines how much of the source channel is mixed into the right speaker. By adjusting the ratio between Log2Alpha and Log2Beta, you can control the stereo positioning of the audio source: - Equal values: Center position - Higher Log2Alpha: Panned left - Higher Log2Beta: Panned right

In karaoke systems, different elements might be positioned differently: - Guide vocals: Often centered (equal coefficients) - Instrumental tracks: May use traditional stereo panning - Sound effects: Can be positioned for dramatic effect

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMUAMixingInfo
member.summary: Represents the mixing configuration for a DVD Multi-channel User Audio (MUA) channel.

remarks.para: DVD MUA mixing information controls how multichannel audio is downmixed to stereo or other channel configurations. This is particularly important for DVD karaoke where multiple audio elements (vocals, instruments, effects) need to be properly positioned and mixed for optimal playback on various audio systems.

Key concepts in MUA mixing: - Channel routing: Which source channels contribute to which output channels - Phase relationships: Whether signals are mixed in-phase or out-of-phase - Speaker targeting: The intended playback position in a surround sound system

Phase relationships are crucial for: - Creating stereo width and spaciousness - Implementing vocal removal techniques (out-of-phase mixing) - Ensuring mono compatibility when channels are summed - Creating special effects like pseudo-surround from stereo

In karaoke applications, this allows sophisticated control over how different elements are presented, enabling features like vocal isolation, dynamic panning, and adaptive mixing based on the playback system's capabilities.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMUAMixingInfo.MixTo0
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this channel is mixed to the left output (channel 0).
member.value: true if this channel contributes to the left stereo output; false if it does not contribute to the left channel.
member.remarks: When true, the channel's audio content will be included in the left speaker output. The actual contribution level is determined by the mixing coefficients in .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMUAMixingInfo.MixTo1
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this channel is mixed to the right output (channel 1).
member.value: true if this channel contributes to the right stereo output; false if it does not contribute to the right channel.
member.remarks: When true, the channel's audio content will be included in the right speaker output. The actual contribution level is determined by the mixing coefficients in .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMUAMixingInfo.Mix0InPhase
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this channel is mixed in-phase to the left output (channel 0).
member.value: true if the signal is mixed in-phase (normal polarity); false if the signal is mixed out-of-phase (inverted polarity).

remarks.para: Phase relationships affect how signals combine: - In-phase: Signals add constructively, maintaining full level - Out-of-phase: Signals may cancel when summed to mono
Out-of-phase mixing is used for: - Creating "vocal removal" effects in karaoke - Widening the stereo image - Creating surround-like effects from stereo speakers

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMUAMixingInfo.Mix1InPhase
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this channel is mixed in-phase to the right output (channel 1).
member.value: true if the signal is mixed in-phase (normal polarity); false if the signal is mixed out-of-phase (inverted polarity).

remarks.para: Different phase relationships between left and right can create various effects: - Both in-phase: Normal stereo imaging - One out-of-phase: Creates asymmetric stereo effects - Both out-of-phase: Can create "surround" or "ambient" effects
In karaoke, this might be used to make guide vocals seem to come from "outside" the main stereo image, making them easier to distinguish from the instrumental track.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMUAMixingInfo.SpeakerPosition
member.summary: Gets or sets the intended speaker position for this channel in a surround sound system.
member.value: A speaker position identifier indicating the intended playback location. Common values include: - 0: Front left - 1: Front right - 2: Front center - 3: Low frequency effects (subwoofer) - 4: Back left (surround left) - 5: Back right (surround right) - Additional values for extended surround formats (7.1, etc.)

remarks.para: This information helps audio decoders properly route channels when playing on surround sound systems. For karaoke content: - Guide vocals are often assigned to the center speaker - Instrumental music uses front left/right - Ambient effects might use surround speakers - Crowd noise or reverb might be in the rear channels
When downmixing to stereo, this position information helps determine appropriate mixing coefficients to maintain proper spatial relationships.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMultichannelAudioAttributes
member.summary: Represents the attributes for DVD multichannel audio streams, providing detailed information about channel mixing and downmixing coefficients for surround sound playback.

remarks.para: DVD-Video supports sophisticated multichannel audio formats, primarily 5.1 and 7.1 surround sound configurations. This class contains the metadata necessary for proper audio channel management, including downmixing coefficients for playback on systems with fewer speakers than the source material.

The multichannel audio system in DVD uses the following standard channel configurations: - 5.1: Front Left, Front Right, Center, LFE (Low Frequency Effects), Surround Left, Surround Right - 6.1: Adds a Rear Center channel - 7.1: Adds Surround Back Left and Surround Back Right instead of single Rear Center

Downmixing is the process of converting multichannel audio to fewer channels (e.g., 5.1 to stereo). The coefficients define how each source channel contributes to the output channels, ensuring proper balance and preventing clipping while maintaining the artistic intent of the mix.

DVD players use these attributes to: - Properly route audio to available speakers - Calculate downmix matrices for stereo or Pro Logic output - Apply dynamic range compression when requested - Maintain proper phase relationships between channels

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMultichannelAudioAttributes.Info
member.summary: Gets or sets an array of DVDMUAMixingInfo objects containing mixing information for each audio channel.

remarks.para: Each element in this array corresponds to one audio channel and contains: - Channel position identifier (e.g., front left, center, surround right) - Phase relationship information - Channel grouping for related channels - Special processing flags (e.g., LFE channel indicators)

The array typically contains: - Index 0: Front Left (L) - Index 1: Front Right (R) - Index 2: Center (C) - Index 3: LFE/Subwoofer (.1) - Index 4: Surround Left (Ls) - Index 5: Surround Right (Rs) - Index 6-7: Additional surround channels for 6.1/7.1 configurations
The mixing information is crucial for maintaining proper soundstage and imaging when the audio is played back on various speaker configurations.

member.value: An array of up to 8 DVDMUAMixingInfo objects, with the actual count depending on the audio format (5.1, 6.1, or 7.1).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDMultichannelAudioAttributes.Coeff
member.summary: Gets or sets an array of DVDMUACoeff objects containing the mixing coefficients for channel downmixing.

remarks.para: These coefficients define the mathematical relationships for downmixing multichannel audio to stereo or other reduced channel configurations. Each coefficient specifies: - The contribution of each source channel to the left output - The contribution of each source channel to the right output - Any phase inversions or delays required - Attenuation levels to prevent clipping

Common downmix scenarios include: - 5.1 to Stereo: Typically uses coefficients like C→L/R: 0.707 (-3dB), Ls/Rs→L/R: 0.707 - 5.1 to Pro Logic: Maintains surround encoding with specific phase relationships - 7.1 to 5.1: Combines rear channels into existing surround channels

The DVD specification includes standard downmix coefficients (e.g., ITU-R BS.775), but content creators can specify custom coefficients to preserve their artistic intent when the audio is played on systems with fewer speakers.
Coefficients are typically expressed as: - Linear values (0.0 to 1.0) - Or in decibels (-∞ to 0 dB) - May include phase information (0° or 180°)

member.value: An array of up to 8 DVDMUACoeff objects corresponding to each audio channel's contribution to the downmixed output.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSPRMArray
member.summary: Represents an array of DVD System Parameter Register (SPRM) values that control DVD player state and behavior.

remarks.para: System Parameter Registers (SPRMs) are a set of 24 read-only registers (SPRM0-SPRM23) that maintain the current state of the DVD player. These registers store critical information about player configuration, user preferences, and current playback state. Unlike General Parameter Registers (GPRMs) which can be modified by DVD content, SPRMs are controlled by the player and reflect its current operational state.

The SPRM registers serve as the interface between DVD content and player capabilities, allowing disc authors to create content that adapts to different player configurations and user preferences. DVD navigation commands can read these values to make decisions about playback flow, menu presentation, and feature availability.
Key SPRM registers include:

item.description: Preferred menu language code (ISO 639-1, e.g., "en" for English)
Current audio stream number and attributes
Current subpicture stream number and display flag
Current angle number (for multi-angle features)
Current title number in Title set
Current Video Title Set (VTS) number
Current Title PGC (Program Chain) number
Current Part of Title (chapter) number
Highlighted button number (0-36, 0 means no button selected)
Navigation timer for auto-actions
Current PGC playback time (in BCD format)
Player audio mixing mode for karaoke (bit flags)
Country code for parental management (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2)
Parental management level (1-8, lower = more restrictive)
Player video configuration (bit 0-1: aspect ratio, bit 2: display mode)
Player audio capabilities (decoder format support flags)
Preferred audio language code (ISO 639-1)
Preferred audio language extension (normal, commentary, etc.)
Preferred subpicture language code (ISO 639-1)
Preferred subpicture language extension (normal, large, children, etc.)
Player region code (bit mask, bit 0-7 for regions 1-8)
Reserved for future use
Reserved for future use
Player state and capabilities extension

remarks.para: These registers enable sophisticated DVD behavior such as: - Automatic language selection based on player preferences - Seamless branching for different versions of content - Parental control enforcement - Multi-angle scene synchronization - Region-specific content protection

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSPRMArray.Registers
member.summary: Gets or sets the array containing all 24 DVD System Parameter Register values.

remarks.para: The array contains 24 16-bit values (SPRM0 through SPRM23), each serving a specific purpose in DVD navigation and playback control. These values are maintained by the DVD player and reflect the current player state, user preferences, and disc navigation position.

Register values are typically accessed by index: - Registers[0]: SPRM0 - Menu description language code - Registers[1]: SPRM1 - Audio stream number - Registers[2]: SPRM2 - Subpicture stream number and display flag - ... and so on through Registers[23]

Some registers use specific bit patterns: - Language codes: Packed ASCII (e.g., 0x656E = "en") - Bit flags: Individual bits represent different states or capabilities - BCD values: Time values in Binary Coded Decimal format - Enumerated values: Predefined constants for specific settings

member.value: An array of 24 short (16-bit signed integer) values representing the current state of all System Parameter Registers.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubpictureAttributes
member.summary: Represents the attributes and characteristics of a DVD subpicture stream.

remarks.para: DVD subpicture streams contain overlay graphics that can be displayed on top of the main video. Each subpicture stream has specific attributes that define its content type, encoding format, language information, and special characteristics. These attributes help DVD players determine how to process and present the subpicture content to users.

Subpictures on DVDs are typically used for: - Subtitles in multiple languages - Closed captions for accessibility - Menu button highlights - Karaoke lyrics with timing information - Director's commentary indicators - Special graphical overlays

A DVD can contain up to 32 subpicture streams, allowing for extensive multilingual support and various overlay features. The player selects which stream to display based on user preferences, disc programming, and these attribute values.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubpictureAttributes.Type
member.summary: Gets or sets the type of content contained in the subpicture stream.
member.value: A value indicating whether the stream contains language-specific content (subtitles/captions) or other graphical overlays.

remarks.para: The Type property is crucial for proper subpicture handling: - Language type: Indicates subtitles or captions that should be selectable based on language preferences - Other type: Indicates special overlays that may be displayed regardless of language settings - NotSpecified: The content type is unknown and should be handled generically
This property affects how the subpicture stream appears in player menus and whether it's automatically selected based on system language settings.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubpictureAttributes.CodingMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the encoding format used for the subpicture graphics data.
member.value: A value indicating the compression and encoding method used for the subpicture bitmap data.

remarks.para: DVD subpictures typically use run-length encoding (RLE) for compression, which is efficient for the type of graphics used in subtitles and overlays. The coding mode determines how the player should decode the subpicture data.

Standard DVD subpictures support: - 2-bit color depth (4 colors including transparency) - Run-length encoded compression - Resolution matching the video frame - Multiple rectangular regions per subpicture

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubpictureAttributes.LanguageID
member.summary: Gets or sets the Windows Language Code Identifier (LCID) for language-type subpictures.
member.value: An integer representing the LCID of the subpicture's language. This value is only meaningful when equals . Common values include 1033 for English (US), 1034 for Spanish, 1036 for French, etc.

remarks.para: The LCID allows for precise language identification beyond simple ISO 639 codes, including regional variants (e.g., Spanish from Spain vs. Spanish from Mexico). This enables DVD players to match subtitles to specific user language preferences.
For non-language subpictures, this value may be 0 or undefined. Applications should only rely on this value when Type indicates language content.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubpictureAttributes.Language
member.summary: Gets or sets the human-readable language name or description of the subpicture stream.
member.value: A string containing the language name (e.g., "English", "Spanish", "French") or a description of the subpicture content (e.g., "Director's Commentary", "Trivia Track").

remarks.para: This property provides a user-friendly representation of the subpicture stream that can be displayed in player menus. For language subtitles, it typically contains the language name. For other types, it may describe the overlay's purpose.
The language string may be localized based on the DVD's target market or may use English names universally. Some DVDs include native language names (e.g., "Español" instead of "Spanish").

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubpictureAttributes.LanguageExtension
member.summary: Gets or sets additional language classification information for the subpicture stream.
member.value: A value providing extended language information such as whether the subtitles are normal, for children, or contain adult content.

remarks.para: The language extension provides additional context about the subpicture content: - Normal: Standard subtitles or captions - Children: Simplified language or content appropriate for children - CC (Closed Captions): Include sound effects and speaker identification - Forced: Subtitles that should display even when subtitles are disabled - Director's Commentary: Special subtitle track with filmmaker notes

This information helps parents control content access and ensures appropriate subtitle selection for different audiences. Players may use this to implement parental controls or accessibility features.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureCoding
member.summary: Specifies the encoding method used for DVD subpicture (subtitle and menu overlay) data streams.

remarks.para: DVD subpictures are overlay graphics used for subtitles, karaoke lyrics, menu buttons, and other visual elements that appear on top of the main video. The DVD-Video specification defines specific compression methods to efficiently store these graphics while maintaining compatibility across all DVD players.

Subpicture data characteristics: - 2-bit color depth (4 colors maximum per subpicture) - Resolution matches the video frame (720x480 NTSC, 720x576 PAL) - Includes transparency information for each pixel - Compressed using run-length encoding to minimize storage

The compression is particularly effective because: - Subtitles contain large areas of transparency - Text and graphics typically use solid colors - Menu highlights often consist of simple geometric shapes - The 4-color limitation encourages simple, compressible designs
Color palette structure: - Color 0: Background (usually transparent) - Color 1: Pattern/foreground (text color) - Color 2: Emphasis 1 (outline or shadow) - Color 3: Emphasis 2 (additional highlight)

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureCoding.RunLength
member.summary: Standard DVD subpicture encoding using run-length encoding (RLE) compression.

remarks.para: Run-length encoding is the primary compression method for DVD subpictures. It works by encoding consecutive pixels of the same color as a count followed by the color value, significantly reducing the data size for typical subtitle and menu graphics.

RLE encoding process: - Pixels are encoded in pairs (2 pixels = 1 byte) - Runs of identical pixel pairs are compressed - Special codes indicate line endings and field switches - Achieves compression ratios of 10:1 or better for typical subtitles

This format is mandatory for all DVD players and ensures universal compatibility. The RLE data is organized as: - Top field data (even lines for interlaced video) - Bottom field data (odd lines for interlaced video) - Display control commands (timing, palette, position)

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureCoding.Extended
member.summary: Extended subpicture coding format with additional capabilities beyond standard RLE.

remarks.para: Extended coding formats may include: - Enhanced compression algorithms - Support for more than 4 colors - Anti-aliased text rendering - Animation sequences for menu transitions - Advanced transparency effects

While the DVD specification allows for extended formats, they must maintain backward compatibility with standard players. Extended features are typically used in special editions or enhanced DVD formats while providing fallback to standard RLE for basic players.
Common extensions include: - HD-DVD and Blu-ray subtitle formats - Proprietary studio enhancements - PC-DVD additional features - Interactive subtitle formats

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureCoding.Other
member.summary: Other or proprietary subpicture coding format not covered by standard specifications.

remarks.para: This value indicates a non-standard encoding format that may be: - Vendor-specific implementations - Experimental or development formats - Region-specific variations - Future format reservations
Players encountering this format should: - Check for codec availability - Provide appropriate error handling - Fall back to standard formats if available - Inform users about compatibility issues
Use of non-standard formats may limit disc playability to specific players or regions, so this is rarely used in commercial releases.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureLangExt
member.summary: Specifies the language extension code for DVD subpicture streams, indicating the intended purpose and display characteristics of subtitles.

remarks.para: DVD-Video allows multiple subpicture streams per title, each serving different purposes beyond simple language translation. The language extension code provides additional context about how the subtitles should be used and displayed, enabling DVDs to offer various subtitle options for different audiences and viewing preferences.

This system allows a single DVD to include: - Multiple subtitle sizes for vision-impaired viewers - Simplified language for children or language learners - Closed captions with sound effect descriptions - Director or actor commentary as subtitles - Forced subtitles for foreign language dialogue in otherwise native-language content

The language extension works in conjunction with the primary language code (ISO 639-1) to fully describe each subpicture stream. For example, a DVD might have: - English (Normal) - Standard subtitles - English (CC) - Closed captions with [sound effects] - English (Big) - Large print for visually impaired - English (Children) - Simplified vocabulary - Spanish (Forced) - Only for English scenes with Spanish dialogue

Players use these codes to: - Automatically select appropriate subtitles based on user preferences - Display forced subtitles regardless of subtitle on/off setting - Offer meaningful choices in the subtitle selection menu - Apply appropriate formatting (size, position) for different subtitle types

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureLangExt.NotSpecified
member.summary: Language extension is not specified or unknown.
member.remarks: Used when the subpicture stream doesn't have a specific extension code assigned. Players should treat this as standard subtitles without special formatting or behavior.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureLangExt.CaptionNormal
member.summary: Normal caption subtitles with standard formatting.

remarks.para: Standard subtitles providing dialogue translation or transcription in normal-sized text. These are the most common subtitle type and are typically: - Positioned at the bottom of the screen - Using standard font size (approximately 5% of screen height) - White or yellow text with black outline/shadow - Displayed for foreign language films or for deaf/hard-of-hearing viewers
Caption subtitles generally only include spoken dialogue and may omit sound effects or speaker identification that would be included in closed captions.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureLangExt.CaptionBig
member.summary: Large-print caption subtitles for visually impaired viewers.

remarks.para: Enhanced subtitles with larger text size for improved readability: - Font size typically 150-200% of normal subtitles - May use high contrast colors (white on black background) - Simplified formatting to maximize legibility - Potentially reduced line length to accommodate larger text
These subtitles help viewers with: - Mild to moderate vision impairment - Viewing from greater distances - Small screen devices - Age-related vision changes

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureLangExt.CaptionChildren
member.summary: Simplified caption subtitles designed for children.

remarks.para: Child-friendly subtitles with adaptations for young readers: - Simplified vocabulary appropriate for reading level - Shorter sentences and phrases - May include reading aids (color coding for different speakers) - Potentially slower display timing for developing readers - Removal of complex idioms or cultural references
These subtitles support: - Early literacy development - Language learning for children - Family viewing with mixed age groups - Educational content consumption

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureLangExt.CCNormal
member.summary: Normal closed captions including dialogue and audio descriptions.

remarks.para: Comprehensive closed captions designed for deaf and hard-of-hearing viewers: - All dialogue with speaker identification when necessary - Sound effect descriptions [door slams], [thunder] - Music descriptions ♪ upbeat music ♪ - Tone indicators (sarcastically), (whispering) - Off-screen sounds and dialogue

Closed captions follow specific standards: - FCC guidelines in the United States - Ofcom standards in the United Kingdom - Similar accessibility regulations in other regions - Typically use specific formatting conventions for different audio elements

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureLangExt.CCBig
member.summary: Large-print closed captions for visually impaired viewers who also need audio descriptions.

remarks.para: Combines the comprehensive information of closed captions with enhanced visibility: - All closed caption content (dialogue, sounds, music) - Larger text size (150-200% of normal) - High contrast formatting - May use abbreviated sound descriptions to fit space constraints

Serves viewers who have both: - Hearing impairment or deafness - Visual impairment requiring larger text This dual accommodation is important for aging populations and certain medical conditions affecting multiple senses.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureLangExt.CCChildren
member.summary: Simplified closed captions appropriate for children, including audio descriptions.

remarks.para: Child-appropriate closed captions that maintain accessibility while being age-appropriate: - Simplified vocabulary for both dialogue and sound descriptions - Child-friendly descriptions of scary or complex sounds - Color coding or icons for different speakers - Filtered content (may omit profanity or mature themes) - Educational enhancements (vocabulary helpers)
Particularly useful for: - Children with hearing impairments - Language learning in educational settings - Noisy environments where audio isn't practical - Building reading skills alongside viewing

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureLangExt.Forced
member.summary: Forced subtitles displayed regardless of subtitle settings, typically for foreign language segments.

remarks.para: Forced subtitles appear automatically for specific scenes and cannot be turned off: - Foreign language dialogue in otherwise native-language films - Alien or fictional language translations - Sign language interpretation - On-screen text translations (signs, letters, computer screens) - Important text messages or emails shown on screen

Implementation notes: - Players must display these even when subtitles are "off" - Usually contains only subset of the film's content - Should not duplicate on-screen burned-in subtitles - May be empty for films without foreign language segments
Common examples: - Russian dialogue in English action films - Elvish in fantasy films - Text messages in thriller movies - News broadcasts in foreign languages

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureLangExt.DirectorCommentsNormal
member.summary: Director's commentary as subtitles with normal formatting.

remarks.para: Special subtitle track containing director or filmmaker commentary: - Behind-the-scenes information synchronized with specific scenes - Technical details about filming locations, special effects - Artistic choices and creative decisions - Anecdotes about cast and crew - References to deleted scenes or alternate versions

These subtitles are typically: - Displayed in addition to or instead of dialogue subtitles - Color-coded or specially formatted to distinguish from dialogue - Synchronized with specific visual elements being discussed - Used when audio commentary track isn't available or practical

Advantages over audio commentary: - Can be read without replacing the film's audio - Accessible to deaf/hard-of-hearing viewers - Available in multiple languages more easily - Can include hyperlinks or chapter references

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureLangExt.DirectorCommentsBig
member.summary: Director's commentary subtitles with large print formatting.

remarks.para: Large-format version of director commentary for improved readability: - Same content as normal director comments - Enlarged text for visually impaired viewers - May use condensed commentary to fit space constraints - High contrast formatting for better visibility
Allows visually impaired film enthusiasts to enjoy: - Behind-the-scenes insights - Technical filmmaking details - Director's artistic vision - Production anecdotes and trivia

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureLangExt.DirectorCommentsChildren
member.summary: Simplified director's commentary subtitles suitable for younger audiences.

remarks.para: Age-appropriate filmmaker commentary for family films: - Simplified technical explanations - Focus on fun facts and trivia - Behind-the-scenes stories about actors and effects - Educational content about filmmaking - Avoidance of complex industry terminology
Designed to: - Inspire young filmmakers - Provide educational content - Maintain child-appropriate language - Encourage interest in movie-making - Complement family viewing experiences
Often found on: - Animated films - Family adventure movies - Educational DVDs - Children's television series

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubpictureStream
member.summary: Represents a complete DVD subpicture stream with its attributes and playback state.

remarks.para: This class encapsulates all information about a single subpicture stream on a DVD, including its attributes (type, encoding, language) and current playback state. DVD subpicture streams are used to overlay graphics on top of the main video, most commonly for subtitles but also for other visual elements.

DVDs can contain up to 32 subpicture streams per title, allowing viewers to choose from multiple subtitle languages or special overlay features. Each stream can be independently enabled or disabled, and only one stream is typically active at a time (though some players support displaying multiple streams simultaneously).

The subpicture system is designed to be bandwidth-efficient, using only about 2-10% of the total disc bandwidth, while providing high-quality text and graphics overlays that can be perfectly synchronized with the video content.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubpictureStream.Attributes
member.summary: Gets or sets the detailed attributes of this subpicture stream.
member.value: A object containing information about the stream's content type, encoding format, language, and other characteristics.

remarks.para: The attributes define the fundamental properties of the subpicture stream: - Content type (language subtitles vs. other overlays) - Encoding format (typically RLE compression) - Language information (LCID and human-readable name) - Special extensions (closed captions, forced subtitles, etc.)

These attributes are read from the DVD's IFO (Information) files during disc initialization and remain constant throughout playback. They help the player software present appropriate options to users and handle the stream correctly.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubpictureStream.IsSubpictureStreamEnabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this subpicture stream is currently enabled for display.
member.value: true if the subpicture stream is active and its content will be rendered on top of the video; false if the stream is available but not currently displayed.

remarks.para: The enabled state of a subpicture stream can change during playback based on: - User selection from the DVD menu or player controls - Automatic selection based on language preferences - DVD navigation commands that force certain subtitles - Parental control settings that may block certain streams

When a stream is enabled, the DVD player decodes its RLE-compressed graphics and composites them onto the video frame. The timing information embedded in the subpicture data ensures perfect synchronization with dialogue or other video events.

Note that "forced" subtitles (marked in the stream's attributes) may display even when the user has disabled subtitles, typically for translating foreign language segments in otherwise native-language content.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubpictureStream.Language
member.summary: Gets or sets the language code associated with this subpicture stream.
member.value: An integer representing the language code. This may be an LCID (Windows Language Code Identifier) or another form of language identification used by the DVD authoring system.

remarks.para: This property provides a quick reference to the stream's language without accessing the full Attributes object. It's particularly useful for: - Building language selection menus - Automatic language matching based on system preferences - Sorting streams by language for user presentation

The language code should match the LanguageID in the Attributes property when the stream type is Language. For non-language streams (graphics overlays), this value may be 0 or have special meaning defined by the DVD authoring.
Common language codes include: - 1033: English (United States) - 1034: Spanish (Traditional) - 1036: French (France) - 1031: German (Germany) - 1040: Italian (Italy) - 1041: Japanese

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureType
member.summary: Specifies the type of content contained in a DVD subpicture stream.

remarks.para: DVD subpictures are overlay graphics that can be displayed on top of the main video content. They are commonly used for subtitles, but can also contain other types of graphical information such as karaoke lyrics, menu highlights, or director's commentary indicators.

The subpicture type helps DVD players and applications determine how to handle and present the subpicture content to users. Language-type subpictures typically contain subtitles or closed captions in various languages, while other types might contain graphical overlays for special features.

DVD subpictures use run-length encoding (RLE) compression and support up to 4 colors with transparency levels. Each subpicture can be positioned anywhere on the screen and can be shown or hidden based on user preferences or DVD navigation commands.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureType.NotSpecified
member.summary: The subpicture type is not specified or unknown.
member.remarks: This value indicates that the DVD authoring did not specify the type of content in the subpicture stream, or the type could not be determined. Applications should handle these streams as generic overlay content.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureType.Language
member.summary: The subpicture contains language-related content such as subtitles or captions.

remarks.para: Language-type subpictures are the most common type and typically contain: - Subtitles for foreign language dialogue - Closed captions for hearing-impaired viewers - Forced subtitles for non-native language segments in the main audio

When a subpicture is marked as Language type, the stream should have an associated language code (LCID) that identifies the language of the text content. This allows DVD players to automatically select appropriate subtitles based on user language preferences.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDSubPictureType.Other
member.summary: The subpicture contains non-language content such as graphics or special overlays.

remarks.para: Other-type subpictures may contain various types of graphical content: - Director's commentary indicators - Scene selection highlights - Easter egg indicators - Graphical overlays for special features - Karaoke timing graphics (though karaoke subtitles are usually Language type) - Production notes or trivia overlays
These subpictures are typically not associated with a specific language and may be displayed regardless of the user's language settings, depending on the DVD's programming.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleAppMode
member.summary: Specifies the application mode or special features enabled for a DVD title.

remarks.para: DVD titles can be authored with special application modes that enable enhanced interactive features beyond standard video playback. The most common special mode is karaoke, which provides synchronized lyrics display and often includes features for vocal removal or scoring.
