The application mode affects how the DVD player processes and presents the content: - Audio channel mixing for karaoke (removing or lowering vocal tracks) - Special subpicture handling for synchronized lyrics - Interactive features like scoring or pitch detection - Modified menu systems optimized for the application type

Understanding the application mode is important for DVD players to: - Enable appropriate audio processing features - Display correct UI elements for the mode - Handle special navigation commands - Process mode-specific data tracks

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleAppMode.NotSpecified
member.summary: The title has no special application mode specified.

remarks.para: This is the default mode for standard DVD video titles. The title contains regular video content without any special interactive features or processing requirements. Most commercial movies and TV shows use this mode.

In NotSpecified mode: - Standard audio tracks play without modification - Subpictures display as normal subtitles or overlays - No special UI elements are required - Standard DVD navigation commands apply

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleAppMode.Karaoke
member.summary: The title is authored for karaoke applications with special audio and subtitle features.

remarks.para: Karaoke mode indicates that the DVD title contains karaoke content with special features: - Multiple audio channels (typically 5: L, R, melody, vocal 1, vocal 2) - Synchronized lyrics displayed through subpicture streams - Channel mixing capabilities to remove or adjust vocals - Optional scoring and pitch detection features

DVD karaoke titles often include: - Multiplex audio allowing users to toggle lead vocals on/off - Guide melodies on separate channels - Colored or highlighted lyrics synchronized to the music - Multiple language versions of the same songs - Special effects like echo or reverb settings

Players detecting karaoke mode should: - Enable audio channel mixing controls - Ensure proper subpicture timing for lyrics - Display karaoke-specific UI elements - Support special karaoke navigation features

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleAppMode.Other
member.summary: The title uses a special application mode other than karaoke.

remarks.para: Other application modes may include: - Educational content with interactive quizzes - Gaming features with DVD-based games - Special audio modes (like DVD-Audio compatibility) - Custom interactive applications - Specialized content like music video compilations with enhanced features

When Other mode is specified, the DVD player should: - Check for additional metadata about the specific application type - Be prepared to handle non-standard navigation commands - Support any special features indicated in the disc's capability flags - Potentially load custom UI elements or processing modules
The specific behavior for Other mode depends on additional information provided in the DVD's IFO files and may require player-specific support for proprietary features.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleAttributes
member.summary: Represents the complete set of attributes and stream information for a DVD title.

remarks.para: A DVD title is a complete program unit on a DVD, such as a movie, TV episode, or special feature. Each title contains its own set of video, audio, and subpicture streams, along with metadata that describes how these streams should be presented and what special features are available.

DVD structure hierarchy: - Disc → Titles → Chapters → Cells - Each title can have up to 99 chapters - Each title can contain up to 8 audio streams - Each title can contain up to 32 subpicture streams - Titles can have different aspect ratios, encoding formats, and features

Title attributes are crucial for: - Determining playback capabilities and requirements - Building stream selection menus - Enabling special features like karaoke or multi-angle viewing - Applying appropriate audio/video processing - Enforcing parental controls and region restrictions

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleAttributes.AppMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the application mode that indicates special features or processing requirements for this title.
member.value: A value indicating whether the title has special features like karaoke mode enabled, or is a standard video title.

remarks.para: The application mode fundamentally changes how the DVD player should handle the title: - NotSpecified: Standard movie/video playback with normal controls - Karaoke: Enables vocal channel mixing, lyrics display, and possibly scoring features - Other: Custom application modes that may require special player support

When karaoke mode is active, the player should: - Enable audio channel selection/mixing controls - Ensure precise subpicture timing for lyrics synchronization - Potentially activate microphone input and echo effects - Display karaoke-specific UI elements like pitch indicators

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleAttributes.VideoAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets the video stream attributes for this title.
member.value: A object containing detailed information about the video encoding, resolution, aspect ratio, and other video characteristics.

remarks.para: The video attributes define the primary visual presentation of the title: - Video compression format (MPEG-1 or MPEG-2) - Resolution (720x480 NTSC, 720x576 PAL, etc.) - Aspect ratio (4:3, 16:9 letterbox, 16:9 pan-scan) - Frame rate (29.97 fps NTSC, 25 fps PAL) - Bit rate and quality settings
DVDs support multiple video angles for the same title, allowing viewers to switch between different camera angles during playback. The video attributes apply to all angles within the title.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleAttributes.NumberOfAudioStreams
member.summary: Gets or sets the total number of audio streams available in this title.
member.value: An integer between 0 and 8 indicating how many audio streams are present. Most commercial DVDs include 1-6 audio streams for different languages and formats.

remarks.para: Multiple audio streams allow DVDs to provide: - Multiple language dubs of the same content - Different audio formats (Dolby Digital, DTS, PCM) - Commentary tracks from directors or actors - Descriptive audio for visually impaired viewers - Different mix versions (stereo, 5.1 surround, etc.)
The number of streams determines how many entries will be valid in the AudioAttributes array. Players should only present available streams to users for selection.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleAttributes.AudioAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets an array containing detailed attributes for each audio stream in the title.
member.value: An array of objects, with one entry for each available audio stream. The array size should match NumberOfAudioStreams.

remarks.para: Each audio stream can have different characteristics: - Audio format (AC3, DTS, LPCM, MPEG) - Number of channels (mono, stereo, 5.1, 7.1) - Sample rate and bit depth - Language code and description - Special attributes (director's commentary, descriptive audio)

Players use these attributes to: - Display audio options in selection menus - Automatically select streams based on user language preferences - Configure audio decoders appropriately - Apply necessary downmixing for stereo output - Handle special features like karaoke channel separation

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleAttributes.MultichannelAudioAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets extended information about multichannel audio capabilities for each stream.
member.value: An array of objects providing additional details about surround sound configurations and special audio features.

remarks.para: Multichannel attributes provide detailed information about: - Specific channel assignments (L, R, C, LFE, LS, RS) - Karaoke channel configurations (melody, vocal guides) - Downmix coefficients for stereo playback - Special processing flags (dialog normalization, dynamic range)

This information is particularly important for: - Home theater systems with full surround capabilities - Karaoke applications requiring channel separation - Ensuring proper audio presentation on various playback systems - Maintaining artistic intent across different speaker configurations

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleAttributes.NumberOfSubpictureStreams
member.summary: Gets or sets the total number of subpicture streams available in this title.
member.value: An integer between 0 and 32 indicating how many subpicture streams are present. Commercial DVDs typically include 2-10 subtitle streams for different languages.

remarks.para: The high number of possible subpicture streams allows DVDs to support: - Subtitles in many languages (often 10-20 for international releases) - Both subtitles and closed captions for the same language - Special subtitle tracks (forced subs, commentary, trivia) - Different subtitle styles (standard vs. hearing impaired) - Region-specific subtitle variations
Not all 32 possible streams are typically used; the actual number of available streams is indicated by this property.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleAttributes.SubpictureAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets an array containing detailed attributes for each subpicture stream in the title.
member.value: An array of objects, with one entry for each available subpicture stream. The array size should match NumberOfSubpictureStreams.

remarks.para: Subpicture attributes describe each overlay stream: - Content type (language subtitles vs. graphics) - Language code and human-readable description - Special flags (forced display, closed captions) - Encoding format (typically 2-bit RLE) - Associated audio stream for synchronization

Players use these attributes to: - Build subtitle selection menus with proper language names - Automatically enable subtitles based on user preferences - Handle forced subtitles that display regardless of settings - Properly decode and display the subpicture graphics - Synchronize subtitle timing with audio and video

Special considerations: - Some subpictures may be empty (no actual content) but still present - Forced subtitles should display even when subtitles are disabled - Closed caption streams may include additional formatting information - Karaoke titles may use subpictures for synchronized lyrics

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleInfo
member.summary: Represents comprehensive information about a DVD title, including its attributes, menu structure, chapters, and parental controls.

remarks.para: A DVD title is a major content unit on a DVD disc, typically representing a movie, episode, or other complete program. Each title contains its own set of chapters, audio tracks, subtitle tracks, and menu systems. DVDs can contain multiple titles - for example, a disc might have the main feature as Title 1, deleted scenes as Title 2, and behind-the-scenes content as Title 3.

item.description: Title: Complete program unit (movie, episode, etc.)
Chapter: Subdivision of a title for navigation (scenes)
Cell: Smallest playback unit containing video/audio data
VOBU: Video Object Unit - group of GOPs (Group of Pictures)

remarks.para:
Title Attributes:
Each title has specific attributes defining its video format, audio options, subtitle availability, and playback restrictions. These attributes help players determine compatibility and available features.

Menu System:
DVD titles often include interactive menus for navigation, language selection, and special features. The menu attributes define the video format and capabilities of these interactive elements.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleInfo.MainAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets the main attributes of the DVD title, including video, audio, and subtitle stream information.
member.value: A object containing comprehensive information about all available streams and their properties within this title.
member.remarks: Main attributes define the actual content streams available during playback, including: video format, multiple audio tracks (different languages, commentary), subtitle options, and angle information for multi-angle scenes.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleInfo.MenuAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets the attributes of the DVD menu system associated with this title.
member.value: A object describing the menu's video format and available language options, or null if the title has no associated menu.
member.remarks:
DVD menus provide interactive navigation and can include:
Main menu: Title selection, setup options
Chapter menu: Scene selection within the title
Audio menu: Language and commentary track selection
Subtitle menu: Subtitle language selection
Special features menu: Bonus content navigation
Menu attributes define the video format used for these interactive screens, which may differ from the main content's video format.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleInfo.NumberOfChapters
member.summary: Gets or sets the total number of chapters (scenes) in this DVD title.
member.value: The chapter count, typically ranging from 1 to 99. Most feature films have 10-30 chapters.

remarks.para: Chapters provide convenient navigation points within a title, similar to bookmarks. They allow viewers to jump directly to specific scenes or segments. Chapter points are typically placed at natural breaks in the content, such as:

item.description: Scene changes in movies
Commercial breaks in TV episodes
Song boundaries in concerts
Topic changes in documentaries

remarks.para: The DVD specification allows up to 99 chapters per title. Chapter information is stored in the Program Chain (PGC) structure of the DVD's IFO files.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleInfo.ParentalLevel
member.summary: Gets or sets the parental control levels supported by this DVD title.
member.value: A flags enumeration indicating which parental levels can access this title. Multiple levels can be set, allowing flexible parental control configurations.

remarks.para: DVD parental controls allow content to be restricted based on viewer age or maturity level. The system uses 8 levels, where Level 1 is the most restrictive (suitable for all ages) and Level 8 is the least restrictive (adult content).

item.description: Level 1: General audiences, all ages
Level 3: Parental guidance suggested
Level 4: PG-13 equivalent
Level 6: Restricted, under 17 requires parent
Level 8: Adults only

remarks.para: When multiple levels are flagged, it indicates the title can be played at any of those levels, potentially with different content (e.g., edited versions for lower levels).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleInfo.TimeCodeFlags
member.summary: Gets or sets the time code flags that indicate special timing or playback characteristics of the title.
member.value: A 64-bit value containing various timing-related flags. The specific bit meanings are defined by the DVD specification and may include drop-frame indicators, film/video source flags, and synchronization markers.

remarks.para: Time code flags provide additional timing metadata that helps ensure proper playback, especially when dealing with mixed frame rates or converted content. Common flags include:

item.description: Drop-frame timecode indicator (for NTSC 29.97 fps content)
Film source flag (24 fps content with 3:2 pulldown)
Progressive/interlaced indicators
Time base references for synchronization

remarks.para: These flags are particularly important for professional video editing and authoring applications that need to maintain frame-accurate timing.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleInfoParentalLevel.None
member.summary: No parental level is set. The title has no parental control restrictions or the parental control system is not used.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleInfoParentalLevel.Level8
member.summary: Parental Level 8 - Adult content with no restrictions. Typically corresponds to NC-17 or X-rated content.
member.remarks: This is the least restrictive level, intended for adult audiences only. Content may include explicit violence, sexual content, or other material inappropriate for minors.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleInfoParentalLevel.Level7
member.summary: Parental Level 7 - Mature adult content. Often used for unrated or adult-oriented material.
member.remarks: Content at this level is intended for mature adults and may contain strong violence, sexual situations, or intense themes not suitable for younger viewers.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleInfoParentalLevel.Level6
member.summary: Parental Level 6 - Restricted content. Typically corresponds to R-rated material (17+ or with parent).
member.remarks: This level usually indicates content with adult themes, strong language, violence, or sexual content that requires mature judgment to view.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleInfoParentalLevel.Level5
member.summary: Parental Level 5 - Parents strongly cautioned. Material may be inappropriate for children under 17.
member.remarks: Content at this level contains material that many parents would find unsuitable for younger teenagers, including intense violence, sexual content, or drug use.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleInfoParentalLevel.Level4
member.summary: Parental Level 4 - Parental guidance for children under 13. Typically corresponds to PG-13 rated content.
member.remarks: This level indicates content that may be inappropriate for children under 13, including mild violence, brief strong language, or suggestive themes.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleInfoParentalLevel.Level3
member.summary: Parental Level 3 - Parental guidance suggested. Typically corresponds to PG-rated content.
member.remarks: Content at this level may contain material that parents might find unsuitable for young children, including mild violence, brief mild language, or scary scenes.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleInfoParentalLevel.Level2
member.summary: Parental Level 2 - General audiences with minimal parental concern. Suitable for most children.
member.remarks: This level indicates content that is generally suitable for children but may contain very mild themes or situations that very young children might find confusing.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDTitleInfoParentalLevel.Level1
member.summary: Parental Level 1 - General audiences, all ages. Typically corresponds to G-rated content.
member.remarks: This is the most restrictive level, indicating content suitable for all ages including young children. Content is free from violence, strong language, and adult themes.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.None
member.summary: No operations are prohibited. All user operations are allowed.
member.remarks: This value indicates complete freedom of navigation and control. It's typically used during normal movie playback where viewers have full control over all DVD features.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.PlayTitleOrAtTime
member.summary: Prohibits jumping to a specific title or time position using time search functionality.
member.remarks: When set, prevents users from using "Go to time" features or direct title selection by number. This is often used to force sequential viewing of content.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.PlayChapter
member.summary: Prohibits direct chapter selection or jumping to a specific chapter by number.
member.remarks: Prevents users from using chapter selection menus or entering chapter numbers directly. Commonly used during credits or copyright notices to prevent skipping.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.PlayTitle
member.summary: Prohibits playing a different title from the current one.
member.remarks: When set, users cannot switch to other titles on the disc. This ensures viewers complete the current title before accessing other content like special features.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.Stop
member.summary: Prohibits the stop operation, forcing playback to continue.
member.remarks: This is rarely used as it can trap users in playback. When set, the stop button is disabled and users must wait for playback to complete or use other allowed navigation.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.ReturnFromSubMenu
member.summary: Prohibits returning from a submenu to the parent menu using the return/back function.
member.remarks: Forces users to make a selection in the current submenu rather than backing out. Often used in configuration menus where a selection is required.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.PlayChapterOrAtTime
member.summary: Prohibits playing from a specific chapter or time position within the current title.
member.remarks: Similar to PlayTitleOrAtTime but restricted to navigation within the current title. Prevents time-based seeking while allowing other forms of navigation.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.PlayPrevOrReplay_Chapter
member.summary: Prohibits playing the previous chapter or replaying the current chapter from the beginning.
member.remarks: When set, the "Previous Chapter" button is disabled. This prevents users from navigating backward through chapters or restarting the current chapter.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.PlayNextChapter
member.summary: Prohibits skipping to the next chapter using the "Next Chapter" function.
member.remarks: Commonly used during opening credits, copyright notices, or advertisements to prevent users from skipping ahead. One of the most frequently encountered UOPs.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.PlayForwards
member.summary: Prohibits fast forward scanning through the content.
member.remarks: Disables all forward scanning speeds (2x, 4x, 8x, etc.). Often used during copyright warnings and studio logos to ensure they are viewed at normal speed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.PlayBackwards
member.summary: Prohibits reverse scanning or playing backward through the content.
member.remarks: Disables all reverse scanning speeds. Less commonly used than forward prohibition, but may be set during menus or special features where reverse playback doesn't make sense.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.ShowMenuTitle
member.summary: Prohibits displaying the title menu (main menu) of the DVD.
member.remarks: When set, users cannot access the main DVD menu using the "Menu" or "Title" button. This forces viewers to remain in the current playback mode without menu access.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.ShowMenuRoot
member.summary: Prohibits displaying the root menu (top menu) of the current title.
member.remarks: The root menu is typically the first menu shown when entering a title's menu system. Prohibiting this prevents users from accessing the top-level navigation of the current title.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.ShowMenuSubPic
member.summary: Prohibits displaying the subpicture (subtitle) selection menu.
member.remarks: Prevents users from accessing subtitle options during playback. This might be used during scenes where subtitle changes could interfere with burned-in text or graphics.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.ShowMenuAudio
member.summary: Prohibits displaying the audio stream selection menu.
member.remarks: Prevents users from changing audio tracks (language, commentary) during playback. May be used during scenes with specialized audio or when audio switching could cause issues.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.ShowMenuAngle
member.summary: Prohibits displaying the angle selection menu for multi-angle scenes.
member.remarks: Prevents access to angle selection menus. Typically set when not in a multi-angle scene or when angle changes would disrupt the viewing experience.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.ShowMenuChapter
member.summary: Prohibits displaying the chapter selection menu (scene selection).
member.remarks: Prevents users from accessing chapter/scene selection menus. Often used to ensure linear viewing of content or during special features without chapter divisions.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.Resume
member.summary: Prohibits resuming playback from a saved position after entering a menu.
member.remarks: When set, the "Resume" function is disabled. Users must restart playback from the beginning or make a new selection rather than continuing from where they left off.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.SelectOrActivateButton
member.summary: Prohibits selecting or activating buttons in interactive menus.
member.remarks: This effectively freezes menu interaction, preventing users from making selections. Rarely used, as it can leave users stuck. May be used during menu transitions.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.StillOff
member.summary: Prohibits exiting from a still frame (pause) condition.
member.remarks: When set during a still frame, users cannot resume playback. The still frame must timeout automatically or be released by the DVD navigation programming.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.PauseOn
member.summary: Prohibits pausing the playback.
member.remarks: Disables the pause function, forcing continuous playback. May be used during time-critical content or interactive features that shouldn't be interrupted.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.SelectAudioStream
member.summary: Prohibits changing the audio stream using the audio button or direct selection.
member.remarks: Prevents switching between different audio tracks (languages, commentary tracks) during playback. Unlike ShowMenuAudio, this blocks direct audio switching without menu access.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.SelectSubPicStream
member.summary: Prohibits changing the subpicture (subtitle) stream using the subtitle button.
member.remarks: Prevents direct subtitle track switching during playback. Users cannot cycle through available subtitle languages or turn subtitles on/off without menu access.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.SelectAngle
member.summary: Prohibits changing the viewing angle during multi-angle scenes.
member.remarks: Disables the angle button during multi-angle sequences. Set when angle changes are not available or would disrupt the intended viewing experience.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.SelectKaraokeAudioPresentationMode
member.summary: Prohibits changing karaoke audio presentation modes.
member.remarks: Specific to karaoke DVDs, this prevents users from switching between different karaoke modes (guide melody on/off, vocal assistance levels, etc.).

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDValidUOPFlag.SelectVideoModePreference
member.summary: Prohibits changing video presentation mode preferences.
member.remarks: Prevents users from changing aspect ratio preferences, pan-scan/letterbox modes, or other video presentation settings during playback.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoAttributes.PanscanPermitted
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the picture can be shown as pan-scan if the display aspect ratio is 4 x 3.
member.value: true if pan-scan display is permitted; otherwise, false.

remarks.para: Pan-scan is a method of adjusting widescreen content for 4:3 displays by cropping the sides and following the action. A human operator determines which portion of the widescreen frame to show at each moment, ensuring important action remains visible.

When this flag is true, 4:3 TV owners can choose to view the content in pan-scan mode, filling their entire screen but losing some picture information on the sides. This was important during the transition from 4:3 to 16:9 displays.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoAttributes.LetterboxPermitted
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the picture can be shown as letterbox if the display aspect ratio is 4 x 3.
member.value: true if letterbox display is permitted; otherwise, false.

remarks.para: Letterboxing preserves the original widescreen aspect ratio by adding black bars above and below the picture on 4:3 displays. This ensures viewers see the complete image as the director intended, though at a smaller size.

When this flag is true, 4:3 TV owners can choose to view widescreen content with letterbox bars, seeing the full width of the original image. This is often preferred by film enthusiasts who want to see the complete composition.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoAttributes.AspectRatio
member.summary: Gets or sets the display aspect ratio (W:H) of the video content.
member.value: A tuple where Item1 is the width component and Item2 is the height component of the ratio. Common values are (4,3) for standard content and (16,9) for widescreen.

remarks.para: The aspect ratio defines the proportional relationship between the video's width and height as it should appear on screen. This is the Display Aspect Ratio (DAR), which may differ from the Storage Aspect Ratio (SAR) due to non-square pixels.

Standard DVD aspect ratios:
4:3 (1.33:1) - Traditional TV format
16:9 (1.78:1) - Widescreen TV format
Note: Theatrical films may be letterboxed within these formats to preserve ratios like 2.35:1 or 1.85:1.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoAttributes.FrameRate
member.summary: Gets or sets the frame rate in frames per second.
member.value: The frame rate as an integer. Common values include 23 (film), 25 (PAL), and 29 (NTSC). Note that actual rates may be fractional (e.g., 23.976, 29.97).

remarks.para:
DVD supports several standard frame rates:
23/24 fps - Film content (actually 23.976 fps for NTSC)
25 fps - PAL video standard
29/30 fps - NTSC video standard (actually 29.97 fps)
Film content (24 fps) on NTSC DVDs uses 3:2 pulldown to convert to 29.97 fps. The IsFilmMode flag indicates when this conversion is present.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoAttributes.FrameHeight
member.summary: Gets or sets the frame height in lines (rows of pixels).
member.value: The number of horizontal lines in the video frame. Standard values are 480 for NTSC and 576 for PAL, though this includes non-visible overscan areas.

remarks.para:
This represents the total number of scan lines, including:
Active video lines (visible picture)
Vertical blanking interval (VBI)
Overscan areas (typically not displayed)
The actual visible resolution is typically specified by SourceResolutionY, while FrameHeight includes the full transmitted signal.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoAttributes.Compression
member.summary: Gets or sets the video compression format used for encoding the video stream.
member.value: The compression type, typically MPEG-2 for standard DVDs or MPEG-1 for Video CDs and low-quality content.

remarks.para:
DVD primarily uses MPEG-2 compression, which provides:
Variable bitrate (VBR) encoding for efficient space usage
Support for interlaced and progressive video
B-frames for better compression efficiency
Bitrates from 1-9.8 Mbps (average 4-8 Mbps for movies)
MPEG-1 is supported for compatibility but offers lower quality and is typically used only for bonus content or Video CD compatibility modes.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoAttributes.Line21Field1InGOP
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether there is user data in line 21, field 1 of the video signal.
member.value: true if Line 21 Field 1 contains data; otherwise, false.

remarks.para: Line 21 is part of the vertical blanking interval (VBI) in NTSC video and is used to carry closed caption data for the hearing impaired. Field 1 typically contains the primary caption channel (CC1/CC2).
This data is encoded in the Group of Pictures (GOP) header in the MPEG stream, allowing closed captions to be synchronized with the video content.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoAttributes.Line21Field2InGOP
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether there is user data in line 21, field 2 of the video signal.
member.value: true if Line 21 Field 2 contains data; otherwise, false.

remarks.para: Field 2 of Line 21 typically contains secondary caption channels (CC3/CC4) or additional data services. This allows DVDs to provide multiple caption options, such as different languages or descriptive captions for the visually impaired.
Both fields together can provide up to 4 different caption channels, enabling rich accessibility features for diverse audiences.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoAttributes.SourceResolutionX
member.summary: Gets or sets the horizontal source resolution in pixels.
member.value: The width in pixels. DVD supports specific values: 352, 704, or 720 pixels.

remarks.para:
DVD horizontal resolutions and their typical uses:
720 pixels - Full D1 resolution, highest quality, most common
704 pixels - Cropped D1, removes analog blanking areas
352 pixels - Half D1, used for long-play modes or bonus content

The 720-pixel format includes pixels for analog blanking compatibility, while 704 pixels represents the active picture area. 352 pixels provides exactly half the horizontal resolution for reduced bitrate requirements.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoAttributes.SourceResolutionY
member.summary: Gets or sets the vertical source resolution in pixels (lines).
member.value: The height in pixels. Values depend on the video system: NTSC supports 240 or 480 lines, PAL supports 288 or 576 lines.

remarks.para:
DVD vertical resolutions by system:
NTSC:
- 480 lines: Full resolution (interlaced or progressive)
- 240 lines: Half resolution (SIF - Source Input Format)
PAL:
- 576 lines: Full resolution
- 288 lines: Half resolution (SIF)
Half-resolution formats are primarily used for Video CD compatibility or extended play modes where reduced quality is acceptable.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoAttributes.IsSourceLetterboxed
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the source video is pre-letterboxed within the encoded frame.
member.value: true if the video contains letterbox bars as part of the encoded image; otherwise, false.

remarks.para: When true, the video has been letterboxed at the source, meaning black bars are encoded as part of the video image rather than added by the player. This affects how subtitles and menu overlays are positioned:

item.description: Subtitles must be placed within the active picture area
Menu highlights are constrained to the visible image
The player cannot remove the letterbox bars

remarks.para: Pre-letterboxing was sometimes used for films with extreme aspect ratios (2.35:1) to ensure consistent presentation, but it wastes encoding bandwidth on black pixels.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoAttributes.IsFilmMode
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the content originated from film (24/25 fps) or video cameras.
member.value: true for film-originated content; false for video camera content. For 625/50 Hz (PAL) systems specifically, this indicates film mode vs. camera mode.

remarks.para: This flag helps video processors optimize playback:

item.description:
Film Mode (true):
- Content shot at 24 fps (cinema) or 25 fps (PAL film)
- Progressive frames (not interlaced)
- May use 3:2 pulldown for NTSC (24→29.97 fps)
- Can be deinterlaced more effectively

Camera/Video Mode (false):
- Content shot at video frame rates
- Typically interlaced (50i or 59.94i)
- Native video timing, no pulldown

remarks.para: Modern displays use this information to apply appropriate deinterlacing algorithms and motion processing, resulting in smoother playback of film content.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoStream.AnglesAvailable
member.summary: Gets or sets the total number of camera angles available in the current multi-angle scene.
member.value: The number of available angles, ranging from 1 (single angle) to 9 (maximum allowed by DVD specification). A value of 1 indicates standard single-angle content.

remarks.para:
When AnglesAvailable is greater than 1, the DVD player should:
Display an angle indicator icon on screen
Enable angle switching controls (unless prohibited by UOP)
Buffer multiple angle streams for seamless switching
Maintain synchronization across all angles

The DVD specification limits multi-angle scenes to 9 simultaneous angles due to data rate and seek time constraints. Each angle must be encoded at a lower bitrate to fit within the maximum combined data rate of 10.08 Mbps.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoStream.CurrentAngle
member.summary: Gets or sets the currently selected camera angle being displayed.
member.value: The current angle number, ranging from 1 to AnglesAvailable. Angle 1 is typically the default or primary camera angle.

remarks.para:
The current angle represents which video stream is being decoded and displayed from the available angles. Users can switch between angles using:
Remote control angle button
On-screen menu selection
Player application controls

Angle numbering conventions:
Angle 1: Primary/default view (often wide shot)
Angle 2+: Alternative views (close-ups, different positions)
Last angle: Sometimes used for special content (director's view)
The player remembers angle selection within a multi-angle scene but typically resets to Angle 1 when entering a new multi-angle block.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoStreamCompression
member.summary: Specifies the video compression format used for encoding DVD video streams.

remarks.para: DVD video compression standards define how video data is encoded and stored on the disc. The DVD-Video specification primarily uses MPEG-2 compression, though MPEG-1 is supported for backward compatibility with Video CD and for certain low-bitrate applications.

item.description:
- Primary DVD-Video codec
- Supports up to 720×576 (PAL) or 720×480 (NTSC)
- Variable bitrate: 1-9.8 Mbps
- Supports interlaced and progressive video
- I, P, and B frame types for efficient compression
- Used for main features and high-quality content

- Legacy format, Video CD compatible
- Maximum 352×288 (PAL) or 352×240 (NTSC)
- Constant bitrate: typically 1.15 Mbps
- Progressive scan only
- Lower quality but smaller file sizes
- Used for long-play content or bonus features
Profiles: Main Profile @ Main Level (MP@ML) for standard DVDs
Chroma Format: 4:2:0 color subsampling
GOP Structure: Typically 12-15 frames (IBBPBBPBBPBB)
Aspect Ratios: Supports both 4:3 and 16:9 with proper flagging
Audio Sync: Maintains synchronization with multiple audio streams

remarks.para:
Quality Considerations:
MPEG-2 on DVD typically allocates 4-8 Mbps for video, with the remaining bandwidth used for audio (up to 6.144 Mbps) and subpictures (up to 3.36 Mbps). The total maximum bitrate for all streams combined is 10.08 Mbps, limited by the 1× DVD drive speed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoStreamCompression.Other
member.summary: Other or unspecified compression format not defined in the DVD-Video specification.
member.remarks: This value indicates a non-standard compression format or that the compression type could not be determined. Standard DVD players may not support such content.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoStreamCompression.MPEG1
member.summary: MPEG-1 video compression (ISO/IEC 11172-2), primarily used for Video CD compatibility.

remarks.para:
MPEG-1 characteristics on DVD:
Lower resolution: 352×288 (PAL) or 352×240 (NTSC)
Constant bitrate: typically 1.15 Mbps
Progressive scan only (no interlacing)
Simpler compression algorithm than MPEG-2
Compatible with Video CD players
MPEG-1 is included in the DVD specification for backward compatibility and is sometimes used for bonus content where longer duration is more important than video quality.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaInfo.DVDVideoStreamCompression.MPEG2
member.summary: MPEG-2 video compression (ISO/IEC 13818-2), the primary compression standard for DVD-Video.

remarks.para:
MPEG-2 is the standard video codec for DVD-Video, offering:
Full D1 resolution: up to 720×576 (PAL) or 720×480 (NTSC)
Variable bitrate (VBR): 1-9.8 Mbps for optimal quality/size balance
Support for both interlaced and progressive content
Advanced motion compensation and prediction
B-frames for better compression efficiency
Closed GOP structure for better seeking and editing

MPEG-2 Main Profile @ Main Level (MP@ML) is used for standard DVDs, providing excellent quality for home theater viewing while fitting full-length movies on a single-layer (4.7 GB) or dual-layer (8.5 GB) disc.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureSource
member.summary: Represents an audio capture source configuration for audio recording and preview operations.
member.remarks: This class encapsulates all settings required to configure an audio capture device, including device selection, format configuration, input line selection, and custom source filters. It supports both physical audio devices and custom audio source implementations through the interface.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureSource.Name
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of the audio capture device to use.
member.value: The friendly name of the audio capture device as reported by the system. An empty string indicates no device is selected.
member.remarks: This should match one of the device names returned by the device enumeration API. If multiple devices have the same name, use the property to distinguish between them.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureSource.SourceFilter
member.summary: Gets or sets a custom audio source filter implementation.
member.value: An instance of a class implementing , or null to use a physical audio device instead.
member.remarks: This property allows you to provide custom audio data programmatically instead of capturing from a physical device. Implement the interface in your class to create a custom audio source. When this property is set, the property is ignored.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureSource.MasterDevice
member.summary: Gets or sets the master device name for audio synchronization.
member.value: The name of the master device used for synchronization, or null if not used.

remarks.para: This is an advanced property used for synchronizing audio capture with another device, typically a video capture device. The audio capture will be synchronized to the timing of the master device.
Warning: This property should only be used if you fully understand audio/video synchronization. Incorrect use can result in audio/video sync issues.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureSource.MasterDevice_Format
member.summary: Gets or sets the format of the master device used for synchronization.
member.value: The format string of the master device, or null if not applicable.
member.remarks: This property should be set when is specified. It defines the format that the master device is using, which affects how synchronization is performed.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureSource.Format
member.summary: Gets or sets the audio format to use for recording and preview.
member.value: A format string describing the audio format (e.g., "44100 Hz, 16-bit, Stereo"). An empty string indicates that the format should be automatically selected.

remarks.para: The format string must match one of the formats supported by the selected audio capture device. You can get the list of supported formats from .
If is true, this property is ignored and the best available format is automatically selected.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureSource.Format_UseBest
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the best available audio format should be automatically selected.
member.value: true to automatically select the best format; false to use the format specified in the property.
member.remarks: When set to true, the system will automatically choose the highest quality format supported by the device, typically preferring formats like 44100 Hz, 16-bit, Stereo when available. This is the recommended setting for most applications.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureSource.Line
member.summary: Gets or sets the audio input line to use for recording and preview.
member.value: The name of the input line (e.g., "Microphone", "Line In", "CD Audio"). An empty string indicates the default line should be used.

remarks.para: The available input lines depend on the selected audio capture device. You can get the list of available lines from .
Not all audio devices support multiple input lines. If the device doesn't support line selection, this property is ignored.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureSource.CustomLatency
member.summary: Gets or sets the custom audio latency in milliseconds.
member.value: The desired audio latency in milliseconds. A value of 0 uses the device default.

remarks.para: This property allows fine-tuning of audio latency for specific scenarios. Lower values reduce delay but may increase CPU usage and the risk of audio dropouts. Higher values provide more stable capture but increase the delay.
Note: Not all audio capture devices support custom latency settings. If unsupported, this value is ignored.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureSource.Path
member.summary: Gets or sets the unique device path for the audio capture device.
member.value: The system-specific device path (e.g., DirectShow moniker string on Windows), or null to select by name only.

remarks.para: This property is optional and primarily used when multiple devices have the same display name. The device path uniquely identifies a specific device instance.
On Windows, this is typically a DirectShow moniker string. You can obtain the device path using the device enumeration API or from .

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with the specified device name.
member.param: The name of the audio capture device to use.

remarks.para: This constructor automatically attempts to detect the preferred audio format for the specified device. If a format with 44100 Hz, 16-bit, 2 channels is available, it will be selected. Otherwise, is set to true.
The constructor temporarily creates a instance to query device capabilities, which is disposed after use.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureSource.#ctor(VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureDeviceInfo)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class using device information.
member.remarks: This constructor uses the device information to set the device name and automatically detect the preferred format. The format detection logic is the same as in the constructor.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureSource.DetectPreferredFormat(VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureDeviceInfo)
member.summary: Automatically detects and sets the preferred audio format based on device capabilities.
member.param: The device information containing the list of supported formats.
member.remarks: This method searches for a format that matches 44100 Hz sample rate, 16-bit depth, and 2 channels (stereo), which is considered the standard CD-quality audio format. If no such format is found, is set to true to let the system choose the best available format.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureSource.Finalize
member.summary: Finalizes an instance of the class.
member.remarks: The finalizer ensures that the is properly disposed if it hasn't been disposed already. This prevents resource leaks when custom audio source filters are used.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.AudioCaptureSource.ToString
member.summary: Returns a string representation of the audio capture source.
member.returns: The name of the audio capture device, or an empty string if no device is selected.
member.remarks: This method is useful for displaying the audio source in user interfaces or for debugging purposes.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAChannel
member.summary: Represents a Broadcast Driver Architecture (BDA) channel configuration for digital TV reception.

remarks.para: This class encapsulates all the parameters required to tune to a specific digital TV channel using BDA-compatible tuner devices. BDA is the Microsoft standard for digital TV reception on Windows, supporting various broadcast standards including DVB-T, DVB-S, DVB-C, and ATSC.
The properties in this class correspond to the MPEG-2 transport stream parameters and tuning information required by the BDA subsystem.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAChannel.ServId
member.summary: Gets or sets the service ID (SID) of the channel.
member.value: The MPEG-2 service identifier that uniquely identifies this service within a transport stream.
member.remarks: The service ID is a 16-bit value used in DVB and ATSC systems to identify a specific service (channel) within a multiplex. This value is found in the Service Description Table (SDT) or Virtual Channel Table (VCT).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAChannel.Name
member.summary: Gets or sets the display name of the channel.
member.value: The human-readable name of the channel as broadcast in the service information.
member.remarks: This is typically the channel name as displayed to users (e.g., "BBC One", "CNN", "Discovery"). The name is usually extracted from the Service Description Table (SDT) in DVB systems or the Virtual Channel Table (VCT) in ATSC systems.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAChannel.ServType
member.summary: Gets or sets the service type of the channel.
member.value: A byte value indicating the type of service as defined in the DVB/ATSC standards.
member.remarks:
Common service type values include:
0x01: Digital television service
0x02: Digital radio service
0x04: Teletext service
0x05: NVOD reference service
0x06: NVOD time-shifted service
0x0A: Advanced codec digital radio
0x16: Advanced codec SD digital television
0x19: Advanced codec HD digital television

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAChannel.FreeCAmode
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the channel is encrypted (Free CA mode).
member.value: true if the channel is encrypted and requires a Conditional Access (CA) system to decrypt; false if the channel is free-to-air (unencrypted).

remarks.para: Free CA (Conditional Access) mode indicates whether the service is scrambled. Encrypted channels require appropriate decryption hardware (CAM modules) or software and valid subscription rights to view.
This value is derived from the free_CA_mode flag in the service descriptor.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAChannel.VideoPid
member.summary: Gets or sets the video stream Packet Identifier (PID).
member.value: The 13-bit PID value identifying the video elementary stream in the transport stream. A value of -1 or 0x1FFF indicates no video stream.

remarks.para: The video PID identifies which packets in the MPEG-2 transport stream contain the video data for this service. This value is obtained from the Program Map Table (PMT) for the service.
Valid PID values range from 0x0010 to 0x1FFE. Special values include: 0x1FFF for null packets and -1 to indicate no video (radio services).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAChannel.AudioPid
member.summary: Gets or sets the audio stream Packet Identifier (PID).
member.value: The 13-bit PID value identifying the primary audio elementary stream in the transport stream. A value of -1 or 0x1FFF indicates no audio stream.

remarks.para: The audio PID identifies which packets in the MPEG-2 transport stream contain the audio data for this service. This typically refers to the primary or default audio stream. Additional audio streams (alternate languages, audio description) may be available but are not represented in this property.
This value is obtained from the Program Map Table (PMT) for the service.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAChannel.Modulation
member.summary: Gets or sets the modulation type used for this channel.
member.value: A value representing the modulation scheme. The interpretation depends on the broadcast standard (DVB-T/T2, DVB-S/S2, DVB-C, ATSC).

remarks.para: The modulation type determines how the digital signal is encoded onto the carrier wave. Common values include QPSK, QAM-16, QAM-64, QAM-256, 8VSB, etc. The specific values and their meanings depend on the tuner type and broadcast standard.
See for standard modulation type values.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAChannel.Frequency
member.summary: Gets or sets the tuning frequency for this channel.
member.value: The frequency in kHz (kilohertz) for terrestrial and cable systems, or in MHz (megahertz) for satellite systems.

remarks.para: The frequency value interpretation depends on the tuner type:

item.description: DVB-T/ATSC: Center frequency in kHz (e.g., 474000 for 474 MHz)
DVB-C: Center frequency in kHz
DVB-S/S2: Transponder frequency in MHz (e.g., 11954 for 11.954 GHz)

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAChannel.Polarisation
member.summary: Gets or sets the signal polarization for satellite reception.
member.value: The polarization type from the enumeration.

remarks.para: Polarization is primarily used for satellite (DVB-S/S2) reception where signals can be transmitted with different polarizations to allow frequency reuse. For terrestrial and cable systems, this property is typically not used.
Common polarizations are:

item.description: Linear Horizontal (H)
Linear Vertical (V)
Circular Left (L)
Circular Right (R)

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAChannel.SymbolRate
member.summary: Gets or sets the symbol rate for this channel.
member.value: The symbol rate in symbols per second (baud rate).

remarks.para: Symbol rate is primarily used for satellite (DVB-S/S2) and cable (DVB-C) systems. It represents the number of symbol changes per second in the modulated signal. Common values include 27500000 for many European satellite transponders.
For terrestrial (DVB-T/ATSC) systems, this property is typically not used as the bandwidth is fixed by the standard.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAChannel.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with default values.
member.remarks: Creates an empty channel configuration. All properties must be set manually before the channel can be used for tuning.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAChannel.#ctor(System.Int16,System.String,System.Byte,System.Boolean,System.Int16,System.Int16,System.Byte)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with specified parameters.
member.param: The service ID (SID) that uniquely identifies the service in the transport stream.
The display name of the channel.
The service type value indicating the type of service (TV, radio, etc.).
true if the channel is encrypted; false if free-to-air.
The PID of the video elementary stream, or -1 if no video.
The PID of the primary audio elementary stream, or -1 if no audio.

remarks.para: This constructor initializes the basic channel parameters but does not set tuning parameters (Frequency, Polarisation, SymbolRate). These must be set separately after construction.
This constructor is typically used when parsing channel information from service information tables or channel scan results.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType
member.summary: Defines the modulation types supported by Broadcast Driver Architecture (BDA) for digital TV reception.

remarks.para: This enumeration represents the various modulation schemes used in digital broadcasting standards worldwide. The modulation type determines how digital data is encoded onto the carrier signal for transmission.
Different broadcasting standards use different modulation schemes:

item.description: DVB-T/T2: Typically uses QPSK, 16-QAM, 64-QAM, or 256-QAM
DVB-S/S2: Primarily uses QPSK, 8PSK, 16APSK, or 32APSK
DVB-C: Uses QAM variants (16, 32, 64, 128, 256)
ATSC: Uses 8VSB for terrestrial and various QAM for cable

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.ModNotSet
member.summary: Indicates that the modulation type has not been set.
member.remarks: This value is used to indicate an uninitialized or invalid state.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.ModNotDefined
member.summary: Indicates that the modulation type is not defined or unknown.
member.remarks: This value may be used when the modulation scheme cannot be determined or is not applicable to the current context.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod16Qam
member.summary: 16-QAM (Quadrature Amplitude Modulation) with 16 constellation points.
member.remarks: Transmits 4 bits per symbol. Commonly used in cable (DVB-C) and terrestrial (DVB-T) systems. Provides moderate data rate with good noise immunity.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod32Qam
member.summary: 32-QAM with 32 constellation points.
member.remarks: Transmits 5 bits per symbol. Less common than other QAM variants but used in some cable systems.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod64Qam
member.summary: 64-QAM with 64 constellation points.
member.remarks: Transmits 6 bits per symbol. Widely used in cable (DVB-C) and terrestrial (DVB-T) broadcasting. Offers good balance between data rate and robustness.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod80Qam
member.summary: 80 QAM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod96Qam
member.summary: 96 QAM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod112Qam
member.summary: 112 QAM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod128Qam
member.summary: 128 QAM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod160Qam
member.summary: 160 QAM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod192Qam
member.summary: 192 QAM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod224Qam
member.summary: 224 QAM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod256Qam
member.summary: 256-QAM with 256 constellation points.
member.remarks: Transmits 8 bits per symbol. Common in cable systems (DVB-C, DOCSIS) and advanced terrestrial systems (DVB-T2). Provides high data rates but requires good signal quality.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod320Qam
member.summary: 320 QAM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod384Qam
member.summary: 384 QAM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod448Qam
member.summary: 448 QAM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod512Qam
member.summary: 512 QAM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod640Qam
member.summary: 640 QAM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod768Qam
member.summary: 768 QAM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod896Qam
member.summary: 896 QAM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.ModQpsk
member.summary: QPSK (Quadrature Phase Shift Keying) with 4 constellation points.
member.remarks: Transmits 2 bits per symbol. Very robust modulation scheme used primarily in satellite (DVB-S/S2) and mobile applications. Offers excellent noise immunity at the cost of lower data rates.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.ModBpsk
member.summary: BPSK (Binary Phase Shift Keying) with 2 constellation points.
member.remarks: Transmits 1 bit per symbol. The most robust but lowest data rate modulation. Used in very noisy environments or for control channels.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.ModOqpsk
member.summary: OQPSK (Offset Quadrature Phase Shift Keying).
member.remarks: A variant of QPSK where the phase transitions are offset to reduce peak-to-average power ratio. Used in some satellite systems.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod8Vsb
member.summary: 8-VSB (8-level Vestigial Sideband) modulation.
member.remarks: The standard modulation for ATSC digital terrestrial television in North America. Transmits approximately 3 bits per symbol with good multipath resistance.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod16Vsb
member.summary: 16-VSB (16-level Vestigial Sideband) modulation.
member.remarks: A higher data rate variant of VSB modulation used in some ATSC applications. Requires better signal conditions than 8-VSB.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.ModAnalogAmplitude
member.summary: Analog amplitude modulation (AM).
member.remarks: Used for legacy analog broadcasts. Included for compatibility with hybrid tuners that support both analog and digital reception.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.ModAnalogFrequency
member.summary: Analog frequency modulation (FM).
member.remarks: Used for legacy analog broadcasts, particularly for audio carriers. Included for compatibility with hybrid tuners.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod8Psk
member.summary: 8-PSK (8-Phase Shift Keying) with 8 constellation points.
member.remarks: Transmits 3 bits per symbol. Commonly used in satellite systems (DVB-S2) for higher data rates than QPSK while maintaining reasonable robustness.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.ModRF
member.summary: RF (Radio Frequency) pass-through mode.
member.remarks: Indicates that the signal should be passed through without demodulation. Used for RF loop-through or when demodulation is handled by another device.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod16Apsk
member.summary: 16-APSK (16-Amplitude Phase Shift Keying).
member.remarks: Advanced modulation used in DVB-S2 combining amplitude and phase modulation. Transmits 4 bits per symbol with better performance than 16-QAM in satellite channels.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.Mod32Apsk
member.summary: 32-APSK (32-Amplitude Phase Shift Keying).
member.remarks: Advanced modulation used in DVB-S2 for high data rates. Transmits 5 bits per symbol. Requires good signal conditions and is typically used for professional applications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.ModNbcQpsk
member.summary: Non-Backward Compatible QPSK.
member.remarks: A variant of QPSK used in some proprietary systems that is not compatible with standard QPSK demodulators.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.ModNbc8Psk
member.summary: Non-Backward Compatible 8-PSK.
member.remarks: A variant of 8-PSK used in some proprietary systems that is not compatible with standard 8-PSK demodulators.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.ModDirectTv
member.summary: DirecTV proprietary modulation.
member.remarks: Special modulation scheme used by DirecTV satellite services in North America. Requires DirecTV-compatible equipment.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAModulationType.ModMax
member.summary: Maximum value marker for the enumeration.
member.remarks: This value is used for validation and boundary checking. It should always be the last value in the enumeration.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAPolarisation
member.summary: Defines the signal polarization types supported by Broadcast Driver Architecture (BDA) for satellite reception.

remarks.para: Signal polarization is a critical parameter in satellite communications. It refers to the orientation of the electromagnetic wave's electric field vector. Different polarizations allow satellite operators to transmit multiple signals on the same frequency without interference, effectively doubling the available bandwidth.
This enumeration is primarily used with DVB-S/S2 (satellite) systems. Terrestrial and cable systems typically do not use polarization as a tuning parameter.
The LNB (Low Noise Block) converter on the satellite dish uses the polarization setting to select which set of transponders to receive.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAPolarisation.NotSet
member.summary: Indicates that the polarization has not been set.
member.remarks: This value is used to indicate an uninitialized state and should not be used for actual tuning operations.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAPolarisation.NotDefined
member.summary: Indicates that the polarization is not defined or not applicable.
member.remarks: This value may be used for systems where polarization is not relevant, such as terrestrial or cable broadcasts.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAPolarisation.LinearH
member.summary: Linear Horizontal polarization.

remarks.para: In linear horizontal polarization, the electric field oscillates horizontally (parallel to the Earth's surface). This is one of the two primary polarization modes used in satellite broadcasting.
On most LNBs, horizontal polarization is selected by applying a lower voltage (typically 13-14V) to the LNB.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAPolarisation.LinearV
member.summary: Linear Vertical polarization.

remarks.para: In linear vertical polarization, the electric field oscillates vertically (perpendicular to the Earth's surface). This is one of the two primary polarization modes used in satellite broadcasting.
On most LNBs, vertical polarization is selected by applying a higher voltage (typically 18-19V) to the LNB.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAPolarisation.CircularL
member.summary: Circular Left (Left-Hand Circular Polarization - LHCP).

remarks.para: In circular polarization, the electric field vector rotates in a circle. Left-hand circular polarization means the field rotates counter-clockwise when viewed in the direction of propagation.

Circular polarization is less common than linear but is used by some satellite systems, particularly in C-band and some Ku-band applications. It offers better resistance to signal degradation from atmospheric effects.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAPolarisation.CircularR
member.summary: Circular Right (Right-Hand Circular Polarization - RHCP).

remarks.para: In circular polarization, the electric field vector rotates in a circle. Right-hand circular polarization means the field rotates clockwise when viewed in the direction of propagation.
Like LHCP, RHCP is used in specific satellite applications where resistance to rain fade and other atmospheric effects is important.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.BDAPolarisation.Max
member.summary: Maximum value marker for the enumeration.
member.remarks: This value is used for validation and boundary checking. It should not be used as an actual polarization setting.
