member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Pan
member.summary: Specifies the camera's pan setting, in degrees. Values range from –180 to +180, with the default set to zero. Positive values are clockwise from the origin (the camera rotates clockwise when viewed from above), and negative values are counterclockwise from the origin.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Tilt
member.summary: Specifies the camera's tilt setting, in degrees. Values range from –180 to +180, with the default set to zero. Positive values point the imaging plane up, and negative values point the imaging plane down.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Roll
member.summary: Specifies the camera's roll setting, in degrees. Values range from –180 to +180, with the default set to zero. Positive values cause a clockwise rotation of the camera along the image-viewing axis, and negative values cause a counterclockwise rotation of the camera.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Zoom
member.summary: Specifies the camera's zoom setting, in millimeters. Values range from 10 to 600, and the default is specific to the device.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Exposure
member.summary: Specifies the exposure setting, in log base 2 seconds. In other words, for values less than zero, the exposure time is 1/2n seconds, and for values zero or above, the exposure time is 2n seconds. For example: Value: Seconds: -3 1/8 -2 1/4 -1 1/2 0 1 1 2 2 4

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Iris
member.summary: Specifies the camera's iris setting, in units of f(stop) * 10.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Focus
member.summary: Specifies the camera's focus setting, as the distance to the optimally focused target, in millimeters. The range and default value are specific to the device.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.ScanMode
member.summary: The ScanMode property specifies the scanning mode of the camera sensor. The property value specifies whether interlace mode should be enabled. A value of 0 indicates that the interlace mode is enabled, and a value of 1 indicates that the progressive (or non-interlace) mode is enabled.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Privacy
member.summary: The Privacy property specifies whether to prevent video from being acquired by the camera sensor. The property value specifies whether privacy mode is enable or disabled. A value of 0 indicates that the camera sensor can capture video images, and a value of 1 indicates that the camera sensor is prevented from capturing video images.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.PanTilt
member.summary: The PanTilt property specifies absolute pan and tilt settings. The property value is a pair of integers that specify a camera's absolute pan and tilt settings. These values are expressed in arc-second units. One arc second is 1/3600 of a degree. Acceptable values range from −180*3600 to +180*3600 arc seconds. If a pan or tilt value is not provided, the default is 0. When making a pan request, specify a positive value to rotate the camera to the right and specify a negative value to rotate the camera to the left. When making a tilt request, a positive value tilts the camera up and a negative value tilts the camera down.
member.remarks: NOT IMPLEMENTED.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.PanRelative
member.summary: The PanRelative property specifies a camera's rotation around the vertical axis. The property value specifies a camera's relative pan setting. The size of the value represents the desired pan speed; a higher value represents a higher speed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.TiltRelative
member.summary: The TileRelative property specifies a camera's vertical tilting status. The property value specifies a camera's relative tilt setting. The size of the value represents the desired tilt speed; a higher value represents a higher speed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.RollRelative
member.summary: The RollRelative property specifies camera rotation around the image viewing axis. The property value specifies a camera's relative roll setting. The size of the value represents the desired rotation speed; a higher value represents a higher speed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.ZoomRelative
member.summary: The ZoomRelative property specifies the zoom status of the camera. The property value specifies a camera's relative zoom setting. The size of the value represents the desired zoom speed; a higher value represents a higher speed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.ExposureRelative
member.summary: The ExposureRelative property specifies the electronic shutter speed. The property value specifies a camera's relative exposure setting. Step size is hardware-dependent. To determine the step size, you can make a get request on the Exposure property.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.IrisRelative
member.summary: The IrisRelative property specifies a camera's aperture setting. The property value specifies a camera's relative iris setting. Both the iris step size and the iris step default value are implementation-specific.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.FocusRelative
member.summary: The FocusRelative property specifies the focus setting of the camera. The property value specifies a camera's relative focus setting. The size of the value represents the speed at which the focal point changes; a higher value represents a higher speed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.PanTiltRelative
member.summary: The PanTiltRelative property specifies horizontal or vertical rotation of the camera and can specify both simultaneously.
member.remarks: NOT IMPLEMENTED.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.FocalLength
member.summary: The FocalLength property retrieves focal length information for a camera.] The property value specifies a camera's focal length.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.AutoExposurePriority
member.summary: The AutoExposurePriority (Low light compensation checkbox in a dialog) property specifies whether the device can dynamically vary the frame rate. The property value specifies whether frame rate can be dynamically varied by the device. 0 - frame rate must remain constant. 1 - frame rate can be dynamically varied by the device.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarConnections
member.summary: Represents a connection between input and output pins on a video crossbar device.
member.remarks: The class defines a routing connection within a crossbar device, mapping a specific input pin to an output pin. Crossbar devices are used in video capture hardware to route multiple input sources (such as composite, S-Video, or component inputs) to different outputs or processing paths.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarConnections.InPin
member.summary: Gets or sets the input pin identifier for the connection.
member.value: The zero-based index of the input pin to connect. This corresponds to a physical input on the crossbar device (e.g., 0 for composite input, 1 for S-Video input).
member.remarks:
Input pin indices typically map to physical connectors on the capture device:
Index Common Input Type
0 Composite Video
1 S-Video
2 Component Video
The actual mapping depends on the specific hardware device.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarConnections.OutPin
member.summary: Gets or sets the output pin identifier for the connection.
member.value: The zero-based index of the output pin to connect to. This typically represents the capture or processing path within the device.
member.remarks: Output pins usually represent different processing or capture paths. Many devices have a single output pin (index 0) for the main capture path, but some professional devices may have multiple outputs for simultaneous capture or preview paths.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarInputPin
member.summary: Represents an input pin on a video crossbar device used for routing video signals.
member.remarks: The class represents an input connection point on a crossbar device. Crossbars are hardware components that allow routing of multiple video and audio inputs to different outputs. This class contains information about a specific input pin, including its routing capabilities and relationships to other pins.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarInputPin.CanRoute
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this input pin can be routed to output pins.
member.value: if the pin supports routing to output pins; otherwise, . Some input pins may be fixed or disabled and cannot be dynamically routed.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarInputPin.Name
member.summary: Gets or sets the display name of the input pin.
member.value: A descriptive name for the pin (e.g., "Composite In", "S-Video In", "Component In"). This name is typically provided by the hardware driver and helps identify the physical input connector.
member.example:
Common pin names include:
"Composite In" - Standard composite video input
"S-Video In" - S-Video input connector
"Component In" - Component video input
"HDMI In" - HDMI digital input

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarInputPin.PinIndex
member.summary: Gets or sets the logical index of the pin within the crossbar.
member.value: The zero-based index used to identify this input pin in the crossbar's routing operations. This may differ from the physical pin index.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarInputPin.RealPinIndex
member.summary: Gets or sets the actual physical pin index on the hardware.
member.value: The real hardware pin index, which may differ from the logical . This represents the actual physical connector on the device.
member.remarks: The real pin index is important when the logical pin arrangement differs from the physical hardware layout, which can occur with some capture devices.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarInputPin.RelatedPinIndex
member.summary: Gets or sets the index of a related pin (typically an audio pin associated with this video pin).
member.value: The index of a related pin, or -1 if no related pin exists. For video input pins, this often references the corresponding audio input pin that should be used together.
member.remarks: Many capture devices have paired video and audio inputs. For example, a composite video input may have an associated left/right audio input. This property helps maintain that relationship for proper signal routing.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarOutputPin
member.summary: Represents an output pin on a video crossbar device used for routing video signals.
member.remarks: The class represents an output connection point on a crossbar device. Each output pin can be connected to one of several input pins, allowing flexible routing of video signals. This class maintains a list of all possible input pins that can be routed to this output.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarOutputPin._inputPins
member.summary: Input pins.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarOutputPin.InputPins
member.summary: Gets the list of input pins that can be connected to this output pin.
member.value: A read-only collection of objects representing all possible input sources that can be routed to this output.
member.remarks: This collection contains all the input pins available on the crossbar device. Not all input pins may be routable to this specific output pin - check the property to determine if a specific routing is possible.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarOutputPin.Name
member.summary: Gets or sets the display name of the output pin.
member.value: A descriptive name for the pin (e.g., "Video Decoder Out", "Video Preview Out"). This name is typically provided by the hardware driver.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarOutputPin.PinIndex
member.summary: Gets or sets the logical index of the pin within the crossbar.
member.value: The zero-based index used to identify this output pin in crossbar routing operations.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarOutputPin.RelatedPinIndex
member.summary: Gets or sets the index of a related pin (typically an audio pin associated with this video pin).
member.value: The index of a related pin, or -1 if no related pin exists. For video output pins, this often references the corresponding audio output pin.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarOutputPin.RoutedTo
member.summary: Gets or sets the index of the input pin currently routed to this output.
member.value: The index of the input pin that is currently connected to this output pin, or -1 if no input is connected.
member.remarks: This property indicates the active routing configuration. Use this to determine which input source is currently being sent to this output.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarOutputPin.Finalize
member.summary: Finalizes an instance of the class.
member.remarks: The finalizer ensures that the input pins collection is properly cleaned up. Exceptions are suppressed to prevent issues during garbage collection.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CrossBarOutputPin.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.remarks: Creates a new output pin with an empty collection of input pins. Input pins should be added to the collection after instantiation.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings
member.summary: Provides configuration settings for custom DirectShow video and audio source filters.
member.remarks: The class allows integration of custom DirectShow filters as video or audio sources. This enables support for proprietary hardware devices, specialized codecs, or custom media sources that aren't natively supported by the framework. You can specify filters by name, CLSID, or category, and configure their media types and formats.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.VideoFilterName
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of the custom video source filter.
member.value: The friendly name of the DirectShow filter to use as a video source. This name must match exactly as registered in the system.

example.code: settings.VideoFilterName = "My Custom Video Source";

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.VideoFilterFormat
member.summary: Gets or sets the video format string for the custom source filter.
member.value: A format string that specifies the desired video format. The exact format of this string depends on the specific filter being used.
member.remarks: Common format strings include resolution and pixel format information, such as "1920x1080" or "YUY2". Consult your filter's documentation for supported format strings.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.VideoFilterFrameRate
member.summary: Gets or sets the frame rate for the custom video source filter.
member.value: The desired frame rate for video capture. The filter must support the specified frame rate.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.VideoFilenameOrURL
member.summary: Gets or sets the file name or URL for filters that support the IFileSourceFilter interface.
member.value: A file path or URL that will be passed to the filter if it implements IFileSourceFilter. This is commonly used for file-based source filters.
member.remarks: Only filters that implement the IFileSourceFilter interface will use this property. For example, this could be used with custom file reader filters or network stream filters.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.VideoFilterCLSID
member.summary: Gets or sets the CLSID (Class Identifier) of the video filter.
member.value: The GUID that uniquely identifies the DirectShow filter. Use this when you know the exact CLSID of the filter you want to instantiate.

example.code: settings.VideoFilterCLSID = new Guid("12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012");

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.VideoFilterCategory
member.summary: Gets or sets the category of the custom video source filter.
member.value: The DirectShow filter category. Default is .
member.remarks: Filter categories help organize and discover filters by their function. Common categories include VideoCaptureSource, VideoCompressor, and LegacyAmFilterCategory.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.VideoFilterAMMediaType
member.summary: Gets or sets the custom AM_MEDIA_TYPE structure for the video source.
member.value: An AM_MEDIA_TYPE object that specifies the exact media type for the video stream. This provides fine-grained control over the media format when needed.
member.remarks: This property is for advanced scenarios where you need to specify an exact media type that cannot be expressed through the format string alone. The object should be a properly formatted AM_MEDIA_TYPE structure.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.AudioFilterName
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of the custom audio source filter.
member.value: The friendly name of the DirectShow filter to use as an audio source. This name must match exactly as registered in the system.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.AudioFilterFormat
member.summary: Gets or sets the audio format string for the custom source filter.
member.value: A format string that specifies the desired audio format. Common formats include sample rate and bit depth information (e.g., "48000Hz 16bit Stereo").

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.AudioFilterCategory
member.summary: Gets or sets the category of the custom audio source filter.
member.value: The DirectShow filter category. Default is .
member.remarks: Audio filter categories include AudioCaptureSource, AudioCompressor, and LegacyAmFilterCategory.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.AudioFilterCLSID
member.summary: Gets or sets the CLSID (Class Identifier) of the audio filter.
member.value: The GUID that uniquely identifies the DirectShow audio filter.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.AudioFilterAMMediaType
member.summary: Gets or sets the custom AM_MEDIA_TYPE structure for the audio source.
member.value: An AM_MEDIA_TYPE object that specifies the exact media type for the audio stream.
member.remarks: Use this for advanced scenarios requiring precise audio format specifications that cannot be expressed through the format string alone.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.AudioFilterPCMConverterAMMediaType
member.summary: Gets or sets the AM_MEDIA_TYPE for an optional PCM converter connected to the audio source.
member.value: An AM_MEDIA_TYPE object for configuring a PCM converter filter that may be inserted after the audio source to convert to standard PCM format.
member.remarks: Some audio sources output compressed or non-standard formats. A PCM converter can be automatically inserted to convert the audio to standard uncompressed PCM format for further processing.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.AudioFilenameOrURL
member.summary: Gets or sets the file name or URL for audio filters that support the IFileSourceFilter interface.
member.value: A file path or URL that will be passed to the audio filter if it implements IFileSourceFilter.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.SourceInterface
member.summary: Gets or sets a custom video source interface implementation.
member.value: An implementation of that will be used instead of DirectShow filters for video capture.
member.remarks: This property allows you to bypass DirectShow entirely and provide your own video source implementation. This is useful for integrating custom hardware or software sources that don't have DirectShow filters.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CustomSourceSettings.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.remarks:
The constructor sets default values:
VideoFilterCategory is set to VideoCaptureSource
AudioFilterCategory is set to AudioCaptureSource
Both CLSIDs are initialized to Guid.Empty

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DecklinkSourceSettings
member.summary: Provides configuration settings for Blackmagic DeckLink video capture devices.
member.remarks: The class is used to configure professional Blackmagic DeckLink capture cards for video input. DeckLink devices are commonly used in broadcast and professional video production environments.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DecklinkSourceSettings.Name
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of the DeckLink device.
member.value: The display name of the DeckLink device (e.g., "DeckLink Studio 4K", "DeckLink Mini Recorder"). This value is used to identify and select the specific DeckLink hardware device from the system.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DecklinkSourceSettings.VideoFormat
member.summary: Gets or sets the video format for the DeckLink input.
member.value: The video format string that specifies the input video standard (e.g., "1080p50", "1080p59.94", "720p60", "NTSC", "PAL"). The available formats depend on the specific DeckLink device model and the connected video source.
member.remarks:
Common format values include:
"1080p50" - 1920x1080 progressive at 50 fps
"1080p59.94" - 1920x1080 progressive at 59.94 fps
"1080i50" - 1920x1080 interlaced at 50 fields/sec
"720p60" - 1280x720 progressive at 60 fps
"NTSC" - Standard definition NTSC
"PAL" - Standard definition PAL

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceRemovedAddedType
member.summary: Specifies the type of media device that was added or removed from the system.
member.remarks: This enumeration is used with device change notification events to identify whether the affected device is a video input, audio input, or audio output device. It helps applications respond appropriately to hardware changes during runtime.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceRemovedAddedType.VideoSource
member.summary: A video capture source device (camera, capture card, etc.).
member.remarks: Includes webcams, USB cameras, capture cards, virtual camera devices, and any other device that provides video input to the system.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceRemovedAddedType.AudioSource
member.summary: An audio capture source device (microphone, line-in, etc.).
member.remarks: Includes microphones, line-in inputs, digital audio interfaces, and any other device that provides audio input to the system.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceRemovedAddedType.AudioOutput
member.summary: An audio playback/output device (speakers, headphones, etc.).
member.remarks: Includes speakers, headphones, digital audio outputs, HDMI audio devices, and any other device that provides audio output from the system.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceSubtype
member.summary: Specifies the subtype or vendor-specific variant of a video capture device.
member.remarks: This enumeration is used to identify specific device models or vendors that may require special handling, custom drivers, or vendor-specific features. It allows the framework to apply device-specific optimizations or workarounds.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceSubtype.Default
member.summary: Default device subtype with no special handling required.
member.remarks: Used for standard devices that follow common interfaces and don't require vendor-specific implementations or workarounds.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceSubtype.FaceVision
member.summary: FaceVision series camera device.
member.remarks: FaceVision cameras may have vendor-specific extensions or require special initialization sequences. These devices often include facial recognition or biometric features.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceSubtype.Sensoray2253
member.summary: Sensoray Model 2253 video capture device.
member.remarks: The Sensoray 2253 is a professional multi-channel video capture device that supports simultaneous capture from multiple sources. It may require specific driver interfaces or configuration parameters.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceType
member.summary: Defines the type of video capture device based on supported output formats.
member.remarks: This enumeration is used to identify the capabilities and output formats supported by video capture devices. Different device types may require different processing pipelines or have specific limitations.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceType.Standard
member.summary: Standard video capture device with basic output capabilities.
member.remarks: Typically supports uncompressed video formats such as RGB or YUV. This is the most common type for webcams and basic capture cards.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceType.StandardAndMPEG2
member.summary: Device supporting both standard output formats and MPEG-2 encoding.
member.remarks: These devices can provide both uncompressed video and hardware-encoded MPEG-2 streams. Common in TV tuner cards and some professional capture devices.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceType.MPEG2Only
member.summary: Device that only outputs MPEG-2 encoded video streams.
member.remarks: These devices perform hardware MPEG-2 encoding and do not provide uncompressed output. Often found in hardware encoder cards and some TV capture devices.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceType.DV
member.summary: Digital Video (DV) camcorder connected via FireWire/IEEE 1394.
member.remarks: DV devices output video in the DV codec format, typically at 25 Mbps for SD video. Commonly used for MiniDV camcorders and professional DV equipment.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceType.MPEG2HDV
member.summary: High Definition Video (HDV) camcorder using MPEG-2 compression.
member.remarks: HDV devices record HD video using MPEG-2 compression over FireWire connection. Supports resolutions up to 1080i with a bitrate of approximately 25 Mbps.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceType.StandardAndH264
member.summary: Device supporting both standard output formats and H.264/AVC encoding.
member.remarks: These modern devices can provide uncompressed video and hardware-accelerated H.264 encoding. Common in newer capture cards and IP cameras with local encoding capabilities.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceType.H264Only
member.summary: Device that only outputs H.264/AVC encoded video streams.
member.remarks: These devices perform hardware H.264 encoding exclusively without uncompressed output. Typical for IP cameras, hardware encoders, and some modern capture devices.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.DeviceType.Unknown
member.summary: Unknown or unidentified device type.
member.remarks: Used when the device type cannot be determined or for devices that don't fit other categories. Applications should handle this type gracefully with appropriate fallback behavior.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ICustomAudioSourceFilter
member.summary: Defines the interface for custom audio source filters that can be integrated into the DirectShow filter graph.
member.remarks: This interface allows developers to create custom audio sources that can be used as input devices in the video capture pipeline. Implementations can provide audio from various sources such as multiple microphones, network streams, or synthesized audio. See the TwoMicsAudioSource class for a sample implementation that demonstrates mixing audio from two microphones.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ICustomAudioSourceFilter.GetOutputPin
member.summary: Gets the output pin of the audio source filter.
member.returns: The DirectShow output pin object that other filters can connect to. This is typically an IPin COM interface wrapped as an object.
member.remarks: The output pin is used by the DirectShow graph builder to connect this audio source to downstream filters such as audio encoders, effects, or renderers. The pin should provide audio data in a format compatible with DirectShow audio filters.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ICustomAudioSourceFilter.Init(System.Object,System.String@)
member.summary: Initializes the audio source filter and adds it to the DirectShow filter graph.
member.param: The DirectShow filter graph object (IGraphBuilder) that this source will be added to.
When the method returns false, contains an error message describing what went wrong. When successful, this parameter is set to null or an empty string.
member.returns: true if the initialization was successful; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: This method should perform all necessary initialization including: - Creating the DirectShow filter - Configuring audio format and parameters - Adding the filter to the provided graph - Preparing the filter to start providing audio data Any resources allocated during initialization should be properly released in the Dispose method.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ICustomVideoSource
member.summary: Defines the interface for custom video sources that can provide video frames to the capture pipeline.
member.remarks: This interface enables developers to create custom video sources from various inputs such as IP cameras, screen capture, generated graphics, or any other video data source. Implementations must handle frame generation, format specification, and event notification. The video source can be used as an input device in video capture and processing scenarios.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ICustomVideoSource.VideoWidth
member.summary: Gets or sets the width of the video frames in pixels.
member.value: The horizontal resolution of the video stream.
member.remarks: This value should be set before starting the video source and should remain constant during capture. Common values include 640, 1280, 1920, etc.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ICustomVideoSource.VideoHeight
member.summary: Gets or sets the height of the video frames in pixels.
member.value: The vertical resolution of the video stream.
member.remarks: This value should be set before starting the video source and should remain constant during capture. Common values include 480, 720, 1080, etc.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ICustomVideoSource.VideoFrameRate
member.summary: Gets or sets the frame rate of the video stream in frames per second.
member.value: The number of frames per second the source will attempt to provide.
member.remarks: Common frame rates include 15, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 50, 59.94, and 60 fps. The actual frame rate may vary depending on the source's capabilities and system performance.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ICustomVideoSource.VideoFillBuffer(VisioForge.Core.Types.RAWVideoFrame)
member.summary: Fills the provided frame buffer with video data.
member.param: The RAWVideoFrame object to be filled with video data.
member.remarks: This method is called by the framework to retrieve video frames from the custom source. The implementation should copy the current video frame data into the provided buffer, respecting the frame's format and dimensions. This method should be thread-safe and performant as it may be called frequently based on the frame rate.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ICustomVideoSource.OnVideoBuffer
member.summary: Occurs when a new video frame is available from the source.
member.remarks: This event allows the custom video source to push frames to the pipeline instead of being polled via VideoFillBuffer. Subscribers can process the frame data provided in the VideoFrameBufferEventArgs. This is useful for sources that generate frames asynchronously or at irregular intervals.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ICustomVideoSource.GetCameraInfo(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String@,VisioForge.Core.Types.Size@)
member.summary: Retrieves information about a camera or video source from the specified URL.
member.param: The URL or connection string for the video source (e.g., RTSP URL, HTTP stream URL).
The username for authentication, if required by the video source. Pass null or empty string if authentication is not needed.
The password for authentication, if required by the video source. Pass null or empty string if authentication is not needed.
When the method returns false, contains an error message describing the connection or authentication failure. When successful, this is set to null or empty string.
When successful, contains the native video size reported by the source. This helps in configuring the VideoWidth and VideoHeight properties appropriately.
member.returns: true if the camera information was successfully retrieved; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: This method is typically used to validate connection parameters and retrieve source capabilities before starting the video stream. It's particularly useful for IP cameras and network video sources that require authentication.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ICustomVideoSource.Start
member.summary: Starts the video source and begins generating or capturing video frames.
member.remarks: This method should initialize any necessary resources, establish connections, and begin the frame generation process. After calling this method, the source should either respond to VideoFillBuffer calls or raise OnVideoBuffer events with video frame data. The VideoWidth, VideoHeight, and VideoFrameRate properties should be properly configured before calling this method.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings
member.summary: Provides configuration settings for screen capture operations, including capture area, frame rate, and visual enhancements.

remarks.para: This class encapsulates all the settings required to configure screen capture functionality, supporting both full-screen and region-based capture modes. It provides fine-grained control over the capture process, including performance optimizations and visual enhancements.

The settings support various capture scenarios: - Full screen capture across multiple displays - Specific window capture using window handles - Custom region capture with coordinate specification - Mouse cursor capture with optional highlighting effects
On Windows 8 and later, the Desktop Duplication API can be enabled for improved performance and lower CPU usage compared to traditional GDI-based capture methods.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.Bottom
member.summary: Gets or sets the bottom boundary coordinate for the screen capture area.
member.value: The Y-coordinate of the bottom edge of the capture rectangle in screen pixels.
member.remarks: This property is only used when is set to false. The value should be greater than to define a valid capture area.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.FrameRate
member.summary: Gets or sets the frame rate at which the screen will be captured.
member.value: A object specifying the capture frame rate.
member.remarks: Higher frame rates provide smoother capture but require more system resources. Common values include 10, 15, 25, or 30 frames per second. The actual achievable frame rate may be limited by system performance.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.FullScreen
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to capture the entire screen or a specific region.
member.value: true to capture the full screen; false to capture only the region defined by , , , and .
member.remarks: When set to true, the coordinate properties are ignored and the entire display specified by is captured.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.GrabMouseCursor
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the mouse cursor should be included in the capture.
member.value: true to include the mouse cursor in the captured video; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the mouse cursor will be rendered on top of the captured screen content. This setting works in conjunction with the mouse highlighting features for enhanced visibility.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.AllowDesktopDuplicationEngine
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the Desktop Duplication API should be used for screen capture.
member.value: true to enable Desktop Duplication API; false to use traditional GDI capture.

remarks.para: The Desktop Duplication API is available on Windows 8 and later versions. It provides significantly better performance and lower CPU usage compared to GDI-based capture methods.
When this option is enabled but the API is not available (e.g., on Windows 7), the system will automatically fall back to GDI capture.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.DisplayIndex
member.summary: Gets or sets the zero-based index of the display monitor to capture.
member.value: The display index where 0 represents the primary monitor.
member.remarks: In multi-monitor setups, this property determines which display to capture. The index corresponds to the system's display enumeration order. Use 0 for the primary display, 1 for the first secondary display, and so on.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.Left
member.summary: Gets or sets the left boundary coordinate for the screen capture area.
member.value: The X-coordinate of the left edge of the capture rectangle in screen pixels.
member.remarks: This property is only used when is set to false. The coordinate is relative to the top-left corner of the specified display.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.Right
member.summary: Gets or sets the right boundary coordinate for the screen capture area.
member.value: The X-coordinate of the right edge of the capture rectangle in screen pixels.
member.remarks: This property is only used when is set to false. The value should be greater than to define a valid capture area.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.Top
member.summary: Gets or sets the top boundary coordinate for the screen capture area.
member.value: The Y-coordinate of the top edge of the capture rectangle in screen pixels.
member.remarks: This property is only used when is set to false. The coordinate is relative to the top-left corner of the specified display.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.Mode
member.summary: Gets or sets the screen capture mode that determines what content is captured.
member.value: A enumeration value specifying the capture mode.
member.remarks: The capture mode determines whether to capture the entire screen, a specific window, or use other specialized capture methods. This property works in conjunction with other settings like for window-specific capture.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.WindowHandle
member.summary: Gets or sets the handle of the window to capture when using window-specific capture mode.
member.value: An representing the window handle (HWND on Windows).
member.remarks: This property is only used when is set to capture a specific window. The handle must refer to a valid window that exists at the time of capture. This property is not serialized to JSON.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.MouseHighlight
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to display a visual highlight effect around the mouse cursor.
member.value: true to enable mouse highlighting; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When enabled, a colored circle appears around the mouse cursor to make it more visible in screen recordings. This is particularly useful for tutorial videos or demonstrations. The highlight appearance can be customized using the related properties.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.MouseHighlightColor
member.summary: Gets or sets the color of the mouse highlight circle.
member.value: A value representing the highlight color. The default value is .
member.remarks: This property only takes effect when is set to true. Choose a color that provides good contrast with your typical screen content.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.MouseHighlightSize
member.summary: Gets or sets the thickness of the mouse highlight circle border in pixels.
member.value: The border thickness in pixels. The default value is 5.
member.remarks: This property controls how thick the highlight circle's border appears. Larger values create a more prominent highlight effect. This property only takes effect when is set to true.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.MouseHighlightDuration
member.summary: Gets or sets the duration for which the mouse highlight remains visible after a click.
member.value: A representing the highlight duration. The default value is 0.7 seconds.
member.remarks: This property determines how long the highlight effect persists after a mouse click, helping viewers notice where clicks occur. The highlight gradually fades out over this duration. This property only takes effect when is enabled.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.MouseHighlightOpacity
member.summary: Gets or sets the opacity level of the mouse highlight effect.
member.value: A value between 0.0 (fully transparent) and 1.0 (fully opaque). The default value is 0.5.
member.remarks: This property controls the transparency of the highlight circle, allowing the underlying screen content to show through. Lower values create a more subtle effect, while higher values make the highlight more prominent.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.MouseHighlightRadius
member.summary: Gets or sets the radius of the mouse highlight circle in pixels.
member.value: The radius of the highlight circle. The default value is 50 pixels.
member.remarks: This property determines the size of the circular highlight area around the mouse cursor. Larger values create a bigger highlight area, making the cursor more prominent in the capture. This property only takes effect when is set to true.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with default values.
member.remarks: The default configuration captures the full primary screen at 10 frames per second without the mouse cursor. The capture area is initially set to 640x480 pixels for non-fullscreen mode, though this is overridden when is true.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.ScreenCaptureSourceSettings.ToString
member.summary: Returns a string representation of the current screen capture settings.
member.returns: A string describing the capture mode and frame rate. For fullscreen mode, returns "Fullscreen@{fps}fps". For region capture, returns "{left}x{top}x{right}x{bottom}@{fps}fps".
member.remarks: This method provides a concise summary of the capture configuration, useful for logging or displaying the current settings to users.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.SeparateCaptureMode
member.summary: Defines the modes for separate capture operations that control how video capture is split across multiple files.

remarks.para: The separate capture mode determines how the captured video is distributed across multiple output files. This is useful for managing large capture sessions by automatically splitting the output based on specific criteria such as time duration or file size.

This enumeration is typically used in conjunction with video capture settings to configure how the capture output should be segmented. The mode affects how the capture system handles file transitions and ensures continuous recording across multiple files.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.SeparateCaptureMode.Normal
member.summary: Normal capture mode where the separate capture process must be controlled manually.
member.remarks: In this mode, the application has full control over when to start and stop separate capture operations. No automatic file splitting occurs, and all captured content is written to a single file until explicitly stopped or a new capture is started.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.SeparateCaptureMode.SplitByDuration
member.summary: Automatically splits the capture into multiple files based on a specified time duration.

remarks.para: When this mode is selected, the capture system automatically creates new output files after the specified duration has elapsed. This ensures that no single file exceeds the defined time limit.
This mode is particularly useful for long recording sessions where you want to maintain manageable file sizes or need to organize content into time-based segments (e.g., hourly recordings).

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.SeparateCaptureMode.SplitByFileSize
member.summary: Automatically splits the capture into multiple files when a specified file size is reached.

remarks.para: In this mode, the capture system monitors the output file size and automatically creates a new file when the current file reaches the specified size limit. This prevents individual files from becoming too large to handle efficiently.

This mode is ideal for situations where storage constraints exist or when working with file systems that have maximum file size limitations. It also helps in managing upload/transfer operations for captured content.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TimeshiftSettings
member.summary: Provides configuration settings for timeshift functionality in video capture operations.

remarks.para: Timeshift enables viewers to pause, rewind, and fast-forward live video streams by continuously recording the stream to temporary storage while simultaneously allowing playback from that storage. This creates a buffer that allows time-shifted viewing of live content.

The implementation uses Stream Buffer Engine (SBE) technology to manage the recording and playback processes. Multiple backing files are used to store the content, with automatic file rotation to manage storage space efficiently.

Common use cases include: - Pausing live TV to resume watching later - Rewinding to replay interesting moments - Fast-forwarding through previously recorded content - Creating a delay buffer for censorship or editing purposes

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TimeshiftSettings.TempFolder
member.summary: Gets or sets the folder path where temporary timeshift files will be stored.
member.value: The full path to the temporary storage folder. Default is the system temp path with "SBE\" subdirectory.

remarks.para: This folder will contain the backing files used for timeshift buffering. Ensure the specified location has sufficient free space to accommodate the expected buffer size based on your and video bitrate settings.
The folder will be created automatically if it doesn't exist. Write permissions are required for the application to create and manage the temporary files.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TimeshiftSettings.RecordingID
member.summary: Gets or sets the unique identifier for this timeshift recording session.
member.value: A that uniquely identifies the recording session.
member.remarks: This ID is used to differentiate between multiple timeshift sessions and to manage the associated temporary files. A new GUID is automatically generated when creating a new instance of this class. The same ID should be used when resuming a session.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TimeshiftSettings.OutputFormat
member.summary: Gets or sets the output format used by the Stream Buffer Engine encoder.
member.value: An value specifying the encoding format.
member.remarks: The output format determines how the video stream is encoded for storage in the timeshift buffer. Different formats offer different trade-offs between quality, file size, and CPU usage. Choose a format that balances your quality requirements with available system resources.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TimeshiftSettings.CaptureMode
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the Stream Buffer Engine should operate in capture mode.
member.value: true to enable direct capture mode; false to use temporary file mode.

remarks.para: When capture mode is enabled, the SBE encoder writes directly to the final output location. When disabled, temporary files are used for buffering, which can provide better performance for timeshift operations but requires additional disk space.
Temporary file mode is typically preferred for timeshift functionality as it allows more flexible seek operations and better manages disk I/O.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TimeshiftSettings.Player_Screen
member.summary: Gets or sets the video view control where the time-shifted content will be displayed.
member.value: An implementation that provides the rendering surface.
member.remarks: This property specifies where the playback of time-shifted content should be rendered. The video view must be properly initialized and attached to a visible UI element before starting timeshift playback. This property is not serialized to JSON.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TimeshiftSettings.Player_AudioOutput_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether audio playback is enabled during timeshift playback.
member.value: true to enable audio output; false to mute audio during playback.
member.remarks: When disabled, the video will play without sound. This can be useful for preview purposes or when audio output is handled by a separate system. Audio is still recorded to the timeshift buffer regardless of this setting.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TimeshiftSettings.Player_AudioOutput_Device
member.summary: Gets or sets the audio output device to use for timeshift playback.
member.value: The name or identifier of the audio output device. Use null or empty string for the default device.

remarks.para: This property allows you to specify which audio device should be used for playback of the time-shifted content. The device name should match one of the available audio output devices on the system.
If the specified device is not available, the system will typically fall back to the default audio output device.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TimeshiftSettings.BackingFileCountMinimum
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum number of backing files to maintain in the timeshift buffer.
member.value: The minimum number of files. Valid range is 4 to 100. Default is 4.

remarks.para: The Stream Buffer Engine uses multiple files to store the timeshift buffer. This property sets the minimum number of files that will be kept at all times. Having multiple files allows for efficient file rotation and prevents fragmentation.
Lower values use less disk space but may impact seek performance. Higher values provide smoother operation but require more storage space.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TimeshiftSettings.BackingFileCountMaximum
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of backing files allowed in the timeshift buffer.
member.value: The maximum number of files. Valid range is 6 to 102. Must be at least 2 greater than . Default is 6.

remarks.para: This property defines the upper limit for the number of backing files. When this limit is reached, the oldest files are deleted to make room for new ones, creating a rolling buffer of content.
The difference between minimum and maximum provides a buffer zone that helps maintain smooth operation during file rotation operations.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TimeshiftSettings.BackingFileDuration
member.summary: Gets or sets the total duration of content that can be stored in all backing files.
member.value: The duration in seconds. Minimum value is 15. Default is 3600 (1 hour).

remarks.para: This property determines how much content history is available for timeshift operations. The actual storage space required depends on this duration and the bitrate of the video being captured.
For example, with a 1-hour duration and a 5 Mbps video stream, approximately 2.25 GB of storage space would be required for the buffer.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TimeshiftSettings.EncodingSettings
member.summary: Gets or sets the encoding settings used for the timeshift buffer.
member.value: An object containing video and audio encoding parameters.

remarks.para: These settings control how the video and audio are encoded when written to the timeshift buffer. The quality and bitrate settings directly impact the storage space required and the CPU usage during capture.
Choose encoding settings that balance quality requirements with available system resources and storage space. Lower bitrates reduce storage requirements but may impact visual quality.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TimeshiftSettings.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with default values.

remarks.para: The default configuration creates a 1-hour timeshift buffer in the system's temporary folder. A new unique recording ID is automatically generated for each instance.
Default values: - Temporary folder: System temp path + "SBE\" - Backing file count: 4-6 files - Buffer duration: 1 hour (3600 seconds) - Recording ID: New GUID

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerMode
member.summary: Defines the operating modes supported by TV tuner devices.

remarks.para: This enumeration represents the different signal types and broadcasting standards that a TV tuner can receive and process. Modern TV tuners often support multiple modes, allowing them to receive various types of broadcasts including television, radio, and digital signals.
The allows multiple modes to be combined, indicating that a tuner supports multiple reception modes or that multiple modes should be scanned during channel searches.
The actual modes available depend on the specific tuner hardware and the broadcasting standards in use in the geographical region where the tuner is operating.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerMode.Default
member.summary: Default tuner mode, typically determined by the tuner hardware or driver.
member.remarks: This value indicates that no specific mode is selected, allowing the tuner to use its default or automatic mode selection.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerMode.TV
member.summary: Analog or digital television reception mode.
member.remarks: Enables the tuner to receive standard television broadcasts. This includes both analog TV signals (NTSC, PAL, SECAM) and digital TV signals, depending on the tuner's capabilities.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerMode.FMRadio
member.summary: FM (Frequency Modulation) radio reception mode.
member.remarks: Configures the tuner to receive FM radio broadcasts, typically in the 88-108 MHz frequency band. FM radio provides higher quality audio compared to AM radio.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerMode.AMRadio
member.summary: AM (Amplitude Modulation) radio reception mode.
member.remarks: Configures the tuner to receive AM radio broadcasts, typically in the 530-1700 kHz frequency band. AM radio has longer range but lower audio quality compared to FM.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerMode.Dss
member.summary: Digital Satellite System reception mode.
member.remarks: Enables reception of digital satellite broadcasts. DSS is a proprietary digital satellite television broadcasting system used primarily in North America. This mode requires appropriate satellite reception equipment.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerMode.DTV
member.summary: Digital Television reception mode.
member.remarks: Specifically enables digital television reception, including standards such as ATSC (North America), DVB-T (Europe and other regions), or ISDB-T (Japan and South America). This mode is distinct from analog TV reception.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerSubChannel
member.summary: Defines the subchannel options for TV tuner operations.

remarks.para: TV tuner subchannels represent additional channels that may be available within a main channel, commonly used in digital television broadcasting where multiple programs can be transmitted on the same frequency using different subchannels.
This enumeration provides options for controlling subchannel selection during tuning operations, including the ability to specify no tuning or use the default subchannel selection.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerSubChannel.NoTune
member.summary: Indicates that no subchannel tuning should be performed.
member.remarks: Use this value when you want to maintain the current subchannel selection or when subchannel tuning is not applicable for the current operation.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerSubChannel.Default
member.summary: Uses the default subchannel selection determined by the tuner or system.
member.remarks: When this value is specified, the TV tuner will automatically select the primary or default subchannel for the tuned frequency. This is typically the main program stream in a multi-program transport.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat
member.summary: Specifies the video format standards supported by TV tuner devices.
member.remarks: This enumeration defines various analog television broadcast standards used worldwide. The standards are grouped into three main families: NTSC (National Television System Committee), PAL (Phase Alternating Line), and SECAM (Séquentiel couleur à mémoire). Each standard has regional variations denoted by letters or numbers. The enumeration also includes bit masks for filtering standards by family.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat.None
member.summary: No video format specified or unknown format.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat.NTSC_M
member.summary: NTSC-M standard used primarily in North America, parts of South America, and some Asian countries.
member.remarks: Operates at 525 lines, 59.94 Hz field rate, and 29.97 Hz frame rate.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat.NTSC_M_J
member.summary: NTSC-M-J standard used exclusively in Japan.
member.remarks: Similar to NTSC-M but with different black level and audio carrier specifications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat.NTSC_433
member.summary: NTSC-433 variant with modified color subcarrier frequency.
member.remarks: Used for pseudo-NTSC signals with 4.43 MHz color subcarrier instead of 3.58 MHz.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat.PAL_B
member.summary: PAL-B standard used in Western Europe, Australia, and parts of Africa and Asia.
member.remarks: Operates at 625 lines, 50 Hz field rate, with 7 MHz channel bandwidth.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat.PAL_D
member.summary: PAL-D standard used in China and some former Soviet republics.
member.remarks: Similar to PAL-B but with different audio carrier specifications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat.PAL_G
member.summary: PAL-G standard used in Western Europe, Scandinavia, and other regions.
member.remarks: Similar to PAL-B but with 8 MHz channel bandwidth.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat.PAL_H
member.summary: PAL-H standard used in Belgium and some other regions.
member.remarks: Similar to PAL-G with minor technical variations.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat.PAL_I
member.summary: PAL-I standard used in the United Kingdom, Ireland, and Hong Kong.
member.remarks: Features 8 MHz channel bandwidth with specific audio carrier offset.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat.PAL_M
member.summary: PAL-M standard used in Brazil.
member.remarks: Unique variant using 525 lines at 59.94 Hz like NTSC but with PAL color encoding.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat.PAL_N
member.summary: PAL-N standard used in Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay.
member.remarks: Uses 625 lines at 50 Hz with modified color subcarrier frequency.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat.PAL_60
member.summary: PAL-60 hybrid standard for NTSC playback on PAL equipment.
member.remarks: Combines PAL color encoding with NTSC line and field rates.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat.SECAM_B
member.summary: SECAM-B standard variant.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat.SECAM_D
member.summary: SECAM-D standard used in former Soviet Union countries.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.TVTunerVideoFormat.SECAM_G
