member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureOutputFormatHelper
member.summary: Provides extension methods for determining the capture mode characteristics of video capture output formats.
member.remarks: This helper class contains extension methods that analyze values to determine their capture characteristics, such as whether they use direct capture or Media Foundation multiplexing. These methods help in routing video capture streams through the appropriate processing pipelines.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureOutputFormatHelper.IsDirectCapture(VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureOutputFormat)
member.summary: Determines whether the specified format uses direct capture mode.
member.param: The video capture output format to evaluate.
member.returns: if the format uses direct capture mode; otherwise, .

remarks.para: Direct capture formats bypass intermediate processing and write directly to the output file using the capture device's native format or a hardware-accelerated encoder. This typically results in lower CPU usage and minimal latency.

The following formats are considered direct capture:
DirectCaptureDV - Digital Video format
DirectCaptureMPEG - MPEG format
DirectCaptureAVI - AVI container
DirectCaptureMKV - Matroska container
DirectCaptureASF - Advanced Systems Format
DirectCaptureMP4_GDCL - MP4 using GDCL encoder
DirectCaptureMP4_Monogram - MP4 using Monogram encoder
DirectCaptureCustom - Custom direct capture implementation

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureOutputFormatHelper.IsMFMux(VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureOutputFormat)
member.summary: Determines whether the specified format uses Media Foundation multiplexing.
member.param: The video capture output format to evaluate.
member.returns: if the format uses Media Foundation multiplexing; otherwise, .

remarks.para: Media Foundation (MF) multiplexing formats use Windows Media Foundation technology to combine audio and video streams into a single container file. This provides better compatibility with modern Windows applications and hardware acceleration support.

The following formats use MF multiplexing:
MP4_HW - Hardware-accelerated MP4 encoding
MPEGTS - MPEG Transport Stream
MOV - QuickTime Movie format
MKVv2 - Matroska version 2 using MF multiplexer

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureSource
member.summary: Represents a video capture source device configuration for DirectShow-based video capture operations.

remarks.para: This class encapsulates the configuration settings for a video capture device, including format selection, frame rate control, and special features like closed captions and raw sample grabbing. It automatically detects and selects optimal capture formats based on device capabilities.

The class supports various capture scenarios including:
Standard video capture devices (webcams, capture cards)
TV tuners with internal MPEG encoders
Devices that can also serve as audio sources
Professional capture devices with multiple output pins

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureSource.Name
member.summary: Gets or sets the display name of the video capture device.
member.value: The device name as it appears in the system's device list.
member.remarks: This is the human-readable name of the device, such as "Logitech HD Webcam" or "USB Video Device".

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureSource.Path
member.summary: Gets or sets the DirectShow device path for unique device identification.
member.value: The DirectShow device path string, or if not specified.

remarks.para: This property is optional but recommended when multiple devices with the same name exist in the system. The device path provides a unique identifier that persists across system restarts.
Use the Video_CaptureDevice_GetDevicePath method to obtain the device path for a specific device.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureSource.InternalMPEGEncoder_Name
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of the internal MPEG encoder for devices with hardware encoding capabilities.
member.value: The encoder name, or an empty string if no internal encoder is available.
member.remarks: Some capture devices, particularly TV tuner cards, include built-in MPEG encoders that can perform hardware compression directly on the device, reducing CPU usage.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureSource.IsAudioSource
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this video capture device should also be used as an audio source.
member.value: if the device should capture audio; otherwise, .

remarks.para: Most modern video capture devices include audio capture capabilities. However, some older TV tuners require a separate audio connection to the sound card and do not support direct audio capture through the video device.
When set to , the framework will attempt to capture both audio and video from the same device, simplifying synchronization.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureSource.Format
member.summary: Gets or sets the specific video format string for capture operations.
member.value: The format string (e.g., "MJPG 1920x1080"), or an empty string to use automatic selection.

remarks.para:
The format string typically includes the codec type and resolution, such as:
"MJPG 1920x1080" - Motion JPEG at 1080p
"YUY2 1280x720" - Uncompressed YUV at 720p
"RGB24 640x480" - RGB at VGA resolution
If left empty and is , the framework will automatically select an appropriate format.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureSource.CustomPinName
member.summary: Gets or sets the custom pin name for devices with multiple output pins.
member.value: The pin name, or to use the default pin.

remarks.para: Professional capture devices may expose multiple output pins, each potentially offering different formats or processing paths. Use the VideoFormatsAllPins property of to enumerate available pins and their formats.

Common pin names include:
"Capture" - Main capture pin
"Preview" - Lower resolution preview pin
"Still" - High resolution still image pin

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureSource.Format_UseBest
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether automatic format selection should be used.
member.value: to automatically select the best format; otherwise, .
member.remarks: When enabled, the framework analyzes available formats and selects the optimal one based on resolution (preferring 4K > 1080p > 720p) and codec (preferring MJPEG for better quality and lower CPU usage).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureSource.UseClosedCaptions
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to capture closed captions if available.
member.value: to enable closed caption capture; otherwise, .
member.remarks: Closed captions are typically available from TV tuner devices capturing broadcast content. When enabled, caption data will be embedded in the output stream or made available through appropriate events.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureSource.UseRAWSampleGrabber
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether raw sample grabbing is enabled for frame-level access.
member.value: to enable raw sample grabbing; otherwise, .

remarks.para: When enabled, the framework inserts a sample grabber filter in the DirectShow graph, allowing direct access to video frames through the OnVideoFrameBufferRAW event. This is useful for custom processing, analysis, or frame capture scenarios.
Note that enabling this feature may impact performance due to the additional memory copies required for frame access.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureSource.FrameRate
member.summary: Gets or sets the target frame rate for video capture.
member.value: A value specifying the desired frame rate.

remarks.para: The actual frame rate achieved depends on device capabilities and the selected format. Not all combinations of resolution and frame rate may be supported by the device.

Common frame rates include:
30 fps - Standard video
60 fps - Smooth motion
25 fps - PAL standard
24 fps - Film standard

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureSource.#ctor(System.String)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with automatic format detection.
member.param: The name of the video capture device.

remarks.para:
This constructor automatically enumerates available devices, finds the matching device by name, and attempts to detect the best capture format. The format selection prioritizes:
4K resolution (3840x2160) if available
1080p resolution (1920x1080) as second choice
720p resolution (1280x720) as third choice
MJPEG codec over uncompressed formats

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureSource.#ctor(VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureDeviceInfo)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class from device information.
member.param: The video capture device information containing capabilities and supported formats.

remarks.para: This constructor uses the provided device information to configure the capture source, automatically selecting the best available format based on the device's capabilities. Unlike the name-based constructor, this avoids the need to re-enumerate devices.
The format detection follows the same prioritization as the name-based constructor, favoring higher resolutions and MJPEG compression when available.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureSource.DetectBestFormat(VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureDeviceInfo)
member.summary: Analyzes available formats and selects the optimal capture format for the device.
member.param: The device information containing available formats and capabilities.

remarks.para:
The format selection algorithm follows these priorities:
Filters out invalid formats (zero width/height) and H.264 formats
Prefers MJPEG formats over uncompressed formats for better performance
Selects resolution in order: 4K (3840x2160) → 1080p (1920x1080) → 720p (1280x720)
Falls back to the first available format if standard resolutions aren't found
Selects the maximum available frame rate for the chosen format
Note: The method contains a duplicate check for 720p resolution which should be 1920x1080 for the 1080p section (lines 151-162).

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureSource.ToString
member.summary: Returns a string representation of this video capture source.
member.returns: The device name as specified by the property.
member.remarks: This override provides a human-readable representation of the capture source, making it suitable for display in user interfaces, logging, and debugging. The returned value is simply the device name without any additional formatting.

example.code: var captureSource = new VideoCaptureSource("Logitech HD Webcam"); Console.WriteLine(captureSource.ToString()); // Output: "Logitech HD Webcam"

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIKey
member.summary: Defines vendor-specific API keys for accessing advanced features of video capture devices.

remarks.para: This enumeration identifies the different vendor-specific features that can be controlled through proprietary APIs. Currently focused on Logitech camera features, these keys are used in conjunction with values to control advanced camera functionality.

Each key represents a specific feature category that may have multiple configuration options or values associated with it. The availability of these features depends on the camera model and installed drivers.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIKey.Logitech_Version
member.summary: Queries or sets the Logitech property set interface version.
member.remarks: Use this key to determine the version of the Logitech API supported by the camera. Different versions may support different features or have different behavior.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIKey.Logitech_FaceTracking
member.summary: Controls face tracking functionality for Logitech cameras.

remarks.para:
This key enables configuration of the camera's face tracking capabilities, including:
Disabling face tracking entirely
Single face tracking (follows one person)
Multiple face tracking (attempts to keep multiple faces in frame)
Face tracking allows the camera to automatically adjust its position to keep faces centered in the frame during video calls or recordings.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIKey.Logitech_LED
member.summary: Controls the LED indicator behavior on Logitech cameras.

remarks.para:
This key configures how the camera's LED indicator behaves:
Always on during streaming
Always off (privacy mode)
Blinking at a specified frequency
Automatic (camera-controlled)
The LED provides visual feedback about the camera's operational state and can be customized for different use cases or privacy requirements.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIKey.Logitech_FindFace
member.summary: Controls automatic face centering for widescreen video streams on Logitech cameras.

remarks.para:
This feature automatically adjusts the camera position to center faces when starting a widescreen video stream. It includes options for:
Enabling/disabling automatic centering
Resetting to default position
Manual face centering on demand
This is particularly useful for video conferencing where optimal framing improves the communication experience.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIKey.Logitech_Zoom
member.summary: Controls the zoom level on Logitech cameras with motorized zoom capability.
member.remarks: Adjusts the camera's optical or digital zoom to change the field of view. The valid zoom range and increments depend on the specific camera model. Zoom can be used in conjunction with pan and tilt for complete PTZ control.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIKey.Logitech_Pan
member.summary: Controls horizontal pan positioning on Logitech PTZ cameras.
member.remarks: Adjusts the camera's horizontal position (left-right movement). This feature is only available on cameras with motorized pan capability. The value range and units depend on the specific camera model.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIKey.Logitech_Tilt
member.summary: Controls vertical tilt positioning on Logitech PTZ cameras.
member.remarks: Adjusts the camera's vertical position (up-down movement). This feature is only available on cameras with motorized tilt capability. The value range and units depend on the specific camera model.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType
member.summary: Defines vendor-specific API values for controlling advanced features of video capture devices.

remarks.para: This enumeration provides access to vendor-specific features that are not part of standard DirectShow or Windows video capture APIs. Currently, it primarily supports Logitech webcam features including face tracking, LED control, automatic face centering, and PTZ (Pan-Tilt-Zoom) controls.

These values are used in conjunction with vendor-specific API calls to control advanced camera features that go beyond basic capture functionality. The availability of these features depends on the specific camera model and installed drivers.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_Version_None
member.summary: No vendor-specific version or feature. Used as a default or placeholder value.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FaceTracking_Off
member.summary: Disables face tracking functionality on Logitech cameras.
member.remarks: When disabled, the camera will not automatically track faces in the video stream. The camera position and zoom will remain fixed at their current settings.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FaceTracking_Single
member.summary: Enables single-face tracking mode on Logitech cameras.
member.remarks: In this mode, the camera automatically tracks and follows a single person's face, adjusting pan, tilt, and zoom to keep the face centered in the frame. This corresponds to the "Follow me" option in the Logitech Webcam Software settings panel.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FaceTracking_Multiple
member.summary: Enables multi-face tracking mode on Logitech cameras.
member.remarks: In this mode, the camera attempts to track multiple faces simultaneously, adjusting the field of view to include all detected faces. This corresponds to the "Follow two or more of us" option in the Logitech Webcam Software settings panel.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_LED_On
member.summary: Sets the camera LED to remain on continuously when streaming video.
member.remarks: This provides a clear visual indicator that the camera is active and capturing video.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_LED_Off
member.summary: Turns off the camera LED completely, even during video streaming.
member.remarks: This setting disables the LED indicator for privacy or aesthetic reasons. Users should be aware that there will be no visual indication when the camera is active.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_LED_Blinking
member.summary: Sets the camera LED to blink at a specified frequency during video streaming.

remarks.para: The blinking frequency is specified in units of 0.1 Hertz through an additional parameter. This frequency determines how often the LED state changes per second.

For example:
Value 5 = 0.5 Hz = one state change every 2 seconds
Value 10 = 1.0 Hz = one state change every second
Value 20 = 2.0 Hz = two state changes per second

The LED alternates between on and off states at the specified frequency. If the frequency value is 0, the current blinking frequency remains unchanged. The precision of the blinking frequency may vary depending on the camera model and system load.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_LED_Auto
member.summary: Sets the camera LED to automatic mode, controlled by the camera firmware.
member.remarks: In automatic mode, the LED typically turns on when the camera is streaming video and turns off when streaming stops. This is the default behavior for most Logitech cameras and provides standard visual feedback about camera status.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FindFace_Mode_Off
member.summary: Turn off automatic centering of the user’s face when a widescreen video stream is initiated. Turning the feature off automatically performs a reset to the default position. Note that even when the feature is off you can still initiate a manual centering process by specifying the value 2 for the value1 field.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FindFace_Mode_On
member.summary: Turn on automatic centering of the user’s face when a widescreen video stream is initiated.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FindFace_Mode_NoChange
member.summary: Do not turn the feature on or off. This value should be used when an action is specified using Reset. Note, however, that specifying a reset action does not prevent you from enabling or disabling the feature at the same time.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FindFace_Reset_None
member.summary: Do not perform any action. This is typically used when the feature should simply be turned on or off.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FindFace_Reset_Default
member.summary: Reset the field of view to its default position, which is typically the center.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FindFace_Reset_Face
member.summary: Re-center the field of view to the current position of the user’s face. Note that for this to work the face tracker must be able to locate the face. If this is not currently possible, the centering process is delayed until the face is locatable again.

member.summary: Configure zoom.

member.summary: Logitech camera - configure pan.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoHardwareAdjustment
member.summary: Defines the types of hardware-level video adjustments available for video capture devices.

remarks.para: These adjustments are implemented at the hardware level by the video capture device or driver, providing real-time image processing without CPU overhead. The availability and range of each adjustment depends on the specific capture device and its driver capabilities.

Hardware adjustments typically offer better performance than software-based processing and should be preferred when available. Use the device's capability queries to determine which adjustments are supported and their valid value ranges.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoHardwareAdjustment.Brightness
member.summary: Controls the overall lightness or darkness of the video image.
member.remarks: Brightness adjustment affects all pixels equally, making the entire image lighter or darker. Typical range is 0-255 or -100 to +100, depending on the device. Default is usually the midpoint.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoHardwareAdjustment.Contrast
member.summary: Controls the difference between light and dark areas in the video image.
member.remarks: Higher contrast makes bright areas brighter and dark areas darker, increasing the dynamic range. Lower contrast reduces the difference, creating a flatter image. Useful for improving visibility in low-contrast scenes.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoHardwareAdjustment.Hue
member.summary: Controls the color tint of the video image along the color wheel.
member.remarks: Hue adjustment rotates colors around the color wheel. For example, adjusting hue can shift reds toward orange or purple. Typically measured in degrees (0-360) or as a normalized value. Useful for correcting color casts or achieving creative effects.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoHardwareAdjustment.Saturation
member.summary: Controls the intensity or purity of colors in the video image.
member.remarks: Higher saturation makes colors more vivid and intense, while lower saturation moves toward grayscale. A value of 0 typically produces a black and white image. Useful for enhancing or muting colors based on scene requirements.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoHardwareAdjustment.Sharpness
member.summary: Controls the edge enhancement of the video image.
member.remarks: Sharpness adjustment enhances or softens edge details in the image. Higher values increase edge contrast, making the image appear crisper but potentially introducing artifacts. Lower values create a softer, more natural look.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoHardwareAdjustment.Gamma
member.summary: Controls the gamma correction curve of the video image.
member.remarks: Gamma adjustment modifies the midtone brightness without significantly affecting highlights or shadows. Values greater than 1.0 lighten midtones, while values less than 1.0 darken them. Standard gamma is typically 2.2 for computer displays.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoHardwareAdjustment.ColorEnable
member.summary: Enables or disables color processing in the video image.
member.remarks: When disabled (value 0), the image is converted to grayscale. When enabled (value 1), full color processing is active. This is different from setting saturation to 0, as it may completely bypass color processing in the hardware.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoHardwareAdjustment.WhiteBalance
member.summary: Controls the color temperature balance of the video image.
member.remarks: White balance adjustment compensates for different lighting conditions to ensure whites appear neutral. Values typically range from warm (lower values, reddish) to cool (higher values, bluish). Many devices also support automatic white balance.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoHardwareAdjustment.BacklightCompensation
member.summary: Enables compensation for strong backlighting conditions.

remarks.para: Backlight compensation helps when the subject is darker than the background, such as a person in front of a window. When enabled (value 1), it brightens the foreground to improve subject visibility.
This feature is particularly useful for video conferencing scenarios where users may be positioned in front of bright backgrounds.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoHardwareAdjustment.Gain
member.summary: Controls the signal amplification level of the video sensor.
member.remarks: Gain adjustment amplifies the video signal, making the image brighter but potentially introducing noise. Higher gain values are useful in low-light conditions but may degrade image quality. Often works in conjunction with exposure settings.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoHardwareAdjustment.PowerLineFrequency
member.summary: Sets the power line frequency for flicker reduction.

remarks.para:
This setting helps eliminate flicker caused by artificial lighting that operates at the local power line frequency. Valid values are:
50 Hz - Common in Europe, Asia, and other regions
60 Hz - Common in North America and some other regions
Setting this incorrectly may result in visible flicker or banding in the video image under artificial lighting conditions.

member.summary: Specifies the color space mode to be used by the Camshift (Continuously Adaptive Mean-Shift) tracking algorithm. The choice of color space can significantly impact the robustness and accuracy of object tracking.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.CamshiftMode.Mixed

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorScalingMode
member.summary: Specifies the scaling strategy for the search window used in object detection algorithms. This mode determines how the detector iterates through different sizes of objects to find matches.
member.remarks: The choice of scaling mode can impact both the performance and accuracy of object detection. For example, if you expect to detect large objects primarily, starting with larger windows might be more efficient.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorScalingMode.GreaterToSmaller
member.summary: The object detector will start searching with larger windows and gradually scale down to smaller ones. This mode can be efficient if the target objects are expected to be large.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorScalingMode.SmallerToGreater

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorSearchMode
member.summary: Specifies the search mode for object detection algorithms. This enumeration defines how the detector scans an image or video frame for objects.
member.remarks: The choice of search mode can significantly affect the performance and the number of detected objects. For example, mode is faster if only one object is expected, while (full scan) is more comprehensive.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorSearchMode.Default
member.summary: The entire image or video frame will be scanned for objects. This is the default and most comprehensive search mode.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorSearchMode.Single
member.summary: Only a single object will be retrieved. The search stops after the first object is found. This mode is useful for performance optimization when only the presence of an object matters.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorSearchMode.NoOverlap
member.summary: If an object has already been detected within an area, that area will not be scanned again for inner or overlapping objects. This can save computation time and prevent redundant detections.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.ObjectDetectorSearchMode.Average
member.summary: If several objects are located within one another (overlapping detections), their bounding boxes will be averaged into a single result. This helps in consolidating multiple detections of the same object.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.BarcodeReaderSettings
member.summary: Provides configuration settings for barcode detection in video frames during video processing operations.

remarks.para: The class is used to configure barcode detection functionality within the video processing pipeline. It allows enabling or disabling barcode detection and specifying the type of barcodes to detect.

When barcode detection is enabled, the video processor analyzes each frame to identify and decode barcodes of the specified type. This is useful for applications such as: - Inventory management systems with video surveillance - QR code-based authentication systems - Automated product scanning in manufacturing - Document processing with embedded barcodes

Performance considerations: - Barcode detection adds computational overhead to video processing - Specifying a specific barcode type (rather than Auto) improves performance - Detection accuracy depends on video quality, barcode size, and lighting conditions

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.BarcodeReaderSettings.Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether barcode detection is enabled during video processing.
member.value: true if barcode detection is enabled; otherwise, false. Default value is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the video processor will analyze frames for barcodes of the specified type. Disabling barcode detection when not needed improves video processing performance.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.BarcodeReaderSettings.Type
member.summary: Gets or sets the type of barcode to detect in video frames.
member.value: The barcode symbology to detect. Default value is .

remarks.para: Specifying a particular barcode type improves detection performance as the processor only needs to look for that specific symbology. Using will attempt to detect all supported barcode types but requires more processing time.

Common use cases for specific barcode types: - : Mobile applications, URLs, digital payments - : Retail products (European Article Number) - : Retail products (Universal Product Code) - : Shipping labels, inventory tracking - : Small items, medical devices

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.HorizontalAlignment
member.summary: Specifies the horizontal alignment of visual elements within video frames during video processing operations.

remarks.para: The enumeration is used throughout the video processing pipeline to control the horizontal positioning of various visual elements such as: - Text overlays and subtitles - Watermarks and logos - Picture-in-picture elements - Graphical overlays and annotations - Motion detection grids and regions
This alignment is relative to the containing element or frame boundaries. The exact behavior depends on the specific video processing component using this enumeration.
When used with text overlays, the alignment point is typically: - Left: The left edge of the text baseline - Center: The horizontal center of the text - Right: The right edge of the text baseline

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.HorizontalAlignment.Left
member.summary: Aligns the element to the left edge of its container.

remarks.para: When applied to text, the left edge of the text is positioned at the specified location. For images and other visual elements, the left edge of the bounding box is used as the alignment point.

This is typically the default alignment for left-to-right languages and is commonly used for: - Subtitle positioning in Western languages - Logo placement in the top-left corner - Status information displays

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.HorizontalAlignment.Right
member.summary: Aligns the element to the right edge of its container.

remarks.para: When applied to text, the right edge of the text is positioned at the specified location. For images and other visual elements, the right edge of the bounding box is used as the alignment point.
Common uses include: - Watermark placement in corners - Right-to-left language text - Timestamp displays - Channel logos for broadcast applications

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.HorizontalAlignment.Center
member.summary: Centers the element horizontally within its container.

remarks.para: The element's horizontal center is aligned with the center of its container. This provides equal spacing on both left and right sides.
Centered alignment is commonly used for: - Main titles and headings - Subtitles and closed captions - Notification messages - Loading indicators - Symmetrical logo placement

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionCHLColor
member.summary: Specifies the color channel to use for highlighting motion areas in video frames during motion detection processing.

remarks.para: The enumeration is used in conjunction with motion detection algorithms to specify which color channel should be emphasized when highlighting detected motion. This provides a simple way to visualize motion by modifying specific color channels in the affected pixels.

When motion is detected in a region, the selected color channel is intensified while other channels may be reduced or left unchanged, creating a colored highlight effect. This technique is particularly useful for: - Security and surveillance applications - Motion analysis and tracking systems - Activity monitoring in specific areas - Visual debugging of motion detection algorithms

The choice of highlight color can affect visibility depending on the video content: - Red: High contrast, easily visible in most scenes - Green: Good visibility, less aggressive than red - Blue: Subtle highlighting, suitable for darker scenes

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionCHLColor.Red
member.summary: Highlights motion areas using the red color channel.

remarks.para: Red highlighting provides high visibility and is commonly used for: - Security alerts and warnings - High-priority motion detection - Areas requiring immediate attention
The red channel typically offers the best contrast against most backgrounds, making it the default choice for many motion detection applications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionCHLColor.Green
member.summary: Highlights motion areas using the green color channel.

remarks.para: Green highlighting offers good visibility while being less aggressive than red: - Normal activity monitoring - Extended viewing sessions (easier on the eyes) - Natural or outdoor scenes where green blends better
Green is often chosen for continuous monitoring applications where operators need to watch screens for extended periods.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionCHLColor.Blue
member.summary: Highlights motion areas using the blue color channel.

remarks.para: Blue highlighting provides subtle motion indication suitable for: - Low-light or night vision scenarios - Discrete monitoring applications - Scenes with warm color tones where blue provides contrast
Blue channel highlighting is less common but can be effective in specific lighting conditions or when a more subtle highlight is desired.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings
member.summary: Provides comprehensive configuration settings for advanced motion detection in video processing pipelines.

remarks.para: The class offers extensive control over motion detection algorithms and visualization options. It supports multiple detection methods and processing techniques suitable for various applications including: - Security and surveillance systems - Traffic monitoring - Industrial automation - Sports analysis - Wildlife observation

The class provides two main configuration aspects: 1. Detection configuration: Controls how motion is detected (detector type, sensitivity, noise suppression) 2. Visualization configuration: Controls how detected motion is displayed (highlighting, grids, colors)

Performance considerations: - Different detector types have varying computational requirements - Enabling visualization features adds processing overhead - Grid-based processing is more efficient for large areas - Object counting requires more CPU than simple motion detection

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.ProcessorType
member.summary: Gets or sets the motion processor type that determines how detected motion is analyzed and visualized.
member.value: The processor type to use for motion analysis. Default is .

remarks.para: The processor type affects both the analysis method and visualization output: - : Detection only, no visualization - : Highlights all motion pixels - : Highlights only motion boundaries - : Identifies and tracks individual objects - : Divides frame into grid for area analysis

Choose the processor based on your application needs: - Use BlobCountingObjects for people counting or object tracking - Use GridMotionAreaProcessing for activity heatmaps or zone monitoring - Use MotionAreaHighlighting for general motion visualization

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.DetectorType
member.summary: Gets or sets the motion detector algorithm used to identify changes between frames.
member.value: The detection algorithm to use. Default is .

remarks.para: Each detector type has different characteristics: - : Fast, detects all movement including camera shake - : Adapts to gradual changes, good for static cameras - : Compares against a reference frame

Selection guidelines: - Use TwoFramesDifference for quick motion detection or moving cameras - Use SimpleBackgroundModeling for fixed surveillance cameras - Use CustomFrameDifference when you have a known background reference

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.DifferenceThreshold
member.summary: Gets or sets the pixel difference threshold for motion detection, ranging from 1 to 255.
member.value: The minimum difference in pixel values to be considered as motion. Default is 15. Valid range is [1-255].

remarks.para: This threshold determines the sensitivity of motion detection. A pixel is considered to have motion if the difference between frames exceeds this value. The difference is typically calculated as the absolute difference in grayscale or color values.

Threshold selection guidelines: - Lower values (1-10): Very sensitive, detects subtle changes, more prone to noise - Medium values (10-30): Balanced detection, suitable for most applications - Higher values (30-50): Less sensitive, detects only significant movement - Very high values (50+): Only detects dramatic changes, good for high-noise environments

Factors affecting threshold selection: - Lighting conditions: Poor lighting requires lower thresholds - Camera quality: Lower quality cameras need higher thresholds to reduce noise - Scene complexity: Busy scenes may need higher thresholds - Application requirements: Security systems often use lower thresholds

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.SuppressNoise
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether noise suppression filtering is applied to reduce false positives.
member.value: true to enable noise suppression; otherwise, false. Default is true.

remarks.para: When enabled, applies a 3x3 erosion morphological filter to remove isolated pixels that are likely to be noise rather than actual motion. This significantly reduces false positives caused by: - Camera sensor noise - Compression artifacts - Small environmental changes (dust, insects) - Electrical interference
Side effects of noise suppression: - May remove small but legitimate moving objects - Can erode the edges of larger objects - Slightly reduces processing speed
Use in conjunction with to restore object boundaries after noise suppression if edge precision is important.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.KeepObjectsEdges
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether object edges are restored after noise suppression.
member.value: true to restore object edges; otherwise, false. Default is false.

remarks.para: When enabled, applies a 3x3 dilation morphological filter after noise suppression to restore object boundaries that may have been eroded. This helps maintain the original size and shape of detected objects while still benefiting from noise reduction.

This property is particularly useful when: - Accurate object size measurement is required - Object boundaries need to be precisely defined - Visual quality of highlighted regions is important - Tracking object contours or shapes
Performance impact: - Adds additional processing step (dilation filter) - Increases processing time by approximately 10-15% - Only applies when is enabled
Note: This property is only applicable for SimpleBackgroundModeling and CustomFrameDifference detector types.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.HighlightColor
member.summary: Gets or sets the color used to highlight detected motion regions in the video output.
member.value: The color for motion highlighting. Default is .

remarks.para: This color is used differently depending on the processor type: - For area highlighting: Overlays or tints motion pixels with this color - For border highlighting: Draws borders around motion regions - For object detection: Draws bounding boxes around detected objects - For grid processing: Colors active grid cells

Color selection considerations: - High contrast colors (red, yellow) for security applications - Subtle colors (light blue, green) for analysis displays - Consider the typical background colors in your video content - Semi-transparent colors can be used for overlay effects
The alpha channel of the color may be used to control transparency, depending on the specific processor implementation.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.MinObjectsHeight
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum height in pixels for an object to be detected and tracked.
member.value: The minimum object height in pixels. Default is 10. Must be positive.

remarks.para: This property filters out objects smaller than the specified height, helping to: - Eliminate noise and small artifacts from detection - Focus on objects of interest (people, vehicles, etc.) - Improve processing performance by ignoring irrelevant motion - Reduce false positives from environmental factors

Typical values for common scenarios: - People detection (640x480): 40-80 pixels - Vehicle detection (1920x1080): 100-200 pixels - Small object tracking: 5-20 pixels - Wildlife monitoring: Varies greatly by species and distance

The optimal value depends on: - Camera resolution and field of view - Distance from camera to objects - Type and size of objects being tracked - Acceptable trade-off between sensitivity and false positives
Note: This property only applies when is set to .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.MinObjectsWidth
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum width in pixels for an object to be detected and tracked.
member.value: The minimum object width in pixels. Default is 10. Must be positive.

remarks.para: Works in conjunction with to define the minimum bounding box size for valid objects. Objects must meet both width and height requirements to be detected.

Common width requirements by application: - Pedestrian detection: 20-60 pixels (depending on resolution) - Vehicle detection: 50-150 pixels - Face detection in crowds: 30-50 pixels - Hand gesture recognition: 40-80 pixels

Setting appropriate minimum dimensions helps: - Filter out noise and shadows - Prevent detection of irrelevant small movements - Focus computational resources on significant objects - Maintain consistent detection quality
Note: This property only applies when is set to .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.GridHeight
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of rows in the motion detection grid.
member.value: The number of grid rows. Default is 16. Valid range is [2-64].

remarks.para: The grid divides the video frame into cells for area-based motion analysis. Each cell independently tracks motion levels, enabling: - Zone-based motion detection - Activity heatmap generation - Directional motion analysis - Region-specific sensitivity settings

Grid resolution considerations: - Higher values (32-64): Fine-grained analysis, more CPU usage - Medium values (16-24): Balanced detail and performance - Lower values (4-8): Coarse analysis, better performance
For a 1920x1080 video: - 16 rows = 67.5 pixels per cell height - 32 rows = 33.75 pixels per cell height - 8 rows = 135 pixels per cell height
Note: This property only applies when is set to .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.GridWidth
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of columns in the motion detection grid.
member.value: The number of grid columns. Default is 16. Valid range is [2-64].

remarks.para: Works with to define the grid resolution. The total number of cells is GridWidth × GridHeight, which affects both analysis precision and processing performance.

Typical grid configurations: - Security monitoring: 16x12 or 20x15 (moderate detail) - Traffic analysis: 32x24 (higher detail for vehicle tracking) - Crowd monitoring: 8x6 (general activity levels) - Sports analysis: 40x30 (precise movement tracking)
The grid aspect ratio should generally match the video aspect ratio for uniform cell sizes. For 16:9 video, use ratios like 16x9, 32x18, etc.
Note: This property only applies when is set to .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.HighlightMotionGrid
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether grid cells with motion are visually highlighted.
member.value: true to highlight active grid cells; otherwise, false. Default is true.

remarks.para: When enabled, grid cells that detect motion above the threshold specified by are colored using . This creates a visual heatmap showing motion distribution across the frame.
Visualization options typically include: - Solid color fill for active cells - Transparency based on motion intensity - Grid lines to show cell boundaries - Gradient coloring for motion levels
Disable highlighting when: - Only motion data/statistics are needed - Implementing custom visualization - Maximizing processing performance - Running headless analysis
Note: This property only applies when is set to .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.MotionAmountToHighlight
member.summary: Gets or sets the motion level threshold for highlighting grid cells.
member.value: The minimum motion level (0.0 to 1.0) required to highlight a cell. Default is 0.15.

remarks.para: This threshold represents the percentage of pixels within a grid cell that must show motion for the cell to be highlighted. The value is normalized: - 0.0 = No motion required (all cells highlighted) - 0.15 = 15% of cell pixels must show motion (default) - 0.5 = 50% of cell pixels must show motion - 1.0 = All pixels must show motion (rarely achieved)

Threshold selection guidelines: - Low values (0.05-0.15): Sensitive detection, shows subtle activity - Medium values (0.15-0.30): Balanced, filters minor disturbances - High values (0.30-0.50): Only significant motion, reduces noise - Very high (0.50+): Only massive changes, like full object movement
The optimal value depends on: - Grid resolution (smaller cells need lower thresholds) - Scene characteristics (busy vs. quiet environments) - Application requirements (security vs. analytics)
Note: This property only applies when is set to and is enabled.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with default values.

remarks.para: Default configuration provides a balanced setup suitable for general motion detection: - Processor: MotionAreaHighlighting (visualizes all motion) - Detector: TwoFramesDifference (fast, simple detection) - Threshold: 15 (moderate sensitivity) - Noise suppression: Enabled - Color: Red highlighting

The default settings are optimized for: - Indoor surveillance with moderate lighting - Detection of human-sized objects - Real-time processing with visual feedback - Balance between sensitivity and false positives

For specific applications, adjust the settings after initialization: - Security: Increase sensitivity, enable object tracking - Analytics: Use grid processing, disable visualization - Outdoor: Increase threshold, enable edge preservation

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectorType
member.summary: Specifies the algorithm used for detecting motion in video frames by analyzing pixel differences over time.

remarks.para: Motion detection algorithms form the foundation of many video analysis applications including security surveillance, traffic monitoring, and activity analysis. Each algorithm has different characteristics in terms of accuracy, performance, and suitability for various scenarios.

The choice of detector affects: - Sensitivity to different types of motion - Handling of lighting changes and shadows - Computational performance requirements - Adaptation to scene changes - False positive rates
All detectors work in conjunction with the to determine what constitutes significant motion versus noise or minor changes.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectorType.CustomFrameDifference
member.summary: Detects motion by comparing each frame against a predefined reference (background) frame.

remarks.para: This detector compares the current frame with a static reference frame that represents the scene without any moving objects. Motion is detected wherever the current frame differs significantly from the reference.

Characteristics: - Requires manual or automatic capture of a clean background frame - Excellent for controlled environments with stable backgrounds - Does not adapt to gradual scene changes (lighting, shadows) - Very sensitive to camera movement or vibration - Low computational requirements

Best suited for: - Indoor surveillance with controlled lighting - Production line monitoring - Museum or gallery security - Detecting intrusions in normally empty areas - Short-term monitoring sessions
Limitations: - Background must be updated if scene changes permanently - Ineffective for outdoor scenes with changing conditions - Cannot handle moved furniture or parked vehicles

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectorType.SimpleBackgroundModeling
member.summary: Detects motion using an adaptive background model that updates over time.

remarks.para: This detector maintains a statistical model of the background that adapts to gradual changes in the scene. It can distinguish between temporary motion and permanent scene changes, updating its background model accordingly.

Characteristics: - Automatically adapts to lighting changes (sunrise/sunset) - Handles shadows and reflections better than frame difference - Can learn to ignore repetitive motion (trees, flags) - Moderate computational requirements - Configurable learning rate for background updates
Best suited for: - Long-term surveillance applications - Outdoor monitoring with changing conditions - Traffic monitoring systems - Parking lot surveillance - Perimeter security
Advanced features: - Gradual incorporation of stationary objects into background - Resistance to sudden illumination changes - Shadow suppression capabilities - Multi-modal background representation
Note: The adaptation rate can typically be configured to balance between quick adaptation to scene changes and resistance to incorporating moving objects into the background model.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectorType.TwoFramesDifference
member.summary: Detects motion by comparing consecutive frames in the video stream.

remarks.para: This is the simplest and fastest motion detection method, comparing each frame only with the immediately preceding frame. Any significant difference between consecutive frames is considered motion.

Characteristics: - Fastest processing speed, minimal CPU usage - No initialization or training required - Works immediately on any video stream - Detects all types of motion equally - Handles camera movement naturally

Best suited for: - Real-time applications with high frame rates - Mobile or embedded systems with limited resources - PTZ (Pan-Tilt-Zoom) camera systems - Drone or vehicle-mounted cameras - Initial motion detection before detailed analysis

Limitations: - Cannot distinguish between object motion and camera motion - Sensitive to noise and compression artifacts - May miss slow-moving objects - No concept of background vs. foreground - Detects changes in lighting as motion
Performance tips: - Works best with stable, high-quality video sources - May require higher threshold values to reduce noise - Can be combined with other techniques for validation

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererEVRDeinterlaceMode
member.summary: Specifies the deinterlacing modes available for the Enhanced Video Renderer (EVR). Deinterlacing converts interlaced video (where each frame consists of two fields captured at different times) into progressive video (where each frame contains all lines of a single moment in time).
member.remarks: Proper deinterlacing is crucial for displaying interlaced content (e.g., from broadcast TV, DVDs) on progressive displays (e.g., computer monitors, LCD TVs) without artifacts like combing. The choice of mode can impact visual quality and CPU/GPU usage.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererEVRDeinterlaceMode.Auto
member.summary: The EVR automatically selects the best deinterlacing method based on the video content and available hardware capabilities. This is generally the recommended setting for optimal quality and performance.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererEVRDeinterlaceMode.ForceHalfInterlace
member.summary: Forces the EVR to skip the second field (in temporal order) of every interlaced frame. This results in half-resolution video but can be useful for very low-latency scenarios or when higher-quality deinterlacing is not needed or causes performance issues.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererEVRDeinterlaceMode.ForceBob
member.summary: Forces the EVR to use bob deinterlacing. Bob deinterlacing creates a full frame from each field by interpolating missing lines, resulting in smoother motion but potentially visible artifacts.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererEVRDeinterlaceMode.AllowDropToHalfInterlace
member.summary: Allows the EVR to drop to half-interlace mode if it is falling behind in rendering. This provides a fallback for performance, sacrificing quality for smoothness.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererEVRDeinterlaceMode.AllowDropToBob
member.summary: Allows the EVR to drop to bob deinterlacing if it is falling behind in rendering. This provides a fallback for performance, sacrificing some quality for smoother playback.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererStretchMode
member.summary: Specifies how video frames are scaled or stretched to fit the display area of a video renderer. This enumeration controls the aspect ratio preservation and filling behavior.
member.remarks: The choice of stretch mode affects how the video appears when its aspect ratio differs from the display area. Some modes preserve the aspect ratio by adding black bars, while others stretch the video to fill the entire area, potentially causing distortion.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererStretchMode.Letterbox
member.summary: Preserves the video's original aspect ratio by adding black bars (letterboxing or pillarboxing) to fill any empty space in the display area.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererStretchMode.Stretch
member.summary: Stretches the video to fill the entire display area, ignoring its original aspect ratio. This may result in a distorted image if the aspect ratios do not match.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererStretchMode.LetterboxToFill
member.summary: Stretches the video to fill the entire display area while preserving its aspect ratio. This is achieved by cropping the video if its aspect ratio does not match the display area. This mode is typically available for WPF renderers.

member.summary: Defines various audio sample formats, including signed/unsigned integers and floating-point types, with different bit depths and endianness. This enumeration is used to specify the format of raw audio data for processing and playback within the MediaBlocks framework.
member.remarks: Understanding the audio format is crucial for correct interpretation and manipulation of audio samples. The `LE` suffix indicates Little-Endian byte order, while `BE` indicates Big-Endian. Formats without a suffix are typically Little-Endian.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.AudioInfoX
member.summary: Represents detailed audio format information for use within the MediaBlocks framework. This class defines properties such as the audio sample format, sample rate, and number of channels.
member.remarks: This information is crucial for configuring audio processing blocks, encoders, and renderers, ensuring that audio data is handled correctly throughout the pipeline.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.BarcodeDetectorEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for barcode detection events within the VisioForge X engine. This class encapsulates information about the detected barcode, including its type, value, and the timestamp of detection.
member.remarks: This event argument is used when a barcode is successfully identified in a video frame or image processed by the X engine. It allows applications to react to barcode detections, such as logging the information, triggering actions, or displaying results.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.BarcodeDetectorEventArgs.BarcodeType

member.summary: Gets the decoded string value of the barcode.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.BarcodeDetectorEventArgs.Timestamp
member.summary: Gets the timestamp of the video frame or image at which the barcode was detected.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.BarcodeDetectorEventArgs.#ctor(System.String,System.String,System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.param: The type of the detected barcode.
The decoded string value of the barcode.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.BarcodeDetectorMode
member.summary: Specifies the operational mode for a barcode detector within the VisioForge X engine. This enumeration defines how the barcode detector interacts with the video processing pipeline.
member.remarks: The choice of mode depends on whether the original video stream needs to be passed through the detector or if only the detection results are required.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.BarcodeDetectorMode.InputOnly
member.summary: In this mode, the barcode detector processes the input video stream but does not pass the video frames to its output. The output pad is effectively closed, meaning no video will be rendered or further processed after detection. This is useful when only the barcode detection results are needed, and the video stream itself is not required downstream.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.BarcodeDetectorMode.InputOutput

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings
member.summary: Provides a set of debugging and control settings for media blocks within the VisioForge X engine. These settings allow for fine-grained control over buffer handling, timing, and error simulation for testing and diagnostic purposes.
member.remarks: This class is primarily intended for developers and advanced users to debug and analyze the behavior of media pipelines. Modifying these settings can significantly alter the performance and stability of media processing.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.CheckImperfectOffset
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to send element messages if buffer offsets and offset_ends do not match up. This helps in debugging issues related to buffer segmentation and continuity.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.CheckImperfectTimestamp
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to send element messages if buffer timestamps and durations do not match up. This helps in debugging issues related to timing and synchronization.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.DataRate
member.summary: Gets or sets the data rate in bytes per second for (re)timestamping buffers. If set to 0, this feature is inactive. Useful for simulating specific data flow rates.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.DropAllocation
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to drop allocation queries. If set to true, the element will not forward allocation queries, which can be used for testing memory management scenarios.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.DropProbability
member.summary: Gets or sets the probability (0.0 to 1.0) that a buffer will be dropped. This can be used to simulate network packet loss or other data corruption scenarios.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.EOSAfter
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of buffers after which an End-Of-Stream (EOS) signal will be sent. A value of -1 means no EOS will be sent based on buffer count. Useful for testing stream termination.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.ErrorAfter
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of buffers after which an error will be simulated. A value of -1 means no error will be simulated based on buffer count. Useful for testing error handling.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.SignalHandoffs
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the identity element should emit a handoff signal when processing a buffer. This signal can be used for external monitoring or debugging of buffer flow.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.Silent
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the media block should operate in silent mode. In silent mode, less debug information might be printed to the console.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.SingleSegment
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to timestamp buffers and eat segments so as to appear as one continuous segment. This is useful for ensuring continuous playback even with fragmented input.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.SleepTime
member.summary: Gets or sets the time in microseconds to sleep between processing each buffer. This can be used to simulate processing delays or to throttle the pipeline for debugging purposes.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.Sync
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the media block should synchronize to the pipeline clock. Enabling synchronization ensures smooth playback and proper timing with other elements in the pipeline.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.DebugMediaBlockSettings.TimestampOffset
member.summary: Gets or sets the timestamp offset in nanoseconds for synchronization. A negative value indicates an earlier synchronization point, while a positive value indicates a later one.

member.summary: Compares the current instance with another object of the same type and returns an integer that indicates whether the current instance precedes, follows, or occurs in the same position in the sort order as the other object. The comparison is based on the font family name.

A value that indicates the relative order of the objects being compared. Value Meaning
Less than zero This instance precedes in the sort order.
Zero This instance occurs in the same position in the sort order as .
Greater than zero This instance follows in the sort order.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IBaseSourceX
member.summary: Defines a base interface for media sources within the VisioForge X engine. This interface serves as a marker for all source elements in the MediaBlocks framework.
member.remarks: Implementations of this interface are responsible for providing media data (video, audio, etc.) to the processing pipeline. Specific source types (e.g., file sources, camera sources, network sources) will implement this interface along with more specialized interfaces.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IEncoderTextInfo
member.summary: Defines an interface for components that can provide textual information about encoder parameters and capabilities. This is useful for debugging, logging, or displaying detailed encoder settings to the user.
member.remarks: Implementations of this interface are typically found in encoder configuration classes within the MediaBlocks framework. It allows for a standardized way to retrieve human-readable descriptions of complex encoder settings.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IEncoderTextInfo.GetParameters
member.summary: Retrieves a string representation of the encoder's current parameters. This string typically includes settings like bitrate, resolution, frame rate, and other configured options.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IEncoderTextInfo.GetCaps
member.summary: Retrieves a string representation of the encoder's capabilities (GStreamer caps). This string describes the media formats and properties that the encoder can handle.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IGetVideoStreamInfo
member.summary: Defines an interface for components that can provide detailed information about a video stream.
member.remarks: This interface is typically implemented by video sources or processing elements that can expose the properties of the video data they handle. It allows other parts of the system to query for video stream characteristics like resolution, frame rate, and codec.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IGetVideoStreamInfo.GetVideoStreamInfo
member.summary: Retrieves detailed information about the video stream.
member.returns: A object containing the video stream's properties.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IMediaBlocksPipelineCustomErrorHandler
member.summary: Defines an interface for custom error handling within a MediaBlocks pipeline. Implementations of this interface can intercept and process errors that occur during pipeline execution.
member.remarks: By implementing this interface and registering it with a MediaBlocks pipeline, developers can gain fine-grained control over how errors are managed. The method allows for custom logic to decide whether the pipeline should attempt to recover from an error or stop.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.IMediaBlocksPipelineCustomErrorHandler.ErrorHandler(Gst.Bus,Gst.Message,Gst.Pipeline)
member.summary: Handles an error message received from the GStreamer bus.
member.param: The GStreamer bus that emitted the error message.
The GStreamer object containing the error details.
The GStreamer instance where the error occurred.
member.returns: true if the error was handled and the pipeline should attempt to continue working; false if the error was not handled or if the pipeline should stop.

member.param: An object to compare with this instance.
member.returns:

Less than zero This instance precedes in the sort order.
Zero This instance occurs in the same position in the sort order as .
Greater than zero This instance follows in the sort order.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX
member.summary: Specifies various pixel formats for images and video frames within the VisioForge X engine. This enumeration defines how color data is stored and interpreted for each pixel.
member.remarks: The choice of pixel format is crucial for correct rendering, processing, and compatibility with different hardware and software components. It includes common RGB, indexed, and alpha-channel formats.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Indexed
member.summary: The pixel data contains color-indexed values, meaning the values are an index to colors in the system color table, as opposed to individual color values.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Gdi
member.summary: The pixel data contains GDI (Graphics Device Interface) colors.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Alpha
member.summary: The pixel data contains alpha values that are not premultiplied.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.PAlpha
member.summary: The pixel format contains premultiplied alpha values.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Extended
member.summary: Reserved for future use or extended pixel formats.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Canonical
member.summary: The default pixel format of 32 bits per pixel. The format specifies 24-bit color depth and an 8-bit alpha channel.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Undefined
member.summary: The pixel format is undefined.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.DontCare
member.summary: No pixel format is specified. This value is typically used as a placeholder or when the format is not relevant.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format1bppIndexed
member.summary: Specifies that the pixel format is 1 bit per pixel and that it uses indexed color. The color table therefore has two colors in it.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format4bppIndexed
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 4 bits per pixel, indexed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format8bppIndexed
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 8 bits per pixel, indexed. The color table therefore has 256 colors in it.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format16bppGrayScale
member.summary: The pixel format is 16 bits per pixel. The color information specifies 65536 shades of gray.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format16bppRgb555
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 16 bits per pixel; 5 bits each are used for the red, green, and blue components. The remaining bit is not used.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format16bppRgb565
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 16 bits per pixel; 5 bits are used for the red component, 6 bits are used for the green component, and 5 bits are used for the blue component.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format16bppArgb1555
member.summary: The pixel format is 16 bits per pixel. The color information specifies 32,768 shades of color, of which 5 bits are red, 5 bits are green, 5 bits are blue, and 1 bit is alpha.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format24bppRgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 24 bits per pixel; 8 bits each are used for the red, green, and blue components.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format32bppRgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 32 bits per pixel; 8 bits each are used for the red, green, and blue components. The remaining 8 bits are not used.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format32bppArgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 32 bits per pixel; 8 bits each are used for the alpha, red, green, and blue components.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format32bppPArgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 32 bits per pixel; 8 bits each are used for the alpha, red, green, and blue components. The red, green, and blue components are premultiplied, according to the alpha component.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format48bppRgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 48 bits per pixel; 16 bits each are used for the red, green, and blue components.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format64bppArgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 64 bits per pixel; 16 bits each are used for the alpha, red, green, and blue components.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format64bppPArgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 64 bits per pixel; 16 bits each are used for the alpha, red, green, and blue components. The red, green, and blue components are premultiplied according to the alpha component.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Max
member.summary: The maximum value for this enumeration.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType
member.summary: Represents the media types supported in RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol) payloads. This enumeration covers common audio and video codecs used in real-time streaming applications.
member.remarks: The RTP protocol is widely used for transmitting real-time data such as audio and video over IP networks. This enum helps in identifying the specific codec and format of the media being transported.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.H264
member.summary: H.264/AVC (Advanced Video Coding). Widely used video compression standard offering good quality and compression. Common in streaming, broadcasting, and video conferencing.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.H265
member.summary: H.265/HEVC (High Efficiency Video Coding). Next-generation video codec offering improved compression over H.264. Designed for 4K/8K resolutions and HDR content.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.VP8
member.summary: VP8 Video Codec. Open-source video codec developed by Google/WebM Project. Commonly used in WebRTC and web-based video applications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.VP9
member.summary: VP9 Video Codec Successor to VP8, offering improved compression efficiency. Used extensively by YouTube and other web platforms.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.JPEG
member.summary: Motion JPEG. Series of JPEG images used for video compression. Commonly used in security cameras and professional video equipment.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.RAW
member.summary: Raw Video Format. Uncompressed video data in its native format. Used in professional video production and high-quality capture.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.AAC
member.summary: Advanced Audio Coding (AAC). Digital audio compression standard offering high quality at lower bitrates. Widely used in streaming services, digital broadcasting, and mobile devices.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.Opus
member.summary: Opus Audio Codec. Open-source, highly versatile audio codec. Excellent for both speech and music, with low latency for real-time applications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.Vorbis
member.summary: Vorbis Audio Codec. Free and open-source audio compression format. Popular in game development and open-source multimedia applications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.MP3
member.summary: MPEG Audio Layer III (MP3). Popular audio compression format with wide device support. Commonly used for music distribution and streaming.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.PCM
member.summary: Pulse Code Modulation (PCM). Raw digital representation of sampled analog signals. Used in professional audio equipment and high-quality recordings.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.G722
member.summary: G.722 Audio Codec. Wideband audio codec operating at 16 kHz sampling rate. Common in VoIP systems and digital telephony applications.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.AMR
member.summary: Adaptive Multi-Rate (AMR) Audio Codec. Speech codec optimized for voice communication. Widely used in GSM and UMTS mobile phone systems.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.RTPMediaType.Unknown
member.summary: The media type is unknown or not specified.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.AESCipher
member.summary: Specifies the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) cipher configuration.

remarks.para: AES is a symmetric encryption algorithm widely used for securing data. This enumeration defines the available AES key sizes and cipher modes.
Both options use CBC (Cipher Block Chaining) mode, which provides better security than ECB mode by making each cipher block dependent on all previous blocks.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.AESCipher.AES_128
member.summary: AES encryption with 128-bit key using CBC (Cipher Block Chaining) mode.

remarks.para: Provides strong encryption suitable for most applications. Uses a 128-bit (16 byte) key and requires a 128-bit initialization vector (IV).
Performance characteristics: Faster than AES-256 while still providing adequate security for most use cases.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.AESCipher.AES_256
member.summary: AES encryption with 256-bit key using CBC (Cipher Block Chaining) mode.

remarks.para: Provides the highest level of security with a 256-bit (32 byte) key. Requires a 128-bit initialization vector (IV) regardless of key size.
Recommended for highly sensitive data or when regulatory compliance requires maximum encryption strength.
