member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.EncryptorDecryptorSettings
member.summary: Provides configuration settings for AES encryption and decryption operations.

remarks.para: This class encapsulates all necessary parameters for AES encryption/decryption, including the cipher type, encryption key, initialization vector (IV), and IV serialization options.
The settings support both AES-128 and AES-256 encryption modes using CBC (Cipher Block Chaining).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.EncryptorDecryptorSettings.Cipher
member.summary: Gets or sets the AES cipher configuration to use for encryption/decryption.
member.remarks: Determines the key size and encryption strength. AES-128 provides good security with better performance, while AES-256 offers maximum security.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.EncryptorDecryptorSettings.Key
member.summary: Gets or sets the encryption key as a hexadecimal string.
member.value: The encryption key in hexadecimal format.

remarks.para: The key length must match the selected cipher: - AES-128: 32 hex characters (16 bytes) - AES-256: 64 hex characters (32 bytes)
Example: "0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF" for AES-128

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.EncryptorDecryptorSettings.IV
member.summary: Gets or sets the initialization vector (IV) as a hexadecimal string.
member.value: The initialization vector in hexadecimal format. Must be 32 hex characters (16 bytes).

remarks.para: The IV is required for CBC mode and must be exactly 16 bytes (32 hex characters) regardless of the AES key size. Each encryption operation should use a unique IV for maximum security.
Example: "FEDCBA9876543210FEDCBA9876543210"

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.EncryptorDecryptorSettings.SerializeIV
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the initialization vector (IV) should be serialized with the encrypted data.
member.value: true if the IV should be prepended to the encrypted data; otherwise, false.

remarks.para: When enabled, the IV is stored at the beginning of the encrypted output, allowing the decryption process to extract it automatically. This simplifies IV management but slightly increases the output size.
This is a common practice as the IV does not need to be kept secret, only unique for each encryption operation.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Special.EncryptorDecryptorSettings.#ctor(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with the specified encryption key and initialization vector.
member.param: The encryption key as a hexadecimal string. Length must match the cipher requirements: 32 hex characters for AES-128, or 64 hex characters for AES-256.
The initialization vector as a hexadecimal string. Must be exactly 32 hex characters (16 bytes) for all AES cipher modes.
member.remarks: The constructor sets the default cipher to AES-128. Change the property after construction if AES-256 is required.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern
member.summary: Specifies the type of video test pattern to generate.

remarks.para: Test patterns are standardized video signals used for calibrating, testing, and troubleshooting video equipment and displays. They help verify proper signal transmission, color accuracy, and display geometry.
These patterns are commonly used in video editing applications as placeholders, for testing video pipelines, or as background elements.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Smpte
member.summary: SMPTE color bars test pattern.
member.remarks: The standard SMPTE (Society of Motion Picture and Television Engineers) color bars pattern used for calibrating video equipment. Contains vertical bars of primary and secondary colors.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Snow
member.summary: Random noise pattern resembling analog TV static.
member.remarks: Generates a random black and white noise pattern, similar to the "snow" seen on analog TVs with no signal. Useful for simulating signal loss or creating noise effects.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Black
member.summary: Solid black color fill.
member.remarks: Generates a completely black frame. Commonly used for fade-outs, blank segments, or as a neutral background.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.White
member.summary: Solid white color fill.
member.remarks: Generates a completely white frame. Used for maximum brightness testing, fade-ins, or as a high-contrast background.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Red
member.summary: Solid red color fill.
member.remarks: Generates a pure red frame. Useful for testing red channel response and color accuracy.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Green
member.summary: Solid green color fill.
member.remarks: Generates a pure green frame. Useful for testing green channel response and color accuracy.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Blue
member.summary: Solid blue color fill.
member.remarks: Generates a pure blue frame. Useful for testing blue channel response and color accuracy.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Checkers1
member.summary: Checkerboard pattern with 1x1 pixel squares.
member.remarks: Finest checkerboard pattern with alternating black and white pixels. Useful for testing display resolution and sharpness.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Checkers2
member.summary: Checkerboard pattern with 2x2 pixel squares.
member.remarks: Medium-fine checkerboard pattern. Good for testing scaling algorithms and pixel accuracy.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Checkers4
member.summary: Checkerboard pattern with 4x4 pixel squares.
member.remarks: Standard checkerboard pattern. Commonly used for testing video compression and transmission quality.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Checkers8
member.summary: Checkerboard pattern with 8x8 pixel squares.
member.remarks: Coarse checkerboard pattern. Useful for basic pattern testing and visual calibration.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Circular
member.summary: Circular pattern with concentric rings.
member.remarks: Generates concentric circles radiating from the center. Useful for testing aspect ratio, display geometry, and radial distortion.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Blink
member.summary: Alternating black and white frames.
member.remarks: Rapidly alternates between black and white frames. Useful for testing frame rate, response time, and temporal processing.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Smpte75
member.summary: SMPTE color bars at 75% intensity.
member.remarks: Similar to standard SMPTE bars but with colors at 75% intensity. Provides a less saturated version for broadcast compliance and preventing over-modulation.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.ZonePlate
member.summary: Zone plate pattern for frequency response testing.
member.remarks: A circular pattern with increasing spatial frequency toward the edges. Used to test resolution limits, aliasing, and frequency response of video systems.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.Gamut
member.summary: Color gamut test pattern.
member.remarks: Displays a range of colors to test the full color gamut capabilities of the display or video pipeline. Useful for color space verification.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.ChromaZonePlate
member.summary: Zone plate pattern with chromatic information.
member.remarks: Similar to the standard zone plate but includes color information. Used to test color resolution, chromatic aberration, and color subsampling artifacts.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTestPattern.SolidColor
member.summary: Solid color fill with configurable color.
member.remarks: Generates a frame filled with a single solid color. The specific color is typically configurable through additional parameters. Useful for color accuracy testing and as a background element.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEdit.VideoTransitionType
member.summary: Specifies the type of visual transition effect between video clips.

remarks.para: Video transitions provide smooth visual effects when switching between video clips in a timeline. These transitions are commonly used in video editing to create professional-looking scene changes.

The transitions are organized by categories: - Wipe transitions (1-99): Linear movements that reveal the new clip - Iris transitions (100-199): Shape-based reveals from center or corners - Clock/radial transitions (200-299): Circular and rotational effects - Matrix transitions (300-399): Grid and pattern-based effects - Fade transitions (500+): Opacity-based transitions
Transition codes follow the SMPTE 258M-2004 standard where applicable.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEffects.LUTInterpolationMode
member.summary: Specifies the method used for interpolating values between defined points in a 3D space. Each method offers different trade-offs between computational complexity, accuracy, and smoothness.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEffects.LUTInterpolationMode.Nearest
member.summary: Uses values from the nearest defined point without any actual interpolation. Fastest method but produces discontinuous results at boundaries between regions. Best used when computational speed is critical and discontinuities are acceptable.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEffects.LUTInterpolationMode.Trilinear
member.summary: Interpolates values using all 8 vertices of the surrounding cube. Performs three linear interpolations along each axis, hence "trilinear". Produces continuous results but may show artifacts at sharp transitions. Computational complexity: O(8) - requires 7 linear interpolations.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEffects.LUTInterpolationMode.Tetrahedral
member.summary: Interpolates using 4 points forming a tetrahedron within the cube. Divides the cube into 5-6 tetrahedra and selects the appropriate one. Provides better handling of diagonal gradients compared to trilinear. Computational complexity: O(4) - requires 3 linear interpolations.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEffects.LUTInterpolationMode.Pyramid
member.summary: Interpolates using 5 points forming a pyramid within the cube. Combines aspects of tetrahedral and trilinear methods. Good balance between accuracy and computational cost. Computational complexity: O(5) - requires 4 linear interpolations.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoEffects.LUTInterpolationMode.Prism
member.summary: Interpolates using 6 points forming a triangular prism within the cube. Useful for datasets with strong directional bias. Better preservation of sharp features along one primary axis. Computational complexity: O(6) - requires 5 linear interpolations.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX
member.summary: Represents detailed information about a video frame, including its dimensions, pixel format, stride, and frame rate. This class is used within the MediaBlocks framework to describe the characteristics of video data.
member.remarks: This information is crucial for configuring video processing blocks, encoders, and renderers, ensuring that video data is handled correctly throughout the pipeline. The property is automatically calculated for common RGB/RGBA formats if not explicitly set.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX._stride
member.summary: The internal backing field for the property.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.Width
member.summary: Gets or sets the width of the video frame in pixels.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.Height
member.summary: Gets or sets the height of the video frame in pixels.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.Format
member.summary: Gets or sets the pixel format of the video frame.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.Stride
member.summary: Gets or sets the stride (or pitch) of the video frame in bytes. This is the number of bytes required to store one row of pixels. If not explicitly set, it will be calculated automatically for common RGB/RGBA formats based on and .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.PlaneCount
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of planes in the video format. Optional. For planar formats (e.g., I420, NV12), this would be 2 or 3. For packed formats (e.g., RGB, YUY2), it's typically 1.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.Strides
member.summary: Gets or sets an array of strides for each plane in a planar video format. Optional.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.Offsets
member.summary: Gets or sets an array of offsets for each plane in a planar video format. Optional.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.FrameRate
member.summary: Gets or sets the frame rate of the video stream.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with default values.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.#ctor(System.Int32,System.Int32,VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFormatX,VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoFrameRate,System.Int32)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with specified dimensions, format, frame rate, and an optional stride.
member.param: The width of the video frame.
The height of the video frame.

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with specified dimensions and frame rate. The format defaults to .
member.param: The width of the video frame.
The height of the video frame.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameInfoX.ToString
member.summary: Returns a string that represents the current instance. The string includes the video format, resolution (widthxheight), and frame rate.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameX
member.summary: Represents a single video frame within the VisioForge MediaBlocks framework. This class extends to include the actual pixel data, timestamp, and duration.
member.remarks: VideoFrameX is designed for efficient handling of video frames in a pipeline, supporting direct memory access for performance. It provides methods for memory allocation, deallocation, data copying, and conversion to other frame types. Proper memory management using and is crucial to prevent memory leaks.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameX.Data
member.summary: Gets or sets a pointer to the unmanaged memory buffer containing the raw video data.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameX.DataSize
member.summary: Gets or sets the total size of the video data buffer in bytes.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameX.Timestamp
member.summary: Gets or sets the presentation timestamp of the video frame.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameX.Duration
member.summary: Gets or sets the duration of the video frame.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameX.Caps
member.summary: Gets or sets the GStreamer caps string that describes the media format of this frame.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameX.#ctor(System.Byte[],System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFormatX)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with a byte array of data. Memory is allocated and data is copied from the provided byte array.
member.param: The byte array containing the video data.
The width of the video frame.
The height of the video frame.
The stride (bytes per row) of the video frame.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameX.#ctor(System.Int32[],System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFormatX)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with an integer array of data. Memory is allocated and data is copied from the provided integer array.
member.param: The integer array containing the video data.
The width of the video frame.
The height of the video frame.
The stride (bytes per row) of the video frame.

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with an existing unmanaged data pointer. This constructor does not allocate new memory; it uses the provided pointer directly.
member.param: A pointer to the raw video data buffer.
The size of the data buffer in bytes.
The width of the video frame.
The height of the video frame.
The stride (bytes per row) of the video frame.

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with default values. No memory is allocated by this constructor.

member.summary: Determines whether this instance is empty (i.e., its pointer is ).
member.returns: true if this instance is empty; otherwise, false.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameX.Alloc
member.summary: Allocates unmanaged memory for the video data buffer based on the and . The field is updated accordingly.
member.remarks: This method should be called before writing pixel data to the pointer. It is crucial to call when the allocated memory is no longer needed.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameX.Alloc(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFormatX)
member.summary: Allocates unmanaged memory for the video data buffer with a specified size.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameX.Alloc(System.Int32)
member.param: The number of bytes to allocate for the video data.
member.remarks: This overload allows for direct control over the allocated buffer size, which can be useful for custom formats.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoFrameX.Free
member.summary: Frees the unmanaged memory previously allocated for the video data buffer.
member.remarks: This method should always be called to prevent memory leaks when the VideoFrameX instance is no longer needed, especially if or was used.

member.summary: Converts the raw video data from the unmanaged buffer into a new managed byte array.
member.returns: A new byte array containing the frame's video data.

member.summary: Copies all information and pixel data from a source to the current instance. If the data buffer size differs, the current instance's buffer will be reallocated.

member.summary: Converts the current instance into a legacy object. This conversion is useful for compatibility with older parts of the framework or external components.
member.returns: A new instance populated with data from the current frame.

member.summary: Creates a deep copy of the current instance. This involves allocating new memory for the data and copying all frame properties and pixel data.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoRendererSettingsX
member.summary: Represents settings for configuring the behavior of a video renderer within the VisioForge X engine. These settings control aspects like aspect ratio preservation and video conversion.
member.remarks: Proper configuration of these settings is important for optimizing video display quality and performance.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoRendererSettingsX.Letterbox
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether letterbox mode is enabled. When true, the video's aspect ratio is preserved by adding black bars if necessary. When false, the video may be stretched to fill the display area. The default value is true.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VideoRendererSettingsX.DisableVideoConverter
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the internal video converter should be disabled. Setting this to true can prevent automatic format conversions, which might be useful for specific scenarios or debugging, but could lead to compatibility issues if the source format is not directly supported by the renderer. The default value is false.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VUMeterXData.ChannelsCount
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of audio channels for which VU meter data is available.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VUMeterXData.Peak
member.summary: Gets or sets an array of peak audio levels for each channel. The values are typically normalized (e.g., 0.0 to 1.0 or -dB to 0 dB).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VUMeterXData.Decay
member.summary: Gets or sets an array of decay audio levels for each channel. Decay represents the gradual decrease in audio level after a peak.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VUMeterXData.RMS
member.summary: Gets or sets an array of RMS (Root Mean Square) audio levels for each channel. RMS provides a measure of the average power of the audio signal.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.VUMeterXEventArgs.MeterData
member.summary: Gets the associated with this event. This data contains the peak, decay, and RMS levels for each audio channel.

member.summary: Gets or sets an array of audio channel mapping routes. Each item in the array defines how a specific source channel should be mapped to a target channel, including any volume adjustments to be applied during the mapping.

member.summary: Gets or sets the total number of output channels. Set to 0 to maintain the same number of channels as the input. If set to a specific value, the output will have exactly that many channels, regardless of the input channel count.

member.summary: Gets or sets pan. Possible values range from �1.0 to 1.0, as follows. -1 - full left, 1 - full right. In a stereo recording, setting the pan level to -1.0 or 1.0 sends the entire signal to one channel. The other channel records silence. Panning has no effect for a mono recording.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioMixerValueType.Mono

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioMixerValueType.MixLevel
member.summary: Mix level. Controls the overall volume level of the mixed audio signal.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioMixerValueType.Pan
member.summary: Pan. Controls the balance between left and right channels. Values typically range from -1.0 (full left) to 1.0 (full right).

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioMixerValueType.Loudness

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioMixerValueType.Treble

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioMixerValueType.Bass

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioPCMConverterSettings
member.summary: Audio PCM converter settings. Defines the parameters for converting audio to PCM (Pulse Code Modulation) format. PCM is an uncompressed digital audio format commonly used for audio processing and storage.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioPCMConverterSettings.Channels
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of audio channels. 1 for mono (single channel) or 2 for stereo (dual channel).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioPCMConverterSettings.SampleRate
member.summary: Gets or sets the sample rate in Hz (samples per second). Common values include 8000, 16000, 22050, 44100, 48000, 96000. Higher sample rates provide better audio quality but require more storage.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioPCMConverterSettings.BPS
member.summary: Gets or sets the bits per sample (bit depth). Common values are 8, 16, 24, or 32 bits. Higher bit depth provides better dynamic range and audio quality.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioPCMConverterSettings.#ctor(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with specified audio parameters.
member.param: The number of audio channels. Use 1 for mono or 2 for stereo.
The bits per sample (bit depth). Common values are 8, 16, 24, or 32 bits.
The sample rate in Hz. Common values include 8000, 16000, 22050, 44100, 48000, 96000.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.ChromaKeySettings
member.summary: Chroma-key settings. Configures the chroma key (green screen) effect that replaces a specific color in the video with a background image. Commonly used for video compositing and special effects.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.ChromaKeySettings.Color
member.summary: Gets or sets the chroma key color to be replaced. This is typically green (RGB: 0, 255, 0) or blue (RGB: 0, 0, 255). Default is a green color (RGB: 128, 218, 128).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.ChromaKeySettings.BackgroundBitmap
member.summary: Gets the background image that will replace the chroma key color. This image will be shown where the chroma key color is detected in the video.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.ChromaKeySettings.ThresholdSensitivity
member.summary: Gets or sets the threshold sensitivity for color detection. Controls how closely a pixel must match the chroma key color to be replaced. Range is typically 0.0 to 1.0. Lower values require closer color matching. Default is 0.1804573.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.ChromaKeySettings.Smoothing
member.summary: Gets or sets the smoothing value for edge blending. Controls how smooth the edges are between the replaced area and the original video. Higher values create softer edges but may create a halo effect. Default is 0.08.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.ChromaKeySettings.#ctor(System.Drawing.Bitmap)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with a background image and default chroma key settings.
member.param: The background image that will replace the chroma key color in the video. This bitmap will be owned by the ChromaKeySettings instance and disposed when the instance is disposed.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.CustomProcessingFilter
member.summary: Represents a custom DirectShow filter to be inserted into the video processing pipeline.
member.remarks: This class allows developers to integrate their own or third-party DirectShow filters into the VisioForge pipeline. The filter can be identified by its name or its CLSID (Class Identifier).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.CustomProcessingFilter.Name
member.summary: Gets or sets the friendly name of the filter. This name is used to find the filter if the CLSID is not provided.
member.value: The display name of the filter. If a CLSID is specified, this name is used as the label for the filter within the processing graph.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.CustomProcessingFilter.CLSID
member.summary: Gets or sets the CLSID (Class Identifier) of the DirectShow filter.
member.value: The unique GUID that identifies the DirectShow filter. If this is set, it will be used to instantiate the filter, which is more reliable than using the name.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.CustomProcessingFilter.BeforeEffects
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the custom filter should be inserted before or after the standard VisioForge effects and sample grabber.
member.value: If set to true, the filter is placed early in the pipeline, before built-in effects. If false, it is placed after them. The default is true.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.CustomProcessingFilter.#ctor(System.String,System.Nullable{System.Guid},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.param: The friendly name of the filter. This is required to identify the filter, especially if no CLSID is provided.
The optional CLSID of the filter. Providing the CLSID is the recommended way to ensure the correct filter is loaded.
A boolean value that determines the filter's position in the pipeline. Set to true to place it before standard effects, or false to place it after. Defaults to true.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkAnalogOutput
member.summary: Specifies the analog video output format for Decklink devices.
member.remarks: This enumeration is used to configure the analog video output type when using Decklink hardware. Different output types support different quality levels and connection types.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkAnalogOutput.Auto
member.summary: Automatically selects the appropriate analog output format based on the connected device.
member.remarks: The system will detect the connected device and choose the best available output format. This is the recommended setting for most use cases.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkAnalogOutput.Composite
member.summary: Composite video output (single RCA/BNC connector).
member.remarks: Composite video combines all video information into a single signal. This is the lowest quality analog video connection but is widely compatible. Typically uses a yellow RCA connector or BNC connector.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkAnalogOutput.Component
member.summary: Component video output (YPbPr - three separate signals).
member.remarks: Component video separates the video signal into three parts: Y (luminance), Pb (blue color difference), and Pr (red color difference). This provides higher quality than composite or S-Video. Typically uses three RCA connectors (red, green, blue) or three BNC connectors.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkAnalogOutput.SVideo
member.summary: S-Video output (Y/C - separate luminance and chrominance).
member.remarks: S-Video (Separate Video) splits the video signal into two parts: luminance (Y) and chrominance (C). This provides better quality than composite but not as good as component. Uses a 4-pin mini-DIN connector.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkBlackToDeckInCapture
member.summary: Specifies the behavior for outputting black frames to the Decklink device during capture operations.
member.remarks: This enumeration controls how the Decklink hardware handles black frame generation when no video signal is being captured or when the capture is paused. This is important for maintaining proper signal output to connected devices.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkBlackToDeckInCapture.Default
member.summary: Uses the default black frame output behavior as determined by the Decklink driver.
member.remarks: The system will use the standard behavior configured in the Decklink driver settings. This is typically the recommended option for most scenarios.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkBlackToDeckInCapture.None
member.summary: Disables black frame output entirely.
member.remarks: No black frames will be sent to the output when capture is stopped or no signal is present. This may result in no signal being sent to connected devices during idle periods. Use with caution as some downstream devices may not handle the absence of signal properly.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkBlackToDeckInCapture.Digital
member.summary: Uses digital black frame generation through the SDK.
member.remarks: Black frames are generated digitally using the Decklink SDK. This ensures a clean digital black signal is sent to the output. Recommended for digital connections (SDI, HDMI).

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkBlackToDeckInCapture.Analogue
member.summary: Uses analogue black frame generation.
member.remarks: Black frames are generated using analogue circuitry. This option is optimized for analogue video outputs. Recommended when using composite, component, or S-Video connections.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkCaptureTimecodeSource
member.summary: Specifies the source for capturing timecode data from a Decklink card during video capture operations.
member.remarks: Timecode is essential for professional video production, providing frame-accurate time references for synchronization and editing. Different video formats and equipment may embed timecode in different parts of the video signal, so selecting the correct source is important for accurate timecode capture.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkCaptureTimecodeSource.Auto
member.summary: Automatically detects and selects the appropriate timecode source.
member.remarks: The system will attempt to detect timecode from both VITC and HANC sources and use whichever is available. If both are present, the system will choose based on signal quality and reliability. This is the recommended setting for most use cases.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkCaptureTimecodeSource.VITC
member.summary: Read timecode from VITC (Vertical Interval Time Code).
member.remarks: VITC embeds timecode data in the vertical blanking interval of the video signal, specifically in the non-visible lines between frames. This method is commonly used in analog video formats and some SD digital formats. VITC is particularly useful for tape-based workflows as it remains readable even when the tape is paused or moving slowly.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkCaptureTimecodeSource.HANC
member.summary: Read timecode from HANC (Horizontal Ancillary Data).
member.remarks: HANC stores timecode and other metadata in the horizontal ancillary data space of digital video signals. This is the standard method for HD-SDI and other modern digital video formats. HANC provides more reliable timecode transmission in digital workflows and supports additional metadata beyond just timecode.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo
member.summary: Provides comprehensive information about a Decklink capture device and manages device enumeration.
member.remarks: This class encapsulates all the information and functionality needed to work with a Decklink capture device, including video format enumeration, audio capabilities detection, and device configuration. It implements to receive notifications about format changes and input events during enumeration.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.DecklinkIntf
member.summary: Gets the underlying Decklink COM interface.
member.remarks: This property provides direct access to the native Decklink SDK interface. Use with caution as improper use can affect device stability.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.DecklinkInputIntf
member.summary: Gets the Decklink input interface for capture operations.
member.remarks: This interface is used to configure and control video/audio input from the Decklink device. It provides methods for enabling inputs, starting/stopping capture, and setting callbacks.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.SupportsFormatDetection
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the device supports automatic input format detection.
member.value: true if device supports format detection; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When format detection is supported, the device can automatically detect and adapt to changes in the input video format (resolution, frame rate, etc.) without manual configuration. This is particularly useful in live production environments where input sources may change.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.Name
member.summary: Gets or sets the display name of the Decklink device.
member.remarks: This is the human-readable name of the device, such as "DeckLink Mini Recorder 4K" or "DeckLink Studio 4K". This name is retrieved from the device driver.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.DeviceMode
member.summary: Gets the operating mode of the Decklink device.
member.remarks: Indicates whether the device is accessed through the WDM driver (for DirectShow compatibility) or through the VisioForge wrapper using the native Decklink SDK. The mode affects available features and performance characteristics.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.AudioOutput
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the device has audio capture capabilities.
member.remarks: When true, the device can capture audio along with video. This is detected during format enumeration by checking if audio packets are received from the device. Most professional Decklink cards support embedded audio capture.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.AudioFormats
member.summary: Gets the list of supported audio formats for the device.
member.remarks: Contains a list of audio format descriptions if the device supports audio capture. The list will be empty if the device doesn't support audio or if audio formats haven't been enumerated yet.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.Initiated
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the device information has been successfully initialized.
member.remarks: This property indicates whether the device has been properly initialized and is ready for use. Check this property before attempting to access device capabilities or perform operations.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.Fill(VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceMode,System.Boolean,System.Collections.Generic.List{VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkVideoFormat},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.String})
member.summary: Populates the device information with pre-enumerated data.
member.param: The operating mode of the device (WDM or VisioForge wrapper).
Indicates whether audio capture is available on this device.
List of supported video formats including resolution, frame rate, and pixel format.
List of supported audio format descriptions.
member.remarks: This method is typically used to populate device information that has been cached or retrieved from another source, avoiding the need to re-enumerate the device.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.#ctor(System.String,VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceMode,VisioForge.Libs.Decklink.SDK.IDeckLink)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.param: The display name of the Decklink device.
The operating mode (WDM or VisioForge wrapper).
member.remarks: Creates a new device information object and queries the device for its capabilities, including whether it supports automatic format detection. The device is not fully enumerated at this point - call to enumerate formats.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.GetVideoFormatsAsync
member.summary: Asynchronously enumerates all supported video formats for the device.
member.returns: A task that returns a list of supported video formats.
member.remarks: This method performs format enumeration by briefly starting capture with format detection enabled. The device will report all detected formats through callbacks. This process may take up to 1 second to complete. The enumeration is non-blocking and runs on a background thread.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.GetVideoFormats
member.summary: Synchronously enumerates all supported video formats for the device.
member.returns: A list of supported video formats.
member.remarks: This method starts a temporary capture session with format detection enabled to discover all supported formats. It waits up to 1 second for format detection to complete. During this process, the device may briefly flash or show signal on connected outputs. Any errors during enumeration are caught and logged, returning an empty list on failure.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.Dispose(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Releases unmanaged and - optionally - managed resources.
member.param: true to release both managed and unmanaged resources; false to release only unmanaged resources.
member.remarks: Properly releases COM interfaces to prevent resource leaks. This is critical for Decklink devices as they have limited resources and improper cleanup can prevent the device from being used by other applications.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.Finalize
member.summary: Finalizes an instance of the class.
member.remarks: Ensures COM interfaces are released even if Dispose() is not called explicitly. However, it's strongly recommended to call Dispose() explicitly or use a using statement.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.Dispose
member.summary: Performs application-defined tasks associated with freeing, releasing, or resetting unmanaged resources.
member.remarks: Call this method when you're finished using the device information object to ensure all COM interfaces are properly released and the device is available for other applications.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.VideoInputFormatChanged(VisioForge.Libs.Decklink.SDK._BMDVideoInputFormatChangedEvents,VisioForge.Libs.Decklink.SDK.IDeckLinkDisplayMode,VisioForge.Libs.Decklink.SDK._BMDDetectedVideoInputFormatFlags)

member.param: Flags indicating what aspects of the format have changed.

Flags indicating the detected signal characteristics (color space, etc.).

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.Decklink.DecklinkDeviceInfo.VideoInputFrameArrived(VisioForge.Libs.Decklink.SDK.IDeckLinkVideoInputFrame,VisioForge.Libs.Decklink.SDK.IDeckLinkAudioInputPacket)
