member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode
member.summary: NVENC error codes.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.Success
member.summary: This indicates that API call returned with no errors.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.NoEncodeDevice
member.summary: This indicates that no encode capable devices were detected.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.UnsupportedDevice
member.summary: This indicates that devices pass by the client is not supported.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.InvalidEncoderDevice
member.summary: This indicates that the encoder device supplied by the client is not valid.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.InvalidDevice
member.summary: This indicates that device passed to the API call is invalid.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.DeviceNotExist
member.summary: This indicates that device passed to the API call is no longer available and needs to be reinitialized. The clients need to destroy the current encoder session by freeing the allocated input output buffers and destroying the device and create a new encoding session.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.InvalidPointer
member.summary: This indicates that one or more of the pointers passed to the API call is invalid.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.InvalidEvent
member.summary: This indicates that completion event passed in ::NvEncEncodePicture() call is invalid.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.InvalidParameter
member.summary: This indicates that one or more of the parameter passed to the API call is invalid.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.InvalidCall
member.summary: This indicates that an API call was made in wrong sequence/order.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.OutOfMemory
member.summary: This indicates that the API call failed because it was unable to allocate enough memory to perform the requested operation.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.EncoderNotInitialized
member.summary: This indicates that the encoder has not been initialized with ::NvEncInitializeEncoder() or that initialization has failed. The client cannot allocate input or output buffers or do any encoding related operation before successfully initializing the encoder.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.UnsupportedParameter
member.summary: This indicates that an unsupported parameter was passed by the client.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.LockBusy
member.summary: This indicates that the ::NvEncLockBitstream() failed to lock the output buffer.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.NotEnoughBuffer
member.summary: This indicates that the size of the user buffer passed by the client is insufficient for the requested operation.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.InvalidVersion
member.summary: This indicates that an invalid struct version was used by the client.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.MapFailed
member.summary: This indicates that ::NvEncMapInputResource() API failed to map the client provided input resource.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.NeedMoreInput
member.summary: This indicates encode driver requires more input buffers to produce an output bitstream.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.EncoderBusy
member.summary: This indicates that the HW encoder is busy encoding and is unable to encode the input. The client should call ::NvEncEncodePicture() again after few milliseconds.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.EventNotRegistered
member.summary: This indicates that the completion event passed in ::NvEncEncodePicture() API has not been registered with encoder driver using ::NvEncRegisterAsyncEvent().

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.GenericError
member.summary: This indicates that an unknown internal error has occurred.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.IncompatibleClientKey
member.summary: This indicates that the client is attempting to use a feature that is not available for the license type for the current system.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.Unimplemeted
member.summary: This indicates that the client is attempting to use a feature that is not implemented for the current version.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.ResourceRegisterFailder
member.summary: This indicates that the ::NvEncRegisterResource API failed to register the resource.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.ResourceNotRegistered
member.summary: This indicates that the client is attempting to unregister a resource that has not been successfully registered.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.NVENCErrorCode.ResourceNotMapped
member.summary: This indicates that the client is attempting to unmap a resource that has not been successfully mapped.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.BitRate
member.summary: Gets or sets bitrate.
member.remarks: Range is 2 - 96.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.MaxBitRate
member.summary: Gets or sets maximal bitrate.
member.remarks: Range is 2 - 96.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.Complexity
member.summary: Gets or sets complexity.
member.remarks: With Speex, it is possible to vary the complexity allowed for the encoder. This is done by controlling how the search is performed with an integer ranging from 1 to 10 in a way that's similar to the -1 to -9 options to gzip and bzip2 compression utilities. For normal use, the noise level at complexity 1 is between 1 and 2 dB higher than at complexity 10, but the CPU requirements for complexity 10 is about 5 times higher than for complexity 1. In practice, the best trade-off is between complexity 2 and 4, though higher settings are often useful when encoding non-speech sounds like DTMF tones. Range is 1 - 10. Default is 3.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.Mode
member.summary: Gets or sets mode.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.BitrateControl
member.summary: Gets or sets bitrate control.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.UseDTX
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether DTX enabled.
member.remarks: Discontinuous transmission is an addition to VAD/VBR operation, that allows to stop transmitting completely when the background noise is stationary. In file-based operation, since we cannot just stop writing to the file, only 5 bits are used for such frames (corresponding to 250 bps).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.UseVAD
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether VAD enabled.
member.remarks: When enabled, voice activity detection detects whether the audio being encoded is speech or silence/background noise. VAD is always implicitly activated when encoding in VBR, so the option is only useful in non-VBR operation. In this case, Speex detects non-speech periods and encode them with just enough bits to reproduce the background noise. This is called ``comfort noise generation'' (CNG).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.UseAGC
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether AGC enabled.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.UseDenoise
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether denoise enabled.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.Quality
member.summary: Gets or sets quality.
member.remarks: Speex is a lossy codec, which means that it achives compression at the expense of fidelity of the input speech signal. Unlike some other speech codecs, it is possible to control the tradeoff made between quality and bit-rate. The Speex encoding process is controlled most of the time by a quality parameter that ranges from 0 to 10. Default value is 8.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.VLCEXEOutput.Video_H264_Quantizer
member.summary: Gets or sets H264 quantizer.
member.remarks: The range of the quantizer scale is 0-51: where 0 is lossless, 23 is default, and 51 is worst possible. A lower value is a higher quality and a subjectively sane range is 18-28. Consider 18 to be visually lossless or nearly so: it should look the same or nearly the same as the input but it isn't technically lossless. The range is exponential, so increasing the CRF value +6 is roughly half the bitrate while -6 is roughly twice the bitrate. General usage is to choose the highest CRF value that still provides an acceptable quality. If the output looks good, then try a higher value and if it looks bad then choose a lower value. (FFMPEG docs).

member.summary: Gets or sets video encoder.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_ErrorResilient
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether error resilient enabled. Error resilient mode indicates to the encoder that it should take measures appropriate for streaming over lossy or noisy links, if possible. Disabled by default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_DropframeThreshold
member.summary: Gets or sets dropframe threshold. Temporal resampling allows the codec to "drop" frames as a strategy to meet its target data rate. This can cause temporal discontinuities in the encoded video, which may appear as stuttering during playback. This trade-off is often acceptable, but for many applications is not. It can be disabled in these cases. This threshold is described as a percentage of the target data buffer. When the data buffer falls below this percentage of fullness, a dropped frame is indicated. Set the threshold to zero (0) to disable this feature. 0 by default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_SpatialResampling_Allowed
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether spatial resampling enabled. Spatial resampling allows the codec to compress a lower resolution version of the frame, which is then upscaled by the encoder to the correct presentation resolution. This increases visual quality at low data rates, at the expense of CPU time on the encoder/decoder.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_SpatialResampling_UpThreshold
member.summary: Gets or sets spatial resampling up watermark. This threshold is described as a percentage of the target data buffer. When the data buffer rises above this percentage of fullness, the encoder will step up to a higher resolution version of the frame.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_SpatialResampling_DownThreshold
member.summary: Gets or sets spatial resampling down watermark. This threshold is described as a percentage of the target data buffer. When the data buffer falls below this percentage of fullness, the encoder will step down to a lower resolution version of the frame.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_LagInFrames
member.summary: Gets or sets lag in frame. If set, this value allows the encoder to consume a number of input frames before producing output frames. This allows the encoder to base decisions for the current frame on future frames. This does increase the latency of the encoding pipeline, so it is not appropriate in all situations (ex: realtime encoding). This is a maximum value - the encoder may produce frames sooner than the given limit. Set this value to 0 to disable this feature.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_TokenPartition
member.summary: Gets or sets VP8 token partition mode. This defines VP8 partitioning mode for compressed data, i.e., the number of sub-streams in the bitstream. Used for parallelized decoding. Value 0 = one token partition. Value 1 = two token partitions. Value 2 = four token partitions. Value 3 = eight token partitions.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_MinQuantizer
member.summary: Gets or sets minimum (best quality) quantizer. The quantizer is the most direct control over the quality of the encoded image. The quantizer range is [0, 63].

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_MaxQuantizer
member.summary: Gets or sets maximum (worst quality) quantizer. The quantizer is the most direct control over the quality of the encoded image. The quantizer range is [0, 63].

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_UndershootPct
member.summary: Gets or sets rate control undershoot tolerance. This value, expressed as a percentage of the target bitrate, describes the target bitrate for easier frames, allowing bits to be saved for harder frames. Set to zero to use the codec default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_OvershootPct
member.summary: Gets or sets rate control overshoot tolerance. This value, expressed as a percentage of the target bitrate, describes the maximum allowed bitrate for a given frame. Set to zero to use the codec default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_Decoder_Buffer_Size
member.summary: Gets or sets decoder buffer size. This value indicates the amount of data that may be buffered by the decoding application. This value is expressed in units of time (milliseconds). For example, a value of 5000 indicates that the client will buffer (at least) 5000 ms worth of encoded data.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_Decoder_Buffer_InitialSize
member.summary: Gets or sets decoder buffer initial size. This value indicates the amount of data that will be buffered by the decoding application prior to beginning playback. This value is expressed in units of time (milliseconds).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_Decoder_Buffer_OptimalSize
member.summary: Gets or sets decoder buffer optimal size. This value indicates the amount of data that the encoder should try to maintain in the decoder's buffer. This value is expressed in units of time (milliseconds).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_Keyframe_MinInterval
member.summary: Gets or sets keyframe minimum interval. This value, expressed as a number of frames, prevents the encoder from placing a keyframe nearer than MinInterval to the previous keyframe. At least MinInterval frames non-keyframes will be coded before the next keyframe. Set MinInterval equal to MaxInterval for a fixed interval.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_Keyframe_MaxInterval
member.summary: Gets or sets keyframe maximum interval. This value, expressed as a number of frames, forces the encoder to code a keyframe if one has not been coded in the last MaxInterval frames. A value of 0 implies all frames will be keyframes. Set MinInterval equal to MaxInterval for a fixed interval.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_AutoAltRef
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether alternate reference frame will be added.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_ARNR_MaxFrames
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of frames to run the temporal filter over. The number of frames has to be less than or equal to lag in frames. The range is [0, 15]. Zero is the default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_ARNR_Strength
member.summary: Gets or sets the relative strength of the blur for the temporal filter. The range is [0, 6]. Zero is the weakest and six is the strongest. Three is the default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_ARNR_Type
member.summary: Gets or sets the type of blur for the temporal filter. The range is [1, 3]. Value 1 = a backward blur. Value 2 = a forward blur. Value 3 = a center blur (default).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_FixedKeyframeInterval
member.summary: Gets or sets fixed keyframe interval. If keyframe generation at a fixed interval is desired, set keyframe mode to kKeyframeModeDisabled, and set the interval using this method. This is most useful when dealing with a variable frame rate video source when a consistent keyframe interval is desired for streaming purposes.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_CPUUsed
member.summary: Gets or sets encoder complexity control. Changes in this value influences, among others, the encoder's selection of motion estimation methods. Values greater than 0 will increase encoder speed at the expense of quality. See libvpx documentation of the VP8ESETCPUUSED option for further information. Value range is [-16,16]. Values outside the range are ignored. The default value for configuration of libvpx used within webmdshow is 0.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_Keyframe_Mode
member.summary: Gets or sets keyframe placement mode. This value indicates whether the encoder should place keyframes at a fixed interval, or determine the optimal placement automatically (as governed by the KeyframeMinInterval and KeyframeMaxInterval).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_StaticThreshold
member.summary: Gets or sets static macroblock threshold. Sets the threshold for macroblocks to be treated as static by libvpx. When active it allows the encoder to skip blocks that it deems static based on the provided threshold. Values > 1000 not advisable, and any value greater than 0 can cause encoding artifacts due to skipped blocks. Values less than 0 are ignored.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_Decimate
member.summary: Gets or sets decimate value. Reduces frame rate of input video by discarding video frames based on Decimate value. For Decimate value N, and N >= 2, the VP8 encoder filter encodes only every Nth frame. Decimate values less or equal 1 disable decimation.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.PropertyPageType
member.summary: Specifies the type of property page to be displayed for a DirectShow filter.

remarks.para: The enumeration defines the various configuration interfaces available for DirectShow filters. Property pages provide a user interface for configuring the properties of a filter, such as a video capture device or a compressor.

These property pages are typically displayed as modal dialogs and allow users to:
Configure device-specific settings (brightness, contrast, etc.)
Select input sources and formats
Adjust compression parameters
View device or filter information
Not all filters support all property page types. The availability of specific property pages depends on the filter's implementation and the interfaces it exposes.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.PropertyPageType.Default
member.summary: The default property page for the filter.

remarks.para: Displays the primary configuration interface for the filter. The content varies depending on the filter type but typically includes the most commonly used settings.
This is the property page shown when no specific page type is requested. For many filters, this may be the only available property page.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.PropertyPageType.CaptureDisplay
member.summary: A property page for configuring the display of a capture device.

remarks.para:
Provides controls for adjusting video display properties such as:
Brightness and contrast
Hue and saturation
Gamma correction
White balance
This page is typically available for video capture devices and webcams that support the IAMVideoProcAmp interface.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.PropertyPageType.CaptureFormat
member.summary: A property page for selecting the output format of a capture device.

remarks.para:
Allows users to configure the capture format including:
Video resolution (width and height)
Frame rate
Color space and pixel format
Compression settings (if applicable)
This page is essential for optimizing capture quality and performance based on the intended use case and available system resources.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.PropertyPageType.CaptureSource
member.summary: A property page for selecting the input source of a capture device.

remarks.para:
Provides options for selecting and configuring input sources such as:
Composite, S-Video, or HDMI inputs
TV tuner channels
Audio input selection
Crossbar routing configuration
This page is typically available for capture cards and TV tuners with multiple input options.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.PropertyPageType.CompressorConfig
member.summary: A property page for configuring the settings of a compressor.

remarks.para:
Provides detailed configuration options for video or audio compressors including:
Bitrate and quality settings
Keyframe intervals
Advanced codec-specific parameters
Profile and level selection
The specific options available depend on the compressor implementation. Some compressors may offer simple quality sliders while others provide extensive professional-level controls.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.PropertyPageType.CompressorAbout
member.summary: A property page that displays information about the compressor.

remarks.para:
Shows informational content about the compressor such as:
Codec name and version
Vendor information and copyright
Supported features and formats
License information
This page is read-only and does not provide configuration options. It's useful for identifying the exact codec being used and its capabilities.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioSource
member.summary: Represents an audio source that can be used in video editing operations.

remarks.para: The class defines an audio file or stream that can be included in a video editing project. It supports various configurations including multi-segment playback, stream selection, playback rate control, and synchronization with video files.

Key features:
Support for multiple file segments with custom start/stop times
Multiple audio stream selection from multi-stream files
Variable playback rate (speed up or slow down audio)
Audio/video synchronization capabilities

Common use cases:
Adding background music to a video
Extracting audio from video files
Creating audio mashups with multiple segments
Synchronizing audio tracks with video content

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioSource.Filename
member.summary: Gets or sets the path to the audio file.
member.value: The full or relative path to the audio file. Supports various audio formats including MP3, WAV, AAC, OGG, FLAC, WMA, and audio streams from video files (MP4, AVI, MKV, etc.).
member.remarks: The file path can be absolute or relative. When extracting audio from video files, ensure the property is set correctly to select the desired audio stream.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioSource.Segments
member.summary: Gets or sets the list of segments to be played from the audio file.
member.value: An array of objects defining the portions of the audio file to include. Each segment specifies a start and stop time within the file.

remarks.para: Segments allow you to use specific portions of an audio file without modifying the original file. Multiple segments can be defined to create a non-linear playback sequence.
If segments overlap, they will be played sequentially, not simultaneously. To play the entire file, use a single segment with null start and stop times.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioSource.StreamNumber
member.summary: Gets or sets the audio stream number to use from multi-stream files.
member.value: The zero-based index of the audio stream to extract. Default is 0 (first audio stream).

remarks.para: Many video files contain multiple audio streams (e.g., different languages, commentary tracks). This property allows selection of a specific audio stream when the source file contains multiple streams.
Use 0 for the first audio stream, 1 for the second, and so on. If the specified stream doesn't exist, the first available audio stream will be used.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioSource.Rate
member.summary: Gets or sets the playback rate (speed) of the audio.
member.value: The playback rate as a multiplier. 1.0 = normal speed (100%), 2.0 = double speed (200%), 0.5 = half speed (50%). Valid range is typically 0.1 to 10.0.

remarks.para: Changing the playback rate affects both the speed and pitch of the audio unless pitch correction is applied. Values greater than 1.0 speed up playback, while values less than 1.0 slow it down.

Common use cases:
Creating slow-motion effects (rate < 1.0)
Creating fast-forward effects (rate > 1.0)
Adjusting audio duration to match video timing
Creating comedic or dramatic effects

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioSource.FileToSync
member.summary: Gets or sets the file path used for synchronization reference.
member.value: The path to the file that this audio should be synchronized with, typically the source video file when extracting audio from a video container.

remarks.para: This property is crucial when extracting audio from video files to maintain proper audio/video synchronization. It ensures that the audio timing matches the video timing from the source file, preventing sync issues.

Common scenarios requiring FileToSync:
Extracting audio track from a video file
Replacing audio in a video while maintaining sync
Using audio from one video file with visuals from another

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioSource.IgnorePlaybackCheck
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to bypass file validation and playback compatibility checks.
member.value: true to skip validation checks and attempt to process the file regardless of potential issues; false to perform normal validation. Default is false.

remarks.para:
When set to true, the system will attempt to process the audio file even if:
The file format is not recognized
The codec is not supported
The file appears to be corrupted
Required codecs are missing

Use this option with caution as it may lead to unexpected behavior or processing failures. It's primarily intended for advanced scenarios where you need to work with non-standard or proprietary formats.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioSource.#ctor(System.String,System.Nullable{System.TimeSpan},System.Nullable{System.TimeSpan},System.String,System.Int32,System.Double)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with a single time segment.
member.param: The path to the audio file. Supports various formats including MP3, WAV, AAC, OGG, FLAC, and audio streams from video containers.
The start time of the segment to use. Set to null to start from the beginning of the file. If both and are null, the entire file is used.
The stop time of the segment to use. Set to null to play until the end of the file. If both and are null, the entire file is used.
Optional file path for synchronization. Required when extracting audio from video files to maintain proper audio/video sync. Typically the same as for video sources.
The zero-based index of the audio stream to use from multi-stream files. Default is 0 (first stream).
The playback rate multiplier. 1.0 = normal speed (100%), 2.0 = double speed (200%), 0.5 = half speed (50%). Valid range is typically 0.1 to 10.0.
member.remarks: This constructor creates an audio source with a single continuous segment. For multiple non-contiguous segments, use the constructor that accepts a array.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioTrackEffect
member.summary: Represents the base class for audio effects that can be applied to an audio track.

remarks.para: The class serves as the foundation for all audio effects that can be applied to audio tracks in video editing operations. It provides timing control to specify when an effect should start and stop within the track.

Key features:
Time-based effect application with start and stop times
Support for applying effects to entire tracks or specific segments
Automatic duration calculation based on start/stop times
Base class for specialized effects like volume, fade, and envelope effects
This is an abstract base class that should be inherited by specific effect implementations such as or .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioTrackEffect.StartTime
member.summary: Gets or sets the time at which the effect begins to be applied.
member.value: A representing the start time of the effect, or null to start from the beginning of the track. When both and are null, the effect is applied to the entire track.

remarks.para: The start time is relative to the beginning of the audio track, not the overall timeline. For example, if an audio track starts at 10 seconds in the timeline and you set StartTime to 5 seconds, the effect will begin 5 seconds after the audio track starts playing.

Common scenarios:
Set to null to apply the effect from the track's beginning
Set to a specific time to delay the effect application
Use with StopTime to create a time window for the effect

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioTrackEffect.StopTime
member.summary: Gets or sets the time at which the effect stops being applied.
member.value: A representing the stop time of the effect, or null to continue until the end of the track. When both and are null, the effect is applied to the entire track.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioTrackEffect.Duration
member.summary: Gets the duration for which the effect is applied.
member.value: A representing the duration of the effect, or null if either or is null.

remarks.para: The duration is automatically calculated as the difference between StopTime and StartTime. If either time is not set (null), the duration cannot be determined and returns null.

This property is useful for:
Validating effect timing before application
Displaying effect duration in user interfaces
Calculating overlap between multiple effects

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioTrackEffect.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.

remarks.para: Creates an audio effect with no time constraints. By default, both and are set to null, which means the effect will be applied to the entire duration of the audio track.
This constructor is typically called by derived classes to initialize the base timing properties. Derived classes can then set specific timing if needed.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioVolumeEnvelopeEffect
member.summary: Represents an audio volume envelope effect that applies a constant volume level to a portion of an audio track.

remarks.para:
Key features:
Set a constant volume level for a specific time range
Volume is specified as a percentage (0-100)
Can be applied to entire track or specific segments
Multiple envelope effects can be applied to create complex volume curves
Unlike which creates gradual transitions, this effect applies an immediate volume change at the start time and maintains it until the stop time.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioVolumeEnvelopeEffect.Level
member.summary: Gets or sets the volume level to apply during the effect period.
member.value:
The volume level as a percentage. Valid range is 0 to 100, where:
0 = Complete silence (mute)
50 = Half volume
100 = Original volume (no change)
Values above 100 may cause distortion

remarks.para: The volume level is applied as a multiplier to the original audio amplitude. For example, a level of 50 will reduce the audio to half its original volume.

Common use cases:
0-20: Background/ambient level
30-50: Reduced volume for ducking under narration
70-90: Slightly reduced for mixing
100: Original level

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioVolumeEnvelopeEffect.#ctor(System.Int32)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with a specified volume level.
member.param: The volume level as a percentage (0-100). 0 represents silence, 100 represents original volume. Values outside this range may be clamped or cause audio distortion.

remarks.para: By default, the effect is configured to apply to the entire audio track (StartTime and StopTime are null). To apply the effect to a specific time range, set the and properties after construction.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioVolumeFadeEffect
member.summary: Represents an audio volume fade effect that creates smooth volume transitions over time.

remarks.para: The class enables creation of professional fade-in and fade-out effects on audio tracks. It provides smooth volume transitions from a minimum to maximum level at the beginning (fade-in) and from maximum to minimum at the end (fade-out) of the effect period.

Key features:
Independent control of fade-in and fade-out durations
Configurable minimum and maximum volume levels
Smooth, linear volume transitions
Can create fade-in only, fade-out only, or combined effects

The effect timeline works as follows:
Effect starts at StartTime with MinLevel volume
Volume fades from MinLevel to MaxLevel over FadeInDuration
Volume remains at MaxLevel until (StopTime - FadeOutDuration)
Volume fades from MaxLevel to MinLevel over FadeOutDuration
Effect ends at StopTime

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioVolumeFadeEffect.MinLevel
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum volume level during fade transitions.
member.value:
The minimum volume level as a percentage (0-100). This is the volume level at:
The start of fade-in (before fading up to MaxLevel)
The end of fade-out (after fading down from MaxLevel)
Default should typically be 0 for complete fades.

remarks.para:
Common values:
0: Complete silence (typical for full fades)
10-20: Subtle background level
30-50: Reduced but audible level
Setting MinLevel above 0 creates a partial fade effect where audio never completely disappears, useful for maintaining some ambient sound or preventing jarring silence.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioVolumeFadeEffect.MaxLevel
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum volume level during the sustained portion of the effect.
member.value:
The maximum volume level as a percentage (0-100). This is the volume level:
Reached after fade-in completes
Maintained during the middle portion of the effect
Starting point for fade-out
Typically set to 100 for normal volume.

remarks.para: The MaxLevel represents the target volume after fade-in and the starting volume for fade-out. It's maintained during the sustained portion between the fade transitions.

Common values:
100: Original/normal volume
80-90: Slightly reduced for mixing
110-120: Boosted volume (use carefully to avoid distortion)

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioVolumeFadeEffect.FadeInDuration
member.summary: Gets or sets the duration of the fade-in transition.
member.value: A representing how long it takes to fade from to at the beginning of the effect. Set to to disable fade-in (start immediately at MaxLevel).

remarks.para: The fade-in begins at the effect's StartTime and transitions the volume from MinLevel to MaxLevel over the specified duration. The transition is typically linear.

Common fade-in durations:
0.5-1 second: Quick, subtle fade for short clips
2-3 seconds: Standard fade for most content
5-10 seconds: Slow, dramatic fade for atmospheric effects

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioVolumeFadeEffect.FadeOutDuration
member.summary: Gets or sets the duration of the fade-out transition.
member.value: A representing how long it takes to fade from to at the end of the effect. Set to to disable fade-out (end immediately at MinLevel).

remarks.para: The fade-out begins at (StopTime - FadeOutDuration) and transitions the volume from MaxLevel to MinLevel. The fade-out must complete by the effect's StopTime.

Important considerations:
FadeOutDuration should not exceed the total effect duration
If FadeInDuration + FadeOutDuration exceeds effect duration, fades may overlap
The transition is typically linear but may vary by implementation

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.AudioVolumeFadeEffect.#ctor(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.TimeSpan,System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with specified fade parameters.
member.param: The minimum volume level as a percentage (0-100). This is the starting volume for fade-in and ending volume for fade-out. Typically 0 for complete fades.
The maximum volume level as a percentage (0-100). This is the target volume after fade-in and the starting volume for fade-out. Typically 100 for normal volume.
The duration of the fade-in transition. Set to to disable fade-in and start immediately at maxLevel.
The duration of the fade-out transition. Set to to disable fade-out and end immediately at minLevel.

remarks.para: By default, the effect applies to the entire track (StartTime and StopTime are null). For fade-out effects, you must set appropriate StartTime and StopTime values after construction to ensure the fade-out occurs at the desired position.
The total effect duration should be at least (fadeInDuration + fadeOutDuration) to avoid overlapping fades. If the durations overlap, the behavior may vary by implementation.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.FFMPEGStream
member.summary: Represents a stream specification for FFMPEG operations in video editing.

remarks.para: The class provides a way to identify and select specific streams from multimedia files when using FFMPEG-based operations. It supports various stream types including video, audio, and subtitle streams.

Stream identification can be done using:
Stream type identifiers: "v" for video, "a" for audio, "s" for subtitles
Numeric indices: "0", "1", "2", etc. for specific stream positions
Combined selectors: "v:0" for first video stream, "a:1" for second audio stream

This class is typically used when:
Extracting specific streams from multi-stream files
Mapping streams during transcoding operations
Selecting streams for processing or muxing
Working with files containing multiple audio tracks or subtitle streams

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.FFMPEGStream.Filename
member.summary: Gets or sets the path to the media file containing the stream.
member.value: The full or relative path to the media file. Supports all formats that FFMPEG can handle, including but not limited to: MP4, MKV, AVI, MOV, MP3, WAV, FLAC, and many others.

remarks.para: The file should be accessible and readable by the FFMPEG process. Both absolute and relative paths are supported, though absolute paths are recommended for reliability.
FFMPEG supports a vast array of multimedia formats and containers. The specific streams available will depend on the file's content and encoding.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.FFMPEGStream.ID
member.summary: Gets or sets the stream identifier used to select a specific stream from the file.
member.value:
A string identifier that specifies which stream to select. Valid formats include:
"v" - Select the default (first) video stream
"a" - Select the default (first) audio stream
"s" - Select the default (first) subtitle stream
"0", "1", "2", etc. - Select stream by absolute index
"v:0", "v:1" - Select specific video stream by index
"a:0", "a:1" - Select specific audio stream by index
"s:0", "s:1" - Select specific subtitle stream by index

remarks.para: Stream indices are zero-based. The first stream of each type has index 0. When using type-specific selectors (v:, a:, s:), the index refers only to streams of that type, not the absolute stream position in the file.

Examples of stream selection:
"v" selects the first video stream found
"a:2" selects the third audio stream (if it exists)
"3" selects the fourth stream in the file, regardless of type
To determine available streams in a file, use FFMPEG's stream analysis capabilities or media information tools before specifying the stream ID.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffect
member.summary: Base abstract class for GPU-accelerated video effects.

remarks.para: This class serves as the foundation for all GPU-based video effects in the VisioForge framework. GPU effects leverage hardware acceleration to provide high-performance video processing with minimal CPU usage.
Derived classes must implement the interface and override the method to specify the concrete effect type.
Effects can be configured to apply during specific time ranges using and properties. Setting both to zero (default) applies the effect for the entire duration.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffect.UpdateRequired
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the effect settings have changed and need to be applied.
member.remarks: This flag is automatically set to true when is called. The video processing pipeline checks this flag to determine if GPU shader parameters need updating. After the effect is applied, the pipeline resets this flag to false.
member.value: true if the effect parameters have been modified and need to be applied; otherwise, false.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffect.StartTime
member.summary: Gets or sets the time when the effect should start being applied.
member.remarks: Set to (default) to apply the effect from the beginning. The effect will not be rendered before this time position is reached in the video stream.
member.value: The start time for the effect. Default is .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffect.StopTime
member.summary: Gets or sets the time when the effect should stop being applied.
member.remarks: Set to (default) to apply the effect until the end. The effect will not be rendered after this time position is passed in the video stream. If both and are zero, the effect is applied for the entire duration.
member.value: The stop time for the effect. Default is .

member.summary: Gets or sets the unique name identifier for this effect instance.
member.remarks: The name can be used to retrieve a specific effect instance from a collection of effects for runtime manipulation. It's recommended to use descriptive names when multiple effects of the same type are applied.
member.value: A string identifier for the effect. Can be null or empty if identification is not needed.

member.remarks: When disabled, the effect is bypassed in the processing pipeline without being removed. This allows for toggling effects on/off without the overhead of adding/removing them.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectBlur
member.summary: Represents a GPU-accelerated blur effect for video processing.

remarks.para: The blur effect applies a Gaussian blur filter to soften the video image by averaging neighboring pixels. This effect is commonly used for creating depth-of-field effects, privacy protection (blurring faces or sensitive information), or artistic purposes.

The blur intensity is controlled by the property, where higher values produce stronger blur effects. The effect is implemented using GPU shaders for optimal performance, allowing real-time processing of high-resolution video.
This effect implements the interface for type-safe access to blur-specific properties.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectBlur.Value
member.summary: Gets or sets the blur intensity value.

remarks.para: The blur value determines the strength of the Gaussian blur applied to the video. A value of 0 produces no blur (original image), while 100 produces maximum blur.

Internally, this value is mapped to the blur kernel size and sigma parameters. Higher values use larger blur kernels, resulting in more pronounced blur effects but potentially higher GPU processing requirements.

31-60 = Medium blur, suitable for background defocus
61-100 = Strong blur, suitable for privacy protection or heavy stylization

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectBrightness
member.summary: Represents a GPU-accelerated brightness adjustment effect for video processing.

remarks.para: The brightness effect adjusts the overall luminance of the video image by adding or subtracting a constant value to/from all pixel color components. This creates a uniform lightening or darkening of the entire image while preserving color relationships and saturation.

The effect is implemented using GPU shaders for optimal performance, enabling real-time brightness adjustment even on high-resolution video streams. The brightness adjustment is applied in linear color space to ensure perceptually uniform results.
This effect implements the interface for type-safe access to brightness-specific properties.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectBrightness.Value
member.summary: Gets or sets the brightness adjustment value.

remarks.para: The brightness value controls how much the image is lightened or darkened. A value of 128 represents no change (neutral), values above 128 lighten the image, and values below 128 darken it.

The adjustment is applied uniformly to all color channels (RGB) to maintain color balance. Extreme values may cause clipping, where very bright areas become pure white (255) or very dark areas become pure black (0).
For best results, combine brightness adjustment with contrast adjustment to maintain image detail while changing overall luminance.

member.value:
An integer value between 0 and 255, where:
0 = Maximum darkening (near black)
1-127 = Darkening effect
128 = No change (original brightness)
129-255 = Lightening effect
255 = Maximum lightening (near white)

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with specified parameters.

An optional name identifier for this effect instance. Default is "Brightness". Used to retrieve specific effect instances from a collection.
The time at which the effect should start being applied. Default is , which applies the effect from the beginning.
The time at which the effect should stop being applied. Default is , which applies the effect until the end.

For subtle adjustments, use values close to 128. For dramatic effects, use values closer to the extremes (0 or 255), but be aware this may result in loss of detail in shadows or highlights.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectContrast
member.summary: Represents a GPU-accelerated contrast adjustment effect for video processing.

remarks.para: The contrast effect adjusts the difference between light and dark areas in the video image. It works by expanding or compressing the tonal range around a midpoint (typically 128), making light areas lighter and dark areas darker (increased contrast) or bringing all tones closer to middle gray (decreased contrast).

The effect is implemented using GPU shaders for optimal performance, enabling real-time contrast adjustment even on high-resolution video streams. The contrast adjustment preserves the overall brightness of the image while modifying the distribution of tones.
This effect implements the interface for type-safe access to contrast-specific properties.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectContrast.Value
member.summary: Gets or sets the contrast adjustment value.

remarks.para: The contrast value controls the difference between light and dark areas in the image. A value of 128 represents no change (neutral), values above 128 increase contrast, and values below 128 decrease contrast.

Higher contrast values create more dramatic images with deeper blacks and brighter whites, but may result in loss of detail in shadows and highlights (clipping). Lower contrast values create flatter, more subdued images that may appear washed out but preserve more detail.
The contrast adjustment is applied using a linear interpolation formula: output = (input - 128) * (contrast / 128) + 128
For optimal results, contrast adjustment is often combined with brightness adjustment to maintain the desired overall luminance while enhancing or reducing tonal separation.

member.value:
An integer value between 0 and 255, where:
0 = Minimum contrast (flat gray image)
1-127 = Reduced contrast (flatter, softer image)
128 = No change (original contrast)
129-255 = Increased contrast (more dramatic, punchy image)
255 = Maximum contrast (extreme black/white separation)

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectContrast.#ctor(System.Boolean,System.Int32,System.String,System.TimeSpan,System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with specified parameters.
member.param: true to enable the effect immediately; false to create the effect in a disabled state.

An optional name identifier for this effect instance. Default is "Contrast". Used to retrieve specific effect instances from a collection.
The time at which the effect should start being applied. Default is , which applies the effect from the beginning.
The time at which the effect should stop being applied. Default is , which applies the effect until the end.

remarks.para: The constructor initializes all properties and sets the effect type to . If both and are zero (default), the effect will be applied for the entire duration of the video.
For natural-looking results, use moderate values (80-180). For artistic effects, more extreme values can be used, but be aware of potential detail loss in shadows and highlights.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType
member.summary: Defines the types of GPU-accelerated video effects available in the VisioForge framework.

remarks.para: This enumeration represents all GPU-based video effects that can be applied to video streams. Each effect type corresponds to a specific GPU shader implementation that performs the video processing operation using hardware acceleration.
GPU effects provide superior performance compared to CPU-based effects, especially for high-resolution video processing, as they leverage parallel processing capabilities of modern graphics hardware.

Effects can be categorized into several groups:
Color adjustments: Brightness, Contrast, Saturation, Darkness
Blur effects: Blur, DirectionalBlur
Stylization: Greyscale, Monochrome, Invert, OldMovie, NightVision
Edge detection: Contour, Emboss
Enhancement: Sharpen, Denoise, DeinterlaceBlend
Special effects: Pixelate, EquiRectangular360, EquiAngularCubemap360

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.Undefined
member.summary: Represents an undefined or uninitialized effect type.
member.remarks: This value is used as a default or error state. An effect with this type should not be processed by the video pipeline.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.Greyscale
member.summary: Converts color video to grayscale by removing all color information.
member.remarks: The grayscale conversion uses standard luminance weights (0.299R + 0.587G + 0.114B) to create perceptually accurate monochromatic images that preserve brightness relationships.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.Blur
member.summary: Applies a Gaussian blur filter to soften the video image.
member.remarks: This effect averages neighboring pixels using a Gaussian kernel, creating a smooth, out-of-focus appearance. Useful for backgrounds, privacy protection, or artistic effects. The blur intensity can be adjusted through the effect's Value property.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.Invert
member.summary: Inverts all color values in the video to create a negative image effect.
member.remarks: Each pixel's RGB values are inverted (255 - original value), creating an effect similar to photographic negatives. White becomes black, red becomes cyan, etc.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.OldMovie
member.summary: Simulates the appearance of old film footage with grain, scratches, and sepia toning.
member.remarks: This complex effect combines multiple techniques including noise generation, random scratches, vignetting, and color grading to recreate the nostalgic look of vintage cinema.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.DirectionalBlur
member.summary: Applies motion blur in a specific direction to simulate movement or speed.
member.remarks: Unlike standard blur which is uniform in all directions, directional blur creates streaking effects along a specified angle. Commonly used to convey motion or create dynamic visual effects.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.Monochrome
member.summary: Converts video to a two-color (typically black and white) image using threshold-based processing.
member.remarks: Different from grayscale, monochrome uses a threshold value to determine whether each pixel becomes pure black or pure white, creating high-contrast artistic effects or improving text readability.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.Pixelate
member.summary: Creates a mosaic effect by reducing the resolution and displaying enlarged pixels.
member.remarks: This effect divides the image into blocks and fills each block with a single color, creating a blocky, pixelated appearance. Often used for censorship or retro gaming aesthetics.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.Brightness
member.summary: Adjusts the overall luminance of the video by adding or subtracting brightness values.
member.remarks: Brightness adjustment uniformly increases or decreases the RGB values of all pixels, making the entire image lighter or darker. Values above 128 lighten, below 128 darken.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.Contrast
member.summary: Adjusts the difference between light and dark areas to enhance or reduce image definition.
member.remarks: Contrast modification expands or compresses the tonal range around the midpoint, making lights lighter and darks darker (high contrast) or bringing all tones closer to middle gray (low contrast).

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.Saturation
member.summary: Controls the intensity of colors in the video from vibrant to completely desaturated.
member.remarks: Saturation adjustment modifies the purity of colors without affecting brightness. Zero saturation produces grayscale, while high saturation creates vivid, intense colors.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.Darkness
member.summary: Applies a darkening effect to create moody or dramatic atmospheres.
member.remarks: Similar to brightness reduction but optimized for creating specific atmospheric effects, often preserving some highlight detail while deepening shadows and midtones.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.Contour
member.summary: Detects and highlights edges in the video to create line-art style effects.
member.remarks: Uses edge detection algorithms (typically Sobel or similar) to identify areas of high contrast change, rendering them as lines while suppressing uniform areas.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.DeinterlaceBlend
member.summary: Removes interlacing artifacts by blending alternating scan lines.
member.remarks: Designed for processing interlaced video content, this effect blends odd and even fields to eliminate comb-like artifacts that appear on moving objects in interlaced footage.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.NightVision
member.summary: Simulates night vision or thermal imaging equipment appearance.
member.remarks: Creates a green-tinted, high-contrast effect similar to military night vision goggles, often including simulated noise and limited dynamic range for authenticity.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.Sharpen
member.summary: Enhances image detail by amplifying high-frequency components.
member.remarks: Sharpening increases edge contrast to make details appear more defined. Uses convolution kernels to detect and enhance edges while preserving overall image structure.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.Denoise
member.summary: Reduces video noise and grain while preserving important detail.
member.remarks: Applies spatial and/or temporal noise reduction algorithms to clean up grainy or noisy video, particularly useful for low-light footage or compressed sources.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.Emboss
member.summary: Creates a 3D relief effect by highlighting edges with light and shadow.
member.remarks: Simulates the appearance of embossed or carved surfaces by applying directional edge detection and rendering the result as if lit from a specific angle.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.EquiRectangular360
member.summary: Converts equirectangular 360-degree video projection to standard flat view.

remarks.para: Transforms spherical 360° video content (typically in 2:1 aspect ratio) into a perspective-correct flat projection. This effect is automatically applied when 360° metadata is detected in the video file.
The transformation allows viewing specific portions of the 360° sphere on standard displays, with controls for pan, tilt, and field of view adjustment.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.GPUVideoEffectType.EquiAngularCubemap360
member.summary: Converts equiangular cubemap 360-degree video projection to standard flat view.

remarks.para: Transforms cubemap-based 360° video content (six cube faces arranged in a specific layout) into a perspective-correct flat projection. This effect is automatically applied when cubemap 360° metadata is detected in the video file.
Cubemap format provides more uniform pixel distribution than equirectangular projection, resulting in better quality at the poles of the sphere.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoInterpolationMode
member.summary: Specifies the interpolation algorithm used when resizing or scaling video frames.
member.remarks: Different interpolation modes offer varying trade-offs between image quality and processing speed. Higher quality modes typically require more computational resources.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoInterpolationMode.NearestNeighbor
member.summary: Uses the nearest pixel value for interpolation, resulting in a blocky appearance but fast processing.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoInterpolationMode.Bilinear
member.summary: Uses a weighted average of the four nearest pixels, providing smoother results than nearest-neighbor but can still appear blurry.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoInterpolationMode.Bicubic
member.summary: Uses a weighted average of 16 nearest pixels, offering higher quality and smoother transitions than bilinear, but is computationally more intensive.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoInterpolationMode.Lancroz
member.summary: A more advanced interpolation method that provides sharp, high-quality results, often used for downscaling images.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererAdjustment
member.summary: Specifies the types of visual adjustments that can be applied to a video renderer for real-time video processing.

remarks.para: This enumeration defines flags for various video adjustments that can be applied during playback or rendering. These adjustments modify the visual characteristics of video content without altering the source material, allowing users to enhance or correct video appearance in real-time.

The values are designed as bit flags, allowing multiple adjustments to be combined using bitwise OR operations. This enables applications to query or set multiple adjustment capabilities simultaneously.

Common use cases include: - Correcting poorly lit or washed-out video content - Enhancing video visibility in different viewing environments - Compensating for display characteristics - Creative color grading and stylization - Accessibility features for users with visual impairments

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererAdjustment.Brightness
member.summary: Adjusts the overall lightness or darkness of the video image.

remarks.para: Brightness controls the black level of the video, affecting all pixels equally. Increasing brightness makes the entire image lighter, while decreasing makes it darker.
Typical value ranges: - Minimum: -100 (darkest) - Default: 0 (no adjustment) - Maximum: 100 (brightest)
Excessive brightness can cause loss of detail in highlights (blown out whites), while too little brightness can crush shadow detail.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererAdjustment.Contrast
member.summary: Adjusts the difference between the lightest and darkest areas of the video.

remarks.para: Contrast controls the range between black and white levels in the video. Higher contrast increases the difference between dark and light areas, while lower contrast reduces this difference, making the image appear flatter.
Typical value ranges: - Minimum: -100 (lowest contrast, gray appearance) - Default: 0 (no adjustment) - Maximum: 100 (highest contrast)
High contrast can create more dramatic images but may lose detail in shadows and highlights. Low contrast preserves detail but may appear washed out.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererAdjustment.Hue
member.summary: Adjusts the tint or color balance of the video by rotating the color wheel.

remarks.para: Hue adjustment rotates all colors in the image around the color wheel. This can correct color casts or create artistic effects by shifting the entire color spectrum.
Typical value ranges: - Minimum: -180 degrees (shifts colors towards magenta/green) - Default: 0 (no adjustment) - Maximum: 180 degrees (shifts colors towards green/magenta)
Small adjustments (±15 degrees) are useful for color correction, while larger adjustments create dramatic color shifts for creative effects.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererAdjustment.Saturation
member.summary: Adjusts the intensity or purity of colors in the video.

remarks.para: Saturation controls the vividness of colors, from grayscale (no saturation) to highly vivid colors (maximum saturation). It affects the color intensity without changing the hue or brightness.
Typical value ranges: - Minimum: -100 (complete desaturation, grayscale) - Default: 0 (no adjustment) - Maximum: 100 (maximum color intensity)
Reduced saturation can create a more muted, film-like appearance, while increased saturation creates more vibrant, eye-catching visuals. Over-saturation can cause color bleeding and loss of detail.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererAdjustmentSupported
member.summary: Represents the video adjustment capabilities supported by a specific video renderer implementation.

remarks.para: This class provides a capability discovery mechanism for video renderers, allowing applications to query which visual adjustments are available before attempting to use them. Different video renderers may support different subsets of adjustments based on their underlying technology, hardware capabilities, or platform limitations.

Applications should use this class to: - Dynamically enable/disable UI controls based on renderer capabilities - Provide fallback behavior when certain adjustments are unavailable - Inform users about available video enhancement options - Optimize performance by only applying supported adjustments

Support for adjustments may vary based on: - Video renderer type (DirectX, OpenGL, Software, etc.) - Graphics hardware capabilities - Video format and codec - Platform-specific limitations - Driver versions and capabilities

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererAdjustmentSupported.Brightness
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether brightness adjustment is supported by the video renderer.
member.value: true if the renderer can adjust video brightness; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When true, applications can safely call brightness adjustment methods without risk of exceptions or undefined behavior.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererAdjustmentSupported.Contrast
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether contrast adjustment is supported by the video renderer.
member.value: true if the renderer can adjust video contrast; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When true, applications can safely call contrast adjustment methods without risk of exceptions or undefined behavior.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererAdjustmentSupported.Hue
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether hue adjustment is supported by the video renderer.
member.value: true if the renderer can adjust video hue (color tint); otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When true, applications can safely call hue adjustment methods without risk of exceptions or undefined behavior. Hue adjustment is often unavailable in grayscale or certain YUV formats.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererAdjustmentSupported.Saturation
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether saturation adjustment is supported by the video renderer.
member.value: true if the renderer can adjust video saturation (color intensity); otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When true, applications can safely call saturation adjustment methods without risk of exceptions or undefined behavior. Saturation adjustment is typically unavailable for grayscale video formats.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererAdjustmentSupported.#ctor(System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with specified capabilities.
member.param: true if brightness adjustment is supported; otherwise, false.
true if contrast adjustment is supported; otherwise, false.
true if hue adjustment is supported; otherwise, false.
true if saturation adjustment is supported; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: This constructor is typically called by video renderer implementations after querying their underlying capabilities. Applications generally receive instances of this class through renderer API methods rather than constructing them directly.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererAdjustmentSupported.AnySupported
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether any video adjustments are supported.
member.value: true if at least one adjustment type is supported; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: This property provides a quick check to determine if any adjustments are available, useful for hiding entire adjustment panels in the UI when no adjustments are supported.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoRendererAdjustmentSupported.AllSupported

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VUMeterEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for events that report VU (Volume Unit) meter levels for audio visualization and monitoring.

remarks.para: This event argument is used in audio processing pipelines to report real-time volume levels for each audio channel. The VU meter data is typically used to create visual representations of audio intensity, such as level meters, peak indicators, or other audio visualization components in media players and audio processing applications.

Each value in the array represents the current volume level for a specific audio channel. For stereo audio, index 0 typically represents the left channel and index 1 represents the right channel. Multi-channel audio (e.g., 5.1, 7.1) will have corresponding indices for each channel.

The values are typically normalized to a specific range (e.g., 0-100 or 0-255) depending on the implementation, where 0 represents silence and the maximum value represents the loudest possible signal before clipping.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VUMeterEventArgs.MeterData
member.summary: Gets an array of integer values representing the current VU meter levels for each audio channel.
member.value: An array of values where each element corresponds to the volume level of an audio channel. The array length corresponds to the number of audio channels in the source material. Values typically range from 0 (silence) to a maximum value (e.g., 100 or 255) representing peak volume.

remarks.para: The interpretation of values depends on the specific implementation: - For percentage-based systems: 0-100 where 100 represents 0 dBFS - For byte-based systems: 0-255 where 255 represents 0 dBFS - Negative dB values may be mapped to the positive integer range

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VUMeterEventArgs.#ctor(System.Int32[])
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with the specified VU meter data.
member.param: An array of integer values representing the VU meter levels for each audio channel. Must not be null. The array should contain one value per audio channel.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VUMeterFFTEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for events that report Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) results for audio frequency analysis.

remarks.para: This event argument contains FFT data that represents the frequency spectrum of audio signals. The FFT transforms time-domain audio samples into frequency-domain data, allowing analysis of which frequencies are present in the audio and their relative amplitudes.

Common uses include: - Spectrum analyzers and frequency visualizers - Audio equalization and filtering analysis - Beat detection and rhythm analysis - Pitch detection and harmonic analysis - Real-time audio effects based on frequency content

The FFT result is an array of complex numbers where: - The magnitude represents the amplitude of each frequency component - The phase represents the phase shift of each frequency component - Each index corresponds to a specific frequency bin
The frequency represented by each bin can be calculated as: frequency = (binIndex * sampleRate) / fftSize

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VUMeterFFTEventArgs.#ctor(NAudio.Dsp.Complex[])
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with the specified FFT results.
member.param: An array of numbers representing the FFT output. Must not be null. The array length should typically be a power of 2 (e.g., 512, 1024, 2048, 4096) for optimal FFT performance.

remarks.para: The FFT size determines the frequency resolution: - Larger FFT sizes provide better frequency resolution but poorer time resolution - Smaller FFT sizes provide better time resolution but poorer frequency resolution

Common FFT sizes: - 512: Fast response, suitable for real-time visualization - 1024: Good balance between frequency and time resolution - 2048: Better frequency resolution for detailed analysis - 4096 or higher: High frequency resolution for precision applications

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VUMeterFFTEventArgs.Result
member.summary: Gets the array of complex numbers representing the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) result.
member.value: An array of objects where each element represents a frequency bin. The first half of the array contains the positive frequencies from 0 Hz to Nyquist frequency (sampleRate/2). The second half contains the negative frequencies (mirror image) which are typically ignored for real signals.

remarks.para: For real audio signals, only the first N/2 + 1 bins are unique (where N is the FFT size), as the remaining bins are complex conjugates of the first half.

To calculate the frequency of a specific bin:
double binFrequency = (binIndex * sampleRate) / fftSize;

To calculate the magnitude (amplitude) of a frequency component:
double magnitude = Math.Sqrt(Result[i].X * Result[i].X + Result[i].Y * Result[i].Y);

To calculate the phase angle of a frequency component:
double phase = Math.Atan2(Result[i].Y, Result[i].X);

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VUMeterMaxSampleEventArgs
member.summary: Provides data for events that report the minimum and maximum audio sample values for peak level monitoring.

remarks.para: This event argument is essential for implementing peak meters, clipping indicators, and dynamic range monitoring in audio applications. It reports the extreme sample values detected within a specific time window, allowing applications to monitor signal peaks and detect potential audio issues.

Common uses include: - Peak level meters with hold functionality - Clipping detection and warning systems - Dynamic range measurement - Automatic gain control (AGC) systems - Audio normalization and leveling

Audio samples are typically normalized to the range [-1.0, 1.0], where: - 0.0 represents silence - 1.0 represents maximum positive amplitude (0 dBFS) - -1.0 represents maximum negative amplitude (0 dBFS) - Values exceeding ±1.0 indicate clipping (distortion)

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.VUMeterMaxSampleEventArgs.#ctor(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with the specified minimum and maximum sample values.
member.param: The minimum sample value detected in the audio stream. Expected range is typically [-1.0, 0.0] for normalized audio, where -1.0 represents maximum negative amplitude.
The maximum sample value detected in the audio stream. Expected range is typically [0.0, 1.0] for normalized audio, where 1.0 represents maximum positive amplitude.

remarks.para: Sample values outside the range [-1.0, 1.0] indicate clipping or improper gain staging. Applications should monitor for values approaching or exceeding these limits to prevent audio distortion.
The time window for detecting these extremes depends on the implementation but is typically synchronized with the audio buffer processing rate (e.g., every 10-50ms).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VUMeterMaxSampleEventArgs.MaxSample
member.summary: Gets the maximum sample value detected by the VU meter within the measurement window.
member.value: A representing the highest audio sample value. For normalized audio, values typically range from 0.0 to 1.0. Values exceeding 1.0 indicate clipping (audio distortion).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VUMeterMaxSampleEventArgs.MinSample
member.summary: Gets the minimum sample value detected by the VU meter within the measurement window.
member.value: A representing the lowest audio sample value. For normalized audio, values typically range from -1.0 to 0.0. Values below -1.0 indicate clipping (audio distortion).

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddVideoRenderer
member.summary: Creates and initializes the video renderer filter for displaying video output.
member.remarks: This method: - Disposes any existing renderer - Creates a new renderer based on Video_Renderer settings (VMR9, EVR, etc.) - Configures OSD (On-Screen Display) support if enabled - Initializes the renderer with appropriate input pin count for PIP and CC - Sets up the renderer in the filter graph The renderer type is selected based on the current mode and output requirements.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.CheckAndConnectVBIRenderer
member.summary: Checks for and connects VBI (Vertical Blanking Interval) data to the video renderer.
member.remarks: This method handles closed caption (CC) data embedded in the VBI: - Checks if the video capture device has a CC output pin - Gets a free input pin on the video renderer - Connects the CC data stream to the renderer for display VBI data typically contains closed captions, teletext, and other metadata.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.CaptureMain
member.summary: The main capture initialization method that sets up the entire capture pipeline.
member.returns: true if capture was successfully initialized; false if initialization failed.
member.remarks: This is the core method that orchestrates the entire capture setup: 1. Creates and configures the DirectShow filter graph 2. Adds appropriate source filters based on capture mode 3. Configures video/audio processing chains 4. Sets up encoders and output formats 5. Initializes renderers for preview 6. Connects all filters in the proper order The method handles various capture modes including video, screen, IP camera, custom sources, and audio-only capture. It also manages network streaming, virtual camera output, and separate capture features.

member.returns: true if the delayed start was successful; false if the graph is not started or async mode is enabled.
member.remarks: This method is used when Start_DelayEnabled is set to true. It allows the graph to be configured completely before starting execution. For async API usage, use StartDelayedAsync instead. The method will fail if the graph hasn't been started or if async mode is enabled.

member.returns: true if the graph was successfully started; false otherwise.
member.remarks: This method is called by both StartDelayed and StartDelayedAsync. It delegates to StartGraph which performs the actual graph execution. Used when Start_DelayEnabled is true to defer graph execution after setup.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.StartGraph
member.summary: Starts the graph.
Starts the DirectShow filter graph and begins media processing.
member.returns: true if the graph was successfully started; false if an error occurred.
member.remarks: This method performs the following operations: 1. Starts any FFMPEG pipe processes before running the graph 2. Calls Run() on the media control interface to begin processing 3. Handles out-of-memory errors for high-resolution capture 4. Starts separate capture threads if enabled 5. Initiates external encoders (FFMPEG, VLC) 6. Saves debug information if debug mode is enabled 7. Sets up frame disconnect monitoring for IP cameras The method changes the playback state to Play upon successful execution.
