member.param: If true, disposing of managed resources; if false, only unmanaged resources.
member.remarks: This method implements the standard .NET dispose pattern: - Sets the disposing flag to prevent re-entrancy - Stops any active capture operations - Calls DisposeCore to release all resources - Marks the object as disposed This method is called by both Dispose() and the finalizer.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.ScreenUpdateDelegate
member.summary: The screen update delegate.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.ScreenUpdateDelegateMethod
member.summary: The screen update delegate method.
Delegate method for updating the video renderer display.
member.remarks: This method is used as a callback to refresh the video display. It handles both synchronous and asynchronous update scenarios: - In async mode, updates are performed on a background thread - In sync mode, updates are performed immediately The method ensures the main video renderer is properly updated.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.IsSourceConnected
member.summary: Checks if the video source has been successfully connected to the filter graph.
member.returns: true if the source is connected and the OnSourceConnected event has been fired; false otherwise.
member.remarks: This property indicates whether the video/audio source has been properly connected to the capture pipeline. The connection is considered complete when the OnSourceConnected event has been triggered. Useful for determining if the capture pipeline is ready for operation.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.IsAsync
member.summary: Indicates whether the capture instance is configured for asynchronous operation.
member.returns: true if async mode is enabled; false for synchronous operation.
member.remarks: When async mode is enabled: - Start/Stop operations should use async methods (StartAsync, StopAsync) - Events are raised on background threads - UI updates require proper thread marshaling This mode is recommended for modern applications to avoid UI blocking.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.GetVideoResolution
member.summary: Gets the video resolution.
Gets the current video resolution from the input source.
member.returns: A Size object containing the video width and height in pixels.
member.remarks: This method returns the actual resolution of the video being captured, which may differ from the requested resolution due to: - Device capabilities - Format constraints - Automatic resolution selection Returns Size.Empty if no video is being captured.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.GetVideoRendererCore
member.summary: Gets the video renderer core.
Gets the core video renderer interface for advanced control.
member.returns: The IVideoRendererBase interface of the main video renderer, or null if not initialized.
member.remarks: This method provides direct access to the underlying video renderer for advanced operations not exposed through the public API. Use with caution as improper use may affect rendering stability. The returned interface depends on the selected renderer type (VMR9, EVR, etc.).

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMPVCVECore#GetVideoRenderer
member.summary: Gets the video renderer.
Gets the video renderer settings (explicit interface implementation).
member.remarks: This method is an explicit implementation of the IMPVCVECore interface. It returns the current video renderer configuration including: - Renderer type (VMR9, EVR, etc.) - Zoom and stretch settings - Flip and rotation parameters - Deinterlacing options

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.CallVideoRendererUpdate(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Updates the video renderer with new dimensions and optionally refreshes the window handle.
member.param: The new width for the video renderer in pixels.
The new height for the video renderer in pixels.
If true, also updates the window handle from the video view.
member.remarks: This method is typically called when: - The video window is resized - The video format changes - The rendering surface needs to be refreshed The method updates all active video renderers including the main renderer and any additional screens configured for multi-monitor output.

member.summary: List NDI sources.
member.param: True to list only sources on this PC.
Which groups do you want to search in for sources.

The list of additional IP addresses that exist that we should query for sources on. For instance, if you want to find the sources on a remote machine that is not on your local sub-net then you can put a comma separated list of those IP addresses here and those sources will be available locally even though they are not mDNS discoverable. An example might be "12.0.0.8,13.0.12.8".

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddNetworkStreamingMP4SW
member.summary: Adds network streaming MP4 (software).
member.returns: true if the MP4 network streaming was successfully configured; false if initialization failed.
member.remarks: This method configures software-based MP4 streaming using H.264 video and AAC audio codecs. It supports CPU and Intel Quick Sync Video (QSV) encoding modes. The video and audio pins are connected to the encoder and released after successful initialization.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddNetworkStreamingFFMPEG
member.summary: Adds network streaming (FFMPEG).
member.returns: true if FFMPEG network streaming was successfully configured; false if initialization failed.
member.remarks: This method configures network streaming using the FFMPEG executable in non-pipe mode. It supports custom FFMPEG arguments and various output muxers. Video and audio inputs are connected separately and pins are released after connection. For NuGet installations or custom redistribution, requires one-time admin registration.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddNetworkStreamingFFMPEGPipe
member.summary: Adds network streaming (FFMPEG).
member.returns: true if FFMPEG pipe network streaming was successfully configured; false if initialization failed.
member.remarks: This method configures network streaming using FFMPEG executable in pipe mode. Pipe mode provides better performance and lower latency than non-pipe mode. It uses named pipes to transfer data directly to FFMPEG without intermediate files. Supports the same customization options as non-pipe mode.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddNetworkStreamingMJPEG
member.summary: Adds network streaming (MJPEG).
Configures Motion JPEG (MJPEG) network streaming.
member.returns: true if MJPEG streaming was successfully configured; false if initialization failed.
member.remarks: This method sets up MJPEG streaming over HTTP, suitable for web browsers and simple clients. MJPEG streams each frame as a separate JPEG image, providing good compatibility but higher bandwidth usage. The stream is accessible via HTTP on the specified port.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddNetworkStreamingNDI
member.summary: Adds network streaming (NDI).
Configures Network Device Interface (NDI) streaming.
member.returns: true if NDI streaming was successfully configured; false if initialization failed.
member.remarks: This method sets up NDI streaming for professional IP video production. NDI provides low-latency, high-quality video over IP networks. It automatically discovers NDI sources and receivers on the network. Requires the NDI runtime to be installed.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddNetworkStreamingHLS
member.summary: Adds HLS network streaming.
Configures HTTP Live Streaming (HLS) for adaptive bitrate streaming.
member.returns: true if HLS streaming was successfully configured; false if initialization failed.
member.remarks: This method sets up HLS streaming, which creates segmented video files and a playlist. HLS is widely supported by mobile devices and web browsers. It provides adaptive bitrate streaming and supports live and on-demand content. The output consists of .m3u8 playlist files and .ts segment files.

member.summary: Adds WMV network streaming.

member.summary: Adds external network streaming.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddNetworkStreamingRTSP
member.summary: Adds RTSP network streaming.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.OSD_Layers_Move(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Moves an On-Screen Display (OSD) layer to a new position.
member.param: The zero-based index of the OSD layer to move.
The new X coordinate (left position) for the layer.
The new Y coordinate (top position) for the layer.
member.returns: true if the layer was successfully moved; false if the operation failed or the ID is invalid.
member.remarks: This method updates the position of an existing OSD layer and re-renders all layers. The coordinates are relative to the top-left corner of the video frame. The video renderer must be initialized before calling this method.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.OSD_Layers_Render
member.summary: Renders all enabled On-Screen Display (OSD) layers to the video output.
member.returns: true if the layers were successfully rendered; false if rendering failed or no layers are enabled.
member.remarks: This method combines all enabled OSD layers into a single bitmap and applies it to the video renderer. It automatically clears the OSD if no layers are enabled. The method requires the video to be playing or in preview mode, and the video dimensions must be known. The rendered OSD will match the video dimensions for proper overlay alignment.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.OSD_Layers_Clear
member.summary: Clears all On-Screen Display (OSD) layers from the collection and removes any overlay from the video.
member.remarks: This method removes all OSD layers and creates a transparent overlay to clear any existing OSD from the video. Use this method to completely reset the OSD system. After calling this method, you'll need to create new layers if you want to display OSD again.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.OSD_Layers_Enable(System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Enables or disables a specific On-Screen Display (OSD) layer.
member.param: The zero-based index of the OSD layer to enable or disable.
If true, the layer will be rendered; if false, it will be hidden.
member.remarks: Disabled layers remain in memory but are not rendered to the video output. Call OSD_Layers_Render after changing the enabled state to see the effect. If the ID is invalid, an error will be logged but no exception will be thrown.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.OSD_Layers_Clear(System.Int32)
member.summary: Clears the content of a specific On-Screen Display (OSD) layer.
member.param: The zero-based index of the OSD layer to clear.
member.remarks: This method clears all drawings from the specified layer by creating a new transparent bitmap. The layer remains in the collection and retains its size and position settings. The graphics object is recreated with high-quality rendering settings. Call OSD_Layers_Render after clearing to update the video display.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.OSD_Layers_Create(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Creates a new On-Screen Display (OSD) layer.
member.param: The left position of the layer relative to the video frame.
The top position of the layer relative to the video frame.
The width of the layer in pixels.
The height of the layer in pixels.
If true, the layer will be visible immediately; if false, it will be hidden.
member.returns: true if the layer was successfully created; false if an error occurred.
member.remarks: Creates a new transparent layer that can be drawn on using other OSD methods. The layer is added to the internal collection and assigned an ID based on its index. Use the returned index (collection count - 1) to reference this layer in other methods.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.OSD_Layers_Delete(System.Int32)
member.summary: Deletes a specific On-Screen Display (OSD) layer from the collection.
member.param: The zero-based index of the OSD layer to delete.
member.returns: true if the layer was successfully deleted; false if the operation failed or the ID is invalid.
member.remarks: This method permanently removes the layer from the collection. All layers with higher indices will shift down by one position. After deletion, the OSD is automatically updated to reflect the change. The video renderer must be initialized before calling this method.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.OSD_Layers_Draw_Image(System.Int32,System.Drawing.Bitmap,System.Drawing.Rectangle,System.Drawing.Rectangle,System.Boolean,System.Drawing.Color)

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore._lockObject
member.summary: The lock object used for thread synchronization during face tracking operations.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddBarcodeReader
member.summary: Adds and configures a barcode reader for detecting barcodes in video frames.
member.remarks: This method initializes the barcode reader with the configured settings including barcode type and enabled state. The reader will process video frames to detect barcodes.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddAudioPCMConverter
member.summary: Adds an audio PCM converter filter to the filter graph for audio format conversion.
member.remarks: This method initializes a PCM converter to convert audio to the specified format including sample rate, bits per sample, and number of channels. The converter is inserted into the audio processing pipeline.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddAudioEnhancer
member.summary: Adds an audio enhancer filter to improve audio quality and apply audio processing effects.
member.remarks: The audio enhancer supports features like normalization, auto-gain control, input/output gain adjustments, and time shifting. It's inserted into the audio processing pipeline after initialization.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddAudioChannelMapper
member.summary: Adds an audio channel mapper filter to remap audio channels.
member.remarks: This filter allows remapping of audio channels, useful for converting between different channel configurations (e.g., stereo to mono, 5.1 to stereo, etc.). If output channel count is not specified, it uses the input channel count.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddVideoResize
member.summary: Adds a video resize filter to crop and/or resize video frames.
member.remarks: This method adds a video resize filter that can: - Crop video frames by removing pixels from edges - Resize video to different dimensions - Apply letterboxing for aspect ratio preservation The filter updates the internal video dimensions after processing. For VideoRenderer mode, an additional decoder filter may be added.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddMaxineResize
member.summary: Adds an NVIDIA Maxine-powered resize filter for AI-enhanced video upscaling.
member.remarks: This method adds an NVIDIA Maxine filter that uses AI models for: - Super-resolution upscaling - Artifact reduction during upscaling Requires NVIDIA GPU with appropriate drivers and Maxine SDK models. The models directory must be specified in the resize settings.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddVideoRotate
member.summary: Adds a video rotation filter to rotate video frames by 90, 180, or 270 degrees.
member.remarks: This filter rotates the video stream according to the Video_Rotation setting. For 90 and 270 degree rotations, the width and height are swapped. An additional decoder filter may be added for VideoRenderer mode.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddAudioSampleGrabber
member.summary: Adds an audio sample grabber to capture raw audio data for processing and analysis.
member.remarks: The sample grabber intercepts PCM audio data and raises the AudioFrameCB1 callback. This is used for audio effects processing, VU meters, and providing audio data to applications. Only works with PCM audio format.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddVideoSampleGrabber
member.summary: Adds a video sample grabber to capture raw video frames for processing and analysis.
member.remarks: The sample grabber intercepts RGB24 video data and raises frame callbacks. Used for video effects processing, motion detection, and providing video frames to applications. Initializes the video effects processor if enabled.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddVideoSampleGrabberPreview(VisioForge.Libs.DirectShowLib.IPin@)
member.summary: Adds a video sample grabber specifically for the preview stream.
member.param: Reference to the video output pin to connect the grabber to.
member.remarks: This sample grabber is separate from the main video grabber and processes preview frames independently. Used when different effects or processing is needed for preview vs capture streams.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddVideoSampleGrabberOutput(VisioForge.Libs.DirectShowLib.IPin@)
member.summary: Adds a video sample grabber specifically for the capture/output stream.
member.param: Reference to the video output pin to connect the grabber to.
member.remarks: This sample grabber processes frames being sent to the capture output. Allows different effects and processing for captured video compared to preview. Connected to the shared capture graph rather than the main graph.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddVideoSampleGrabberStill
member.summary: Adds a video sample grabber specifically for capturing still images from the video stream.
member.remarks: This sample grabber is configured for one-shot capture of still images. It connects to the still pin of the video capture device if available. The grabber captures RGB24 format images and raises the FrameBufferCB24Still callback. A null renderer is attached to complete the graph without displaying the still images.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddAudioVUMeter
member.summary: Adds an audio VU (Volume Unit) meter for visualizing audio levels.
member.remarks: The VU meter processes audio data from the sample grabber to calculate volume levels. It uses the audio format parameters (sample rate, channels, bits per sample) from the grabber. The meter raises OnAudioVUMeter events with volume and frequency data. This is useful for creating audio level visualizations in the UI.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddNAVUMeter
member.summary: Adds an advanced NAudio-based VU meter with additional audio analysis capabilities.
member.remarks: This professional VU meter provides: - Volume level analysis with configurable sensitivity - FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) calculations for frequency analysis - Maximum level detection for peak monitoring Requires the audio sample grabber to be enabled. Raises multiple events for different audio analysis results.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddVideoEffects
member.summary: Adds the main video effects processing filter to the filter graph.
member.remarks: This method inserts the video effects processor into the video pipeline. The processor handles various effects including: - Image and text overlays - Color adjustments and filters - Transformations and distortions The filter is configured based on the video renderer mode and enabled effects. Frame callbacks are set up for applying effects to video frames.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddVideoFilters(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Adds custom DirectShow video filters to the filter graph.
member.param: If true, adds filters that should be inserted before effects processing; if false, adds filters that should be inserted after.
member.remarks: This method allows insertion of third-party DirectShow filters into the video pipeline. Filters can be specified by CLSID or by name from the registered filters list. The OnFilterAdded event is raised when a filter is successfully added. Filters are connected automatically to the video output pin.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.ProcessAudio(VisioForge.Core.DSP.DSPProcessor@,VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.SampleGrabberBufferCBEventArgs)
member.summary: Processes audio frames through the DSP (Digital Signal Processing) effects chain.
member.param: The DSP processor instance to use for processing audio effects.
Sample grabber event arguments containing audio buffer data and format information.
member.remarks: This method initializes the processor with audio format parameters if not already initialized. It then processes the audio buffer through the configured effects chain. Effects may include equalization, compression, reverb, and other audio transformations.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AudioFrameCB1(System.Object,VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.SampleGrabberBufferCBEventArgs)
member.summary: Callback method that handles audio frames from the audio sample grabber.
member.param: The source of the event (typically the audio sample grabber).
Event arguments containing the audio buffer data, format, and timing information.
member.remarks: This callback is the main audio processing entry point that: - Applies audio effects if enabled - Processes VU meter data for volume visualization - Provides audio data to the application via OnAudioFrameBuffer event The method handles both standard and professional VU meter processing. All exceptions are caught to prevent interruption of the audio stream.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddAForgeMotionDetector
member.summary: Initializes and configures the AForge.NET motion detection system.
member.remarks: This method sets up motion detection using the AForge.NET framework. It cleans up any existing motion detector before creating a new one. The detector is configured with settings from Motion_DetectionEx property. Motion detection events are wired up to notify when motion is detected.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.OnAForgeData(System.IntPtr,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Drawing.Imaging.PixelFormat)
member.summary: Processes video frame data through the AForge.NET motion detection system.
member.param: Pointer to the raw image data in memory.
Width of the image in pixels.
Height of the image in pixels.
Pixel format of the image data (e.g., RGB24, RGB32).
member.remarks: This method feeds video frames to the AForge motion detector for analysis. Motion detection algorithms are applied to identify movement in the video. Only processes frames when motion detection is enabled and configured.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.GenerateSeparateCaptureFilename
member.summary: Generates a unique filename for separate capture files based on the configured mask.
member.returns: A formatted filename string with date/time placeholders replaced with current values.
member.remarks: This method creates filenames for the separate capture feature which splits recordings into multiple files. The filename mask can contain date/time placeholders like %yyyy, %MM, %dd, %hh, %mm, %ss. The %ext placeholder is replaced with the extension from the main output filename. Used when SeparateCapture_Mode is set to split by duration or file size.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.ProcessEffects(System.IntPtr,System.Int32,System.Boolean,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.TimeSpan,VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoStreamType)
member.summary: Processes and applies video effects to a video frame.
member.param: Pointer to the raw video frame data to process.
Size of the frame data in bytes.
Whether the frame needs to be flipped (unused in this method).
Width of the video frame in pixels.
Height of the video frame in pixels.
Byte stride of the video frame.
Timestamp of the current frame for time-based effects.
Type of stream (Main, Preview, or Capture) to determine which effects to apply.
member.remarks: This method is the central video effects processing pipeline that: - Merges image logos efficiently by pre-rendering them once - Merges text and scrolling text logos with timestamp support - Applies NVIDIA Maxine AI effects (denoise, artifact reduction) - Processes other video effects through the effects processor Effects are filtered by stream type and time range. Performance optimizations include caching rendered logos and selective updates.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.ProcessVideoRGB(System.IntPtr,System.Int32,System.Boolean,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.TimeSpan,VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoStreamType)
member.summary: Main video frame processing method that handles RGB24 format video frames.
member.param: Pointer to the raw RGB24 video frame data.
Size of the frame data in bytes.
If true, flips the frame horizontally to correct DirectShow orientation.
Width of the video frame in pixels.
Height of the video frame in pixels.
Byte stride of the video frame.
Type of stream (Main, Preview, or Capture) being processed.
member.remarks: This is the core video processing method that: - Updates frame timing and position information - Handles separate capture file splitting - Applies video effects and GPU effects - Performs motion detection and face tracking - Processes barcode detection - Raises various frame events for application consumption - Manages frame buffers and format conversions The method includes extensive error handling and performance optimizations. All video processing passes through this central method.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.VideoFrameBufferCB24(System.Object,VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.VideoFrameBufferEventArgs)
member.summary: Callback method that handles RGB24 video frames from the video effects filter.
member.param: The source of the event (typically the video effects filter).
Event arguments containing the video frame data and metadata.
member.remarks: This callback is used when the video sample grabber is disabled. It processes video frames that have already passed through the effects filter. The frames are in RGB24 format and are forwarded to the main processing method.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.VideoFrameBufferCB24SG(System.Object,VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.SampleGrabberBufferCBEventArgs)
member.summary: Callback method that handles video frames from the main video sample grabber.
member.param: The source of the event (typically the main video sample grabber).
Event arguments containing the video frame buffer, dimensions, and timing information.
member.remarks: This is the primary video frame callback for processing captured video. Frames are flipped horizontally to correct for DirectShow's coordinate system. The method forwards frames to ProcessVideoRGB for effects, motion detection, and other processing. This callback handles frames from the main video stream.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.VideoFrameBufferCB24SGPreview(System.Object,VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.SampleGrabberBufferCBEventArgs)
member.summary: Callback method that handles video frames from the preview sample grabber.
member.param: The source of the event (typically the preview sample grabber).
Event arguments containing the preview frame buffer and metadata.
member.remarks: This callback processes frames specifically for the preview stream. Preview frames may have different effects applied compared to the capture stream. Unlike the main stream, preview frames are not flipped horizontally. This allows separate processing pipelines for preview and capture.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.ProcessFaceTracking(System.IntPtr,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Drawing.Imaging.PixelFormat,System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: Processes video frames for face detection and tracking using Haar cascades.
member.param: Pointer to the raw video frame data.
Length of the buffer in bytes.
Width of the video frame in pixels.
Height of the video frame in pixels.
Pixel format of the video frame.
member.remarks: This method implements a two-phase face tracking system: 1. Detection phase: Uses Haar cascades to detect faces in downsampled frames 2. Tracking phase: Uses Camshift algorithm to track detected faces efficiently The detection runs periodically while tracking runs on every frame for performance. Detected faces can be highlighted with rectangles if Face_Tracking.Highlight is enabled. The OnFaceDetected event is raised with face locations and frame data.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.FrameBufferCB24Still(System.Object,VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.SampleGrabberBufferCBEventArgs)
member.summary: Callback method that handles still image frames from the video capture device.
member.param: The source of the event (typically the still image sample grabber).
Event arguments containing the image buffer data, dimensions, and format information.
member.remarks: This callback processes still images captured from the video stream. It provides the captured image data through two events: - OnStillVideoFrameBuffer: Provides raw buffer data - OnStillVideoFrameBitmap: Provides a Bitmap object The image is flipped vertically to correct for DirectShow's bottom-up format. Applications can modify the image data by setting UpdateData in the event args.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.AddMotionDetection
member.summary: Initializes and configures the motion detection system.
member.remarks: This method creates a motion detector that analyzes video frames for movement. The detector is configured with settings from the Motion_Detection property. Motion events are wired up to notify when motion levels exceed thresholds. The detector provides both motion level values and a motion matrix showing areas of movement.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.dsMotionDetector_OnMotion(System.Object,VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.MotionDetectionEventArgs)
member.summary: Handles motion detection events from the motion detector.
member.param: The motion detector that detected movement.
Event arguments containing motion level and motion matrix data.
member.remarks: This event handler forwards motion detection results to application code. The motion level indicates the amount of movement detected (0-100). The motion matrix provides detailed information about which areas contain motion.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.ProcessMotion(System.IntPtr)
member.summary: Processes a video frame through the motion detection algorithm.
member.param: Pointer to the raw video frame data to analyze for motion.
member.remarks: This method feeds video frames to the motion detector for analysis. It uses the current frame dimensions to properly interpret the frame data. Motion detection algorithms compare the current frame with previous frames. All exceptions are suppressed to prevent interruption of video processing.

Main method for the channel tuning process that runs on a separate thread.
member.remarks: This method performs automatic channel scanning to find all available channels. It iterates through the channel range, testing each frequency for a valid signal. Found channels are added to the internal collection with their frequency information. The process can be cancelled by setting the FTVTunerCancelChannelScan flag. Progress is reported through the OnTVTunerTuneChannels event.

Provides GStreamer bus message handling for VideoEditX, managing pipeline state changes, errors, and events. This partial class handles all asynchronous communication from the GStreamer pipeline including state transitions, error propagation, end-of-stream notifications, and video overlay setup. Essential for monitoring and controlling timeline-based video editing operations through the GStreamer Editing Services (GES) framework. Implements the . Implements the .

Provides proper resource disposal for VideoEditX, ensuring clean shutdown of GStreamer pipelines, timeline objects, and associated media assets. This partial class implements the IDisposable pattern to properly release GES resources including clips, tracks, layers, and encoding profiles. Essential for preventing memory leaks in video editing applications.

Provides license management and activation functionality for VideoEditX SDK. This partial class handles license key validation, activation with user credentials, and license requirement checking for various video editing features. Manages the transition from trial to licensed operation and ensures proper licensing compliance for professional video editing capabilities. Implements the . Implements the .

Provides comprehensive logging and telemetry functionality for VideoEditX SDK using Serilog and Sentry. This partial class manages structured logging to files and debug output, error event propagation, and optional telemetry collection during development. Configures logging levels, file rotation, and integrates with Sentry for crash reporting and debugging support in video editing operations. Implements the Implements the

Cross-platform Video Editing SDK core class that provides non-linear video editing capabilities. This class supports timeline-based editing with multiple tracks, transitions, effects, text overlays, and audio mixing. Built on GStreamer Editing Services (GES) for professional-grade video editing features including precision editing, keyframe animation, and multi-format export across all platforms. member.summary: Provides high-level methods for video fingerprinting analysis, comparison, and search operations.
member.remarks: The class is the main entry point for video fingerprinting operations. It provides methods to generate fingerprints from video files, compare videos for similarity, and search for video fragments within larger videos. The class handles the complexity of video decoding, frame processing, and fingerprint generation, providing a simple API for common video fingerprinting tasks. All methods are static and support asynchronous operations.

member.summary: Generates a fingerprint from a video file optimized for whole-video comparison operations.
member.param: The video source configuration including file path, time range, and processing options.
Optional callback to receive error messages during processing.
Optional callback to receive progress updates (0-100) during processing.
member.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains the generated or null if an error occurred.
member.remarks: This method generates fingerprints optimized for comparing entire videos or large segments to determine overall similarity. It processes the complete specified time range and creates a comprehensive fingerprint. For searching short fragments within longer videos, use instead. The method handles video decoding, frame extraction, optional transformations (cropping, resizing), and ignored area masking automatically.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPAnalyzer.GetSearchFingerprintForVideoFileAsync(VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPFingerprintSource,VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPErrorCallback,VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPProgressCallback)

Optional callback to receive error messages during processing.
Optional callback to receive progress updates (0-100) during processing.
member.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains the generated or null if an error occurred.
member.remarks: This method generates fingerprints optimized for searching video fragments within larger videos. It's designed to create fingerprints of short clips (e.g., commercials, intros, or specific scenes) that can then be located within full-length videos. For comparing entire videos, use instead. The method includes detection for processing issues like stuck frames.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPAnalyzer.Compare(VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPFingerPrint,VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPFingerPrint,System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: Compares two video fingerprints to determine their similarity.
member.param: The first video fingerprint to compare.
The second video fingerprint to compare.
Maximum time shift allowed during comparison. The comparison will test alignments within this time range to find the best match.
member.returns: A difference score where lower values indicate greater similarity. Returns if either fingerprint is null.
member.remarks: This method is used to compare fingerprints generated with . The shift parameter allows for temporal misalignment between videos, which is useful when comparing videos that may have different intros or be slightly out of sync. The comparison is performed in one-second increments.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPAnalyzer.SearchAsync(VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPFingerPrint,VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPFingerPrint,System.TimeSpan,System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Asynchronously searches for occurrences of a video fragment within a larger video.
member.param: The fingerprint of the video fragment to search for (needle). Should be generated using .
The fingerprint of the video to search within (haystack). Can be generated using either fingerprint generation method.
The duration of the fragment being searched for. Used to prevent overlapping matches when searching for multiple occurrences.
Maximum allowed difference score for a valid match. Lower values require closer matches. Typical values range from 5 to 20.
If true, searches for all occurrences of the fragment. If false, returns only the first match.
member.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains a list of timestamps where matches were found, or an empty list if no matches.
member.remarks: This method is ideal for finding commercials, intros, or specific scenes within longer videos. The search is performed on a background thread to avoid blocking.

member.summary: Searches for occurrences of a video fragment within a larger video.
member.param: The fingerprint of the video fragment to search for (needle). Should be generated using .
The fingerprint of the video to search within (haystack). Can be generated using either fingerprint generation method.
The duration of the fragment being searched for. Used to prevent overlapping matches when searching for multiple occurrences.
Maximum allowed difference score for a valid match. Lower values require closer matches. Typical values range from 5 to 20.
If true, searches for all occurrences of the fragment. If false, returns only the first match.
member.returns: A list of timestamps where matches were found. Returns an empty list if no matches are found or if either fingerprint is null.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPAnalyzer.CompareVideoFilesAsync(VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPFingerprintSource,VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPFingerprintSource,System.TimeSpan,VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPErrorCallback,System.Int32)
member.summary: Compares two video files to determine if they contain the same content.
member.param: Configuration for the first video file to compare.
Configuration for the second video file to compare.
Maximum time shift allowed during comparison. The comparison will test alignments within this time range to find the best match.
Optional callback to receive error messages during processing.
Maximum difference score to consider videos as matching. Default is 500. Lower values require closer matches.
member.remarks: This is a convenience method that combines fingerprint generation and comparison into a single operation. It generates comparison fingerprints for both videos and then compares them. This method is suitable for determining if two video files contain the same content, even if they have different encodings, resolutions, or minor edits. The threshold parameter should be adjusted based on the expected similarity and quality requirements.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPFingerprintFromFrames
member.summary: Creates video fingerprints from individual image frames.
member.remarks: The class allows creation of video fingerprints from a sequence of image frames rather than from a video file. This is useful when processing video streams, generated content, or when frames are already available in memory. The class accepts frames in RGB24 format or as Bitmap objects and builds a fingerprint that can be used for content matching. This class is only available on Windows platforms.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPFingerprintFromFrames.#ctor(System.Double,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.TimeSpan)

The width of the video frames in pixels.
The height of the video frames in pixels.
The total expected duration of the video content.
member.remarks: All frames pushed to this instance must match the specified width and height. The frame rate is used to calculate proper timestamps for each frame. The total duration should be an estimate of the complete video length to properly initialize the fingerprinting algorithm.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPFingerprintFromFrames.Push(System.Byte[])
member.summary: Adds an RGB24 frame to the fingerprint generation process.
member.param: A byte array containing the frame data in RGB24 format (3 bytes per pixel).
member.exception: Thrown when the buffer size doesn't match the expected size (width * height * 3).
member.remarks: The frame data must be in RGB24 format with pixels stored in row-major order. Each pixel consists of 3 bytes representing red, green, and blue channels. Frames should be pushed in chronological order for accurate fingerprint generation.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPFingerprintFromFrames.Push(System.Drawing.Bitmap)
member.summary: Adds a bitmap frame to the fingerprint generation process.
member.exception: Thrown when the frame dimensions don't match the expected width and height.
member.remarks: The method accepts bitmaps in any pixel format and automatically converts them to RGB24 format if necessary. For best performance, provide frames already in 24bppRgb format. The bitmap is not modified and can be reused after this call. Frames should be pushed in chronological order.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPFingerprintFromFrames.Push(System.IntPtr,System.Int32)
member.summary: Adds an RGB24 frame from unmanaged memory to the fingerprint generation process.
member.param: Pointer to the frame data in RGB24 format in unmanaged memory.
Size of the frame data in bytes. Must equal width * height * 3.
member.remarks: This method is useful when working with frames from native libraries or when frames are already available in unmanaged memory. The timestamp for each frame is automatically calculated based on the frame rate and the order in which frames are pushed.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting.VFPFingerprintFromFrames.Build
member.summary: Builds the final video fingerprint from all processed frames.

member.summary: Gets or sets the custom resolution to which video frames should be resized before fingerprinting.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.AForge.VFMJPEGStream.ForceBasicAuthentication
member.summary: Force using of basic authentication when connecting to the video source.

remarks.para: For some IP cameras (TrendNET IP cameras, for example) using standard .NET's authentication via credentials does not seem to be working (seems like camera does not request for authentication, but expects corresponding headers to be present on connection request). So this property allows to force basic authentication by adding required HTTP headers when request is sent.
Default value is set to .

member.summary: Wait for video source has stopped.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.AForge.VFMJPEGStream.Stop
member.summary: Stop video source.

remarks.para: Stops video source aborting its thread.

para.note: Since the method aborts background thread, its usage is highly not preferred and should be done only if there are no other options. The correct way of stopping camera is signaling it stop and then waiting for background thread's completion.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSVLCEXEOutput.VideoH264Quantizer
member.summary: Gets or sets H264 quantizer.
member.remarks: The range of the quantizer scale is 0-51: where 0 is lossless, 23 is default, and 51 is worst possible. A lower value is a higher quality and a subjectively sane range is 18-28. Consider 18 to be visually lossless or nearly so: it should look the same or nearly the same as the input but it isn't technically lossless. The range is exponential, so increasing the CRF value +6 is roughly half the bitrate while -6 is roughly twice the bitrate. General usage is to choose the highest CRF value that still provides an acceptable quality. If the output looks good, then try a higher value and if it looks bad then choose a lower value. (FFMPEG docs).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoErrorResilient
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether error resilient enabled. Error resilient mode indicates to the encoder that it should take measures appropriate for streaming over lossy or noisy links, if possible. Disabled by default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoDropframeThreshold
member.summary: Gets or sets dropframe threshold. Temporal resampling allows the codec to "drop" frames as a strategy to meet its target data rate. This can cause temporal discontinuities in the encoded video, which may appear as stuttering during playback. This trade-off is often acceptable, but for many applications is not. It can be disabled in these cases. This threshold is described as a percentage of the target data buffer. When the data buffer falls below this percentage of fullness, a dropped frame is indicated. Set the threshold to zero (0) to disable this feature. 0 by default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoSpatialResamplingAllowed
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether spatial resampling enabled. Spatial resampling allows the codec to compress a lower resolution version of the frame, which is then upscaled by the encoder to the correct presentation resolution. This increases visual quality at low data rates, at the expense of CPU time on the encoder/decoder.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoSpatialResamplingUpThreshold
member.summary: Gets or sets spatial resampling up watermark. This threshold is described as a percentage of the target data buffer. When the data buffer rises above this percentage of fullness, the encoder will step up to a higher resolution version of the frame.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoSpatialResamplingDownThreshold
member.summary: Gets or sets spatial resampling down watermark. This threshold is described as a percentage of the target data buffer. When the data buffer falls below this percentage of fullness, the encoder will step down to a lower resolution version of the frame.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoLagInFrames
member.summary: Gets or sets lag in frame. If set, this value allows the encoder to consume a number of input frames before producing output frames. This allows the encoder to base decisions for the current frame on future frames. This does increase the latency of the encoding pipeline, so it is not appropriate in all situations (ex: realtime encoding). This is a maximum value - the encoder may produce frames sooner than the given limit. Set this value to 0 to disable this feature.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoTokenPartition
member.summary: Gets or sets VP8 token partition mode. This defines VP8 partitioning mode for compressed data, i.e., the number of sub-streams in the bitstream. Used for parallelized decoding. Value 0 = one token partition. Value 1 = two token partitions. Value 2 = four token partitions. Value 3 = eight token partitions.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoMinQuantizer
member.summary: Gets or sets minimum (best quality) quantizer. The quantizer is the most direct control over the quality of the encoded image. The quantizer range is [0, 63].

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoMaxQuantizer
member.summary: Gets or sets maximum (worst quality) quantizer. The quantizer is the most direct control over the quality of the encoded image. The quantizer range is [0, 63].

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoUndershootPct
member.summary: Gets or sets rate control undershoot tolerance. This value, expressed as a percentage of the target bitrate, describes the target bitrate for easier frames, allowing bits to be saved for harder frames. Set to zero to use the codec default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoOvershootPct
member.summary: Gets or sets rate control overshoot tolerance. This value, expressed as a percentage of the target bitrate, describes the maximum allowed bitrate for a given frame. Set to zero to use the codec default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoDecoderBufferSize
member.summary: Gets or sets decoder buffer size. This value indicates the amount of data that may be buffered by the decoding application. This value is expressed in units of time (milliseconds). For example, a value of 5000 indicates that the client will buffer (at least) 5000 ms worth of encoded data.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoDecoderBufferInitialSize
member.summary: Gets or sets decoder buffer initial size. This value indicates the amount of data that will be buffered by the decoding application prior to beginning playback. This value is expressed in units of time (milliseconds).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoDecoderBufferOptimalSize
member.summary: Gets or sets decoder buffer optimal size. This value indicates the amount of data that the encoder should try to maintain in the decoder's buffer. This value is expressed in units of time (milliseconds).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoKeyframeMinInterval
member.summary: Gets or sets keyframe minimum interval. This value, expressed as a number of frames, prevents the encoder from placing a keyframe nearer than MinInterval to the previous keyframe. At least MinInterval frames non-keyframes will be coded before the next keyframe. Set MinInterval equal to MaxInterval for a fixed interval.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoKeyframeMode
member.summary: Gets or sets keyframe placement mode. This value indicates whether the encoder should place keyframes at a fixed interval, or determine the optimal placement automatically (as governed by the KeyframeMinInterval and KeyframeMaxInterval).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoKeyframeMaxInterval
member.summary: Gets or sets keyframe maximum interval. This value, expressed as a number of frames, forces the encoder to code a keyframe if one has not been coded in the last MaxInterval frames. A value of 0 implies all frames will be keyframes. Set MinInterval equal to MaxInterval for a fixed interval.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoAutoAltRef
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether alternate reference frame will be added.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoARNRMaxFrames
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of frames to run the temporal filter over. The number of frames has to be less than or equal to lag in frames. The range is [0, 15]. Zero is the default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoARNRStrength
member.summary: Gets or sets the relative strength of the blur for the temporal filter. The range is [0, 6]. Zero is the weakest and six is the strongest. Three is the default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoARNRType
member.summary: Gets or sets the type of blur for the temporal filter. The range is [1, 3]. Value 1 = a backward blur. Value 2 = a forward blur. Value 3 = a center blur (default).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoFixedKeyframeInterval
member.summary: Gets or sets fixed keyframe interval. If keyframe generation at a fixed interval is desired, set keyframe mode to kKeyframeModeDisabled, and set the interval using this method. This is most useful when dealing with a variable frame rate video source when a consistent keyframe interval is desired for streaming purposes.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoCPUUsed
member.summary: Gets or sets encoder complexity control. Changes in this value influences, among others, the encoder's selection of motion estimation methods. Values greater than 0 will increase encoder speed at the expense of quality. See libvpx documentation of the VP8E_SET_CPUUSED option for further information. Value range is [-16,16]. Values outside the range are ignored. The default value for configuration of libvpx used within webmdshow is 0.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoStaticThreshold
member.summary: Gets or sets static macroblock threshold. Sets the threshold for macroblocks to be treated as static by libvpx. When active it allows the encoder to skip blocks that it deems static based on the provided threshold. Values > 1000 not advisable, and any value greater than 0 can cause encoding artifacts due to skipped blocks. Values less than 0 are ignored.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSWebMEncoder.VideoDecimate
member.summary: Gets or sets decimate value. Reduces frame rate of input video by discarding video frames based on Decimate value. For Decimate value N, and N >= 2, the VP8 encoder filter encodes only every Nth frame. Decimate values less or equal 1 disable decimation.

member.summary: Switch to Runtime Config mode. This will reset all settings to default, and no changes to the settings will be saved. You can use this to programmatically configure LAV Audio without interfering with the users settings in the registry. Subsequent calls to this function will reset all settings back to defaults, even if the mode does not change.
member.param: if set to true [b runtime configuration].
member.remarks: Note that calling this function during playback is not supported and may exhibit undocumented behaviour. For smooth operations, it must be called before LAV Audio is connected to other filters.

member.summary: Obtain stream stats.
member.remarks: STATSG has to be qualified because it is defined both in System.Runtime.InteropServices and System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes. The STATSTG structure is shared by streams, storages and byte arrays. Members irrelevant to streams or not available from System.IO.Stream are not returned, which leaves only cbSize and grfMode as meaningful and available pieces of information. grfStatFlag is used to indicate whether the stream name should be returned and is ignored because this information is unavailable.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.MediaInfo.MediaInfoFilesCache
member.summary: Provides an in-memory cache for media file information to optimize repeated access to file metadata. This cache stores MediaInfoReader instances to avoid redundant file analysis operations, significantly improving performance when accessing the same media files multiple times.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.MediaInfo.MediaInfoFilesCache._cache

member.param: The DirectShow context for media operations and logging.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaInfo.MediaInfoFilesCache.Finalize

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaInfo.MediaInfoFilesCache.Clear

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaInfo.MediaInfoFilesCache.GetInfo(System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Retrieves media information for the specified file, using cache if available. If the file information is not cached, it analyzes the file and stores the result for future access. This method significantly improves performance for repeated access to the same media files.

When true, uses the LibMediaInfo library for analysis (more comprehensive but slower). When false, uses DirectShow filters (faster but may not support all formats).
member.returns: A MediaInfoReader instance containing comprehensive media file information including video streams, audio streams, subtitles, and format details.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore
member.remarks: Audio effects can be applied to individual audio streams (0-3) or to all streams simultaneously using streamIndex = -1. Effects are processed in real-time using DirectSound audio processors. Custom audio effect filters can also be added via CLSID registration.
member.summary: MediaPlayerCore DVD playback functionality. This partial class contains all DVD-specific playback methods including chapter navigation, menu control, audio/subtitle stream selection, and display configuration. Supports standard DVD navigation features and integrates with DirectShow DVD filters.
member.remarks: DVD playback requires appropriate DVD decoder filters to be installed on the system. The class provides both synchronous and asynchronous methods for all DVD operations. DVD navigation uses the DirectShow DVD Navigator filter internally.
member.summary: MediaPlayerCore engine methods. This partial class contains core engine functionality including filter graph management, DirectShow event handling, motion detection, settings persistence, and various playback control methods.
member.remarks: This class handles low-level DirectShow operations, event processing, and core playback engine functionality. It includes DVD event processing, motion detection algorithms, and frame-accurate navigation capabilities.
member.summary: Defines event handlers for the MediaPlayerCore class, providing notifications for various playback states, DVD navigation, audio/video processing, and error conditions.
member.remarks: This partial class contains all event declarations and their corresponding invocation methods. Events are organized by category: DVD events, playback control events, frame processing events, audio analysis events, and error/diagnostic events.
member.summary: Partial implementation of MediaPlayerCore that provides standard media player control functionality and video effects manipulation through interface implementations.
member.remarks: This partial class implements the IMediaPlayerControls interface to provide standard media playback operations (play, pause, stop, seek) and the IVideoEffectsControls interface for real-time video effect adjustments. Methods in this class primarily delegate to the core MediaPlayerCore implementation while providing interface-compliant signatures.
member.summary: Partial class containing initialization logic and factory methods for creating MediaPlayerCore instances with various configurations.
member.remarks: This file contains constructors and initialization methods that set up the media player infrastructure, including DirectShow filters, audio processors, video renderers, and platform-specific components.
member.summary: Partial class containing license validation logic for MediaPlayerCore features.
member.remarks: This file implements license checking for features that require Professional or Premium editions of the SDK. It validates the current configuration and raises events when unlicensed features are detected.
member.summary: Partial class containing logging, telemetry, and error handling functionality for MediaPlayerCore.
member.remarks: This file implements comprehensive logging using Serilog, error event propagation, and telemetry collection via Sentry for debugging and quality improvement. All logging is configurable and respects user privacy settings.
member.summary: MediaPlayerCore class. Main Media Player SDK class that perform all real work.
Partial class containing On-Screen Display (OSD) functionality for MediaPlayerCore.
member.remarks: This file implements a layer-based OSD system that allows overlaying text, images, and graphics on video playback. Multiple layers can be created, positioned, and rendered with transparency and color key support. OSD is useful for watermarks, subtitles, logos, and dynamic information overlays.
member.summary: Partial class containing Picture-in-Picture (PiP) functionality for MediaPlayerCore.
member.remarks: This file implements PiP support, allowing multiple video sources to be displayed simultaneously with the main video. PiP sources can include video files, live camera feeds, screen captures, or IP camera streams. Each PiP source can be positioned, sized, and layered independently. Currently requires VMR9 video renderer.
member.summary: Partial class containing playlist management functionality for MediaPlayerCore.
member.remarks: This file implements a playlist system that allows sequential playback of multiple media files or streams. The playlist supports local files and network URLs, provides navigation controls (next/previous), and can be modified during playback. Files are played in the order they were added to the playlist.
member.summary: Partial class containing property definitions and configuration settings for MediaPlayerCore.
member.remarks: This file defines all public properties used to configure media playback, including: audio/video settings, effects, rendering options, source modes, and advanced features. Properties implement INotifyPropertyChanged for data binding support.
member.summary: Partial class containing media file metadata (tags) reading functionality for MediaPlayerCore.
member.remarks: This file provides methods to read metadata tags from various media file formats including ID3 tags from MP3 files, Vorbis comments from Ogg files, and metadata from MP4, WMV, and other container formats.
member.summary: Partial class containing CPU-based video effects management for MediaPlayerCore.
member.remarks: This file implements the video effects system that processes frames using CPU-based algorithms. Effects include color adjustments, transforms, overlays, and filters. Effects are processed in the order they were added and can be enabled/disabled dynamically during playback.
member.summary: Partial class containing GPU-accelerated video effects management for MediaPlayerCore.
member.remarks: This file implements hardware-accelerated video effects using DirectX 11 compute shaders. GPU effects provide better performance than CPU effects, especially for high-resolution video and complex processing. Requires DirectX 11 compatible graphics hardware.
member.summary: Partial class containing video renderer configuration and control for MediaPlayerCore.
member.remarks: This file manages the video rendering subsystem including renderer selection, display updates, deinterlacing, and hardware-based video adjustments. Different renderers (EVR, VMR9, VMR7) offer various features and compatibility levels.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Audio_Effects_DS_Chorus(System.Int32,System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSChorusPhase,VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSChorusWaveForm,System.Single)
member.summary: Configures a DirectSound Chorus effect that creates a richer, fuller sound by simulating multiple voices or instruments playing in unison. The effect works by mixing the original signal with slightly delayed and pitch-modulated copies.
member.param: Index of the audio stream to configure (0-3 for individual streams, -1 for all streams).
The unique identifier name of the chorus effect to configure.

Base delay time in milliseconds (0.0 - 20.0). Controls the time offset of the chorus voices.
Typical values: 10-25 ms for subtle chorus, 40-60 ms for pronounced effect

Modulation depth as percentage (0.0 - 100.0). Controls how much the delay time varies.
Higher values create more dramatic pitch variations and "warbling"

Feedback percentage (-99.0 to 99.0). Controls how much of the output is fed back to the input.
Positive values create resonant effects, negative values create hollow effects

LFO (Low Frequency Oscillator) rate in Hz (0.0 - 10.0). Controls the speed of delay modulation.
Lower values (0.1-2.0) create slow, sweeping effects; higher values create vibrato

Phase relationship between channels (DSChorusPhase enum). Controls stereo width:
Phase_Neg180 - Wide stereo image
Phase_Neg90 - Moderate stereo spread
Phase_Zero - Mono chorus
Phase_90 - Moderate stereo spread
Phase_180 - Wide stereo image (inverted)
LFO waveform shape (DSChorusWaveForm enum). Triangle waves sound smoother, sine waves sound more natural.

Balance between processed (wet) and original (dry) signal (0.0 - 100.0).
0 = dry only, 50 = equal mix, 100 = wet only

remarks.para: Common chorus settings:

list.item: Subtle thickening: delay=15, depth=10, feedback=0, frequency=1.1, wetDryMix=30
Classic chorus: delay=30, depth=25, feedback=25, frequency=1.5, wetDryMix=50
Extreme effect: delay=40, depth=100, feedback=50, frequency=5.0, wetDryMix=70

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Audio_Effects_DS_Compressor(System.Int32,System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Configures a DirectSound Compressor effect that reduces the dynamic range of audio by automatically lowering the volume of loud sounds while keeping quiet sounds unchanged. Essential for professional audio processing, broadcast limiting, and preventing clipping.
member.param: Index of the audio stream to configure (0-3 for individual streams, -1 for all streams).
The unique identifier name of the compressor effect to configure.

Attack time in milliseconds (0.01 - 500.0). How quickly the compressor responds to signals exceeding the threshold.
Fast attack (0.1-10 ms): Catches transients but may sound unnatural
Slow attack (10-100 ms): Preserves transients but may miss peaks

Output gain in dB (-60.0 to 60.0). Compensates for volume reduction caused by compression.
Typically set to restore perceived loudness after compression

Look-ahead time in milliseconds (0.0 - 4.0). Allows the compressor to "see" incoming peaks.
Helps prevent transients from passing through uncompressed

Compression ratio (1.0 - 100.0). Determines how much signals above threshold are reduced.
1:1 = No compression
2:1 = Gentle compression (2 dB input = 1 dB output above threshold)
4:1 = Moderate compression
10:1 = Heavy compression
20:1+ = Limiting

Release time in milliseconds (50.0 - 3000.0). How quickly compression stops after signal drops below threshold.
Fast release (50-100 ms): Responsive but may cause "pumping"
Slow release (200-1000 ms): Smooth but may over-compress quiet passages

Threshold level in dB (-60.0 to 0.0). Signal level at which compression begins.
0 dB = Compress everything
-10 dB = Compress only loud peaks
-20 to -30 dB = Typical for general compression

remarks.para: Common compressor presets:

list.item: Vocal: attack=5, gain=3, preDelay=0, ratio=3, release=100, threshold=-15
Master bus: attack=10, gain=2, preDelay=0.5, ratio=2, release=200, threshold=-12
Limiting: attack=0.1, gain=0, preDelay=1, ratio=20, release=50, threshold=-3
Bass: attack=10, gain=4, preDelay=0, ratio=4, release=200, threshold=-20

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Audio_Effects_DS_Distortion(System.Int32,System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Configures a DirectSound Distortion effect that adds harmonic content and "grit" to audio by clipping and shaping the waveform. Commonly used for electric guitar, bass, and creative sound design to add aggression, warmth, or lo-fi character to audio.
member.param: Index of the audio stream to configure (0-3 for individual streams, -1 for all streams).
The unique identifier name of the distortion effect to configure.

Distortion intensity/hardness (0.0 - 100.0). Controls the sharpness of clipping.
0-20: Soft clipping, warm overdrive
20-50: Moderate distortion, tube-like
50-80: Hard distortion, aggressive
80-100: Extreme clipping, fuzz effect

Pre-distortion gain in dB (-60.0 to 0.0). Input level before distortion.
Higher values drive the distortion harder, creating more harmonics
Typical: -20 to -10 dB for moderate distortion

Post-distortion EQ bandwidth in Hz (100.0 - 8000.0). Width of frequency boost/cut.
Narrow (100-500): Focused tone shaping
Wide (1000-8000): Broad tonal changes

Post-distortion EQ center frequency in Hz (100.0 - 8000.0). Frequency to boost/cut after distortion.
200-500 Hz: Adds body and warmth
1000-2000 Hz: Adds presence and bite
3000-5000 Hz: Adds brightness and edge

Pre-distortion low-pass filter cutoff in Hz (100.0 - 8000.0). Removes high frequencies before distortion.
Lower values (500-2000) create smoother, warmer distortion
Higher values (4000-8000) preserve brightness and create harsher tones

remarks.para: The signal flow is: Input → Low-pass filter → Gain → Distortion → EQ → Output
Common distortion presets:

list.item: Warm overdrive: edge=15, gain=-15, postEQBandwidth=1000, postEQCenterFrequency=800, preLowpassCutOff=3000
Rock distortion: edge=50, gain=-10, postEQBandwidth=2000, postEQCenterFrequency=2000, preLowpassCutOff=5000
Fuzz bass: edge=80, gain=-5, postEQBandwidth=500, postEQCenterFrequency=250, preLowpassCutOff=1000
Lo-fi effect: edge=30, gain=-20, postEQBandwidth=3000, postEQCenterFrequency=1500, preLowpassCutOff=2000

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Audio_Effects_DS_Echo(System.Int32,System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Int32,System.Single)
member.summary: Configures a DirectSound Echo effect that creates delayed repetitions of the audio signal. Unlike reverb, echo produces distinct, audible repetitions that can create spatial depth, rhythmic patterns, or psychedelic effects.
member.param: Index of the audio stream to configure (0-3 for individual streams, -1 for all streams).
The unique identifier name of the echo effect to configure.

Feedback percentage (0.0 - 100.0). Controls how much of the echo output is fed back into the input.
0-30: Single or few echoes that fade quickly
30-60: Multiple echoes with moderate decay
60-90: Many echoes with slow decay
90-100: Near-infinite echoes (use carefully to avoid feedback loops)

Left channel delay in milliseconds (1.0 - 2000.0). Time between original sound and echo.
Common values:
50-150 ms: Slapback echo (rockabilly vocals)
200-400 ms: Quarter/eighth note echoes at typical tempos
500-1000 ms: Long echoes for ambient effects

Right channel delay in milliseconds (1.0 - 2000.0). Can differ from left for stereo effects.
Set equal to leftDelay for mono echo, or vary for ping-pong effects

Stereo ping-pong mode (0 or 1). When enabled, echoes alternate between left and right channels.
0 = Normal stereo echo, 1 = Ping-pong echo effect

Balance between processed (wet) and original (dry) signal (0.0 - 100.0).
0 = dry only, 50 = equal mix, 100 = wet only
Typical: 20-40 for subtle echo, 50-70 for prominent effect

remarks.para: Echo vs Reverb: Echo creates distinct repetitions, while reverb creates a wash of reflections.
Common echo presets:

list.item: Slapback: leftDelay=120, rightDelay=120, feedback=15, panDelay=0, wetDryMix=30
Stereo spread: leftDelay=250, rightDelay=375, feedback=40, panDelay=0, wetDryMix=35
Ping-pong: leftDelay=500, rightDelay=500, feedback=50, panDelay=1, wetDryMix=40
Ambient: leftDelay=1000, rightDelay=1500, feedback=70, panDelay=0, wetDryMix=60

list.item: Creates and configures the DVD Navigator filter
Sets up IDvdInfo2 and IDvdControl2 interfaces for DVD control
Configures custom video/audio decoders if specified
Sets up video effects and rendering pipeline
Configures audio processing and effects
Initializes DVD-specific options like HMSF timecode events

remarks.para: Called internally during DVD playback initialization.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.DVDSubpictureConfigure
member.summary: Configures the DVD subpicture (subtitle) stream connections in the filter graph. Handles the routing of subpicture data from the DVD source through decoders to the video renderer.

remarks.para: DVD subpictures include:

list.item: Subtitles in various languages
Closed captions (Line21 data)
Menu highlights and overlays
Karaoke lyrics or other overlay graphics

remarks.para: This method ensures proper connection of subpicture streams through the decoder to the video renderer for overlay display.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.DVDAudioConfigure
member.summary: Configures the complete DVD audio pipeline including custom decoders, audio renderers, effects processors, and audio analysis components.

remarks.para: This method handles:

list.item: Custom audio decoder setup (if specified)
Audio format detection (AC3, MPEG, etc.)
Audio renderer configuration based on playback mode
Audio effects chain initialization
VU meter and audio analysis setup
Channel mapping and audio enhancement

remarks.para: DVD audio can include multiple formats like Dolby AC3, DTS, MPEG audio, or LPCM. The method automatically detects and configures the appropriate decoder.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.ReversePlayback_NextFrame
member.summary: Advances to the next frame during reverse playback mode or returns to forward direction. Provides frame-by-frame forward navigation even when in reverse playback mode.

remarks.para: When in reverse playback mode, this method moves forward one frame, which can be used to fine-tune position after reverse seeking.
Common usage scenarios:

list.item: Fine-tuning position after reverse navigation
Implementing jog/shuttle controls
Frame-accurate editing workflows
Creating smooth variable-speed playback

remarks.para: For standard forward frame-stepping when not in reverse mode, use NextFrame() instead.
