member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnFilterAdded
member.summary: Occurs when a new DirectShow filter is added to the filter graph.
member.remarks: This event is useful for debugging filter graph construction and for accessing specific filters for advanced configuration. The event provides the filter name and interface pointer for direct manipulation. Note: This event is only available when using the DirectShow engine.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnError
member.summary: Occurs when any error is encountered during media playback or processing.
member.remarks: This is the primary error notification mechanism. Errors can include file access issues, codec problems, hardware failures, or invalid operations. Always subscribe to this event to handle errors gracefully and provide appropriate user feedback. The event args contain error codes, descriptions, and suggested recovery actions.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnLicenseRequired
member.summary: Occurs when a feature requires a valid license but none is found or the current license is insufficient.
member.remarks: This event fires when attempting to use Professional or Premium features without appropriate licensing. The event args indicate which feature requires licensing and the minimum license level needed. Use this to prompt users to upgrade or activate their license.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnAudioFrameBuffer
member.summary: Occurs when a new audio frame buffer is available for processing.
member.remarks: This event provides raw audio samples for real-time processing, analysis, or visualization. Audio data is provided as a byte array with format information (sample rate, channels, bit depth). Performance note: This event fires frequently (typically 20-50 times per second), so handlers should be optimized for performance and avoid blocking operations.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnDataFrameBuffer
member.summary: Occurs when a new data frame (subtitles, metadata, or other non-AV data) is received.
member.remarks: This event is specific to the FFMPEG engine and provides access to data streams such as subtitles, closed captions, or embedded metadata. The frame data includes timing information for synchronization with audio/video streams. Note: Only available when using the FFMPEG engine.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnFFMPEGSourceTimestamp
member.summary: Occurs when the FFMPEG source decoder processes a new frame with timestamp information.
member.remarks: This event provides precise timestamp data for each decoded frame, useful for synchronization, frame-accurate seeking, and timing analysis. The event includes both presentation timestamp (PTS) and decode timestamp (DTS) values. Note: Only available when using the FFMPEG engine.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnVideoFrameBuffer
member.summary: Occurs when a new video frame buffer is available for processing.
member.remarks: This event provides raw video frame data in various pixel formats (RGB, YUV, etc.) for real-time processing, analysis, or custom rendering. The frame data includes resolution, stride, and format information. Performance note: Handle this event efficiently as it fires at the video frame rate (e.g., 30-60 times per second). Consider using async processing for heavy operations.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnVideoFrameBufferWPF
member.summary: Occurs when a new video frame buffer is available, optimized for WPF applications.
member.remarks: This WPF-specific event provides video frames in a format optimized for WPF rendering, typically as WriteableBitmap-compatible data. Use this instead of OnVideoFrameBuffer in WPF applications for better performance and easier integration with WPF imaging. The event is marshaled to the UI thread when necessary.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnVideoFrameBitmap
member.summary: Occurs when a new video frame is available as a System.Drawing.Bitmap object.
member.remarks: This event provides video frames as Bitmap objects for easy integration with Windows Forms or any code using System.Drawing. The bitmap is a managed copy of the video frame, suitable for display or further processing. Note: Creating bitmaps has performance overhead; use OnVideoFrameBuffer for better performance in high-throughput scenarios.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnFaceDetected
member.summary: Occurs when one or more faces are detected in a video frame.
member.remarks: This event fires only when face detection is enabled and faces are found in the frame. The event args contain face locations, confidence scores, and optional facial landmarks. Face detection must be enabled via video effects settings before this event will fire. Performance note: Face detection is CPU/GPU intensive; adjust detection frequency based on your performance requirements.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnAudioVUMeter
member.summary: Occurs when new audio level meter (VU meter) data is available.
member.remarks: This event provides real-time audio level information for creating visual audio meters. Data includes peak and RMS levels for each audio channel, typically ranging from -60dB to 0dB. Update frequency depends on audio processing settings but is usually 10-30 updates per second for smooth visualization.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnAudioVUMeterProVolume
member.summary: Occurs when professional-grade audio volume level data is available from VU Meter Pro.
member.remarks: This event provides high-precision audio level measurements with additional metrics beyond basic VU meters, including true peak, loudness units (LUFS), and dynamic range. Requires VU Meter Pro to be enabled. Useful for broadcast compliance and professional audio monitoring applications.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnAudioVUMeterProFFTCalculated
member.summary: Occurs when FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) frequency analysis data is available from VU Meter Pro.
member.remarks: This event provides frequency spectrum data for creating spectrum analyzers and frequency visualizations. FFT data includes magnitude values across frequency bins, typically 256-2048 bins covering the audible spectrum (20Hz-20kHz). Requires VU Meter Pro with FFT analysis enabled.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnAudioVUMeterProMaximumCalculated
member.summary: Occurs when peak hold and minimum/maximum audio level statistics are calculated by VU Meter Pro.
member.remarks: This event provides statistical audio level data including peak hold values, minimum levels over a time window, and clipping detection. Useful for peak indicators, overload warnings, and dynamic range analysis. Update frequency is typically lower than real-time levels (1-5 Hz).

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnMotion
member.summary: Occurs when motion is detected in the video stream based on configured motion detection settings.
member.remarks: This event fires only when motion detection is enabled and motion exceeding the configured threshold is detected. Event args include motion level (0-100%), affected regions, and motion vector data if available. Use motion detection settings to configure sensitivity, regions of interest, and minimum motion duration to reduce false positives.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnNetworkSourceStop
member.summary: Occurs when a network media source (RTSP, RTMP, HTTP stream) stops or loses connection.
member.remarks: This event is specific to network streams and helps distinguish between intentional stops and connection failures. Use this to implement reconnection logic, display connection status, or switch to backup streams. Note: Only available when using the FFMPEG engine with network sources.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnStart
member.summary: Occurs when media playback successfully starts after calling Play() or at the beginning of a new file.
member.remarks: This event indicates that the media pipeline is fully initialized and playback has begun. Use this event to update UI controls, start timers, or perform actions that depend on active playback. For playlist mode, this fires at the start of each file.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnLoop
member.summary: Occurs when playback reaches the end and automatically restarts due to loop mode being enabled.
member.remarks: This event only fires when the Loop property is true and playback cycles from end to beginning. Use this to track loop iterations, update loop counters, or perform actions at each loop point. For seamless looping, ensure any event handlers execute quickly to avoid playback gaps.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnPause
member.summary: Occurs when media playback is paused via the Pause() method or automatic pausing.
member.remarks: This event confirms that playback has been successfully paused and the media pipeline is in a paused state. Audio/video rendering stops but the current position is maintained. Use this to update pause/play button states and disable time-sensitive operations.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnResume
member.summary: Occurs when media playback resumes from a paused state via Resume() or Play().
member.remarks: This event indicates that playback has successfully resumed from the exact position where it was paused. Use this to restore UI states, restart timers, or resume any operations that were suspended during pause.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnStop
member.summary: Occurs when media playback stops completely, either by calling Stop() or reaching the end.
member.remarks: This event indicates that the media pipeline has been shut down and resources released. The StopEventArgs indicate whether the stop was user-initiated or due to reaching the end. After this event, the player returns to an uninitialized state and requires Play() to restart.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnPlaylistFinished
member.summary: Occurs when all items in a playlist have completed playback.
member.remarks: This event fires after the last item in a playlist finishes playing and loop mode is disabled. Use this to display completion messages, automatically load new playlists, or return to a menu interface. This event will not fire if loop mode is enabled for the playlist.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnNewFilePlaybackStarted
member.summary: Occurs when playback of a new media file begins, either individually or as part of a playlist.
member.remarks: This event provides information about the newly started file including filename, duration, format details, and playlist index if applicable. Use this to update now-playing displays, load file-specific settings, or log playback history. Fires after OnStart for each new file.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnMIDIFileInfo
member.summary: Occurs when MIDI file information becomes available during playback of MIDI files.
member.remarks: This event provides MIDI-specific information such as tempo changes, instrument programs, lyrics, and other MIDI metadata. Only fires when playing MIDI files (.mid, .midi, .kar). Event frequency depends on MIDI content but typically occurs at tempo changes, program changes, or lyric events.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#State
member.summary: Gets the current playback state of the media player.
member.value: The current state: Stopped, Playing, Paused, or Finished. Use this property to update UI controls or determine valid operations.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#Duration
member.summary: Gets the total duration of the currently loaded media file.
member.returns: A TimeSpan representing the total media duration. Returns TimeSpan.Zero if no media is loaded or duration cannot be determined (e.g., live streams).

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#DurationAsync
member.summary: Asynchronously gets the total duration of the currently loaded media file.
member.returns: A task that returns a TimeSpan representing the total media duration. Use this method when accessing duration from UI threads to avoid blocking.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#OpenAsync(System.String)
member.summary: Asynchronously opens a media file for playback, clearing any existing playlist.
member.param: The full path to the media file or a valid URL for network streams.
member.returns: A task that returns true if the file was successfully added to the playlist. Note: This method only prepares the file; call PlayAsync() to start playback.
member.remarks: Supported formats depend on installed codecs and the selected media engine. Common formats include MP4, AVI, MKV, MP3, AAC, and various streaming protocols.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#Pause
member.summary: Pauses the current media playback while maintaining the current position.
member.returns: true if the pause operation was successful; false if the player is not in a pauseable state (e.g., already paused, stopped, or no media loaded).
member.remarks: Pausing stops audio/video rendering but keeps all resources allocated for quick resume. The OnPause event will fire upon successful pause.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#Play(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Starts or preloads media playback from the current position.
member.param: If true, initializes the media pipeline and buffers content without starting playback. Useful for reducing start latency when playback timing is critical.
member.returns: true if the operation was successful; false if no media is loaded or an error occurred.
member.remarks: When onlyPreload is true, the media graph is built and initial buffering occurs, but playback remains paused. Call Play(false) or Resume() to begin actual playback after preloading.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#PlayAsync(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Asynchronously starts or preloads media playback from the current position.
member.param: If true, initializes the media pipeline and buffers content without starting playback. Useful for reducing start latency when playback timing is critical.
member.returns: A task that returns true if the operation was successful; false if no media is loaded or an error occurred.
member.remarks: This async version is recommended for UI applications to prevent blocking during media initialization, which can take several seconds for large files or network streams.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#Position_Get
member.summary: Gets the current playback position within the media file.
member.returns: A TimeSpan representing the current position. Returns TimeSpan.Zero if no media is loaded or playback hasn't started. For live streams, represents time since stream start.
member.remarks: Position accuracy depends on the media format and codec. Some formats may only provide approximate positions between keyframes.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#Position_GetAsync
member.summary: Asynchronously gets the current playback position within the media file.
member.returns: A task that returns a TimeSpan representing the current position. Use this method when accessing position from UI threads to avoid blocking.
member.remarks: This method is particularly useful when updating position displays frequently, as it prevents UI thread blocking during position queries.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#Position_Set(System.TimeSpan,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Seeks to a specific position within the media file.
member.param: The target position as a TimeSpan. Must be between zero and the media duration.
Currently not used in this implementation. In other contexts, would determine whether to seek to the nearest keyframe (faster but less accurate) or exact position.
member.remarks: Seeking performance varies by media format. Formats with keyframes (H.264, MPEG) may have seek delays. Some formats or network streams may not support seeking. The actual position after seeking may differ slightly from the requested position.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#Position_SetAsync(System.TimeSpan,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Asynchronously seeks to a specific position within the media file.
member.param: The target position as a TimeSpan. Must be between zero and the media duration.
Currently not used in this implementation. In other contexts, would determine whether to seek to the nearest keyframe (faster but less accurate) or exact position.
member.returns: A task that completes when the seek operation finishes. The player may still be buffering after the task completes.
member.remarks: Use this async version for smoother UI responsiveness, especially when seeking in large files or network streams where seek operations can take several seconds.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#Resume
member.summary: Resumes playback from a paused state at the current position.
member.returns: true if playback was successfully resumed; false if the player was not in a paused state or an error occurred.
member.remarks: Resume only works when the player is paused. Use Play() to start from a stopped state. The OnResume event will fire upon successful resume.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#Stop
member.summary: Stops playback and releases all media resources.
member.remarks: Stopping releases the media pipeline, decoders, and buffers. The playback position returns to the beginning. To pause while maintaining position and resources, use Pause() instead. The OnStop event will fire when stop is complete.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#StopAsync
member.summary: Asynchronously stops playback and releases all media resources.
member.returns: A task that completes when all resources have been released and the player is fully stopped.
member.remarks: Use this async version to prevent UI blocking during resource cleanup, which can take time for complex media graphs or when releasing hardware decoders.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#Volume_Get
member.summary: Gets the current audio playback volume level.
member.returns: The volume as a normalized value between 0.0 (muted) and 1.0 (maximum volume). Note: The actual loudness depends on system volume and audio hardware.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#Volume_Set(System.Double)
member.summary: Sets the audio playback volume level.
member.param: The desired volume as a normalized value between 0.0 (muted) and 1.0 (maximum). Values outside this range will be clamped.
member.remarks: This controls the media player's volume independently of system volume. Changes take effect immediately during playback.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#NextFrame
member.summary: Advances playback by exactly one video frame while maintaining paused state.
member.returns: true if the frame advance was successful; false if not in a valid state (e.g., not paused, no video stream, or at end of file).
member.remarks: Useful for frame-by-frame analysis or precise editing. Only works when paused. The exact frame duration depends on the video frame rate (e.g., ~33ms for 30fps video).

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#PrevFrame
member.summary: Moves playback back by one video frame while maintaining paused state.
member.returns: Always returns false as this functionality is not currently implemented. Frame-accurate reverse seeking requires specialized decoder support.
member.remarks: Previous frame functionality is complex due to video compression using inter-frame dependencies. Most codecs only decode forward efficiently.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IMediaPlayerControls#GetFileThumbnail(System.String)
member.summary: Generates a thumbnail image from the specified media file.
member.param: The full path to the media file from which to extract a thumbnail.
member.returns: An SKBitmap containing the thumbnail image, typically from the first frame. Returns null if the file cannot be opened or contains no video.
member.remarks: This method opens the file temporarily to extract a frame. For better performance when generating multiple thumbnails, consider caching results. The thumbnail is taken from the beginning of the file (TimeSpan.Zero).

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IVideoEffectsControls#VideoEffects_SetBrightness(System.Double)
member.summary: Adjusts the video brightness level in real-time.
member.param: Brightness adjustment from -1.0 (darkest) to 1.0 (brightest). 0.0 represents no change from original brightness.
member.remarks: This effect is implemented using separate lightness (positive values) and darkness (negative values) filters for optimal quality. Changes apply immediately to the current video stream. The effect persists until cleared or the value is reset to 0.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IVideoEffectsControls#VideoEffects_SetContrast(System.Double)
member.summary: Adjusts the video contrast level in real-time.
member.param: Contrast adjustment from -1.0 (minimum contrast) to 1.0 (maximum contrast). 0.0 represents no change from original contrast.
member.remarks: Contrast affects the difference between light and dark areas. Positive values increase contrast (making darks darker and lights lighter), while negative values reduce it. Changes apply immediately during playback.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IVideoEffectsControls#VideoEffects_SetSaturation(System.Double)
member.summary: Adjusts the video color saturation level in real-time.
member.param: Saturation adjustment from -1.0 (grayscale) to 1.0 (maximum saturation). 0.0 represents normal color saturation.
member.remarks: Saturation controls color intensity. Negative values reduce color toward grayscale, while positive values make colors more vivid. Extreme positive values may cause color clipping. Changes apply immediately during playback.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IVideoEffectsControls#VideoEffects_SetGrayscale(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Enables or disables grayscale conversion of the video.
member.param: true to convert video to grayscale (black and white); false to show normal color.
member.remarks: When enabled, all color information is removed, showing only luminance values. This is different from setting saturation to -1.0 as it uses a proper luminance conversion algorithm. Useful for artistic effects or improving visibility of details.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IVideoEffectsControls#VideoEffects_SetFlipX(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Enables or disables horizontal flipping (mirroring) of the video.
member.param: true to flip the video horizontally (mirror image); false for normal orientation.
member.remarks: Horizontal flip creates a mirror image, reversing left and right. Useful for selfie-style video or correcting mirrored sources. Note: The internal effect name "FlipDown" is used for historical compatibility but performs horizontal flipping.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IVideoEffectsControls#VideoEffects_SetFlipY(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Enables or disables vertical flipping of the video.
member.param: true to flip the video vertically (upside down); false for normal orientation.
member.remarks: Vertical flip rotates the image 180 degrees around the horizontal axis. Useful for correcting inverted video sources. Note: The internal effect name "FlipRight" is used for historical compatibility but performs vertical flipping.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IVideoEffectsControls#VideoEffects_SetInvert(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Enables or disables color inversion (negative image) effect on the video.
member.param: true to invert all colors; false for normal colors.
member.remarks: Color inversion creates a negative image where each color is replaced by its complementary color (255 - original value for each RGB channel). White becomes black, red becomes cyan, etc. Useful for artistic effects or improving visibility of certain content types.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VisioForge#Core#Types#IVideoEffectsControls#VideoEffects_Clear
member.summary: Removes all active video effects and restores the original video appearance.
member.remarks: This method clears all effects added through this interface or the Video_Effects_Add method, including brightness, contrast, saturation, flips, and any custom effects. The video immediately returns to its original, unprocessed state. Effects must be reapplied if needed.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.CreateAsync(VisioForge.Core.Types.IVideoView)
member.summary: Asynchronously creates a new MediaPlayerCore instance with a specified video view.

member.returns: A task that returns a fully initialized MediaPlayerCore instance ready for use.
member.remarks: This factory method is recommended for UI applications to prevent blocking during initialization. The video view is automatically attached and configured for optimal rendering based on the UI framework.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.CreateAsync

member.returns: A task that returns a fully initialized MediaPlayerCore instance ready for use.
member.remarks: Use this factory method for audio-only playback, background processing, or when you'll set the video view later. The player is fully functional but won't display video until a video view is attached.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.#ctor(VisioForge.Core.Types.IVideoView,System.Boolean)

If true (default), immediately initializes all components. If false, you must call Init() or InitAsync() manually before use.
member.remarks: Deferred initialization (initialize=false) is useful when you need to configure properties before the player infrastructure is created.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with default settings.
member.remarks: Creates a player without a video view and immediately initializes all components. For video playback, attach a video view using appropriate methods before playing. This constructor is suitable for simple audio playback scenarios.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.#ctor(System.Boolean)

member.remarks: Use deferred initialization when you need to set properties that affect initialization behavior, such as custom redistributable paths or specific renderer modes.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.InitAsync
member.summary: Asynchronously initializes the media player infrastructure and all required components.
member.returns: A task that completes when initialization is finished.
member.remarks: This method performs the same initialization as Init() but runs on a background thread to prevent UI blocking. Called automatically by CreateAsync factory methods.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Init
member.summary: Initializes the media player infrastructure including DirectShow components, audio processors, video renderers, and platform-specific features.
member.remarks:
This method performs extensive initialization: - Configures logging and telemetry - Sets up DirectShow filter graphs and components - Initializes audio DSP processors for multi-channel audio - Configures video renderers based on OS capabilities - Enumerates available audio output devices - Sets up effect processors and OSD layers - Configures redistributable paths for codecs
Initialization is typically automatic but can be deferred using appropriate constructors.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.CheckRequiredLicense(System.Boolean@,System.Boolean@)
member.summary: Checks the current configuration for features requiring specific license levels and reports any licensing requirements through the OnLicenseRequired event.
member.param: Output parameter set to true if Standard edition features are sufficient. Always true as Standard is the base license level.
Output parameter set to true if Professional edition features are required based on the current configuration.
member.remarks:
This method is called during initialization and configuration changes to validate license requirements. Features checked include: - Advanced source modes (MMS, Memory, VLC-based streaming) - Motion detection capabilities - Reverse playback functionality
When unlicensed features are detected, the OnLicenseRequired event is raised with details about which features require upgrading.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.LoggerClose

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.LoggerConfigure(System.Boolean)

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.LoggerSentryOnStartConfigure

This information helps diagnose configuration issues and missing dependencies. Only runs when Debug_Telemetry is enabled and a debugger is attached. All file attachments are temporary and cleaned up automatically.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.PlayAsync(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Asynchronously starts media playback or prepares the media for delayed playback.
member.param: If true, only builds and prepares the playback graph without starting actual playback. Use this with PlayDelayed() to start playback at a precise moment. Default is false.
member.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result is true if playback started successfully or the graph was prepared successfully, false if an error occurred.

remarks.para: This method performs the following operations:

list.item: Builds the DirectShow filter graph based on media type
Initializes video and audio renderers
Applies configured effects and filters
Starts playback (unless onlyPreload is true)

remarks.para: Use Cases:

remarks.para: This is the synchronous version. For async operations, use PlayAsync().

Source_URL - For network streams
Source_Stream - For memory streams
DVD folder path - For DVD playback

remarks.para: The method will automatically:

Build appropriate filter graph
Configure audio/video renderers
Apply any configured effects
Start playback from the beginning

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Frame_GetCurrent
member.summary: Captures the current video frame from the sample grabber, including any applied video effects.
member.returns: A Bitmap containing the current processed video frame, or null if capture failed, no video is playing, or sample grabbing is not enabled. The caller is responsible for disposing the returned Bitmap.

remarks.para: Prerequisites:

list.item: Video_Sample_Grabber_Enabled must be true (set before Play)
Video must be currently playing or paused
Valid video stream must be present

remarks.para: This method captures frames after video effects processing, so the returned frame includes any applied effects like:

list.item: Color adjustments (brightness, contrast, etc.)
Geometric transforms (rotation, flip)
Filters and overlays
Text/image overlays

remarks.para: Performance note: Enabling sample grabber may impact playback performance, especially for high-resolution video.

New horizontal position in pixels from the left edge of the video.
New vertical position in pixels from the top edge of the video.
member.returns: true if the layer was successfully moved and re-rendered; false if the operation failed or invalid parameters were provided.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OSD_Layers_Render
member.summary: Renders all enabled OSD layers to the video surface by compositing them into a single overlay.
member.returns: true if layers were successfully rendered; false if rendering failed or no enabled layers exist.
member.remarks:
This method creates a composite bitmap from all enabled layers in their z-order, then applies it to the video renderer. The overlay respects transparency settings and is scaled to match the current video dimensions. Call this after making changes to layers to update the display.
Requirements: - Video must be playing or paused (not stopped) - Video dimensions must be valid (non-zero) - At least one layer must be enabled

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OSD_Layers_Clear
member.summary: Removes all OSD layers and clears the overlay from the video surface.
member.remarks: This method deletes all layer objects and their associated resources, then updates the video renderer to remove any visible overlay. Use this for complete OSD cleanup or when switching between different OSD configurations.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OSD_Layers_Clear(System.Int32)
member.summary: Clears the content of a specific OSD layer while preserving the layer itself.
member.param: Zero-based index of the layer to clear. Must be less than the total layer count.
member.remarks: This method resets the layer's bitmap to transparent, removing all drawn content while maintaining the layer's size, position, and other properties. The graphics context is recreated with high-quality rendering settings. After clearing, the video overlay is updated to reflect the change.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OSD_Layers_Enable(System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Enables or disables a specific OSD layer without removing it.
member.param: Zero-based index of the layer to modify. Must be less than the total layer count.
true to make the layer visible during rendering; false to hide it.
member.remarks: Disabled layers are skipped during rendering but retain their content and properties. This allows temporary hiding of overlays without losing their configuration. Call OSD_Layers_Render() after changing enable state to update the display.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OSD_Layers_Create(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Creates a new OSD layer with specified dimensions and position.
member.param: Horizontal position in pixels from the left edge of the video surface.
Vertical position in pixels from the top edge of the video surface.
Width of the layer in pixels. Should not exceed video width.
Height of the layer in pixels. Should not exceed video height.
true to immediately enable the layer for rendering; false to create it disabled.
member.returns: true if the layer was successfully created; false if creation failed.
member.remarks: The new layer is added to the end of the layer list, giving it the highest z-order (rendered on top). The layer is initialized with a transparent background and high-quality graphics settings. Use the returned layer index (count-1) for subsequent operations on this layer.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OSD_Layers_Delete(System.Int32)
member.summary: Deletes a specific OSD layer and removes it from the display.
member.param: Zero-based index of the layer to delete. Must be less than the total layer count.
member.returns: true if the layer was successfully deleted; false if deletion failed or invalid ID.
member.remarks: Deleting a layer removes it from the layer list and updates the video overlay. Layer indices above the deleted layer are shifted down by one. The layer's resources are automatically disposed. Consider using OSD_Layers_Enable(false) if you need to temporarily hide a layer without losing its content.

Horizontal position within the layer to draw the image, in pixels.

true to treat the specified color as transparent; false to draw the image as-is.

member.returns: A task that returns true if the position was successfully updated; false otherwise.
member.remarks: This method allows dynamic repositioning and resizing of PiP sources during playback. The rectangle coordinates are relative to the main video surface, not the window. Alpha blending provides smooth transparency effects for professional-looking overlays. Only available when using async API mode.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.PIP_Sources_SetSourcePosition(System.Int32,System.Drawing.Rectangle,System.Single)
member.summary: Sets the position, size, and transparency of a Picture-in-Picture source.
member.param: Zero-based index of the PiP source to modify. Index 0 is the main video.
Rectangle defining the position (X, Y) and size (Width, Height) in pixels on the video surface.
Transparency level from 0.0 (fully transparent/invisible) to 1.0 (fully opaque). Use values like 0.5 for semi-transparent overlays.
member.returns: true if the position was successfully updated; false otherwise.
member.remarks: This method allows dynamic repositioning and resizing of PiP sources during playback. The rectangle coordinates are relative to the main video surface, not the window. Alpha blending provides smooth transparency effects for professional-looking overlays. Only available when using synchronous API mode.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.PIP_Sources_SetSourcePositionIntl(System.Int32,System.Drawing.Rectangle,System.Single)
member.summary: Internal implementation for setting Picture-in-Picture source position and transparency.
member.param: One-based index of the PiP source when not playing, zero-based during playback.
Rectangle defining position and size on the video surface.
member.remarks: When playback is stopped, this updates the PiP object properties for later use. During playback, it directly calls the video renderer's SetStreamPosition and SetStreamAlpha methods to apply changes immediately.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.AddPIPDevices
member.summary: Initializes and connects all configured Picture-in-Picture sources to the DirectShow graph.
member.remarks:
This internal method is called during playback initialization to set up PiP sources. It performs the following for each PiP source: - Creates appropriate source filters (LAV or standard DirectShow) - Connects sources to the video renderer's input pins - Configures stream sizes and positions - Sets up any required color space converters
Currently only supports file-based PiP sources with LAV or standard DirectShow filters. Requires VMR9 video renderer for PiP functionality.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Playlist_GetPosition
member.summary: Gets the current position (index) within the playlist.
member.returns: Zero-based index of the currently playing or selected item. Returns 0 if playlist is empty.
member.remarks: The position indicates which file is currently playing or will play next. This value persists between playback sessions until changed or the playlist is cleared.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Playlist_SetPosition(System.Int32)
member.summary: Sets the current position within the playlist without starting playback.
member.param: Zero-based index of the item to make current. Must be within valid range.
member.returns: true if the position was successfully set; false if the index is out of range.
member.remarks: This method only changes the playlist position; it doesn't start playback. Use Play() after setting position to begin playing from the new position. If currently playing, stop and play again to switch to the new item.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Playlist_Reset
member.summary: Resets the playlist position to the beginning (first item).
member.remarks: This method sets the current index to 0 but doesn't affect playback state. Useful for restarting playlist playback from the beginning after reaching the end.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Playlist_PlayNext
member.summary: Stops current playback and starts playing the next item in the playlist.
member.returns: true if successfully moved to and started playing the next item; false if already at the end of the playlist.
member.remarks: This method automatically stops the current file, advances the playlist position, and starts playing the next file. If Loop mode is enabled and this is the last item, it will wrap to the first item. The OnNewFilePlaybackStarted event will fire when the new file begins playing.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Playlist_PlayNextAsync
member.summary: Asynchronously stops current playback and starts playing the next item in the playlist.
member.returns: A task that returns true if successfully moved to and started playing the next item; false if already at the end.
member.remarks: This async version prevents UI blocking during the stop/start transition. Particularly useful for network streams or large files where stopping might take time. The method awaits both stop and play operations to complete.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Playlist_PlayPrevious
member.summary: Stops current playback and starts playing the previous item in the playlist.
member.returns: true if successfully moved to and started playing the previous item; false if already at the beginning.
member.remarks: This method automatically stops the current file, moves back one position, and starts playing the previous file. Returns false if currently at index 0. The OnNewFilePlaybackStarted event will fire when the new file begins playing.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Playlist_PlayPreviousAsync
member.summary: Asynchronously stops current playback and starts playing the previous item in the playlist.
member.returns: A task that returns true if successfully moved to and started playing the previous item; false if at the beginning.
member.remarks: This async version prevents UI blocking during the stop/start transition. Useful for maintaining responsive UI when dealing with network streams or large files.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Playlist_Clear
member.summary: Removes all items from the playlist and resets the position to zero.
member.remarks: This method clears all playlist entries but doesn't stop current playback. After clearing, you'll need to add new items before playing again. The playlist position is reset to 0 for consistency.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Playlist_Add(System.String)
member.summary: Adds a media file or stream URL to the end of the playlist.
member.param: Full path to a local file or a valid stream URL. Supported URL protocols: http://, https://, rtsp://, rtmp://, udp://, tcp://
member.returns: true if the item was successfully added; false if the path is invalid or file doesn't exist.
member.remarks: This method validates local file existence but doesn't verify URL accessibility. Items are added to the end of the playlist. Use Playlist_Insert to add at specific positions. The playlist can contain a mix of local files and network streams.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Playlist_Remove(System.String)
member.summary: Removes the first occurrence of a specific file or URL from the playlist.
member.param: The exact file path or URL to remove. Must match exactly.
member.returns: true if the item was found and removed; false if not found in the playlist.
member.remarks: This method uses exact string matching. If multiple identical entries exist, only the first is removed. The current position may be adjusted if the removed item was before the current position.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Playlist_RemoveAt(System.Int32)
member.summary: Removes the playlist item at the specified index.
member.param: Zero-based index of the item to remove.
member.returns: true if an item was removed; false if the index is out of range.
member.remarks: Removing an item shifts all subsequent items down by one position. If the removed item is currently playing, playback continues but the current index may need adjustment. Consider stopping playback before removing the currently playing item.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Playlist_Insert(System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: Inserts a media file at a specific position in the playlist.
member.param: Full path to the file to insert. Must exist on disk.
Zero-based position where the item should be inserted. Items at and after this position are shifted up.
member.returns: true if the file was inserted; false if the file doesn't exist.
member.remarks: Unlike Playlist_Add, this method only accepts local files, not URLs. The file existence is verified before insertion. If the index is beyond the current count, the item is added at the end.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Playlist_GetFilename(System.Int32)
member.summary: Retrieves the file path or URL of the item at the specified playlist position.
member.param: Zero-based index of the item to retrieve.
member.returns: The full file path or URL at the specified index; empty string if index is out of range.
member.remarks: Use this to display playlist contents, check what will play next, or verify playlist entries. The returned path is exactly as it was added to the playlist.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Playlist_GetCount
member.summary: Gets the total number of items currently in the playlist.
member.returns: The count of playlist items. Returns 0 for an empty playlist.
member.remarks: Use this to validate indices before calling other playlist methods, display playlist information, or determine if the playlist is empty. The count includes all items regardless of their playback status.

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.PropertyChanged
member.summary: Occurs when a property value changes, enabling data binding and change notifications.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OnPropertyChanged(System.String)
member.summary: Raises the PropertyChanged event for the specified property.
member.param: Name of the property that changed. Automatically populated by CallerMemberName attribute.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Loop
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether media playback should automatically restart when reaching the end.
member.value: true to enable continuous looping; false for single playback. Default is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the OnLoop event fires each time playback restarts. For playlists, this loops the entire playlist, not individual files.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Loop_DoNotSeekToBeginning
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to skip seeking to the beginning when loop mode restarts playback.
member.value: true to restart from the current position; false to seek to beginning before restarting. Default is false.
member.remarks: This property only affects behavior when Loop is true. Use this for seamless looping of content that doesn't require position reset, improving performance and avoiding visual glitches during loop transitions.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Info_UseLibMediaInfo
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to use the MediaInfo library for detailed file analysis.
member.value: true to use MediaInfo for comprehensive metadata; false to use basic DirectShow info. Default is true.
member.remarks: MediaInfo provides extensive metadata including codecs, bitrates, frame rates, audio channels, subtitles, and container details. Disable this for faster file loading if detailed metadata isn't needed.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Audio_OutputDevice
member.summary: Gets or sets the audio output device name for playback.
member.value: The friendly name of the audio device as returned by Audio_OutputDevice_GetList(). Empty string or null uses the system default audio device.
member.remarks: Set this property before calling Play() to route audio to a specific device. Requires Audio_PlayAudio to be true. Use Audio_OutputDevice_GetList() to enumerate available devices. The device name must match exactly.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Audio_PlayAudio
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether audio output is enabled during playback.
member.value: true to play audio through speakers/headphones; false to mute audio output. Default is true.
member.remarks: Disabling audio output doesn't affect audio processing - effects, level meters, and audio sample events still function. Use this for video-only playback or when processing audio without audible output.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Audio_Channel_Mapper
member.summary: Gets or sets audio channel mapping configuration for custom channel routing.
member.value: AudioChannelMapperSettings object defining how input channels map to output channels. null disables channel mapping.
member.remarks: Use channel mapping to reroute audio channels (e.g., swap left/right, extract specific channels, or create custom surround configurations). Useful for multi-language content or correcting channel misalignment.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Audio_Effects_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether audio effect processing is enabled.
member.value: true to enable audio effects pipeline; false to bypass all audio effects. Default is false.
member.remarks: This is the master switch for all audio effects. Individual effects must also be configured and enabled. Disabling this improves performance when effects aren't needed. Effects include EQ, dynamics, reverb, and custom DSP.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Audio_Effects_Tempo_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether tempo/pitch control effect is enabled.
member.value: true to enable tempo adjustment without pitch change; false to disable. Default is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, use Audio_Effects_Tempo_Value to adjust playback speed while maintaining original pitch. Useful for language learning, music practice, or time-stretching. Disabling this also resets playback speed to 1.0x. Requires Audio_Effects_Enabled to be true.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Audio_Effects_Tempo_Value
member.summary: Gets or sets the tempo adjustment value for time-stretching audio.
member.value: Tempo multiplier in permille (1000 = normal speed). Range: 500 (half speed) to 2000 (double speed). Default is 1000.
member.remarks: This adjusts playback speed without changing pitch. Examples: - 500 = 0.5x speed (slower) - 1000 = 1.0x speed (normal) - 1500 = 1.5x speed (faster) - 2000 = 2.0x speed (double) Requires Audio_Effects_Tempo_Enabled to be true.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Audio_Enhancer_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the audio enhancement processor is enabled.
member.value: true to enable multi-band audio enhancement; false to disable. Default is false.
member.remarks: The audio enhancer provides professional audio processing including normalization, auto-gain control, and multi-band dynamics. Configure individual enhancement parameters using Audio_Enhancer methods. Useful for improving audio quality or matching levels across different content.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Audio_Sample_Grabber_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether raw audio sample capture is enabled.
member.value: true to enable audio frame capture events; false to disable. Default is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the OnAudioFrameBuffer event provides raw audio samples for custom processing, analysis, or recording. Has minimal performance impact but should be disabled when not needed. Audio format details are provided in the event arguments.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Audio_VUMeter_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether basic audio level metering is enabled.
member.value: true to enable VU meter events; false to disable. Default is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the OnAudioVUMeter event provides real-time audio levels for creating visual meters. For more advanced metering with FFT and professional features, use Audio_VUMeter_Pro_Enabled instead.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Audio_VUMeter_Pro_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether professional audio metering and analysis is enabled.
member.value: true to enable advanced audio analysis; false to disable. Default is false.
member.remarks: VU Meter Pro provides professional audio monitoring features: - High-precision level metering with true peak detection - FFT spectrum analysis (OnAudioVUMeterProFFTCalculated) - Maximum sample tracking (OnAudioVUMeterProMaximumCalculated) - Volume level events (OnAudioVUMeterProVolume) Has higher CPU usage than basic VU meter.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.FAudio_VUMeter_Pro_Volume
member.summary: Internal storage for VU Meter Pro volume level.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Audio_VUMeter_Pro_Volume
member.summary: Gets or sets the reference volume level for VU Meter Pro calculations.
member.value: Volume level as a percentage (0-100). Default is 100.
member.remarks: This affects the sensitivity of the VU meter display. Lower values make the meter more sensitive to quiet signals. The value is applied to the VU Meter Pro filter immediately if it's already initialized.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore._filenamesOrURL
member.summary: Internal playlist storage containing file paths and URLs.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore._currentFilename

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore._currentIndex

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore._videoView
member.summary: Video display surface implementation.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.VideoView
member.summary: Gets or sets the video display surface for rendering video output.
member.value: An IVideoView implementation (WinForms, WPF, MAUI, etc.) or null for audio-only.
member.remarks: The video view determines where video frames are displayed. Different UI frameworks provide different implementations. Setting this automatically attaches the player to the view. Set to null for audio-only playback or when using Virtual Camera or NDI output modes.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.FVideoRenderer
member.summary: Internal storage for video renderer configuration.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Renderer
member.summary: Gets or sets video renderer configuration including renderer type and display options.
member.value: VideoRendererSettings object containing renderer mode, aspect ratio, and other display settings.
member.remarks: The renderer type affects compatibility and features: - EVR: Enhanced Video Renderer (Windows 7+) - recommended - VMR9: Video Mixing Renderer 9 - legacy, supports PiP - VMR7: Older systems only - Custom: For special rendering scenarios Changes apply immediately during playback.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Source_MemoryStream
member.summary: Gets or sets the memory stream source for playing media from memory buffers.
member.value: MemoryStreamSource object providing media data, or null if not using memory mode.
member.remarks: Used only when Source_Mode is set to MediaPlayerSourceMode.Memory. Implement the MemoryStreamSource interface to provide media data from memory buffers, encrypted sources, or custom storage. The source must provide data in a format DirectShow can parse (container with headers).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Source_Mode
member.summary: Gets or sets the media source type determining which playback engine to use.
member.value: The source mode: LAV (recommended), MediaFoundation, FFMPEG, etc. Default is LAV.
member.remarks: Different source modes offer different capabilities: - LAV: Best codec support, hardware acceleration, recommended for most uses - MediaFoundation: Native Windows, good for DRM content - FFMPEG: Cross-platform, good for streaming protocols - Memory_DS: For playing from memory buffers - HTTP_RTSP_VLC: VLC engine for network streams Set before calling Play().

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Source_GPU_Mode
member.summary: Gets or sets the GPU decoder type when using hardware acceleration.
member.value: LAVGPUDecoder enumeration value specifying which GPU decoder to use. Default depends on system capabilities.
member.remarks: Hardware decoding offloads video decoding to GPU, reducing CPU usage: - DXVA2: DirectX Video Acceleration 2 (Windows) - D3D11: Direct3D 11 (Windows 8+) - NVIDIA: NVIDIA CUVID/NVDEC - Intel: Intel Quick Sync Video Only applies when using LAV source mode. The system falls back to software decoding if the selected GPU decoder isn't available.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Source_Custom_CLSID
member.summary: Gets or sets the CLSID of a custom DirectShow source filter.
member.value: GUID string in format "{XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX}" or empty for default.
member.remarks: Use this to specify a custom DirectShow source filter for specialized media formats or hardware devices. The filter must be registered on the system and compatible with IFileSourceFilter or similar interfaces. Only used when Source_Mode is set to appropriate custom mode.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore._state
member.summary: Current playback state (thread-safe).

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.State
member.summary: Gets the current playback state of the media player.
member.returns: Current PlaybackState: Free (stopped), Playing, Paused, or Finished.
member.remarks: Use this to determine valid operations. For example, Pause() only works when Playing, Resume() only works when Paused. The state is updated automatically and corresponding events fire on state changes.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Play_PauseAtFirstFrame
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to automatically pause after displaying the first frame.
member.value: true to pause at first frame; false to play normally. Default is false.
member.remarks: Useful for preview scenarios where you want to show the first frame without playing. The player enters Paused state after the first frame is rendered. Call Resume() to continue playback. This provides a visual preview while keeping the player ready for immediate playback.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Play_DelayEnabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether delayed start mode is enabled for synchronized playback.
member.value: true to enable two-phase startup; false for normal immediate playback. Default is false.
member.remarks:
Delayed start allows precise synchronization of multiple players: 1. Set Play_DelayEnabled = true 2. Call Play() to build the graph and prepare playback 3. Call Play_DelayedStart() on all players simultaneously
This minimizes startup lag when synchronizing multiple video streams, as all time-consuming initialization is done in advance.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Selection_Active
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether playback range selection is active.
member.value: true to limit playback to the selected range; false for full file playback. Default is false.
member.remarks: When active, playback is constrained between Selection_Start and Selection_Stop. Useful for playing specific segments, creating clips, or loop points. The player automatically stops or loops when reaching Selection_Stop.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Selection_Start
member.summary: Gets or sets the start position for range-based playback.
member.value: TimeSpan indicating where selected playback should begin. Must be less than Selection_Stop and within media duration.
member.remarks: Only used when Selection_Active is true. Set this before or during playback to define the beginning of a playback range. The player automatically seeks to this position when starting if beyond it.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Selection_Stop
member.summary: Gets or sets the end position for range-based playback.
member.value: TimeSpan indicating where selected playback should end. Must be greater than Selection_Start.
member.remarks: Only used when Selection_Active is true. When playback reaches this position, it stops (or loops if Loop is enabled). Use TimeSpan.Zero to play to the end of the media file.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Custom_Video_Decoder
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of a custom video decoder filter to use instead of the default.
member.value: DirectShow filter name for video decoding, or empty string/null for automatic selection.
member.remarks: Override the default video decoder selection for specific codec requirements or hardware decoders. The filter must be installed and registered on the system. Common examples: "LAV Video Decoder", "ffdshow Video Decoder", "Microsoft DTV-DVD Video Decoder". Use Audio_CustomFilter_ListAll() to see available filters.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Custom_Splitter
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of a custom splitter/demuxer filter for parsing media containers.
member.value: DirectShow filter name for splitting, or empty string/null for automatic selection.
member.remarks: Override the default splitter for specific container formats or features. Splitters parse container formats (AVI, MP4, MKV) and separate audio/video streams. Examples: "LAV Splitter", "Haali Media Splitter", "AVI Splitter". Must be compatible with your media format.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Custom_Audio_Decoder
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of a custom audio decoder filter to use instead of the default.
member.value: DirectShow filter name for audio decoding, or empty string/null for automatic selection.
member.remarks: Override the default audio decoder for specific codec support or processing features. Examples: "LAV Audio Decoder", "ffdshow Audio Decoder", "AC3Filter". The decoder must support the audio format in your media files. Use Audio_CustomFilter_ListAll() to enumerate available filters.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Virtual_Camera_Output_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether video output is redirected to Virtual Camera SDK.
member.value: true to output video as a virtual webcam; false for normal display. Default is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, video is sent to VisioForge Virtual Camera instead of the display. This allows the media player output to appear as a webcam in other applications. Screen rendering is disabled, but OnVideoFrame events still work for monitoring. Requires Virtual Camera SDK to be installed and licensed.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.NDI_Output
member.summary: Gets or sets NDI (Network Device Interface) output configuration for network video streaming.
member.value: NDIOutput object with streaming settings, or null to disable NDI output.
member.remarks: NDI enables low-latency video streaming over IP networks for professional workflows. When configured, video is sent to the network instead of screen display. Configure the NDI source name, groups, and other settings in the NDIOutput object. OnVideoFrame events remain available. Requires NDI runtime to be installed.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Virtual_Camera_Output_LicenseKey
member.summary: Gets or sets the license key for Virtual Camera SDK output functionality.
member.value: Valid Virtual Camera SDK license key string, or null/empty for trial mode.
member.remarks: Required when Virtual_Camera_Output_Enabled is true and using licensed features. Without a valid key, output may include watermarks or time limitations. Contact VisioForge for licensing. The key is validated when starting playback.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Virtual_Camera_Output_AlternativeAudioFilterName
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of an alternative audio filter to use with Virtual Camera output.
member.value: DirectShow filter name for audio processing or rendering, or null for default.
member.remarks: When using Virtual Camera output, you may need to route audio through a specific filter for compatibility or features. The filter can be: - Audio renderer (e.g., "Default DirectSound Device") - Audio processor (e.g., "Audio Resampler") This overrides normal audio routing when Virtual_Camera_Output_Enabled is true.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Effects_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether CPU-based video effects processing is enabled.
member.value: true to enable video effects pipeline; false to bypass all effects. Default is false.
member.remarks: This is the master switch for CPU-based video effects (brightness, contrast, deinterlacing, etc.). Individual effects must also be configured via Video_Effects_Add(). For GPU-accelerated effects, use Video_Effects_GPU_Enabled. Enabling effects increases CPU usage and may impact performance.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Resize

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore._videoResize
member.summary: Internal storage for video resize settings.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Crop
