member.value: VideoCropSettings defining crop margins, or null to disable cropping.
member.remarks: Use cropping to: - Remove black bars (letterboxing/pillarboxing) - Focus on specific regions of interest - Change aspect ratio by removing content Crop values are in pixels from each edge. Applied after scaling but before other video effects.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore._videoCrop
member.summary: Internal storage for video crop settings.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Effects_GPU_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether GPU-accelerated video effects are enabled.
member.value: true to enable GPU effects processing; false to disable. Default is false.
member.remarks: GPU effects provide hardware-accelerated processing for better performance with effects like color correction, denoising, and transitions. Requires compatible graphics hardware (DirectX 11). Configure individual GPU effects via Video_Effects_GPU_Add(). Can be used alongside CPU effects.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Sample_Grabber_UseForVideoEffects
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to use sample grabber for video effects processing.
member.value: true to process effects via sample grabber; false for in-place processing. Default is true.
member.remarks: Sample grabber mode provides more control over effect processing and ensures effects work with all video formats, but may have slight performance impact. In-place mode is faster but may not support all combinations of codecs and effects. Generally, leave this enabled unless you have specific performance requirements.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore._motionDetectionSettings
member.summary: Internal storage for motion detection configuration.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Motion_Detection
member.summary: Gets or sets motion detection configuration for detecting movement in video.
member.value: MotionDetectionSettings object with detection parameters, or null to disable.
member.remarks: Motion detection analyzes video frames to detect movement and can trigger the OnMotion event. Configure sensitivity, detection zones, and algorithms in the settings object. Useful for security, automation, or activity monitoring. Processing overhead depends on algorithm and frame size. Settings are applied immediately to the motion detector if active.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.MIDI_Renderer
member.summary: Gets or sets the MIDI synthesizer device for playing MIDI files.
member.value: MIDI device name as returned by MIDI_Renderer_GetList(), or empty for default.
member.remarks: Selects which MIDI synthesizer to use for .mid and .kar file playback. Options typically include "Microsoft GS Wavetable Synth" (default) and any hardware MIDI devices or software synthesizers installed. Better synthesizers provide higher quality instrument sounds.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.MultiScreen_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether multi-monitor video display is enabled.
member.value: true to enable output to multiple displays; false for single display. Default is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, video can be displayed on multiple monitors simultaneously. Configure additional screens using MultiScreen_AddScreen() method. Each screen can have independent size and position settings. Useful for video walls, multi-monitor workstations, or presentation systems. Requires appropriate video renderer (typically VMR9).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Motion_DetectionEx
member.summary: Gets or sets advanced motion and object detection configuration.
member.value: MotionDetectionExSettings with AI-based detection parameters, or null to disable.
member.remarks: Motion Detection Ex provides advanced detection capabilities: - Object classification (person, vehicle, animal) - Object tracking across frames - Zone-based detection with multiple areas - Reduced false positives using AI Requires more processing power than basic motion detection. Settings are applied immediately if detection is active.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.FChromaKey
member.summary: Internal storage for chroma key (green screen) configuration.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.ChromaKey
member.summary: Gets or sets chroma key (green/blue screen) removal configuration.
member.value: ChromaKeySettings object with color and tolerance values, or null to disable.
member.remarks: Chroma key removes a specific color (typically green or blue) from video, making it transparent. Used for: - Green screen effects - Virtual backgrounds - Compositing multiple video sources Configure key color, similarity tolerance, and blend settings. Requires GPU effects to be enabled. Settings apply immediately.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.FBarcodeReaderEnabled
member.summary: Internal flag for barcode detection state.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Barcode_Reader_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether barcode and QR code detection is enabled.
member.value: true to scan video frames for barcodes; false to disable scanning. Default is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, video frames are analyzed for barcodes and QR codes. Detected codes trigger the OnBarcodeDetected event with decoded data. Configure barcode types to detect via Barcode_Reader_Type property. Detection has CPU overhead; enable only when needed. The internal barcode reader is updated immediately when changed.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Barcode_Reader_Type
member.summary: Gets or sets which types of barcodes to detect in video frames.
member.value: BarcodeType flags indicating which barcode formats to scan for. Can combine multiple types using bitwise OR.
member.remarks: Common types include: - QR codes (2D) - Code128, Code39 (1D barcodes) - EAN/UPC (retail barcodes) - DataMatrix, PDF417 (2D codes) Limiting types improves performance. Detection accuracy depends on video quality, barcode size, and lighting conditions.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Face_Tracking
member.summary: Gets or sets face detection and tracking configuration.
member.value: FaceTrackingSettings with detection parameters, or null to disable face tracking.
member.remarks: Face tracking detects and follows human faces in video: - Face detection with bounding boxes - Multiple face tracking - Optional facial landmark detection - Face recognition capabilities The OnFaceDetected event fires when faces are found. Requires significant CPU/GPU resources depending on settings.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.MaximalSpeedPlayback
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to play media as fast as possible without timing constraints.
member.value: true to disable frame timing and play at maximum speed; false for normal playback. Default is false.
member.remarks: Maximal speed mode is useful for: - Rapid file analysis or scanning - Batch processing or transcoding - Testing and benchmarking Audio is typically disabled in this mode. Actual speed depends on decoding complexity and system performance.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Encryption_Key
member.summary: Sets the encryption key for playing protected media files.
member.value: Can be: string (text key), byte[] (binary key), or string (path to key file). Type is determined by Encryption_KeyType property.
member.remarks: Used for playing encrypted media files. The key format and encryption method must match how the file was encrypted. Common uses: - DRM-protected content - Secure media distribution - Private video archives Set both Encryption_Key and Encryption_KeyType before playback.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Encryption_KeyType
member.summary: Gets or sets how to interpret the Encryption_Key value.
member.value: EncryptionKeyType: String, Binary, or File. Must match the key format provided in Encryption_Key.
member.remarks: Determines how the Encryption_Key property is processed: - String: Key is a text string - Binary: Key is a byte array - File: Key is a file path to read the key from Set this before playing encrypted content.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.ReversePlayback_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether reverse (backwards) playback mode is enabled.
member.value: true to play video in reverse; false for normal forward playback. Default is false.
member.remarks: Reverse playback plays video backwards from current position. This feature: - Requires Professional edition - Uses frame caching (configure with ReversePlayback_CacheSize) - Works best with keyframe-based codecs - May have performance limitations with high-resolution video When disabled while paused, clears the frame cache and resumes forward playback.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.SDK_BuildDate
member.summary: Gets the build date of the currently loaded SDK assembly.
member.returns: DateTime when this SDK version was compiled.
member.remarks: Useful for version verification and troubleshooting. The build date helps identify specific SDK releases when the version number alone isn't sufficient.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.SDK_Version
member.summary: Gets the version number of the currently loaded SDK assembly.
member.remarks: Use this to verify SDK compatibility and features. Version numbers follow semantic versioning where Major changes indicate breaking changes, Minor changes add features, and Build/Revision are for bug fixes.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.ReversePlayback_CacheSize
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of frames to cache for reverse playback performance.
member.value: Number of frames to keep in memory. Larger values improve reverse playback smoothness but use more RAM. Default varies by video resolution.
member.remarks: Reverse playback requires caching decoded frames because most video codecs only decode forward efficiently. Optimal cache size depends on: - Video resolution (HD needs more memory) - Available RAM - Desired smoothness Typical values: 30-60 for HD, 100+ for SD video.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.ConsoleUsage
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the SDK is being used in a console application.
member.value: true for console/service applications; false for GUI applications. Default is false.
member.remarks: Enable this when using the SDK in console applications, Windows services, or other non-GUI environments. This adjusts internal behavior to avoid UI dependencies and message pumping requirements. Some features requiring UI interaction may be limited.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.CustomRedist_Path
member.summary: Gets or sets the custom path for redistributable DirectShow filters and codecs.
member.value: Full path to the folder containing .ax and .dll files, or null for default locations.
member.remarks: Use this to specify where the SDK should load filters from: - Portable installations - Isolated codec sets - Version-specific filters The path should contain LAV Filters, ffdshow, or other required codecs. Files are loaded from this path before system-registered filters.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.CustomRedist_DisableDialog
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to suppress the missing codec warning dialog.
member.value: true to disable the warning dialog; false to show it when codecs are missing. Default is false.
member.remarks: By default, the SDK shows a dialog when required codecs aren't found during initialization. Enable this for: - Automated/unattended applications - Custom error handling - Embedded scenarios You should implement your own codec detection if disabling this dialog.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.CustomRedist_Enable(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Enables or disables the use of custom redistributable filters.
member.param: true to load filters from CustomRedist_Path; false to use only system-registered filters.
member.remarks: Call this before initializing playback. When enabled, filters from the custom path take precedence over system filters. Useful for ensuring consistent behavior across different systems or using specific filter versions.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.CustomRedist_IsEnabled
member.summary: Gets whether custom redistributable filter loading is currently enabled.
member.returns: true if loading filters from custom path; false if using system filters only.
member.remarks: Use this to verify the current filter loading configuration, especially when troubleshooting codec issues or verifying deployment settings.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.CustomRedist_Auto
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to automatically detect and use redistributable filters in the application folder.
member.value: true to auto-detect filters in app folder and subfolders; false for manual configuration only. Default is true.
member.remarks: When enabled, the SDK automatically searches for filter files in: - Application folder - x86/x64 subfolders (based on process architecture) - Common codec folder names This simplifies deployment by allowing filters to be copied with your app. Disable for full control over filter loading.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.CustomParameters
member.summary: Gets or sets custom key-value parameters for advanced SDK configuration.
member.value: Dictionary of parameter names and values for SDK customization.
member.remarks: Used for advanced scenarios and experimental features not exposed through standard properties. Parameters may include: - Undocumented performance tuning - Beta feature flags - Vendor-specific options Consult VisioForge support for available parameters. Invalid parameters are ignored.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.OSD_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets whether On-Screen Display (OSD) overlay system is enabled.
member.value: true to enable OSD layer support; false to disable all overlays. Default is false.
member.remarks: Must be set before calling Play(). When enabled, you can add text, images, and graphics overlays using OSD_Layers methods. OSD is useful for: - Watermarks and logos - Subtitles and captions - Time/date stamps - Custom graphics Requires compatible video renderer (EVR or VMR9).

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Tags_Read(System.String)
member.summary: Reads metadata tags from a media file without loading it for playback.
member.param: Full path to the media file to read tags from.
member.returns: MediaFileTags object containing all available metadata, or null if reading fails.
member.remarks:
Supported metadata includes: - Basic tags: Title, Artist, Album, Year, Genre, Comment - Advanced tags: AlbumArtist, Composer, Publisher, Conductor - Technical info: Bitrate, Duration, Codec information - Embedded artwork: Cover images and thumbnails
Supported formats include: - Audio: MP3 (ID3v1/v2), MP4/M4A, WMA, OGG Vorbis, FLAC - Video: MP4, MKV, AVI (limited), WMV
All text values are returned as strings. Artwork is returned as byte arrays. This method is lightweight and doesn't require initializing playback.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.FVideoEffectsLock
member.summary: Thread synchronization lock for video effects collection access.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Effects_Add(VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.IVideoEffect)
member.summary: Adds a video effect to the processing pipeline.
member.param: Video effect implementation to add. Must implement IVideoEffect interface.
member.remarks:
Effects are processed in the order they are added. Common effect types include: - Color adjustments: brightness, contrast, saturation, hue - Transforms: rotate, flip, crop, resize - Overlays: text logos, image watermarks, scrolling text - Filters: blur, sharpen, denoise, edge detection - Special effects: fade, chroma key, picture-in-picture
Effects can be added before or during playback. Remember to set Video_Effects_Enabled = true for effects to be processed. The effect's Name property should be unique for later retrieval.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Effects_Get(System.String)
member.summary: Retrieves a video effect by its name for runtime modification.
member.param: The name assigned to the effect when created. Case-insensitive.
member.returns: The IVideoEffect instance if found; null if no effect with that name exists.
member.remarks:
Use this to modify effect parameters during playback. For example: - Adjust brightness/contrast in response to user input - Update text overlay content - Enable/disable effects dynamically - Animate effect parameters
Cast the returned interface to the specific effect type to access its properties. The search is case-insensitive for convenience.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Effects_Clear
member.summary: Removes all video effects from the processing pipeline.
member.remarks:
This method: - Removes all effects immediately - Properly disposes of effects that hold resources (logos, images) - Restores original video appearance - Is thread-safe and can be called during playback
Effects that implement IDisposable (ImageLogo, TextLogo, ScrollingTextLogo) are disposed to free resources like loaded images or fonts. After clearing, you can add new effects without stopping playback.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Effects_Remove(System.String)
member.summary: Removes a specific video effect from the processing pipeline.
member.param: The exact name of the effect to remove (case-sensitive).
member.remarks:
Removes the first effect found with the specified name. If multiple effects have the same name, only the first is removed. The method: - Safely removes the effect during playback - Disposes of effects that hold resources - Maintains the order of remaining effects - Silently succeeds if the effect is not found
Use this for dynamic effect management, such as removing temporary overlays or disabling specific processing based on conditions.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Effects_GPU_Add(VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.IGPUVideoEffect)
member.summary: Adds a GPU-accelerated video effect to the processing pipeline.
member.param: GPU video effect implementation. Must implement IGPUVideoEffect interface.
member.remarks:
GPU effects leverage DirectX 11 compute shaders for high-performance processing: - Color grading and correction - Advanced denoising and sharpening - Real-time video stabilization - Complex transitions and blending - AI-powered effects (super-resolution, style transfer)
Requirements: - DirectX 11 compatible GPU - Video_Effects_GPU_Enabled must be true - Compatible video renderer (EVR preferred)
GPU effects can be combined with CPU effects. Processing order is maintained. Effects are identified by their Name property for later modification.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Effects_GPU_Get(System.String)
member.summary: Retrieves a GPU video effect by its name for runtime modification.
member.param: The unique name assigned to the effect when created.
member.returns: The IGPUVideoEffect instance if found; null if no effect with that name exists.
member.remarks:
Use this to modify GPU effect parameters during playback: - Adjust shader parameters in real-time - Enable/disable effects based on performance - Animate effect properties - Update textures or lookup tables
Cast the returned interface to the specific GPU effect type to access its specialized properties and shader parameters.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Effects_GPU_Clear
member.summary: Removes all GPU video effects from the processing pipeline.
member.remarks:
Immediately removes all GPU effects and releases associated GPU resources: - Shader resources and textures - Compute buffers - DirectX 11 device contexts
This operation is thread-safe and can be performed during playback. The video returns to its original appearance. GPU resources are properly released to prevent memory leaks.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Effects_GPU_Remove(System.String)
member.summary: Removes a specific GPU video effect from the processing pipeline.
member.param: The exact name of the GPU effect to remove.
member.remarks:
Removes the named effect and releases its GPU resources: - Unloads compute shaders - Releases texture resources - Frees GPU memory allocations
The removal is immediate and thread-safe. Other effects continue processing in their original order. If the effect is not found, the method completes silently without error.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Renderer_UpdateAsync(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Asynchronously updates video renderer display settings to handle window size changes.
member.param: New display width in pixels. Pass 0 to use current window width.
New display height in pixels. Pass 0 to use current window height.
member.returns: A task that completes when the renderer has been updated.
member.remarks: Call this method when the video display window is resized to ensure proper video scaling and aspect ratio. The method recalculates display parameters and notifies the renderer of the new dimensions. Safe to call during playback. Only available when using async API mode.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Renderer_Update(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Updates video renderer display settings to handle window size changes.
member.param: New display width in pixels. Pass 0 to use current window width.
New display height in pixels. Pass 0 to use current window height.
member.remarks: Call this method when the video display window is resized to ensure proper video scaling and aspect ratio. The method recalculates display parameters and notifies the renderer of the new dimensions. Safe to call during playback. Only available when using synchronous API mode.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Renderer_UpdateIntl(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Internal implementation for updating video renderer display settings.
member.param: If true, also updates the window handle binding.
member.remarks: This method performs the actual renderer update including: - Invoking UI thread updates via the video view - Recalculating display parameters - Updating window handle if requested - Refreshing the DirectShow filter graph

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Renderer_SetAuto
member.summary: Automatically selects the best available video renderer for the current system.
member.remarks:
Selection priority: 1. EVR (Enhanced Video Renderer) - Windows 7+ with best features 2. VMR-9 (Video Mixing Renderer 9) - Windows XP+ with good features 3. Legacy Video Renderer - Fallback for older systems
EVR is preferred for modern systems as it provides: - Better performance and quality - DXVA hardware acceleration - Advanced deinterlacing - Improved color space handling

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Renderer_SetCustomWindowHandle(System.IntPtr)

member.param: Native window handle (HWND) where video should be rendered.
member.remarks: Use this to render video to a specific window handle instead of the default video view. Useful for: - Rendering to external windows - Custom UI frameworks - Multi-window applications The handle must remain valid throughout playback.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Renderer_Deinterlace_Modes_Fill
member.summary: Populates the list of available deinterlacing modes from the video renderer.
member.remarks: Queries the video renderer (typically VMR9) for supported deinterlacing algorithms. Different modes offer various quality/performance tradeoffs: - Bob: Fast but lower quality - Weave: Simple, may show combing - Motion Adaptive: Better quality, more CPU - Motion Compensated: Best quality, highest CPU The available modes depend on graphics hardware capabilities.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.MediaPlayerCore.Video_Renderer_Deinterlace_Modes
member.summary: Gets the list of available deinterlacing modes supported by the current video renderer.
member.returns: Observable collection of deinterlacing mode names.
member.remarks:
Deinterlacing removes interlacing artifacts from video sources like: - Analog TV captures - DV camcorder footage - Some broadcast content
The list is populated on first access and cached. Available modes depend on the video renderer and graphics hardware. Returns empty collection if deinterlacing is not supported.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.IMediaPlayerCore
member.summary: Defines the core interface for Media Player SDK implementations, providing access to underlying player functionality, DVD controls, and source mode information.
member.remarks: This interface extends IMPVCVECore and serves as the foundation for all media player implementations. It provides access to the concrete MediaPlayerCore instance, DVD navigation controls (when playing DVDs), and information about the current media source type and playback engine.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.IMediaPlayerCore.GetCore
member.summary: Gets the underlying MediaPlayerCore instance that implements this interface.
member.returns: The concrete MediaPlayerCore implementation providing full access to all player functionality, properties, and events.
member.remarks: Use this method when you need access to functionality not exposed through the interface abstraction, such as platform-specific features or advanced configuration.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.IMediaPlayerCore.GetDVDControl
member.summary: Gets the DirectShow DVD navigation control interface for DVD playback control.
member.returns: An IDvdControl2 interface for controlling DVD navigation, or null if not playing a DVD or if the DirectShow engine is not in use.
member.remarks: This interface provides DVD-specific controls such as menu navigation, chapter selection, angle changes, and audio/subtitle stream selection. Only available when using the DirectShow engine (LAV mode) with DVD content.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.IMediaPlayerCore.GetDVDInfo
member.summary: Gets the DirectShow DVD information interface for querying DVD properties and state.

member.remarks: This interface provides read-only access to DVD information such as current domain, title/chapter count, available audio/subtitle streams, parental level settings, and disc region information. Only available when using the DirectShow engine with DVD content.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.MediaPlayer.IMediaPlayerCore.GetSourceMode
member.summary: Gets the current media source mode indicating which playback engine is in use.
member.returns: The active MediaPlayerSourceMode: LAV (DirectShow with LAV Filters), File (DirectShow), MediaFoundation, FFMPEG, or other specialized modes.
member.remarks: The source mode determines which underlying technology is used for media playback. Different modes offer different capabilities: - LAV: Best compatibility and codec support via DirectShow - MediaFoundation: Native Windows API, good for DRM content - FFMPEG: Cross-platform support, best for streaming protocols The mode is typically set in Player.SourceMode before playback.

Initialize an image.
member.param: The byte stride between pixels vertically.
The pointer to the pixel buffer.
The type of the components of the pixels.
One of { NVCV_CHUNKY, NVCV_PLANAR } or one of the YUV layouts.
Location of the buffer: one of { NVCV_CPU, NVCV_CPU_PINNED, NVCV_GPU, NVCV_CUDA }.
member.returns: NvCVStatus. NVCV_SUCCESS if successful. NVCV_ERR_PIXELFORMAT if the pixel format is not yet accommodated.

member.summary: Allocate memory for, and initialize an image. This assumes that the image data structure has nothing meaningful in it.
member.param: The desired width of the image, in pixels.
The desired height of the image, in pixels.
The type of the components of the pixels.
One of { NVCV_CHUNKY, NVCV_PLANAR } or one of the YUV layouts.
Location of the buffer: one of { NVCV_CPU, NVCV_CPU_PINNED, NVCV_GPU, NVCV_CUDA }.

The row byte alignment. Choose 0 or a power of 2. 1: yields no gap whatsoever between scanlines; 0: default alignment: 4 on CPU, and cudaMallocPitch's choice on GPU. Other common values are 16 or 32 for cache line size.
member.returns: NvCVStatus. NVCV_SUCCESS - if the operation was successful. NVCV_ERR_PIXELFORMAT - if the pixel format is not accommodated. NVCV_ERR_MEMORY - if there is not enough memory to allocate the buffer.

member.summary: Reallocate memory for, and initialize an image. This assumes that the image is valid. It will check bufferBytes to see if enough memory is already available, and will reshape rather than realloc if true. Otherwise, it will free the previous buffer and reallocate a new one.
member.param: The type of the components of the pixels.
One of { NVCV_CHUNKY, NVCV_PLANAR } or one of the YUV layouts.
Location of the buffer: one of { NVCV_CPU, NVCV_CPU_PINNED, NVCV_GPU, NVCV_CUDA }.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.NvidiaMaxine.VideoEffects.API.NvCVImageAPI.NvCVImage_Transfer(VisioForge.Core.NvidiaMaxine.VideoEffects.API.NvCVImage,VisioForge.Core.NvidiaMaxine.VideoEffects.API.NvCVImage,System.Single,System.IntPtr,VisioForge.Core.NvidiaMaxine.VideoEffects.API.NvCVImage)
member.summary: Transfer one image to another, with a limited set of conversions.
member.param: The scale factor that can be applied when one (but not both) of the images is based on floating-point components; this parameter is ignored when all image components are represented with integer data types, or all image components are represented with floating-point data types.
The stream on which to perform the copy. This is ignored if both images reside on the CPU.

The temporary buffer that is sometimes needed when transferring images between the CPU and GPU in either direction (can be empty or NULL). It has the same characteristics as the CPU image, but it resides on the GPU.
member.returns: NvCVStatus. NVCV_SUCCESS - if successful. NVCV_ERR_PIXELFORMAT - if one of the pixel formats is not accommodated. NVCV_ERR_CUDA - if a CUDA error has occurred. NVCV_ERR_GENERAL - if an otherwise unspecified error has occurred.
member.remarks:
If any of the images resides on the GPU, it may run asynchronously, so cudaStreamSynchronize() should be called if it is necessary to run synchronously. The following table indicates (with X) the currently-implemented conversions: +-------------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+ | | u8 --> u8 | u8 --> f32 | f32 --> u8 | f32 --> f32 | +-------------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+ | Y --> Y | X | | X | X | | Y --> A | X | | X | X | | Y --> RGB | X | X | X | X | | Y --> RGBA | X | X | X | X | | A --> Y | X | | X | X | | A --> A | X | | X | X | | A --> RGB | X | X | X | X | | A --> RGBA | X | | | | | RGB --> Y | X | X | | | | RGB --> A | X | X | | | | RGB --> RGB | X | X | X | X | | RGB --> RGBA | X | X | X | X | | RGBA --> Y | X | X | | | | RGBA --> A | X | | | | | RGBA --> RGB | X | X | X | X | | RGBA --> RGBA | X | X | X | X | | RGB --> YUV420 | X | | X | | | RGBA --> YUV420 | X | | X | | | RGB --> YUV422 | X | | X | | | RGBA --> YUV422 | X | | X | | | RGB --> YUV444 | X | | X | | | RGBA --> YUV444 | X | | X | | | YUV420 --> RGB | X | X | | | | YUV420 --> RGBA | X | X | | | | YUV422 --> RGB | X | X | | | | YUV422 --> RGBA | X | X | | | | YUV444 --> RGB | X | X | | | | YUV444 --> RGBA | X | X | | | +-------------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+ where * Either source or destination can be CHUNKY or PLANAR. * Either source or destination can reside on the CPU or the GPU. * The RGB components are in any order (i.e. RGB or BGR; RGBA or BGRA). * For RGBA (or BGRA) destinations, most implementations do not change the alpha channel, so it is recommended to set it at initialization time with [cuda]memset(im.pixels, -1, im.pitch * im.height) or [cuda]memset(im.pixels, -1, im.pitch * im.height * im.numComponents) for chunky and planar images respectively. * YUV requires that the colorspace field be set manually prior to Transfer, e.g. typical for layout=NVCV_NV12: image.colorspace = NVCV_709 | NVCV_VIDEO_RANGE | NVCV_CHROMA_INTSTITIAL; * There are also RGBf16-->RGBf32 and RGBf32-->RGBf16 transfers. * Additionally, when the src and dst formats are the same, all formats are accommodated on CPU and GPU, and this can be used as a replacement for cudaMemcpy2DAsync() (which it utilizes). This is also true for YUV, whose src and dst must share the same format, layout and colorspace.
When there is some kind of conversion AND the src and dst reside on different processors (CPU, GPU), it is necessary to have a temporary GPU buffer, which is reshaped as needed to match the characteristics of the CPU image. The same temporary image can be used in subsequent calls to NvCVImage_Transfer(), regardless of the shape, format or component type, as it will grow as needed to accommodate the largest memory requirement. The recommended usage for most cases is to supply an empty image as the temporary; if it is not needed, no buffer is allocated. NULL can be supplied as the tmp image, in which case an ephemeral buffer is allocated if needed, with resultant performance degradation for image sequences.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.NvidiaMaxine.VideoEffects.API.NvVFXAPI.NvVFX_SetImage(System.IntPtr,System.String,VisioForge.Core.NvidiaMaxine.VideoEffects.API.NvCVImage@)
member.summary: Set the selected image descriptor. A shallow copy of the descriptor is made (preserving the pixel pointer), so that an ephemeral NvVFXImage_Init() wrapper may be used in the call to NvVFX_SetImage() if desired, without having to preserve it for the lifetime of the effect. The effect does not take ownership of the pixel buffer.
member.param: The selector of the effect image to configure.
Pointer to the image descriptor to be used for the selected effect image. NULL clears the selected internal image descriptor.
member.returns: NvCVStatus. NVCV_SUCCESS if the operation was successful. NVCV_ERR_EFFECT if an invalid effect handle was supplied. NVCV_ERR_SELECTOR if the chosen effect does not understand the specified selector and data type. NVCV_ERR_PARAMETER if the value was out of range.

member.summary: Get a copy of the selected image descriptor. If GetImage() is called before SetImage(), the returned descriptor will be filled with zeros. Otherwise, the values will be identical to that in the previous SetImage() call, with the exception of deletePtr, deleteProc and bufferBytes, which will be 0.
member.param: The selector of the effect image to retrieve.
The place to store the selected image descriptor. A pointer to an empty NvCVImage (deletePtr==NULL) should be supplied to avoid memory leaks.
member.returns: NvCVStatus. NVCV_SUCCESS if the operation was successful. NVCV_ERR_EFFECT if an invalid effect handle was supplied. NVCV_ERR_SELECTOR if the chosen effect does not understand the specified selector and data type. NVCV_ERR_PARAMETER if the value was out of range.

member.param: The selector of the effect string to retrieve.

member.returns: NvCVStatus. NVCV_SUCCESS if the operation was successful. NVCV_ERR_EFFECT if an invalid effect handle was supplied. NVCV_ERR_SELECTOR if the chosen effect does not understand the specified selector and data type. NVCV_ERR_PARAMETER if the value was out of range.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.NvidiaMaxine.VideoEffects.Effects.MaxineBaseEffect.AllocTempBuffers
member.summary: Allocate one temp buffer to be used for input and output. Reshaping of the temp buffer in NvCVImage_Transfer() is done automatically, and is very low overhead. We expect the destination to be largest, so we allocate that first to minimize reallocs probablistically. Then we Realloc for the source to get the union of the two. This could alternately be done at runtime by feeding in an empty temp NvCVImage, but there are advantages to allocating all memory at load time.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Streaming.MJPEGSource
member.summary: MJPEG video source.

remarks.para: The video source downloads JPEG images from the specified URL, which represents MJPEG stream.
Sample usage:

para.note: Some cameras produce HTTP header, which does not conform strictly to standard, what leads to .NET exception. To avoid this exception the useUnsafeHeaderParsing configuration option of httpWebRequest should be set, what may be done using application configuration file.

remarks.code: <configuration> <system.net> <settings> <httpWebRequest useUnsafeHeaderParsing="true" /> </settings> </system.net> </configuration>

member.name: E:VisioForge.Core.Streaming.MJPEGSource.NewFrame
member.summary: New frame event.

remarks.para: Notifies clients about new available frame from video source.

para.note: Since video source may have multiple clients, each client is responsible for making a copy (cloning) of the passed video frame, because the video source disposes its own original copy after notifying of clients.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Streaming.MJPEGSource.Proxy
member.summary: Gets or sets proxy information for the request.

remarks.para: The local computer or application config file may specify that a default proxy to be used. If the Proxy property is specified, then the proxy settings from the Proxy property overridea the local computer or application config file and the instance will use the proxy settings specified. If no proxy is specified in a config file and the Proxy property is unspecified, the request uses the proxy settings inherited from Internet Explorer on the local computer. If there are no proxy settings in Internet Explorer, the request is sent directly to the server.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Streaming.MJPEGSource.HttpUserAgent
member.summary: User agent to specify in HTTP request header.

remarks.para: Some IP cameras check what is the requesting user agent and depending on it they provide video in different formats or do not provide it at all. The property sets the value of user agent string, which is sent to camera in request header.
Default value is set to "Mozilla/5.0". If the value is set to , the user agent string is not sent in request header.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Streaming.MJPEGSource.ForceBasicAuthentication
member.summary: Force using of basic authentication when connecting to the video source.

remarks.para: For some IP cameras (TrendNET IP cameras, for example) using standard .NET's authentication via credentials does not seem to be working (seems like camera does not request for authentication, but expects corresponding headers to be present on connection request). So this property allows to force basic authentication by adding required HTTP headers when request is sent.
Default value is set to .

member.summary: Adds an audio effect to the specified audio stream.
member.param: The index of the audio stream (0-3), or -1 to apply to all streams.
The type of audio effect to add (e.g., Amplify, Echo, Reverb).
A unique name identifier for this effect instance.
True to enable the effect immediately, false to add it in disabled state.
The time position when the effect should start being applied.
The time position when the effect should stop being applied.
member.remarks: Effects can be added to individual audio streams or all streams simultaneously. The same effect type can be added multiple times with different names and parameters. Time-based effects allow for dynamic audio processing during playback.

member.summary: Configures parameters for an amplify audio effect.
member.param: The index of the audio stream (0-3), or -1 to apply to all streams.
The unique name of the amplify effect to configure.
The amplification level (10000 = no change, 20000 = 2x amplification, 5000 = 0.5x).
True to amplify each channel independently, false to use channel 0's value for all channels.
member.remarks: The amplify effect allows volume adjustment of audio streams. Values below 10000 reduce volume, values above 10000 increase it. Be careful with high values as they may cause audio clipping. Separate channel control is useful for stereo balance adjustments.

member.summary: Configures and adds a Blackmagic Decklink professional video/audio output to the processing pipeline.
member.returns: True if the Decklink renderer was successfully added, false otherwise.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.FastEdit_ExtractAudioStreamAsync(System.String,System.TimeSpan,System.TimeSpan,System.String)
member.summary: Extracts the audio stream from a video file without re-encoding.
member.param: Path to the input video file containing audio.
The time position to start extraction from.
The time position to stop extraction at.
Path where the extracted audio file will be saved.
member.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if successful.
member.remarks: This method performs fast audio extraction without re-encoding, preserving the original audio quality. The output format is determined by the file extension of outputFile. Requires FFMPEG executable files to be deployed with your application. Premium Edition license required for production use.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.FastEdit_CutFileAsync(System.String,System.TimeSpan,System.TimeSpan,System.String)
member.summary: Cuts a segment from a video file without re-encoding.
member.param: Path to the input video file to cut from.
The time position to start the cut from.
The time position to end the cut at.
Path where the cut video segment will be saved.
member.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if successful.
member.remarks: This method performs fast cutting without re-encoding, preserving original quality. The cut may not be frame-accurate for some codecs due to keyframe limitations. Requires FFMPEG executable files to be deployed with your application. Premium Edition license required for production use.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.FastEdit_MuxStreamsAsync(System.Collections.Generic.List{VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.FFMPEGStream},System.Boolean,System.String)
member.summary: Multiplexes (combines) audio and video streams from multiple files into a single output file.
member.param: List of source streams to multiplex, each specifying file path and stream type.
If true, cuts all streams to match the duration of the shortest stream.
Path where the multiplexed output file will be saved.
member.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if successful.
member.remarks: This method combines streams without re-encoding, making it very fast. Commonly used to add audio tracks to video files or combine separate audio/video streams. The streams must be compatible with the output container format. Premium Edition license required for production use.

member.summary: Joins multiple video files into a single output file without re-encoding.
member.param: Array of input file paths to join together.
Path where the joined output file will be saved.
member.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains true if successful.
member.remarks: This method performs fast concatenation without re-encoding. member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.UnbanLAV
member.summary: Removes LAV filters from the blacklist to enable their use.
member.remarks: LAV filters are high-quality open-source DirectShow filters. This method enables their use and blacklists conflicting Microsoft filters when LAV is available. LAV filters typically provide better codec support and performance.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.BanLAV
member.summary: Adds LAV filters to the blacklist to prevent their use.
member.remarks: Disables LAV filters and re-enables Microsoft DTV filters. This may be necessary for compatibility with certain systems or when LAV filters cause issues. The system will fall back to default Windows codecs.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.CheckRequiredLicense(System.Boolean@,System.Boolean@,System.Boolean@)
member.summary: Check and report required license.
member.param: When this method returns, contains true if standard license is required; otherwise, false.
When this method returns, contains true if professional license is required; otherwise, false.
When this method returns, contains true if premium license is required; otherwise, false.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.OnErrorCall(System.Object,VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.ErrorsEventArgs)
member.summary: Handles error events and dispatches them to the appropriate handler.
member.param: The object that raised the error event. Can be null.
Contains error details including severity and message.
member.remarks: This method ensures thread-safe error handling by invoking the error handler on the UI thread if a video view is available, otherwise handles it directly.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.VFErrorProviderOnOnErrorInvoker(VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.ErrorsEventArgs)
member.summary: Invokes the error handler delegate on the UI thread.
member.param: Contains error details to be processed.
member.remarks: This method is called via the video view's invoke mechanism to ensure error handling occurs on the correct thread.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.LoggerClose
member.summary: Closes and disposes the current logger instance.
member.remarks: Replaces the current logger with a silent logger that discards all messages, then properly disposes of the old logger to free resources.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.LoggerConfigure(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Configures the logging system based on current settings.
member.param: If true, enables error event notifications; if false, disables them.
member.remarks: This method sets up the logger with appropriate sinks based on debug mode: - In debug mode: Logs to file and debug output with detailed information - In release mode: Only logs errors to debug output - Optionally configures Sentry for telemetry if enabled

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.LoggerSentryOnStartConfigure
member.summary: Configures Sentry telemetry with diagnostic information at startup.
member.remarks: This method collects and attaches various diagnostic data to Sentry: - Current SDK settings as JSON - Available DirectShow filters - Audio output devices - System PATH environment variables - Custom redistributable files information This data helps diagnose issues when errors are reported.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.InvokeErrorHandler(System.Object,VisioForge.Core.Types.Events.ErrorsEventArgs)
member.summary: Invokes the appropriate error handler for the given error event.
member.param: Error details including message and severity.
member.remarks: This method handles errors by: 1. Checking for specific missing DLL errors in debug mode 2. Invoking the OnError event if handlers are registered 3. Displaying error dialogs if message dialogs are enabled Special handling is provided for missing MFP DLL errors.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.AddNetworkStreamingFFMPEG
member.summary: Configures network streaming using FFMPEG executable for RTMP, RTSP, or UDP protocols.
member.remarks: This method sets up FFMPEG-based network streaming by: - Creating an FFMPEG output filter configured for streaming - Connecting video and optionally audio streams - Supporting custom FFMPEG arguments for advanced streaming scenarios - Using a tee filter to split the stream for simultaneous file output and streaming Commonly used for streaming to services like YouTube, Twitch, or custom RTMP servers.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.AddNetworkStreamingNDI
member.summary: Configures network streaming using NDI (Network Device Interface) protocol.
member.remarks: NDI enables high-quality, low-latency video streaming over IP networks. This method: - Creates an NDI sender with a specified stream name - Connects video and optionally audio streams - Uses a tee filter to allow simultaneous file output and NDI streaming NDI is commonly used in professional broadcast and production environments for real-time video exchange between devices on the same network.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.AddNetworkStreamingHLS
member.summary: Configures HLS (HTTP Live Streaming) output for adaptive bitrate streaming.
member.remarks: HLS is Apple's adaptive streaming protocol that works over standard HTTP. This method: - Creates an HLS encoder using Media Foundation - Generates segmented video files and M3U8 playlists - Optionally starts a built-in HTTP server for testing - Supports both video and audio streams HLS is widely supported on mobile devices and modern browsers, making it ideal for web-based video delivery.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.AddNetworkStreamingSW
member.summary: Configures software-based network streaming using built-in MP4 encoder.
member.remarks: This method uses the software MP4 encoder with network streaming capabilities. Features: - Supports various streaming protocols through the MP4 encoder - Includes video resizing and cropping options - Can use NVENC hardware acceleration if available - Supports AAC or MP3 (LAME) audio encoding This is a fallback option when FFMPEG or specialized streaming methods are not available or suitable.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.AddOutputAVIAudio
member.summary: Connects audio streams to the AVI encoder and builds the audio output pipeline.
member.returns: true if all audio connections and build operations succeed, false otherwise.
member.remarks: This method connects up to 4 audio output pins to the AVI encoder. Each audio stream is connected to a specific encoder input. After all connections are made, the encoder is built to finalize the audio pipeline.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.AddOutputMKVv1Audio
member.summary: Connects audio streams to the MKV encoder and builds the audio output pipeline.
member.returns: true if all audio connections and build operations succeed, false otherwise.
member.remarks: This method connects up to 4 audio output pins to the MKV encoder. The implementation is identical to AVI audio handling as both use the same encoder. MKV (Matroska) container supports multiple audio streams.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.AddOutputAVIVideo
member.summary: Configures and initializes the AVI video encoder with specified settings.
member.returns: true if the video encoder is successfully initialized, false otherwise.
member.remarks: This method: - Creates and configures the AVI encoder with video codec settings - Optionally configures audio compression (ACM or MP3/LAME) - Connects the video output pin to the encoder - Builds the encoder pipeline if no audio is present The AVI format supports various video codecs through VFW (Video for Windows).

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.AddOutputMKVv1Video
member.summary: Configures and initializes the MKV (Matroska) video encoder with specified settings.
member.returns: true if the video encoder is successfully initialized, false otherwise.
member.remarks: This method: - Creates and configures the MKV encoder (using AVI encoder in Matroska mode) - Configures video compression settings - Optionally configures audio compression - Connects video output pin to the encoder MKV is a flexible container format supporting multiple video/audio streams and subtitles.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.AddOutputFFMPEGEXEVideoPipe(System.String,VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.FFMPEGEXEOutput)
member.summary: Configures and initializes FFMPEG output using pipe-based communication for video encoding.
member.param: The output file path where the encoded video will be saved.
FFMPEG output configuration containing codec and muxer settings.
member.returns: true if the FFMPEG pipe output is successfully initialized, false otherwise.
member.remarks: This method uses pipe-based communication with FFMPEG executable for encoding. It supports: - Custom FFMPEG arguments for advanced encoding options - Network streaming (RTMP, RTSP, UDP) in addition to file output - Both video and audio streams Pipe-based approach provides more flexibility than DirectShow filters.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.AddOutputWebMAudio
member.summary: Connects the audio stream to the WebM encoder and builds the audio pipeline.
member.returns: true if audio connection and build operations succeed, false otherwise.
member.remarks: WebM uses Vorbis or Opus audio codecs. This method applies audio parameters and connects the primary audio pin. WebM container only supports a single audio stream.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.AddOutputWebMVideo
member.summary: Configures and initializes the WebM video encoder with VP8/VP9 codec settings.
member.returns: true if the WebM encoder is successfully initialized, false otherwise.
member.remarks: This method: - Creates and configures the WebM encoder with VP8/VP9 settings - Adds a video effects filter for YUY2 color space conversion - Supports advanced VP8/VP9 encoding parameters - Handles both constant bitrate and quality-based encoding WebM is an open-source container format designed for web video.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.AddOutputM4A
member.summary: Creates an M4A (MPEG-4 Audio) output file with AAC audio encoding.
member.returns: true if the M4A encoder is successfully initialized, false otherwise.
member.remarks: M4A is an audio-only MPEG-4 container format commonly used for: - Music files with AAC encoding - Audiobooks and podcasts - iTunes-compatible audio This method configures the MP4 encoder in audio-only mode.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.AddOutputMFVideo(VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEdit.VideoEditOutputFormat)
member.summary: Configures and initializes Media Foundation-based output encoder for various formats.
member.param: The output format type (MP4_HW, MPEGTS, MKVv2, MOV).
member.returns: true if the Media Foundation encoder is successfully initialized, false otherwise.
member.remarks: This method uses Windows Media Foundation for hardware-accelerated encoding. Supported formats: - MP4_HW: Hardware-accelerated MP4 with H.264/H.265 - MPEGTS: MPEG Transport Stream for broadcasting - MKVv2: Matroska container using MF muxer - MOV: QuickTime movie format Validates resolution limits for MS H.264 encoder (max 1920x1080).

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.AddAudioChannelMapper
member.summary: Adds audio channel mapping filters to all active audio output pins.
member.remarks: This method inserts audio channel mapper filters into the audio pipeline to: - Remap audio channels (e.g., stereo to mono, channel swapping) - Adjust channel count for output compatibility - Mix or split audio channels as configured The mapper is applied to all active audio pins (up to 4 streams). If output channel count is not specified, it auto-detects from the first pin.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.AddAudioEnhancer
member.summary: Adds audio enhancement filters to all active audio output pins.
member.remarks: This method inserts audio enhancer filters into the audio pipeline to: - Normalize audio levels - Apply automatic gain control - Adjust input/output gains per channel - Apply time shifting for synchronization The enhancer is applied to all active audio pins (up to 4 streams). Each stream can have independent enhancement settings.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Audio_Enhancer_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether audio enhancer is enabled.
member.remarks: When enabled, applies audio enhancement processing to improve audio quality. This may include noise reduction, normalization, and other audio improvements.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Audio_Effects_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether audio effects are enabled.
member.remarks: When enabled, allows applying various audio effects to the audio stream. This includes effects like echo, reverb, pitch shift, and other DSP effects.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Audio_Preview_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether audio playback is enabled during preview.
member.remarks: Controls whether audio is played during video preview mode. Set to false to mute audio during preview while still processing it for output.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Audio_Channel_Mapper
member.summary: Gets or sets the audio channel mapper settings.
member.remarks: Configures how audio channels are mapped from input to output. Useful for remapping stereo to mono, changing channel assignments, or mixing channels.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Audio_VUMeter_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the audio VU meter is enabled.
member.remarks: When enabled, provides real-time audio level monitoring through VU meter events. The VU meter displays the amplitude of the audio signal.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Audio_VUMeter_Pro_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the professional audio VU meter is enabled.
member.remarks: Provides advanced VU meter functionality with enhanced audio visualization. Includes additional features like peak hold, stereo visualization, and frequency analysis. This is the newer, more feature-rich version of the VU meter.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.FAudio_VUMeter_Pro_Volume
member.summary: Internal field for storing the VU meter pro volume level.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Audio_VUMeter_Pro_Volume
member.summary: Gets or sets the volume level used by the professional VU meter, in percentage (0-100).
member.remarks: Controls the input sensitivity of the VU meter. Higher values make the meter more sensitive to quieter sounds.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Custom_Video_Decoder
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of a custom video decoder to use.
member.remarks: Allows specifying a custom DirectShow filter for video decoding. Leave empty to use the default decoder selection mechanism.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Custom_Audio_Decoder
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of a custom audio decoder to use.
member.remarks: Allows specifying a custom DirectShow filter for audio decoding. Leave empty to use the default decoder selection mechanism.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Mode
member.summary: Gets or sets the video editing operation mode.
member.remarks: Determines the primary function of the video editor: - Preview: Only preview without saving - Convert: Convert between formats - Edit: Full editing capabilities

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Output_Filename
member.summary: Gets or sets the full path and filename for the output file.
member.remarks: Specifies where the edited video will be saved. The file extension should match the selected output format.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Output_Format
member.summary: Gets or sets the output file format configuration.
member.remarks: Defines the container format, codecs, and encoding settings for the output file. Different output format classes provide settings for MP4, AVI, WMV, etc.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.State
member.summary: Gets the current playback state of the video editor.
member.returns: The current playback state (Stopped, Playing, Paused, etc.).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Start_DelayEnabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether delayed start mode is enabled.
member.remarks: This feature allows preparing the video processing graph without immediately starting playback. Useful for synchronizing multiple video editors or reducing startup latency. When enabled: 1. Call Start() to build the graph and prepare resources 2. Call StartDelayed() to begin actual playback/processing This enables near-instantaneous start since all initialization is already complete.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_FrameRate
member.summary: Gets or sets the output video frame rate.
member.remarks: Determines the frames per second (FPS) of the output video. Common values include 25, 29.97, 30, 50, 59.94, and 60 FPS.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Preview_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether video preview is enabled.
member.remarks: Controls whether the video is displayed in the preview window during editing. Set to false to process video without displaying it (headless mode).

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.FVideoRenderer
member.summary: Internal field for storing video renderer settings.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Renderer
member.summary: Gets or sets the video renderer configuration.
member.remarks: Configures how video is displayed, including renderer type (EVR, VMR9, etc.), aspect ratio handling, and display synchronization options.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Resize
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether video resizing is enabled.
member.remarks: When enabled, the output video will be resized to the dimensions specified in Video_Resize_Width and Video_Resize_Height properties.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Resize_Height
member.summary: Gets or sets the target height for video resizing, in pixels.
member.remarks: Only applied when Video_Resize is enabled. Should be set in conjunction with Video_Resize_Width to maintain aspect ratio if desired.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Resize_Width
member.summary: Gets or sets the target width for video resizing, in pixels.
member.remarks: Only applied when Video_Resize is enabled. Should be set in conjunction with Video_Resize_Height to maintain aspect ratio if desired.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Crop
member.summary: Gets or sets the video cropping configuration.
member.remarks: Defines the area of the video to keep by specifying crop margins. Useful for removing black bars, unwanted edges, or focusing on a specific region.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Subtitles
member.summary: Gets or sets the subtitle overlay configuration.
member.remarks: Configures subtitle rendering including font, color, position, and timing. Supports various subtitle formats like SRT, ASS, and embedded subtitles.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Rotation
member.summary: Gets or sets the video rotation angle.
member.remarks: Rotates the video by the specified angle (0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees). Useful for correcting orientation of videos recorded on mobile devices.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Effects_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether CPU-based video effects are enabled.
member.remarks: Enables processing of video effects using the CPU. These effects may have higher quality but lower performance compared to GPU effects.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Effects_GPU_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether GPU-accelerated video effects are enabled.
member.remarks: Enables hardware-accelerated video effects using the GPU. Provides better performance but requires compatible graphics hardware.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Effects_AllowMultipleStreams
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether video effects can use independent preview and output streams.
member.remarks: When enabled, different effects can be applied to preview and output streams independently. This allows showing a clean preview while applying effects only to the output, or vice versa.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.FMotionDetection
member.summary: Internal field for storing motion detection settings.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Motion_Detection
member.summary: Gets or sets the motion detection configuration.
member.remarks: Configures motion detection algorithms including sensitivity, detection zones, and motion highlighting options. Useful for security applications or activity monitoring.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.FChromaKey
member.summary: Internal field for storing chroma key settings.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.ChromaKey
member.summary: Gets or sets the chroma key (green screen) configuration.
member.remarks: Configures color-based transparency for compositing. Commonly used for green screen or blue screen effects to replace backgrounds.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Dynamic_Reconnection
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether dynamic source reconnection is enabled.
member.remarks: By default, the basic render engine loads every source before rendering a project. This can result in a long start-up time. With dynamic reconnection, sources are loaded only when needed. This can shorten the start-up time, but possibly interfere with smooth playback. Generally, the more source clips that a project uses, the more you might benefit from dynamic reconnection. Best suited for projects with many short clips where not all sources are needed simultaneously.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Custom_Resizer_CLSID
member.summary: Gets or sets the CLSID of a custom video resizer filter.
member.remarks: Allows specifying a custom DirectShow filter for video resizing operations. The filter must implement the appropriate interfaces for video transformation. Reference: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/dd377478(v=vs.85).aspx

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.fMotionDetectionEx
member.summary: Internal field for storing extended motion detection settings.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Motion_DetectionEx
member.summary: Gets or sets the advanced motion and object detection configuration.
member.remarks: Provides extended motion detection capabilities including object tracking, advanced algorithms, and more sophisticated detection parameters.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.FBarcodeReaderEnabled
member.summary: Internal field for storing barcode reader enabled state.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Barcode_Reader_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether barcode detection is enabled.
member.remarks: When enabled, the system will attempt to detect and decode barcodes in the video stream. Detected barcodes will trigger events with the decoded data.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Barcode_Reader_Type
member.summary: Gets or sets the type of barcode to detect.
member.remarks: Specifies which barcode symbologies to look for (QR Code, Code128, EAN, etc.). Can be set to detect multiple types or a specific type for better performance.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.ConsoleUsage
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the SDK is being used in a console application.
member.remarks: Enable this when using the SDK in a console application without a GUI. This adjusts internal behavior for headless operation.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Decklink_Input_Capture_Timecode_Source
member.summary: Gets or sets the timecode source for Decklink capture devices.
member.remarks: Specifies which timecode track to read from the Decklink input (VITC, LTC, etc.). Used for professional video production workflows requiring frame-accurate timecode.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Decklink_Output
member.summary: Gets or sets the configuration for Decklink video output devices.
member.remarks: Configures professional Blackmagic Decklink cards for video output. Includes settings for video mode, audio channels, and output routing.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Loop
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether playback should loop continuously.
member.remarks: When enabled, playback will automatically restart from the beginning when reaching the end. Useful for continuous playback scenarios or demo displays.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Network_Streaming_Audio_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether audio is included in network streaming.
member.remarks: When disabled, only video will be streamed over the network. Useful for reducing bandwidth when audio is not needed.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Network_Streaming_Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether network streaming is enabled.
member.remarks: Enables streaming the video output over a network using various protocols. The stream can be accessed by network clients for remote viewing.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Network_Streaming_Format
member.summary: Gets or sets the network streaming protocol format.
member.remarks: Determines the streaming protocol to use (RTSP, RTMP, HTTP, etc.). Different formats have different compatibility and feature sets.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Network_Streaming_WMV_Maximum_Clients
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of simultaneous streaming clients for WMV format.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Effects_Add(VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.IVideoEffect)
member.summary: Adds a video effect to the processing pipeline.
member.param: The video effect to add, implementing IVideoEffect interface.
member.remarks: Effects are processed in the order they are added. Multiple effects of the same or different types can be added. Effects can include: - Color adjustments (brightness, contrast, saturation) - Image overlays and logos - Text overlays - Geometric transformations - Various filters and artistic effects Thread-safe operation.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Effects_Get(System.String)
member.summary: Retrieves a video effect by its unique name.
member.param: The name of the effect to retrieve (case-insensitive).
member.returns: The video effect with the specified name, or null if not found.
member.remarks: Effect names are case-insensitive for convenience. Use this method to modify effect parameters during runtime. Thread-safe operation.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Effects_Clear
member.summary: Removes all video effects from the processing pipeline.
member.remarks: This method: - Properly disposes of effects that hold resources (ImageLogo, TextLogo, ScrollingTextLogo) - Clears the entire effects collection - Is thread-safe Call this method when switching projects or cleaning up resources.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Effects_Remove(System.String)
member.summary: Removes a specific video effect from the processing pipeline.
member.param: The name of the effect to remove (case-sensitive).
member.remarks: This method: - Finds the effect by exact name match - Properly disposes of effects that hold resources - Removes the effect from the collection - Is thread-safe If the effect is not found, no action is taken.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Effects_GPU_Add(VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoEffects.IGPUVideoEffect)
member.summary: Adds a GPU-accelerated video effect to the processing pipeline.
member.param: The GPU video effect to add, implementing IGPUVideoEffect interface.
member.remarks: GPU effects provide hardware-accelerated video processing using DirectX 11. Benefits include: - Significantly faster processing compared to CPU effects - Real-time performance for complex effects - Lower CPU usage Requires a DirectX 11 compatible graphics card. Effects are processed in the order they are added.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Effects_GPU_Get(System.String)
member.summary: Retrieves a GPU video effect by its unique name.
member.param: The name of the GPU effect to retrieve.
member.returns: The GPU video effect with the specified name, or null if not found.
member.remarks: Use this method to access and modify GPU effect parameters during runtime. GPU effects can be adjusted in real-time without rebuilding the pipeline.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Effects_GPU_Clear
member.summary: Removes all GPU video effects from the processing pipeline.
member.remarks: This method clears all GPU-accelerated effects. GPU resources are properly released. Use this when switching projects or cleaning up GPU resources.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.Video_Effects_GPU_Remove(System.String)
member.summary: Removes a specific GPU video effect from the processing pipeline.
member.param: The name of the GPU effect to remove.
member.remarks: Removes the specified GPU effect and releases its resources. If the effect is not found, no action is taken. The remaining effects continue processing in order.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.WMV_CustomProfile_AudioCodecs(VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WMVStreamMode)
member.summary: Gets a collection of available WMV audio codecs for the specified streaming mode.
member.param: The WMV streaming mode (CBR, VBR_Peak, VBR_Quality, etc.).
member.returns: An observable collection containing the names of compatible audio codecs.
member.remarks: This method enumerates Windows Media audio codecs that support the specified mode. Only codecs with at least one compatible format for the mode are included. Common codecs include Windows Media Audio 9, 9.1, 9.2, and Professional.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.WMV_CustomProfile_AudioFormats_GetCount(System.String,VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WMVStreamMode)
member.summary: Gets the count of audio formats available for a specific codec and streaming mode.
member.param: The name of the audio codec.
member.returns: The number of compatible audio formats.
member.remarks: This helper method counts formats that support the specified combination of codec and mode. Used internally to filter codecs that have no compatible formats.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.WMV_CustomProfile_AudioFormats(System.String,VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WMVStreamMode)
member.summary: Gets a collection of audio formats available for a specific WMV codec and streaming mode.
member.param: The name of the audio codec to query formats for.
The WMV streaming mode (CBR, VBR, etc.).
member.returns: An observable collection containing format descriptions (e.g., "44100 Hz, Stereo, 128 kbps").
member.remarks: Audio formats include combinations of: - Sample rate (8000 Hz to 48000 Hz) - Channels (Mono/Stereo) - Bitrate (varies by codec and mode) The available formats depend on the selected codec and streaming mode.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.WMV_CustomProfile_SaveToFile(System.String,VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WMVOutput)
member.summary: Saves a custom WMV profile configuration to a file.
member.param: The path where the profile file (.prx) will be saved.
The WMV output settings containing the profile configuration.
member.remarks: Creates a Windows Media profile file that can be: - Shared between applications - Loaded later for consistent encoding settings - Used with Windows Media Encoder The profile includes all audio/video codec settings, bitrates, and quality parameters.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.WMV_CustomProfile_VideoCodecs(VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WMVStreamMode)
member.summary: Gets a collection of available WMV video codecs for the specified streaming mode.
member.param: The WMV streaming mode (CBR, VBR_Peak, VBR_Quality, etc.).
member.returns: An observable collection containing the names of compatible video codecs.
member.remarks: This method enumerates Windows Media video codecs that support the specified mode. Common codecs include: - Windows Media Video 9 - Windows Media Video 9 Advanced Profile - Windows Media Video 9 Screen The availability depends on the Windows Media components installed.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.WMV_Internal_Profiles
member.summary: Gets a collection of built-in Windows Media profile names.
member.returns: An observable collection containing the names of all internal WMV profiles.
member.remarks: Internal profiles are predefined configurations provided by Windows Media Format SDK. These include optimized settings for various scenarios: - Dial-up, broadband, and LAN streaming - Different quality levels (low, medium, high) - Specific devices (portable players, etc.) Using internal profiles ensures compatibility and optimal performance.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.VideoEditCore.WMV_V8_Profiles(System.Collections.Generic.List{System.String}@,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.String}@)
member.summary: Gets lists of Windows Media Version 8 profile names and their descriptions.
member.param: Output list that will contain profile names.
Output list that will contain profile descriptions.
member.remarks: WMV V8 profiles are legacy profiles from Windows Media 8. Each profile has: - A short name for selection - A detailed description of its purpose and settings These profiles maintain compatibility with older Windows Media players. The lists are parallel - names[i] corresponds to descriptions[i].

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.FastEncrypt.Start(System.String[],System.String,VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.EncryptionKeyType,System.Object,System.Boolean,System.String,System.Boolean,System.String,System.Guid)
member.summary: Starts the fast encryption process for the specified video files.
member.param: Array of source video file paths to encrypt.
Path for the encrypted output file.
The type of encryption key (password, binary, etc.).
If true, uses version 9 encryptor; otherwise uses version 8.
If true, blocks until completion (for console applications).
Optional directory for saving debug graph files.
Optional GUID for custom source filter.
member.returns: True if encryption started successfully, false otherwise.
member.remarks: This method builds a DirectShow graph that: - Reads the source files without decoding - Passes the data through the encryption filter - Writes the encrypted data to the output file Multiple source files are concatenated in the output.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoEdit.FastEncrypt.Stop
member.summary: Stops the encryption process immediately.
member.remarks: The output file may be incomplete if stopped before completion.

member.summary: Pauses the encryption process.
